body:
## What was wrong

Checklist row 1 ("a test that fails on the pre-change tree and passes after") decided whether to read `red.txt` and `green.txt` from a path list: `src/`, `harness/`, `scripts/`. A PR whose code root was `benchmarks/` (competitive PR 3c) or `.claude/hooks/` (#642 twice, #643) read `n.a.` with a red/green pair sitting on disk, and each reviewer graded the row by hand and wrote that the row was not evidence. Workflows FINDINGS W-38, four instances.

## The fix

`dod_checklist.row1_verdict(changed, red, green)` grades a pair that exists whatever the path. `CODE_ROOTS` (`src/`, `harness/`, `scripts/`, `benchmarks/`, `tests/`, `.claude/hooks/`) decides only whether an absent pair is unmet or n.a. A red run that dies at collection (`error`, exit 2) counts as red, as the remedy said.

Row 3 is unchanged, and the remedy's "rows 1 and 3" is withdrawn for row 3. The first draft widened its gate to `benchmarks/`; review round 1 found that inert, because the row routes to `scripts/dod_changelog.py`, which requires an entry for `src/` only, so the row would read met with no entry, a parameter present and doing nothing.

The decision moved out of `main()` into a function so it can be tested: a full checklist run spawns pytest twice.

## A third path list (W-43, open)

`CODE_ROOTS` here is the third path list in the hooks, beside `_common.TIER_PATHS` (what the full-tier stamp covers) and `pre_commit.CODE_ROOTS` (what needs a fast tier), each with a different membership. A hooks-only commit skips the fast tier while this checklist calls the same edit a code change. Found by the reviewer; recorded as W-43 with the three lists, their purposes and the remedy, not unified in this PR because each list answers a different question and the fast-tier trigger is `pre_commit`'s decision.

## Reproduction

`tests/test_dod_checklist_code_roots.py`, six tests over the function. `red.txt`: the committed test file in a scratch worktree at main 6edd8eba (the file's first line names the ref), 6 failed, the function did not exist. `green.txt`: 71 passed over the new file, `test_workflows_registered.py` and `test_hook_budget_tree_kill.py`. This PR's own checklist is the first one the new row 1 grades from evidence: its code root is `.claude/hooks/`, which the old rule read as n.a.

## Record

FINDINGS W-38 FIXED with the row-3 half withdrawn; W-43 opened; ARCHAEOLOGY row. No CHANGELOG entry: workflows layer, as #632, #642 and #643. Label `no-changelog`.

## Checklist

| DoD | item | verdict | evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | A test that fails on the pre-change tree and passes on the post-change tree, run on the no | met | evidence/red.txt fails=True; evidence/green.txt passes=True |
| 2 | `ruff check src/` clean and the touched test files green locally BEFORE the full suite (Pr | met | fast tier pass=True; full tier pass=True (skip ceilings are verdict rows inside) |
| 3 | A `CHANGELOG.md` `[Unreleased]` entry that states what was wrong, why, and what the fix ma | n.a. | no change under src/ |
| 4 | If a tool was added or its description changed: README tool reference, `CLAUDE.md` Key Fil | n.a. | surface unchanged (names and descriptions via scripts/surface_diff.py) |
| 5 | If a benchmark artifact moved: every mirror re-synced in the same PR (`results.md`, `METHO | n.a. | benchmarks/ untouched |
| 6 | If a config key, env var or CLI subcommand was added: a row in `CONFIGURATION.md` or `CLI- | n.a. | config.py and cli/ untouched |
| 7 | If a new background, persistent or network behaviour was added: a README disclosure in "Ba | n.a. | no thread/socket/http/scheduled addition in the diff |
| 8 | If a number is published in a response (a rate, a share, a confidence): a `*_basis` field  | n.a. | no new rate/share/confidence key in the diff |
| 9 | For a contributor PR: trial-merged onto `main` and run locally before the merge; `license/ | n.a. | our own PR |
| 10 | `python -m harness fast` passes; for a change under `benchmarks/`, `harness/` or `server.p | met | fast pass=True; bench pass=not required |
| 11 | If a test was retired: a `harness/retired.json` entry with the lesson and the replacement  | n.a. | no test file deleted |
| 12 | If a threshold moved: tightened with the old value appended to `history`, or loosened with | n.a. | harness/thresholds.json untouched |

Checklist: 12/12 met or n.a.; unmet: none. Generated by .claude/hooks/dod_checklist.py against main.

## Review

Reviewer subagent, two rounds. Round 1 (de603827): REQUEST CHANGES; the row 3 widening was inert, `CODE_ROOTS` was a third path list with a third membership, a collection error did not count as red, and the red evidence named no ref. All taken at a4b61787: the widening reverted and withdrawn from the remedy, W-43 opened for the three lists, `error` counts as red with a test, red.txt names its ref. Round 2: APPROVE, two notes. Full verdict in `.claude/state/evidence/review.md`.

### gRPC-Go xDS servers: Denial of Service (DoS) via crash due to missing `:authority` and `Host` headers
[CVE-2026-84445](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-84445) / [GHSA-2v4p-qf9q-27wj](https://redirect.github.com/advisories/GHSA-2v4p-qf9q-27wj)

<details>
<summary>More information</summary>

#### Details
A vulnerability exists in gRPC-Go servers configured with `xds.NewGRPCServer()` where a crafted request missing both `:authority` and `Host` headers can cause a server panic, resulting in a Denial of Service (DoS).

Servers built with `xds.NewGRPCServer` install an xDS routing interceptor on every RPC. This interceptor looks up the request’s `:authority` header to pick a virtual host. The HTTP/2 server transport previously accepted requests that had neither `:authority` nor `Host`. When this happened, the xDS routing interceptor attempted to access the first element of an empty slice of authorities, leading to an index out of bounds panic. Since the per-RPC goroutine does not recover from panics, the entire server process would terminate.

This panic occurs in the interceptor pipeline, meaning the transport credentials handshake (TLS, mTLS, or ALTS) and HTTP/2 connection establishment must complete successfully before the crafted request can reach this logic.
- Insecure/Standard TLS: If the server permits insecure (plaintext) connections or standard credentials (where client certs are not checked), any unauthenticated remote attacker can trigger the crash.
- mTLS / ALTS: If strict transport-level authentication is enforced at the network edge or transport layer (e.g., requiring a valid client certificate), the attacker must possess valid transport credentials to initiate the stream and trigger the panic.

##### Impact
An attacker can cause a complete outage of the gRPC server by sending a request missing both `:authority` and `Host` headers, provided they can successfully establish a transport connection.

##### Patches
The issue has been addressed in `master` (and backported to `1.83.2` and `1.82.2`). The fix updates the HTTP/2 transport layer to reject requests missing both `:authority` and `Host` headers early, maintaining consistency with and other gRPC language implementations.

#### Severity
High

author: vjpixel
body:
Closes #7688.

## O buraco

`build-apoiador-allowlist.ts` era o **único sync de audiência do projeto que sobrescrevia o estado anterior sem nunca olhar para ele**. Tinha guard para dado FALTANDO (`data.error` fail-closed, `findTransientFailureContacts` recusando push parcial) e nenhum para dado que ENCOLHEU.

Medido ao vivo em 08/09/2026: o push do limiar novo (#7658, R$10+ → R$25+) levou o KV de **21 para 10 e-mails — 52% de remoção — sem nenhum aviso proporcional**. Ali a queda era esperada; a mesma queda causada por uma leitura parcial do apoia.se teria sido aplicada exatamente igual.

E o custo de errar aqui não é um e-mail futuro: quem sai perde acesso às **5 Retrospectivas do Mês já publicadas** (`article:2604-05` … `article:2608-09` no KV `ARTICLES`) — a página passa a mostrar paywall para quem entrava ontem.

Os quatro syncs vizinhos (`sync-apoio-nivel-beehiiv`, `sync-apoio-nivel-brevo`, `sync-apoio-mensal-tag-kit`, `sync-apoio-especial-tag-kit`) já recusam push acima de 30%.

## O que muda

1. **Lê a allowlist atual do KV antes de escrever** (`getTextFromWorkerKV`, que já existia). Este passo simplesmente não existia — o script só sabia escrever por cima.
2. **Remoções acima de 30% recusam o push inteiro.** Usa `APOIO_TAG_BLAST_RADIUS_THRESHOLD` e `diffTagMembership`/`evaluateTagBlastRadius` (`lib/shared/kit-apoio-tag.ts`, #7659) **importados**, não reimplementados: é a mesma pergunta pela 5ª vez, e ter duas respostas diferentes para ela seria a origem do próximo bug.
3. **Loga o diff com a lista explícita** de quem entra e quem sai — quem revisa precisa ver *quem* perde acesso, não só quantos.
4. **Falha na LEITURA também recusa.** Sem o estado anterior o guard não roda, e sobrescrever às cegas é o que esta issue fechou. `--force-blast-radius` cobre os dois casos, declarando o risco.

`parseCurrentAllowlist` trata chave ausente como `[]` (1º push, nenhuma remoção possível) mas **lança** em conteúdo corrompido — tratar lixo como "lista vazia" zeraria as remoções e liberaria a sobrescrita, que é o silêncio exato que o guard existe para impedir.

## Testes

15 casos novos, incluindo a regressão do incidente (21 → 10 agora bloqueia), a fronteira exata do limiar (30% passa, 31% bloqueia), 1º push nunca bloqueia, esvaziar a lista inteira bloqueia, e o parser recusando cada forma de conteúdo inválido.

## Verificado ao vivo

Rodei `--push` contra o KV real com os dados de hoje: leu 10, comparou, 0 mudanças, gravou o mesmo valor. O caminho de leitura funciona contra a API de verdade, e o push é idempotente.

```
[build-apoiador-allowlist] diff vs KV: +0 entram · -0 saem · 10 já corretos (allowlist atual: 10).
[build-apoiador-allowlist] --push: enviando 10 e-mail(s) pro KV ALLOWLIST...
[build-apoiador-allowlist] push concluído.
```

removal-declaration: não remove nada — acrescenta o guard que faltava, reusando os helpers da #7659 em vez de reimplementar.

author: bettercallzaal
body:
`gh pr merge --squash --delete-branch` reports success and does not delete the remote head on this
repo. **3 for 3** - #698, #699, #700. #699 was the PR that added the "verify the branch is deleted"
rule, and the rule caught its own PR one command later.

A documented step gets followed at roughly the rate people remember it. This makes it structural.

## What it does

```
scripts/merge-pr.sh <pr-number>
```

1. asserts the PR is **OPEN** before touching anything (a merged or closed one means branch fresh off main)
2. merges, keeping the **full** output - no `| tail`
3. confirms `mergedAt` is actually set, because reported success is not merged
4. measures the remote and deletes the head **itself** if it survived
5. re-measures, and warns if the repo is not back to its at-rest 1 head
6. exits non-zero unless the PR is merged AND the remote is clean

Guards verified before shipping:

```
$ scripts/merge-pr.sh          -> usage, exit 2
$ scripts/merge-pr.sh 698      -> "PR #698 is MERGED, not OPEN", exit 1
```

The happy path is verified by this PR merging itself with it.

## The tail is part of the bug

Every observation of this so far came through a `| tail`, which is its own way to miss the answer -
the same masked-output failure this repo has already been bitten by in measured commands. The
script keeps everything gh says.

## Cause: narrowed, still unknown, recorded as unknown

Ruled out, so nobody re-checks them:

- **token scope** - `gh auth status` shows `repo`, sufficient to delete a ref
- **repo permission** - `git push origin --delete` succeeds with the same credentials every time, which it could not if permission were the problem
- **a documented caveat** - `gh pr merge --help` says "Delete the local and remote branch after merge", no exception

What would close it: capture a merge's full output, stderr included, no tail, and read what gh says.
Not guessing at it in the meantime - a plausible wrong cause would send the next session to re-auth
a token that is already fine.

`node scripts/validate.mjs` and `node scripts/test-all.mjs` both pass.

author: tristanspeakeasy
body: ## Linear - [AIM-223](https://linear.app/speakeasy/issue/AIM-223/feat-platform-mcp-support-for-mcp-inventory-user-journeys) ## Summary - Add a shared, transaction-scoped Shadow MCP distribution-admission evaluator with exact whole-audience matching. - Add an organization/project/URL-scoped standing-decision query and generated SQLc output. - Give approval decisions, supersession, policy create/update/delete, and Platform risk mutations one project-lock ordering contract. - Keep this slice behavior-neutral: no distribution path calls the evaluator yet, and no rollout flag or new refusal is enabled. ## Motivation The next Shadow MCP distribution slice must validate a plugin's complete audience against one consistent policy and standing-decision snapshot. Existing policy and decision writers did not all take their locks in the same order, so wiring admission directly into those paths would make the safety boundary difficult to review and vulnerable to races. This establishes the shared evaluator and lock protocol first. ## Review notes - Receipt locks remain outermost; the project enforcement lock is transaction-reentrant and now precedes policy, request, and exclusion domain locks. - Empty plugin audiences reach nobody, legacy approved decisions with no principals retain their established Everyone meaning, and malformed state fails closed. - Focused race-enabled tests, server lint, and the server build pass. One unchanged ClickHouse retro-exclusion test fails consistently in isolation and does not exercise this change. - Distribution enforcement, rollout controls, repair reporting, and the reviewed workflow remain separate follow-up PRs. --- ## Summary by cubic Centralizes Shadow MCP distribution admission behind one shared, transaction-scoped evaluator so the next distribution slice can validate a plugin's complete audience against one consistent policy and standing-decision snapshot. Behavior is unchanged: no distribution path calls the evaluator yet, and no rollout flag or new refusal is enabled. Supports AIM-223. **Refactors** - Adds `shadowmcp/admission` with `Check`, `Evaluate`, and `LockProject`; verdicts are `empty_audience`, `not_required`, `covered`, or `approval_required`. - Evaluator normalizes wildcard and directory group/attribute principals to canonical form for exact whole-audience matching. - Standardizes project enforcement lock ordering across inventory resolution, decision, supersession, policy create/update/delete, bypass approve/revoke, and backfill paths. - Adds SQLc query `GetStandingServerDecisionForAdmission` scoped by organization, project, and target, excluding superseded, deleted, and unknown-status rows. - Empty audiences reach nobody, legacy approved decisions with no granted principals retain their Everyone meaning, malformed principals or decisions fail closed, and cross-organization checks are rejected. Written for commit 01ca544f5ecfbb73aadc0d814c00d4625528ab68. Summary will update on new commits.

author: joeyhoworkojr-del
body:
## What this changes

The homepage made you pick a league before it would show you anything, and on most days one of the two tabs was empty. A Wednesday in September has one NFL game and no college football; a Tuesday has neither. Choosing "NCAAF" only to be told there is nothing on is a wasted decision, not information.

### One board, grouped by day

`GET /api/v1/board` replaces asking for each league separately. It merges today's scoreboard with the week ahead for both leagues, drops games that finished on an earlier day, dedupes on `(league, event_id)`, sorts live games first and then by kickoff, and groups the result by the **ET calendar day** a game is played on — ET because that is the day the sport is played on, not the day UTC happens to be in.

Days with nothing on them are not in the response at all, which is what makes the board roll forward: it opens on the next day that has football rather than on an empty Today.

Sixty games carry a full model run. Beyond that a game still appears with its teams, kickoff and line, and says it has **not been projected** rather than claiming the model looked and found no edge — those are different statements and the card no longer conflates them.

### The page

One grid, a league tag on every card, live games at the top, day chips across the week. A finished game gets its own card — the score and who won — rather than the pre-game card, because spread and total pills read as picks and offering a pick on a settled game is a claim about something already decided.

Player projections sit under the featured game, labelled from the response they came back in and marked as projections rather than posted lines.

### Navigation

Live, Props and Upcoming leave the nav. They are no longer separate places: live games sort to the top of the board, projections are under the featured game, the week is in the day chips. **All three routes still resolve**, so existing links and bookmarks are unaffected. The bottom bar's Live slot goes to Results.

### Edge AI diagnosability

A failed answer now shows the provider's own last error under it. It was already recorded server-side and already public on `/ai/status`; the panel only ever said "temporarily unreachable", which gives neither the user nor staff any way to tell a five-minute blip from a misconfiguration nobody has noticed for a week.

## Verification

- 551 backend tests pass, including 10 new ones covering the board: both leagues on one board, empty-today rolling forward, live sorting first, ET day grouping, dedup across feeds, old finished games excluded, per-league counts, and games past the projection cap still being listed.
- 110 frontend tests pass, including 10 rewritten homepage tests for the merged board.
- 35/35 Playwright checks pass, including the nav assertions the nav changes touch.
- Screenshot harness clean at 390 / 768 / 1440 — no horizontal overflow, correct background.
- `npm run build` exits 0.

The harness also gained `SHOT_VIEWPORTS` / `SHOT_PAGES` filters so the sweep can be run in bites; unset, it behaves exactly as before, which is what CI runs.

## Not included

The CFBD key issue is unresolved — the code path is verified against a real response shape, but the deployment's `/api/v1/data/sources` output is still needed to say why it is not returning data.

body:
Run: graphs-observed-record-4
Task: graphs-observed-record-outcome-kinds-epic
Review verdict: approve
Arbitration verdict: approve

`_quarantine_task` in harness/epic.py now takes a required keyword-only `kind: Literal["refused", "no_work", "unverified", "infra"]`. It writes `kind` into the returned entry and into the `record_attempt` call, and adds `patch_kept: True` to both only when `kind == "unverified"`. The calling convention is unchanged: every site still does `quarantined.append(_quarantine_task(...))`.

Every existing `_quarantine_task` call site now passes a kind: fix-loop refusal passes `refused`, the `invoke_graphs` swarm-failure loop and the non-harness-fault build-quarantine branch pass `no_work`, and the `validate_chunk`-unsatisfied branch passes `unverified`. The three plain `quarantined.append({...})` bypass sites (attempt cap, budget-over-cap, harness-fault) each gained `"kind": "no_work"` on the dict literal, without routing through `_quarantine_task` and without an added `record_attempt` call, so none of them grows the attempt count.

`infra` is never passed to `_quarantine_task`. At both `_open_phase_worktree` failure branches in `_run_phase` (initial open and the recreate-and-reopen retry), the phase record now also gets `record["phase_failed_to_start"] = record["reason"]`, alongside the existing phase-grain quarantine entry; no task-grain entry is added.

tests/test_epic_driver.py: extended the checks-failure, validate_chunk-unsatisfied, fix-loop-refusal, attempt-recording and attempt-cap tests to assert the new `kind` (and `patch_kept` where relevant). Added `test_an_unverified_quarantine_keeps_the_patch_and_records_it_kept`, which drives a real file-backed work item through a `validate_chunk` failure and reads the attempt back via `workstore.read_item` (going through the real installed `record_attempt`, not a mock) to confirm `kind`/`patch_kept` land on both the phase entry and the item's attempt. Added `test_a_worktree_that_cannot_be_opened_fails_the_phase_not_a_task`, which monkeypatches `harness.epic._open_phase_worktree` to fail and asserts `phase_failed_to_start` on the phase record with no task-grain quarantine entry.

author: hajisensai
body:
**develop 现在的 Build Release APK 是红的**（`2.3.0+1262`，run [34295332459](https://github.com/hajisensai/Fushi/actions/runs/34295332459)），红在 `Run package tests`。这条修它。

## 根因

`packages/fushi_core/test/` 里三条降级保护守卫造「未来版本的库」时把 `user_version` 写死成 **99**：

- `migration_downgrade_test.dart` — `opening a future-version DB is refused, not destructively rebuilt`、`BUG-075: future-version refusal is clean under foreign_keys=ON`
- `migration_paired_peers_v31_test.dart` — `opening a future-version DB is refused with the downgrade exception`

两处注释还都写着「99 恒大于任何未来 bump 不会 stale」。这个假设在 schema 升到 99（v98 → v99，每来源资料语言 + 刮削字段锁）那一刻失效：99 不再大于当前版本，`database.dart` 的 `if (from > to)` 降级保护分支根本不进，`expectLater(..., throwsA(FushiDatabaseDowngradeException))` 拿到的是正常返回的 `QueryRow`。

三条守卫护的是 **BUG-075 家族**——历史上打开高版本库会 DROP 掉所有表重建，把用户书库抹掉过两次。守卫失效意味着这条数据保护回归不再有人看着。

## 修法

不换一个更大的硬编码数字（那只是把腐烂推迟），改成**从代码派生**：

```dart
final int kFutureSchemaVersion =
    FushiDatabase.forTesting(NativeDatabase.memory()).schemaVersion + 1;
```

读 `schemaVersion` 只是取常量 getter，不触发 drift 的 lazy open，所以这个探针实例不建表、不落盘。此后任何 schema bump 都不会让这三条守卫 stale。

其余 `expect(db.schemaVersion, 99)` 是**钉当前版本**的正确断言（bump 时本来就该改），不动；`fushi/test/database/downgrade_protection_test.dart` 之前已被改成 999，语义正确，本条也不动它。

## 我的责任

这是那次 schema bump 的漏网：连带断言我只扫了 `fushi/test`，没扫 `packages/*/test`。后者只有 CI 的 `Run package tests` 会跑 —— 本地按爆炸半径挑的定向测试结构上碰不到它，`flutter analyze` 也不覆盖 `packages/*`。

## 验证

| 项 | 结果 |
|---|---|
| `packages/fushi_core` 全量 `flutter test` | **82 passed**，exit 0（改前 3 红） |
| `packages/fushi_core` `dart analyze --fatal-infos` | No issues found |
| 全仓扫描其它 `user_version = 99` / `'dbVersion', 99` | 无残留 |

body:
## What changed

- New `/commit` skill (`.claude/skills/commit/SKILL.md`): commits the working tree on a feature branch only. If invoked on `main`, it derives a `feature/<name>` branch from the pending diff, shows the name, and creates it. Runs `ruff format`, `ruff check` and `pytest` before staging, stages only the files that belong to the change, and writes a conventional commit message. Never pushes.
- New `/pr` skill (`.claude/skills/pr/SKILL.md`): pushes the current feature branch, opens a PR against `main` using the repository template, watches CI and prints the URL. User-invoked only (`disable-model-invocation: true`). Never merges or approves.
- `CLAUDE.md`: two lines under Commands documenting the start-of-work checkout and the `/commit` then `/pr` flow. Merging stays a human decision on GitHub.

## Why

The harness had hooks and subagents but no defined path from working tree to pull request. Without one, commits landed on `main` or on branches with names nobody reviewed, and pre-commit checks depended on remembering to run them. These two skills make the branch workflow the default and put the ruff and pytest gate in front of every commit.

## How it was verified

- [x] `uv run pytest` passes locally (6 passed in 0.78s)
- [x] `uv run ruff check .` passes locally (All checks passed; `ruff format .` left 10 files unchanged)
- [x] Evidence captured under docs/evidence/ if this is a TDD milestone. Not applicable: this is a development harness change with no TDD section affected. No delivery runtime code is touched.

Both skills were exercised end to end on this branch: `/commit` created `feature/git-skills` from `main`, ran the checks and produced the single commit here; `/pr` pushed the branch and opened this pull request.

## Summary

A `resource memory` block that is the entire body of a function is a domain policy hidden from every caller: each pays a copy of the result, none can share a domain across calls.  The block belongs at the call site.  The type checker now warns on that shape (the program is sound, so a warning, not an error); `CONTRACT_EXECUTION_CONTEXTS.md` law 9 states the rule and the task spec §8 says each stage *call* opens a block.

## Highlights

- `TypeChecker::warn_whole_body_domain`: a block-bodied function — or a concept's default method — whose only statement is a `resource memory` block gets `resource block '<name>' is the whole body of '<fn>': open the domain where the function is called instead`.
- Only a memory block is a domain: another resource kind (`resource gpu compute =>`) as the whole body costs its callers nothing and warns nothing — the gate `check_resource_block` uses.
- `typecheck_test`: the whole-body shape warns and still checks, for a function and for a concept default method; a block that is part of a body does not; a gpu whole-body function does not.
- Contract law 9 names a `resource memory` block; spec §8 reworded.

## Test plan

- [x] `task build`, `task test` (`typecheck_test`)
- [x] `task bootstrap-test`
- [x] clang-format on changed lines

## Review rounds

Two scoped `codex exec` rounds against the E3 head (APPROVE at the reviewed head `f326eb3`): round 1 — concept default methods bypassed the warning (minor); round 2 — no findings.  Round 3 (`da7449e`), after the codex-cloud threads: the warning gated on `memory`, the one-use `warning` wrapper inlined.

No-Issue: follow-up to Task 35 E3 per docs/task_specs/TASK_35_ALLOCATION_DOMAINS.md §8

author: softmaxwell
body:
## Summary

Glory levels were earned but conferred zero combat power — the six `levelX()` buff accessors in `src/ctf/glory.nim` (windup/hp/fire-cooldown/spray-reset/grenade-charges/carrier-speed) landed dead at GV10 ("unwired increment 1/3", `04096969`) and stayed that way. Owner ruling 2026-08-21 ("Maxwell wants power") plus board card `2d30dba3` ask for levels to measurably change combat. This wires all six into the real combat call sites they were built for:

- `levelWindupTicks` → `startFireWindup` / `selectGunShot`'s `triggerTick` reconstruction (L1 −1 tick, L5 another −1)
- `levelMaxHp` → `maxHpFor` gained an optional `level` param (default 0, so every untouched caller stays byte-identical), threaded through its hp-ceiling call sites (match-start hp is unaffected since level is always 0 there; medkit/bandage/floor-paint heal caps, respawn hp, and the post-game "almost" achievement's owed-respawn budget all now read the buffed ceiling)
- `levelFireCooldown` → `applyFire` (L4 −25%, composes under the existing shield/carrier/trench slowdown)
- `levelSprayReset` → `startArcFire` (L2 −40% of the recharge half only)
- `levelGrenadeCharges` → `tryPickupGrenades` sets the charge count on pickup, `throwGrenade` decrements and only clears `hasGrenade` at 0 (L4+ now actually yields two throws — the field existed, unread, since the GLORY port)
- `levelCarrierSpeedPct` → `applyInput`'s carrier speed tax (L5 waived)

`levelGunRange` stays unwired on purpose — it's retired dead code per its own GLORY C2 comment (always a 100% no-op).

BR S2 arm E's `hitPoints=4` is untouched: `maxHpFor(level=0)` is byte-identical to before, and a fresh life always starts at level 0.

## Paired-seed evidence (proves the buffs FIRE, not just compile)

**Primary: controlled paired demo**, `tools/demo_level_buffs.nim` (committed, `nim r tools/demo_level_buffs.nim`). Two seats on the same `SimServer`, one pinned `level=0` ("recruit"), one pinned `level=5`/MaxLevel ("legend"). Every row calls the real sim proc and reads the field it wrote:

| # | Buff | Proc exercised | recruit (L0) | legend (L5) |
|---|------|-----------------|--------------|-------------|
| 1 | levelWindupTicks | startFireWindup | fireWindup=5 | fireWindup=3 |
| 2 | levelMaxHp (default config) | maxHpFor (spawn) | hp=3 | hp=4 |
| 2b | levelMaxHp (battle-royale-s2 arm E, hp=4) | maxHpFor (spawn) | hp=4 | hp=5 |
| 3 | levelFireCooldown | applyFire | cooldown=12 | cooldown=9 |
| 4 | levelSprayReset | startArcFire | cooldown=25 | cooldown=17 |
| 5 | levelGrenadeCharges | tryPickupGrenades/throwGrenade | 1 charge, hasGrenade=false after 1 throw | 2 charges, hasGrenade=true after 1 throw |
| 6 | levelCarrierSpeedPct | applyInput | velX=492 (60-tick steady state) | velX=704 |

8/8 PASS, exit 0.

**Secondary: same seed (42), same bot binary, ON binary vs OFF binary**, full 16-seat episode via `tools/record_fixture.sh`, re-simulated with `tools/extract_events.nim` (hash-checked, so a clean run also proves determinism):

| | OFF (no buffs) | ON (buffs wired) |
|---|---|---|
| ticks to game over | 4,831 | 11,295 |
| events recorded | 2,124 | 6,103 |
| total shots fired (16 seats) | 470 | 1,101 |
| total shots hit (16 seats) | 109 | 281 |

Both trajectories are byte-identical through the shared opening and diverge once combat starts producing xp — the two numbers above corroborate the change reaches full-episode outcomes; the controlled demo above is the clean per-buff attribution.

## Version handling

- `GloryVersion` 14 → 16 (15 already claimed and merged by #467 — rebased onto it, resolved the changelog conflict by prepending v16 ahead of v15).
- `GameVersion` **60 → 61** (branch first landed at 60, but #476, `maxwell/veteran-perception-label`, independently committed its own GameVersion 60 claim ~9 minutes earlier and merged to main as `17509ef6`). Per AGENTS.md's "second to merge renumbers" rule, this PR renumbers to 61 and is now rebased on top of #476. **#476 landed as GameVersion 60; this PR is 61.**
  - `GameVersion` is a bare compile-time string, never read inside `gameHash` or mixed into any hashed field — so this PR's combat rules and hash trajectory are byte-identical whether numbered 60 or 61. The 9 committed `.bitreplay` fixtures were **patched in place** (a same-length "60"→"61" byte swap in each file's fixed-width `gameVersion` header field — the codec's own `u16 length + ASCII bytes` `ReplayString` format) rather than re-recorded, since re-recording would roll a new live bot race for no behavioural reason. All 9 re-verified to re-simulate hash-clean and byte-identical (same tick count/events/winner/shots) at GV61 as they did when this PR was still numbered GV60.
  - `ReplayCompatibleGameVersions` updated `["60"] → ["61"]`.
  - The derived goldens (`capture-seed1.claims.json`, `format2-legacy.golden.bin`, shell replay `manifest.bin`/`play-call.bin`) were regenerated via their fast, deterministic `-d:` flag test runners (no live recording, no dice-roll) and came out byte-identical to their prior (pre-renumber) content — confirming the relabel didn't touch any simulated byte.

## Review fixes (independent review of the original GV60 commit, before the #476 renumber)

1. **GameVersion collision** — see above (renumbered 60 → 61, fixtures patched not re-recorded).
2. **Missed call site** — `sim.nim`'s post-game "almost" achievement's `fullHp` (`maxHpFor`) now passes `p.level`, so a levelled winning team's owed-respawn hp budget isn't undercounted against the unlevelled base.
3. **Windup reconstruction race** — `selectGunShot` no longer re-derives the arm tick from a freshly-read `shooter.level` (which a grenade/spray hit on the independent `applyGrenadeInput` channel could bump across L1/L5 mid-windup, desyncing the shot's actionId from the already-emitted `GunTrigger` event's). Added `Player.windupStartTick`, snapshotted in `startFireWindup`, read directly in `selectGunShot` — analysis-only (feeds no damage/RNG/position math), excluded from gameHash like the other broadcast-only fields. New regression test in `tests/test_rich_events.nim` levels a shooter mid-windup and asserts the `GunTrigger`/`Shot`/`ShotImpact` actionIds still pair.
4. **Demo coverage** — `tools/demo_level_buffs.nim` gained a second `maxHp` pass on the battle-royale-s2 arm E shape (`hitPoints=4`, `brMode=true`): 4→5 at the buff level, not only the classic-CTF default's 3→4.

## Test plan

- [x] `nim check -d:noSignalHandler --threads:on src/ctf.nim` (both variants) — clean
- [x] 4/4 native shards green: 2,167 OK / 0 FAILED (full run, post-rebase onto #474/#475)
- [x] Fast re-check after rebasing onto #476 (GameVersion 60, merged `17509ef6`): `tests/test_replay.nim` (14 OK / 0 FAILED) + `tests/test_rich_events.nim` (11 OK / 0 FAILED) + `tools/demo_level_buffs.nim` (8/8 checks) — CI runs the full 4 shards on push
- [x] All 9 replay fixtures re-simulate hash-clean at GameVersion 61, byte-identical stats to their pre-renumber recordings
- [x] `tools/ci/check_gameversion.sh origin/main` — OK, GV61 above base's GV59
- [x] `tools/demo_level_buffs.nim` — 8/8 checks PASS (six buffs + the BR arm E maxHp re-check)
- [x] Paired same-seed ON/OFF full-episode comparison — diverges as expected once combat starts
- [x] New regression test: mid-windup level-up keeps GunTrigger/Shot/ShotImpact actionIds paired
- [x] `git rev-list --count HEAD --not --remotes` — 0 (fully pushed)

**Not merging this PR** — leaving for review per task instructions.

author: mlpditto
body:
Follow-up to #1083. Those were static markup, fixable by wrapping the sentence in a lang span. **Toasts cannot be** — `showToast` does `msg.textContent = m`, so a span renders as literal text. The interleaving has to come out of the copy.

I swept **every** `showToast` call carrying Thai or Korean and ran each through the real walker. Six of eight were broken; the other two were already fine (their interpolations are numbers, which the walker absorbs correctly).

| written | rendered with TH/KR off |
|---|---|
| `…for security ถูกปิดนอก localhost เพื่อความปลอดภัย` | `…for security localhost` |
| `💾 Draft saved · บันทึก draft แล้ว` *(2 sites)* | `💾 Draft saved draft` |
| `🏅 New badge unlocked: ${names} · ปลดล็อก Badge ใหม่` | `🏅 New badge unlocked: Streak Master Badge` |
| `Case marked as ${status} · 케이스를 ${status}로 표시` | `Case marked as approved approved` |

Each non-Latin half now says it in its own script — `localhost` → เครื่องพัฒนา, `draft` → ฉบับร่าง, `Badge` → แบดจ์ — and the Korean drops the repeated `${status}` for 케이스 상태 변경 완료. **The English half is untouched in all six.**

## The sixth was a different leak

The Korean half of the bulk-review toast wrapped a value in `( )`, and a closing bracket sits **after** the run, so the backward-only expansion never reached it: `+0.10 pts each)` with a bare bracket left over.

Pre-existing — **not** from the V97.41 bracket rule, which only governs what the walk may absorb going *left*. The brackets become a `·` separator instead.

## Verification

Both toggle states, with the badge string **read back out of the served file** rather than retyped:

```
EN only  →  🏅 New badge unlocked: Streak Master
            Bulk reviewed 3 case(s) +0.10 pts each
            Case marked as approved · −0.10 pts reverted
both     →  full bilingual text, nothing dropped
```

No new console errors. No writes were made from localhost.

author: steipete
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Resolves unnecessary cold plugin-loading work in the core storage migration tests. In successful main CI, the WAL-backed auth/meeting migration case took 15.418 seconds. The fixture exposed every bundled plugin although these two cases only assert core SQLite sources, migration receipts, and managed-worktree ordering.

This is part of the maintainer-requested test performance work. Timing source: [main CI run 34298388636](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34298388636/job/102300061878).

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing cold-plugin fixture helper to create a real, neutral candidate package with an explicitly empty migration inventory. Remove the full bundled-plugin symlink and its unused second copy. Doctor still discovers actual candidate metadata and executes the real core migrations.

The two storage cases retain all SQLite and WAL operations, source/receipt assertions, and cleanup. The caller-execution sibling keeps the real bundled plugins and their migration descriptors; the inventory sibling continues to exercise declared plugin actions and maintenance ownership.

## User Impact

Faster developer and CI feedback without a production behavior, schema, timeout, or shard-count change.

## Evidence

Same full two-case file, original/candidate/restored-original, Node 24.19.0 and pnpm 12.3.4:

| Source | WAL case | Second case | Whole command |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Original | 17.431s | 1.342s | 32.08s |
| Candidate | 2.041s | 1.085s | 10.46s |
| Restored original | 16.932s | 1.280s | 25.46s |

The conservative comparison saves 14.891 seconds in the WAL case and 15.00 seconds overall. The first original also had a colder transform cache, so its entire difference is not attributed to the patch. No memory improvement claim.

Final candidate plus the existing inventory sibling: 9/9 cases passed in two files; WAL case 2.005s. Required changed checks, formatting and diff checks passed. Independent managed P2 review: scoped-clean, no actionable findings.

Production delta 0; test/support +17/-12. No test cases or assertions removed.

author: masonwells1
body:
## What this fixes

An intermittent CI failure where **every test passes but the job still exits non-zero**. Seen on PR #592 head `0eb710369` (run `34187499784`, attempt 1, job `101939658042`): 359 files / 5,123 tests all green, `Errors 1`.

```
ReferenceError: window is not defined
 ❯ getCurrentEventPriority  react-dom.development.js:10993:22
 ❯ requestUpdateLane        react-dom.development.js:25495:19
 ❯ dispatchSetState         react-dom.development.js:16648:14
 ❯ src/components/watchdog/WatchdogFlagBanner.tsx:108:36   <- setLoading(false)
 ❯ src/components/watchdog/WatchdogFlagBanner.tsx:141:5    <- await fetchFlags(seq)
This error originated in "src/components/JobDetailRoute.test.tsx"
```

## Root cause

`WatchdogFlagBanner` ended every load with `if (seq === loadSeq.current) setLoading(false)`. That token answers only *"has a **newer** load started?"* — it is silent on *"is there still a component to write to?"*. Unmount with nothing newer behind it (navigate away from `/jobs/:id` while the watchdog RPC is in flight) leaves the token matching, so the component writes state into a torn-down tree.

React 18's `dispatchSetState` reaches `requestUpdateLane` → `getCurrentEventPriority` **before** it discovers the fiber is unmounted, and that function reads a bare `window`. Once Vitest has torn down the jsdom environment, that reference throws. Hence the signature: all tests green, one unhandled rejection, non-zero exit.

This is the repo-wide `async load without a record guard` class, not a #592 regression — the banner is byte-identical to `main` on that branch.

## The change

A second, **independent** operand: a `mounted` ref cleared by an unmount cleanup, checked alongside `loadSeq` at the three post-await write sites. Kept *alongside* the sequence token rather than replacing it — "superseded" and "gone" are different questions and neither implies the other.

The same defect sat ~70 lines down in `FlagItem.handleDismiss`, whose `setPending(false)` / `setDismissing(false)` run after two awaits; both are now guarded. `dismissIdem.resetKey()` and `onDismissed()` are **deliberately left ungated** (documented in-code): the dismiss already committed server-side, so retiring the idempotency key is a fact about the RPC, not about the row still being on screen, and `onDismissed()` drives the parent's already-guarded refetch.

## Proof — run in both directions

`WatchdogFlagBanner.unmount.test.tsx` reproduces the race deterministically instead of waiting for it: holds the read pending, unmounts with no newer load behind it, removes the global `window` binding the way teardown does, then resolves.

- Against the **unguarded** component it **fails** with the identical `ReferenceError: window is not defined` from `dispatchSetState`.
- Against the **guarded** component it **passes**.
- The real trigger, `src/components/JobDetailRoute.test.tsx` (not authored here), passes alongside it.
- Full suite: **360 files / 5,124 passed / 123 skipped / 0 errors**, exit 0 — CI's own 359 / 5,123 plus this one new test. Typecheck and eslint clean.

Verified against `main` at `214125f4b`; `main` has since moved to `8deb2e48a`, whose three new commits do not touch this component.

## Scope / risk

Frontend-only, three files. No migration, no schema change, no money or RLS path. Not yet merged or deployed — opening this for review only.

author: robertcsakany
body:
Implements OpenSpec change `fix-openspec-board-worktree-button-gating`.

## Why

The OpenSpec board's per-card **New worktree** action was gated on
`sessions.some(s => s.cwd === boardCwd && !!s.gitBranch)`. `gitBranch` is only
populated for the folder-HEAD poll work-set, so an ordinary git repo with no
live session in its cwd rendered **no button at all** — indistinguishable from
a render bug. Three divergent gates existed for the same question (board
`gitBranch`; sidebar inline `some(s => s.isGitRepo !== false)`, which fails
CLOSED on zero sessions; `folderIsGitRepo`, which fails OPEN).

## What

- New pure helper `packages/client/src/lib/git/folder-worktree-availability.ts`
  — `resolveWorktreeAvailability` returns `{ available, reason? }`:
  preference gate first (`undefined` reads as ON, so no cold-load flash),
  then `folderGitMap` as **positive evidence only** (`null` = unknown — it
  conflates non-git, unborn repo, read error and stale cache), then a session
  reporting `isGitRepo === false`, else fail open. Folder/session identity goes
  through the shared `pathKey`.
- Board, sidebar `+ New Worktree` and `folderIsGitRepo` all consume it, so the
  three gates collapse into one rule.
- Board renders the action **always**, `disabled` + explaining `title` when
  unavailable (design D7) — an unavailable state is now directly assertable.
- Sidebar behaviour change (design D6): a pinned git folder with zero sessions
  now shows `+ New Worktree`.
- Repairs `tests/e2e/helpers/openspec-board.ts`, which waited on the
  `folder-open-home-<cwd>` testid deleted by `add-folder-actions-menu` — every
  `openBoard`-based spec was dying there.

## Verification

- Full `npm test` green on the merged tree (18180 passed).
- New L1 suite (14 cases) + rewritten board/sidebar RTL rows; the former
  "button absent" assertions become "present + disabled + reason".
- New L3 spec `tests/e2e/openspec-board-worktree-availability.spec.ts`, proven
  **red against the old gate** and green with the fix in the docker harness.
- Enforcers green: check-conventions, dox-byte-gate, i18n-lint --strict,
  i18n-parity, knip-config, knip-ratchet (+ baseline-diff).
- `@review` pass: no blocking findings; both non-blocking findings fixed
  (thread `folderGitMap` into `folderIsGitRepo`; de-vacuum the E10
  path-normalization assertion).

QA/manual tasks deferred to post-merge verification.

author: yuyz-cyber
body: ACK downloads currently decode tar stdout as UTF-8 per WebSocket frame. Binary bytes and UTF-8 characters split across frames are replaced irreversibly, corrupting file contents and potentially hiding later archive members such as `reward.json`. Set `binary=True` for both download streams and consume stdout directly as bytes. Accumulate directory stderr as bytes and decode it after collection so the existing missing-directory diagnostics still work. This keeps the fix within the two download methods; extraction behavior and retry policy are unchanged. Regression tests feed real tar archives through the Kubernetes `WSClient` decoder with a mocked socket and deterministic 1,021-byte frames. They check Chinese/emoji text, arbitrary binary data, a trailing reward file, benign stderr, and a split UTF-8 directory error. Validation (Python 3.13): - Kubernetes 32.0.1: all five new tests fail against the original implementation and pass with this patch; 158 ACK/GKE/tar-transfer unit tests pass. - Locked dependencies (Kubernetes 35.0.0): `uv run --no-sync pytest tests/unit/environments/` — 1,862 passed, 16 skipped. - `uv run --no-sync ruff check --fix .`, `uv run --no-sync ruff format .`, `uv run --no-sync ty check`, and `git diff --check` pass. - No live ACK cluster validation was performed in this contribution run. Fixes #3143. This PR was developed with AI assistance. ---

author: agustinsacco
body:
Typing `/` on a workspace home screen did nothing. The same key in a session opens a menu of every skill, prompt and extension command pi resolved, so starting a new lane meant remembering a skill's exact name or sending a throwaway first prompt to earn the menu.

**Why it was missing.** Not the textarea: `ComposerField` is already shared, and it deliberately owns no popups (its docstring says the `/` and `@` menus stay with the caller). Only the chat composer implemented them. The obstacle behind that was the list itself, which is session state: `bootstrapSession` asks the session's own pi `get_commands` at spawn. Home has no session and no pi process.

**What changed**
- `electron/pi/commands.ts` asks a throwaway `pi --mode rpc --no-session` for `get_commands` — the same probe the skills page already used privately, which is now a caller of it rather than a second copy. Exposed as `pi:commands`, cached per workspace for 60s (short: a skill is a file the user just wrote). Empty when pi cannot be run, which degrades to the old no-menu behaviour.
- `useSlashMenu` owns when the menu is open, what it matches, the keymap and what picking does. `Composer` and `WorkspaceHome` both drive it. Home offers no native commands: `/compact`, `/export` and `/name` act on a session that does not exist yet.
- The `/` menu now suppresses the `@` menu. They could both open on `/foo@bar`, and rendering showed two popups while the keymap only ever addressed the command one.

The send path needed nothing. Slash commands have always gone to pi as ordinary prompt text, so a command typed as a lane's first message already worked.

**Not in scope:** the home composer still has no `@` file mentions. Nothing blocks it now.

Write-up: `docs/log/2026-09-08-home-slash-commands.md`

**Validation**
- `npm run validate` (typecheck, lint, prettier, 2038 unit tests): green
- `npm run test:e2e`: 51 passed, including a new case that opens the menu on home, picks with Enter, then does the same in the session composer
- Two existing e2e tests used an exact-match `textarea[placeholder="…"]` selector and broke on the new `( / commands )` placeholder hint; both are prefix matches now

author: smdurgan
body:
## What

Firm-voice establishment (ADR 0085) is an Operator **admin** instructing the seat to characterize how the **firm** writes by reading the firm's own letters **across many matters**. That cross-matter read is the job, but the ss#2167 read-time matter-mixing fence (`matter_gate.content_read_refusal`) refused the survey's second matter — so the product motion could never run. The 2026-09-01 A&P establishment HARD_STOP was preceded by exactly this refusal on the survey's second matter.

## The fix, and the one safety line it holds

The mixing control has two enforcement points; this lifts only the first:

- **READ time** — `content_read_refusal`, a hard block. **Exempted** for a marked admin establishment session.
- **SEND time** — `multi_matter_session`, which downgrades any cross-matter outbound to a human draft. **Untouched**, and fires regardless of attribution.

Establishment never sends (the skill's whole ceiling is "never sends"), so nothing outbound loses a control, and the send-time downgrade remains the backstop for the impossible case. The harm the read fence guards — one client's facts reaching another client — is an outbound event, and the outbound layer is intact.

The exemption is set at `pre_llm_call` in the establishment plugin, **only after the seat classified the sender as a firm admin** against the authored allow list (the same gate that guards the establishment tools). A non-admin turn is never marked.

## Tests

5 new in `test_matter_mixing.py`, each positive paired with the falsifying negative: a marked session reads a second matter; an unmarked peer is still refused; a falsy id is never marked; clearing the mark restores the fence; the send-time signal is unaffected. Full overlay suite green: **3832 passed, 2 skipped**.

## Ship path

Merge → bump `OVERLAY_REF` in ss-console → Captain reprovisions `hermes-ashton-price` → re-send the 09-01 blessing on the Initialization thread and watch stage→analyze→install.

body:
## What this PR does

Adds **yaps-translation**, a purpose-specific Yaps plugin for Grok Build. Translate text, Markdown, and SRT subtitles privately with local Yaps translation models. Preserve subtitle timing and create separate translated files.

- Type: remote source, one skill and one local stdio MCP server.
- Source: https://github.com/richawo/yaps-plugins/tree/84b97889aa96ab3aef57b0a36bf6150dce9babbe/grok/plugins/yaps-translation
- Pinned SHA: `84b97889aa96ab3aef57b0a36bf6150dce9babbe`
- Homepage: https://yaps.ai
- Runtime: exact `yaps-cursor-runtime@0.3.0`. The shared npm name retains Cursor for compatibility; this manifest sets the host to Grok.

## Ownership

- [x] I own this plugin or have the right to distribute it.
- [x] The source ownership is explained below.

Richard Awoyemi maintains Yaps under the established `richawo` GitHub account, including the existing public Yaps plugin repository and published Cursor packages. This is the maintainer's source, not an unofficial copy. There is no separate Yaps GitHub organization for this package. The source and skill are MIT licensed, with the license included in the plugin folder. Desktop models keep their own licenses.

## Checklist

- [x] Added exactly one entry in `.grok-plugin/marketplace.json`.
- [x] Remote source pins a full public, reachable, 40-character commit SHA.
- [x] Regenerated `.grok-plugin/plugin-index.json` using the upstream generator.
- [x] `python3 scripts/validate-catalog.py` passes locally.
- [x] `python3 scripts/generate-plugin-index.py --check` passes locally.
- [x] Homepage, clear description, brand-scoped keywords, README, and Grok manifest included.
- [x] License is stated.

## Security

- [x] No `curl | bash`, arbitrary remote scripts, downloaded native executables, or installation lifecycle scripts. The explicit npm bootstrap is described below.
- [x] No plugin code reads or exfiltrates SSH keys, `.env` files, tokens, or credential files.
- [x] No lifecycle hooks or generic shell-execution tools. The server exposes the selected workflow's tools and its readiness/setup controls.

`npx` downloads the exact declared package and its JavaScript dependencies from `registry.npmjs.org`, then starts a local stdio server. This is a disclosed executable dependency, not a claim that installation runs no downloaded code. The readable package starts only the already installed Yaps CLI or native MCP helper. It does not download a desktop engine.

The existing desktop app can contact `yaps-api.richardawoyemi.workers.dev` for account refresh, model assets, and diagnostics. Asset endpoints vary with the installed desktop release; older versions can use Hugging Face and GitHub assets. Required model installation follows the user's authorization and reuses installed models. The wrapper has no separate telemetry uploader. The README describes this boundary and links the desktop privacy policy.

The plugin uses the existing signed-in Yaps desktop account and requests no API keys or separate credentials. Media and notes remain on disk unless returned as requested tool results to the Grok host; returned results are subject to that host's data handling. Local file access and existing Yaps permissions apply. The MCP tool profile limits this entry to the described workflow; output-producing tools preserve the original input file.

## Notes for reviewers

This is one of twelve separately scoped workflows sharing one maintained runtime. Each is submitted in its own PR to follow the one-entry rule. Source subdirectories avoid duplicating helper implementations or requiring twelve new repositories.

All twelve skills pass the skill validator and the upstream component extractor reports exactly one skill and one MCP server per package. The exact published npm package has direct macOS MCP initialization and readiness coverage using the Grok configuration, with the expected tool profile.

These checks do not establish live Grok host tool execution, fresh Windows testing of this package, full workflow output quality, or a fresh model download for every feature. The integration requires a Grok Build environment that can start local MCP processes beside an installed Yaps desktop engine; cloud-only access to another computer is not claimed.

## 概要

Issue #2444 の実装。外的に終了したセッション（tmux 消滅 / CLI が shell に落ちた / 再起動）の行が `chat_messages.archived = 0` のまま残り、再起動後の会話に前セッションの行が連続して見える問題を修正する。

`archived` を書く経路は kill-session route の 1 箇所だけで、しかも生きたセッションが無いと archive する前に 404 で返る。本番 DB の実測では `archived = 0` の 8 スコープ 327 行すべてが、既に tmux セッションを持たない死んだセッションのものだった。

## 変更内容

- `src/lib/session/session-generation-archive.ts`（新規）: 当該 `(worktreeId, instanceId)` の未 archive 行を `deleteMessagesByInstance` で archive し、`recomputeLastUserMessage` でサイドバーのメタデータを追従させ、`messages_invalidated` を送出
- `agent-session-lifecycle.ts`: `beginAgentSession()` から try/catch 付きで呼ぶ。DB を持たない環境の既存テストを壊さず、archive の失敗はログのみでセッション起動を止めない
- **境界は `beginAgentSession` であって adoption mark ではない**: codex / opencode の relaunch 経路は `reconcileExistingSession` が adoption mark を立てるため、mark を読むとこの機能が対象とする終わり方をちょうど取りこぼす
- `vibe-local.ts`: 唯一 fence を呼んでいなかった生成経路に追加
- `realtime/types.ts`: `MessagesInvalidatedReason` に `'session_generation'` を追加（受信側は理由で分岐しない契約なので後方互換）

「死を観測した瞬間に archive」は採らない。`has-session` のタイムアウトなどで一時的に `isRunning=false` になったときに生きている会話を消すため。schema は変更していない。

## 検証

契約 `.commandmate/tasks/issue-2444.yaml` の全ゲートが exit 0:

| ゲート | 結果 |
|---|---|
| work-evidence | PASS |

| unit | PASS |

**#2443（並行開発中）との整合**: #2443 の行更新は `updateMessageContent` を通り、その SET 句は `content` / `summary` / `log_file_name` / `request_id` のみで `archived` を含まないため、本 PR が archive した行を更新しても `archived = 0` へは戻らない。

DDL code fences and identifier code spans in PR comments are now sized to their content, and the DDL blocks in one comment share a size budget, so text the PR author controls cannot break out of the structure holding it or push a comment past GitHub's size limit.

## Why

DDL and the identifiers in it (table, namespace, keyspace, shard, schema path, database, check name) are author-controlled text, and a quoted identifier may legally contain a backtick, or a newline followed by three backticks. With a fixed three-backtick fence that identifier closes the block early and the rest of the statement renders as markdown, headings included; in a one-backtick code span the same name ends the span at its first backtick. The DDL must stay byte-for-byte copyable, so the delimiters adapt rather than the content. Because the fence grows with the longest backtick run inside the statement, a statement made mostly of backticks renders at three times its own length, so the bound is on the rendered block rather than on the statement alone — and because a comment renders one block per table or keyspace, the bound is on the comment rather than on one block.

## What

- The plan DDL block, the apply progress DDL row, the apply summary DDL row, and the VSchema diff share one fence writer that picks a fence longer than any backtick run in the content (minimum three), so the block can only close where SchemaBot closes it.
- All DDL blocks in one comment draw on a single 32,768-byte budget, fences included. Each block takes an equal share of what remains and charges back what it used, so a short statement leaves its slack to the ones after it. A statement past its share is cut on a character boundary to the longest prefix that fits and the block is followed by a visible marker pointing at the PR's schema files.
- Every identifier read from the PR's schema files, its `schemabot.yaml`, or a command's `-d` flag is rendered through one code-span helper: control and format characters are removed, whitespace runs collapse to one line, the delimiter is a backtick run longer than any run inside the name, and a name that sanitizes to nothing still renders as a matched pair. Table cells additionally escape the column separator. The older helper that stripped backticks out of the value is gone; its callers use this one, so a recorded statement keeps its own quoting. Values SchemaBot mints itself (apply IDs, environments, SHAs) keep the plain span.
- Log text is different — it is not meant to be copied as code — so the existing log sanitizer that splits backtick runs is unchanged.
- Upholds AV-8; its *Enforced:* line now names the fence sizing, the per-comment DDL budget, and the identifier code span, and cites the test that renders every identifier surface with a hostile name so a site that bypasses the helper fails CI.

## Before / after

Each column reads top to bottom in the order the pieces appear in an apply summary: the identifier heading, then the DDL block, then what bounds its size. The example identifier is `x`, a newline, three backticks, a newline, `# injected` — legal in PostgreSQL when quoted. Before, the author's text decides where the span and the block end; after, only SchemaBot's delimiters do, and the comment cannot grow without limit.

## What & why

Governor Gary (2026-09-09): before requesting that humans perform UAT, **every Sophia instance should perform UAT first** — machine self-UAT — then hand over. The SunMint map thread exposed the gap: a human was asked to click-test a feature while the agent's own runtime verification was still queued. This makes the self-UAT-before-human-UAT rule durable for **all** agents that read this shared context.

## Changes
- **OPERATING_INSTRUCTIONS.md** — the roadmap UAT-phase bullet now carries a **mandatory self-UAT** paragraph: the implementing agent must run its own end-to-end verification against live beta (or a locally served equivalent, stated explicitly) and report pass/fail evidence per criterion BEFORE asking a human to UAT. Applies to every Sophia instance / agent in the workspace. If self-UAT isn't possible, the gap must be stated, not skipped.
- **GLOSSARY.md** — UAT entry redefined as two stages: **(1) machine self-UAT (mandatory)** and **(2) human UAT (always-stop gate)**; closing blockquote updated to note human UAT is a second, independent confirmation, never the first exercise of the change.

Refs LinklyAI/linkly-ai-workspace#112

⚠️ **合并顺序**：需先合并并发版 `LinklyAI/linkly-ai-api#39`，本 PR 才能合并。

## 背景

api 在 #112 把 cloud-only 工具改名为 `library_search` / `library_link`，并把断开并入 `library_link` 的 `action`。Skill 里的工具名和 Slot 满规则要跟着改。

## 方案

工具名全部改新名；`slot_exhausted` 规则改为「用户点名 → `library_link` 带 `action: "unlink"` → 再 link；未点名 → `list_libraries` 列出并询问，绝不自己挑」；工具参考里 unlink 作为 `library_link` 的子节，`action` 进参数表；写工具说明改为「Local / LAN 只有 `note_save`，云端网关上 `library_link` 也写」。

- `SKILL.md`
  - 工具清单、可达性表、Slot 满规则
- `references/mcp-tools-reference.md`
  - 开头计数与写工具；`library_search` / `library_link` 节；unlink 子节；`note_save` 的写工具说明
- `references/cli-reference.md`
  - `--remote` 注释

## 验证

- 文案与 api `tools-registry.ts` 描述逐条对照
- 装上本分支跑 Agent eval，见 `linkly-ai-workspace/specs/moses/112-mcp-unlink-library/验收脚本/README.md` §2.3

### Windows 手工验证

不适用——本 PR 仅改文档。

## 追加 1：禁止重复连接的规则只限 link（commit 35ee482）

- 动机：评审 P2-2。
- 根因：合并后 `library_link` 同时承担断开，「`is_linked: true` 就不要再调 `library_link`」会把用户已点名的 unlink 也拦住。
- 改法：规则改为「不要再 link（显式 link、省略、null 都算）；用户点名要释放时 `action: "unlink"` 仍可用；只提到库名不算授权，『把 A 换成 B』不必追问」。

Upstream extraction, unit 3 (notes/upstream-expert-provider-contract-draft-2026-09-09.md). Draft; two reviews required before ready (astra_mid: review 1, astra: review 2 incl. GPU).

**Base**: `lab/upstream-37190-base` d38903ceebac = upstream/main a97dacb7106e + PR #37190 c66868c8c12f (notes/upstream-37190-base-merge-2026-09-09.md). **Head**: 60ba5b983889 (last GPU-verified production state: b5ac54ed; 60ba5b98 adds docstrings and moves one log line). **Dependencies**: #37190 (provider surface). The native consumer path (not in this PR) additionally depends on #44.

**Commits on this head**
- Knob: `OffloadConfig.moe_expert_cache_provider` (`cached` default, `row`) wired EngineArgs -> CLI -> config, hash-covered (tests).
- `RowCacheWeightProvider`: CachedWeightProvider surface plus NVFP4 global-scale slot buffers, owner-stream contract, forward-scoped map, LRU with in-forward victim protection, staged copies on a provider-owned copy stream (release event on the owner stream -> copy stream waits -> six-tensor copies -> ready event -> owner waits), invalidate ordered against in-flight copies. Expert maps are uploaded as one pinned non-blocking copy each; per-element device writes stalled the host until the owner stream drained (d26e289).
- (b1) `CachedWeightProvider`: optional keyword-only `w13_scale_2`/`w2_scale_2` with `buf_*_scale_2` slot buffers; `ExpertWeightResult` and the path without them unchanged.
- (c) `RoutedExperts`: provider selection by the knob; `_maybe_init_expert_lru_cache(scale_suffix, *, scale_2_suffix)` repoints per-expert global-scale parameters at slot buffers before the quant config is built; `run_with_expert_cache` typed against a Protocol.
- Load path: with the cache enabled, `ModelOptNvFp4FusedMoE.create_weights` allocates the per-expert weights and block scales in CPU pinned memory; `prepare_nvfp4_moe_layer_for_marlin` converts host-resident sources `expert_chunk` (64) experts at a time on the accelerator into pinned host outputs (device sources: unchanged single pass); the providers alias the pinned results.
- (b2) `ModelOptNvFp4FusedMoE`: `supports_expert_lru_cache` True only for the Marlin backend (expert-major final layout, globals read through the quant config); cache installed after the backend conversion, before quant config/kernel; `apply` through `run_with_expert_cache`; monolithic rejects a cache.

- Loader interaction: `device_loading_context` restores CPU-resident parameters by name after processing; the cache marks its scale slot buffers device-resident (`DEVICE_RESIDENT_ATTR`) so they are not pulled back. Ordinary replacements keep the previous contract; the context no longer retains moved Parameter objects.
- Breakable CUDA graphs: for models that are not torch-compiled, the MoE custom ops are eager break points for layers holding a provider (uncached MoE layers stay captured), and both guards accept `VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=1` as the alternative to compile splitting. The legacy layer-name placeholder is resolved once per op.
- Byte accounting at cache setup and periodic row-provider stats.
- Stream ownership in the row provider is tracked, not enforced: the release event is recorded on the stream of the previous accepted `prepare()` (where that forward read the slots) and the current stream becomes the owner after waiting on the ready event; resident-map writes are serialized with the slot copies (copy stream in `prepare()`, owner stream in `invalidate()`). Contract: sequential host calls, all consumer reads enqueued on the current stream before the next `prepare()`.

**Tests**
- CPU/mock: `tests/config/test_moe_expert_cache_provider.py`, `tests/kernels/moe_provider/test_row_provider_cpu.py`, `test_row_provider_staging_mock.py` (event call order).
- CUDA: `tests/kernels/moe_provider/test_row_provider_cuda.py` (eviction reuse with a pre-captured graph reader kept unfinished while the next prepare is enqueued; previous reader output oracle-checked; six-tensor bytes on the reused slot; every route planned once; other-stream rejection; invalidate->prepare ordering), `tests/kernels/moe/test_expert_lru_cache.py` (scale_2 lifecycle/validation added), `tests/kernels/moe/test_nvfp4_expert_cache_consumer.py` (Marlin capability-gated; both providers x device/host sources; distinct per-expert globals; overflow every forward; per-pass `g1/g2_alphas[slot]` equal to the uncached layer's final globals of the mapped expert; live-buffer identity; output match; chunked host repack byte-equal to the device path for N=128 and N=96), `tests/kernels/moe/test_nvfp4_marlin_repack_args.py` (CPU: non-positive expert_chunk rejected before side effects).

**Executed**: Mac: ruff, format, mypy, pre-commit; CPU+mock provider tests (9 passed, run outside the repo conftest). GPU (astra, overlay on this base, head d26e289): `tests/kernels/moe_provider` + `test_expert_lru_cache.py` 51 passed. GPU on the exact a97 build (astra, head b2b5ec19): `tests/kernels/moe_provider`, `test_expert_lru_cache.py`, `test_nvfp4_expert_cache_consumer.py`, `test_nvfp4_marlin_repack_args.py` = 63 passed, 0 skipped (results/upstream-provider-exact-b2b5ec199799-20260909). **Real checkpoint (astra, mid cross-checked)**: integration head `lab/upstream-provider-ple-mmap` (this PR merged onto `lab/upstream-ple-mmap-base` a7a3d7a5 = upstream/main a97dacb7 + proposed sync PLE #54129; 4c79d366 for the row run, fcf878ad for the cached run) on RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Max-Q 96 GiB limited to 48 GiB by balloon; Marlin backend; `--moe-expert-cache-size 208 --moe-expert-cache-split token`; chunk 512; max_num_seqs 1; breakable CUDA graphs auto-on (compilation mode NONE), cudagraph_mode PIECEWISE, capture sizes [1, 2]; sync PLE mmap; no speculation. Both providers: load 35.54 GiB, 48 layers cached at 208/512, KV 9.86 GiB, captures at 1 and 2 tokens recorded twice each (profiling and actual capture; 98 graphs / 97 eager breaks per capture), two probe requests answered correctly (a 64-token explanation and a 5-token arithmetic answer 3288). Host cgroup peak reached the 100 GiB budget without OOM; capacity samples (25 at load, 4 during generation) recorded no error. Results: cached results/upstream-provider-checkpoint-fcf878ad5781-cached-20260909 (head 0b6fe947), row results/upstream-provider-checkpoint-4c79d366113b-row-20260909 (head b5ac54ed), each with an independent review file. Exact suite at 4c79d366: 71 passed, 0 skipped. Limits: short smokes only; the servers were stopped externally after the requests and the logs keep the shutdown EngineDeadError/semaphore warnings (not a clean shutdown claim); no speed comparison between providers, no long-output quality, no per-step replay counters, no concurrent-consumer guarantee (sequential-consumer stream contract, see the class docstring).

**Equal-capacity pair on the same head (astra, mid cross-checked; integration head e5c920b0; same launch except `--moe-expert-cache-provider`; two fixed tokenized prompts A 1070 / B 753 tokens, max_tokens 2048, one request each, no repeats; results/upstream-provider-pair-e5c920b0fdda-20260909)**:

| provider | A: output / TTFT / client decode | B: output / TTFT / client decode |
|---|---|---|
| cached | 926 tok / 10.16 s / 18.24 tok/s | 1616 tok / 6.36 s / 18.84 tok/s |
| row | 878 tok / 9.39 s / 19.76 tok/s | 1306 tok / 6.14 s / 19.66 tok/s |

Single observations with differing outputs (greedy paths diverge between providers), so this is a check, not a speed claim: the row provider's staged copies show a few percent higher client decode rate at N=208. Both are far below the lab fork's post-fix figure (66 tok/s at a 26 GiB tier with the in-graph planner); that is a different configuration and not a single-variable comparison. Pi agents now receive Buzz's complete session instructions in their native system prompt. The prior launcher supplied only the base prompt and left persona, team instructions, and memory in the first user message.

author: golf1052
body:
## Root cause

Captured JPEGs can store rotation/mirroring in EXIF instead of their pixel layout. `WriteUploadStateCoreAsync` copied those pixels directly into `PHContentEditingOutput.RenderedContentUrl`. [PhotoKit requires edited content to bake in its orientation](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/photos/phcontenteditingoutput/renderedcontenturl), so it rejects these edits with `PHPhotosErrorDomain` **3302**.

The upload itself has already succeeded: the iPhone queue contained two reports with saved server receipts, but local acknowledgement exhausted its retries. Using a local copy of an affected JPEG reproduced the rejection in an iOS simulator; the same PhotoKit write and read-back succeed with this fix.

## Changes

- Render rotated/mirrored editing input upright at full resolution before writing upload status; leave already-upright JPEGs byte-for-byte unchanged before stamping.
- Preserve EXIF capture date/GPS and custom XMP, while updating orientation and pixel dimensions. Use the existing JPEG XMP writer rather than relying on ImageIO to round-trip custom XMP.
- Keep queue receipts, retry behavior, asset IDs, and the server API unchanged. After installing the fix, **Retry** on an already-accepted report completes only its local acknowledgement; it does not submit a duplicate.
- Add a synthetic native iOS smoke app covering all eight EXIF orientations, pixel placement, dimensions, metadata, exact receipt timestamps, and repeat rendering. Run it in Debug in mobile CI and document local use.

## Validation

- Full iOS simulator and Android app **Debug** builds succeed. Android required isolated build artifacts because the existing `obj/Debug` tree had an `R.txt` file lock.
- Native PhotoKit round-trip with the affected JPEG: fails before the fix (3302), succeeds and reads the expected acknowledgement after the fix.
- All eight native synthetic orientation cases pass.
- 61 existing targeted queue, catalog, XMP, EXIF, and metadata-preservation tests pass.
- Connected Pixel 8a shows its existing report in **Already reported**, with no pending report; no fabricated production reports were sent.

The installed phone apps and their report/photo data have not been replaced or reset. The affected photo was used only in local diagnostic artifacts, not committed to the repository. Android's MediaStore implementation is unchanged; the upright-rendering requirement is specific to PhotoKit.

author: ondrik
body:
Adds `.github/workflows/tests.yml` so the branch rulesets on `main` and `devel` have an actual check behind them — until now a PR could be approved and merged without anything being built.

## What it runs

`make test` on the default MoToBuddy `__float128` backend: unit API, circuit smokes, rotation-cache, benchmark structure + semantics, and the metamorphic suite.

## Notes on the choices

- **`libgmp-dev` is the only missing dependency** on `ubuntu-latest`. `cmake`, `g++` and `python3` are preinstalled, but are named explicitly so the job fails loudly rather than mysteriously if the runner image changes.
- **No dependency caching.** `make init` clones MoToBuddy at the `MOTOBUDDY_COMMIT` pin and builds `libbuddy.a` in well under a minute; a stale cache carries more risk than a rebuild.
- **`concurrency` with `cancel-in-progress`** so a new push to a PR supersedes the previous run.
- **`permissions: contents: read`** — the job needs nothing else.

## Verified locally

```
make init && make test
```

passes on the pinned MoToBuddy `61b4195`, in ~6s:

| suite | result |
|---|---|
| `test_unit_api` | 10634 assertions, 30/30 sections |
| `test_circuits` | 8/8 |
| `test_rotation_cache` | 24/24 |
| `test_benchmarks` | 17/17 |
| `test_benchmark_semantics` | 62 assertions, 6/6 sections |
| `test_metamorphic` | 1005 assertions, 9/9 sections |

## Known caveat

The workflow triggers on PRs to both `main` and `devel`, but **`main` does not yet contain `tests/` or the `test` target** — it is 34 commits behind `devel`. A PR into `main` from a branch based on current `main` will therefore fail this check until `devel` lands on `main`. The realistic next PR to `main` is `devel` → `main`, whose merge commit does carry the suite.

Suggested follow-up once this has run green: add `tests` to `required_status_checks` on the `require-pull-request` ruleset, so the gate actually blocks on it.

author: gabrielfmorais
body:
Docs-only. Duas coisas que a auditoria iPhone-first deixou **registradas em vez de resolver sozinha**, porque nenhuma é decisão de implementação.

## G8 — o preview DEV desta máquina não entra, e isso bloqueia a D-90 inteira

**Medido**, não deduzido: `400 invalid_credentials` contra o endpoint de token do Supabase Auth para `dev.preview@haircare.local`. A **anon key é válida** — o endpoint de settings responde e confirma `google: false`, batendo com a D-84 — e a senha do `.env.local` foi conferida sem aspas e sem espaço em branco.

⚠️ **Consequência:** o preview alcança **só a abertura e o login**. Nenhuma tela autenticada pode ser observada, e *"validado no DEV real"* deixa de ser possível para qualquer fatia de produto.

**Quem age (dono):** Authentication → Users → Add user, com o email e a senha do `.env.local` e **"Auto Confirm User"** marcado (runbook §5). É o gate mais barato da lista e o que mais custa enquanto durar.

## SPEC-061 — a OQ1 da SPEC-060, em draft e explicitamente para NÃO começar ainda

O app **não navega por rotas, navega por estado**: um enum de oito destinos num `useState`, a pilha de dois níveis feita **à mão** (`dataSources` volta para `you` porque alguém escreveu isso no `onBack`), e o parâmetro de `share` num segundo estado paralelo. O `expo-router` está montado com **uma rota só**, então o iOS **não tem o que reconhecer** quando o polegar arrasta da borda.

⚠️ É a interação mais automática que existe num iPhone, e quando nada acontece a leitura não é *"este app não tem esse gesto"*, é *"este app travou"*.

⛔ **Duas travas bloqueantes, e nenhuma é de implementação:**

1. **Falta um ADR de navegação.** As portas são montadas no topo de `apps/mobile/src/app/index.tsx` e passadas por prop; uma rota montada pelo router **não herda isso**, e a ADR-001 diz que a tela recebe suas portas mas não diz **por onde**. CLAUDE.md §1.4: mudança arquitetural sem ADR não se faz. O rascunho traz duas saídas e uma recomendação.
2. **Falta o G8.** Os oito destinos ficam atrás do login, e refatorar navegação sem conseguir **clicar por ela** contraria a D-90 no ponto exato em que ela mais importa.

## Escopo

Zero código, zero migration, zero backend. `check-docs-links` verde (96 referências), lint verde.

body: ## Summary - The transform worker's temporary request files now have a single owner, and a cleanup failure can no longer replace a decided result with an error. ## User Impact - On the one-shot worker path, a temp-directory cleanup failure (most likely on Windows, where a killed worker can still hold the files open) used to escape over an already decided result. It is now logged as a warning, the way the resident path always treated it. Both were needed to bring `TransformWorkerHost` under the file-length limit after the temp-IO extraction. ## Verification - `uloop compile`: `ErrorCount 0`. - `uloop run-tests` over the six affected transform-worker test classes: 117 tests, 117 passed, 0 failed. - File length: with the threshold set to 400 SLOC, none of the touched files is reported; the repository-wide check exits 0. - `uloop hot-reload --status` and `--revert-all` responses captured before and after the change are byte-identical.

author: zhangguiping-xydt
body:
Related: #141264, #141268

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where clients calling `POST /v1/responses` would treat an output-token-limited partial reply as a completed answer.

## Why This Change Was Made

The endpoint preserves the agent's authoritative length outcome as an incomplete response and final message, with `incomplete_details.reason: "max_output_tokens"`. Streaming sends `response.incomplete` and the existing `[DONE]` marker. Failure and tool-choice checks retain priority over truncation.

This retains the contributor's repair and aligns the terminal event with the public Open Responses protocol. One final status supplies the message, response, and event; output budgets and provider behavior stay unchanged.

## User Impact

JSON clients can detect a partial answer from its response status. Streaming clients receive the matching incomplete event, including SDK event listeners. Normal completions and failures retain their current behavior.

## Evidence

- Real authenticated Gateway requests through a controlled local provider: main reported completed in both JSON and streaming after authoritative length termination; the candidate reports incomplete, `max_output_tokens`, an incomplete final message, and exactly one `response.incomplete` event plus one `[DONE]` marker.
- Matching before/after controls preserve normal completion, provider failures, content filtering, whole-agent timeout, client cancellation and recovery, required-tool rejection, ordered client calls, usage, response identity, and same-runtime session history. Both Chat Completions length modes remain correct.
- Fresh source-blind acceptance exercised 19 additional public HTTP cases, including identical text with different termination reasons, misleading truncation wording, required-tool precedence, and continuation after an incomplete response. No behavioral findings.
- The actual installed OpenAI SDK receives exactly one incomplete callback for the length case and one completed callback for its normal control; both accumulated final responses retain the correct status and text.
- Focused Responses and Chat Completions suites: 257 passed. Updated regressions fail on main for completed status/event, and on the original contributor implementation for the terminal event and failed-message status.
- Targeted formatting, lint, and diff checks passed. Full hosted checks and the exact-head landing review gate are required before merge.

The runtime proof uses a synthetic provider through normal agent transport. Cancellation proves disconnection and upstream teardown; no stored cancellation result is claimed. History proof covers a same-runtime continuation. Raw prompts, credentials, identifiers, and infrastructure metadata remain private.
