author: maxlestage
body:
**What this changes**

`docs/ROADMAP.md` seulement — un relevé, et les deux erreurs de lecture qui l'ont précédé.

**Why**

Relevé par `first-region` sur le point d'entrée d'Alpine 3.20 :

| | ce que la série précédente disait | maintenant |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| lecture linéaire | 70 instructions, arrêt à l'octet 291 | **454 instructions**, arrêt à l'octet 1575 |
| ce qui l'arrête | `fa f4` — `cli` puis `hlt` | `cc cc cc…` — le remplissage entre deux fonctions |
| traduction | arrêtée sur `wrmsr`, puis sur `cli` | **la région entière**, 2 150 octets de module |

**C'est la première fois que le point d'entrée d'un vrai noyau se traduit jusqu'au bout.** Ce n'est pas la pagination seule qui l'a fait — c'est la série entière : `cpuid`, les sélecteurs, les tables de descripteurs, les MSR, les registres de contrôle, puis la traduction d'adresse.

**Deux erreurs de lecture, et les deux entrent dans la feuille de route.**

*Le noyau n'est pas une image plate.* La charge utile décompressée d'un `bzImage` est un **ELF**, et j'ai d'abord extrait « le point d'entrée » à l'octet 0x90 du fichier — c'est-à-dire dans l'en-tête ELF. Le relevé disait alors « quatre instructions, puis l'octet 9 ne se lit pas », ce qui **ressemblait à un résultat**. `0x1000090` est une adresse *virtuelle* ; le décalage dans le fichier se lit par les en-têtes de programme, et vaut 0x200090.

*Et ce détour a montré autre chose.* Le segment qui porte le point d'entrée est chargé à `0xffffffff81000000` — le **demi-haut**. C'est exactement la limite écrite en fermant la tranche P2 : la lecture des **instructions** n'est pas paginée, l'hôte résout une région par son adresse telle quelle. Je l'avais notée comme une réserve ; le premier vrai noyau qu'on regarde la porte.

**Ce que ce relevé ne dit toujours pas** : il compile, il n'exécute pas. La distance qui reste tient en une phrase — l'adresse à laquelle l'hôte doit chercher sa région est virtuelle.

**How it was verified**

`./scripts/verify.sh` : `==> OK`, **code de sortie 0**. Aucun test ajouté ni retiré (2 364).

Le relevé se refait ainsi, sur la charge utile décompressée :

```
python3 -c 'import struct,sys
d=open(sys.argv[1],"rb").read()
e=struct.unpack("<Q",d[24:32])[0]; ph=struct.unpack("<Q",d[32:40])[0]
n=struct.unpack("<H",d[56:58])[0]
for i in range(n):
    o=ph+i*56
    if struct.unpack("<I",d[o:o+4])[0]!=1: continue
    off,va,_,sz,_=struct.unpack("<QQQQQ",d[o+8:o+48])
    if va<=e<va+sz: open(sys.argv[2],"wb").write(d[e-va+off:][:65536])' vmlinux.bin entree.bin
cargo run -p wisq-vm --release --example first-region -- entree.bin
```

body:
The keyboard covers the bottom of a form for as long as you're typing,
which is exactly when Save needs to be reachable. Every form that saves
now puts its primary action at the top right instead:

- Edit task, Create group and Join group set it as the stack's
  headerRight, so it sits beside the screen title.
- Settings (Profile) and the group card's rename form have no stack
  header of their own, so a new <FormHeader> gives them the same shape:
  section title left, action right, above the fields.

Alongside that, every action button now carries an icon. The glyphs live
in one place (src/constants/icons.ts) keyed by action rather than by
screen, so save/edit/delete draw the same thing everywhere; history's
row actions swap their text glyphs (↺ ✓ ✕ 🗑) for the same Ionicons.

New shared pieces:
- HeaderAction: the icon + label pill used for a form's primary action,
  with HeaderActionSlot for the trailing inset the web JS header lacks.
- FormHeader: title + actions row for forms without a stack header.
- PrimaryButton takes an optional `icon`.

Also lets the group card's invite-code row wrap, since the Share button
is wider with a glyph and was clipping against the card edge.

Verified with tsc, expo lint, and a web export driven in a browser:
Edit task, Settings, Create/Join group, History and the group card all
render their actions as intended.

AX1 currently requires a synchronous WebGL renderer and stops permanently after context loss. This adds an optional asynchronous WebGPU factory while retaining the existing WebGL2 release baseline, and rebuilds a lost generation using fresh authenticated world and zone data.

The factory reports the backend after initialization, bounds initialization time, disposes late results, and handles capability/init fallback. React effects are bound to renderer readiness and retire old tickets/snapshots/GLB completions. Context/device loss triggers at most two rebuilds on WebGL2. The world core receives its generation's explicit world context.

Active shader compatibility is covered by an instanced TSL particle view and the existing external emissive pulse applied through standard material intensity. All 18 source particle generators remain byte-identical. No gameplay authority is added to rendering.

Validation so far: TypeScript and production build pass; full local suite 805 passed / 100 explicitly skipped; latest focused regressions 29 passed; 42/42 migration chain entries verified. GitHub tree is byte-identical to the locally checked tree. Local browser installation timed out, so actual browser acceptance remains pending.

The dedicated AIM-290 lane requires real authenticated MariaDB/zone sessions, WebGL2 and initialized WebGPU, actual context loss and GPUDevice.destroy(), manifest/hash parity, screenshots and recovery receipts on phone/tablet/desktop profiles. SwiftShader demonstrates software rendering, not hardware performance or live production gameplay. This remains Draft until those gates are read back.

AIM-290; parent AIM-287. Prerequisite PR #283 production closure is separately verified. AIM-291–294 remain open.

author: kerti
body:
PRD §7.5's envelope reaches the phone: open one for an occasion, collect and disburse against it, close it and see the leftover roll into Kas Utama. The backend landed in M4 — this is the screen that reaches it. Frontend only; no backend file, no migration, no regenerated `internal/store/`.

## The one design call

Contributions and disbursements are deliberately **not** their own route and **not** their own form. They are ordinary `POST /api/transactions` calls tagged to the envelope's purpose, so the detail view hands off to M6.8's record form via `/record?purpose=<id>` with the purpose pre-chosen; direction is decided there by the toggle that already exists.

The first cut of this slice grew its own contribute/disburse form inside `Incidentals.tsx` — every field `RecordTransaction.tsx` already has, a second time. That is the second concept the prime directive forbids, and two record forms drift. It was replaced with the hand-off before this commit; the screen came down from 679 lines to 536.

`RecordTransaction` gains one optional prop, `initialPurposeId`, for that hand-off. It is honoured only when the fund actually has that purpose — a stale link to one that no longer exists falls back to the `kind: "main"` row rather than leaving the picker matching nothing and the form unsubmittable for no visible reason. An absent or malformed `?purpose=` is the same fallback (`Number('')` is `0` and finite, so the parse requires a positive integer).

## Trust surface

Totals come from `GET /api/incidentals/{purposeID}` and are rendered as given — nothing here re-sums a transaction list, and `formatIDR` runs at the display edge only. The rolled amount is shown even when it is zero: a zero rollover is an honest answer, not a missing one. A second close surfaces the named `incidental_already_closed` 409 in Indonesian, never the wire message.

## Files

`web/src/lib/incidentals.ts`, `web/src/screens/Incidentals.tsx`, `web/src/screens/Incidentals.test.tsx`, `web/e2e/incidentals.spec.ts` (new) · `App.tsx`, `Home.tsx`, `Home.test.tsx`, `RecordTransaction.tsx`, `copy/id.ts` (touched).

## Verification

`make check` green — golangci-lint, `go test -race`, oxlint, tsc, vitest, web build. vitest covers the open/all filter, the zero-rollover close and the double-close refusal; buttons are `size="lg"` for the 44px minimum, and a discrepancy uses the attention token, never alarm-red.

**`make e2e` has not been run** — `web/e2e/incidentals.spec.ts` is written and its selectors cross-checked against the matching vitest queries, but executing it is the maintainer's step.

No ADR draft tag drops here and `docs/Decisions.md` is unchanged — nothing was decided that #152 did not already settle.

Closes #152

author: chenghit
body:
Fixes a regression #23 introduced, plus a pre-existing one it made worse by proximity.

`_ensure_athena_table` lost its early cache return, so every Athena query in a warm
session re-ran the destination-to-S3-path translation before the resolver's own cache
check was reached. On a Firehose destination that is one `DescribeDeliveryStream` per
query, which is capped at **5 requests per second, per account per Region, and is not
adjustable**. The cold start regressed the other way too, since that translation used
to sit inside the setup lock.

Both pre-resolution lookups are now memoized **and locked**. The lock is the
load-bearing half: a memo alone leaves the cold fan-out untouched, because the
read-modify-write is not atomic. Ten threads with a 100 ms stand-in for the AWS call:

| | unlocked | locked |
|---|---|---|
| `resolve_s3_log_path` | 10 | 1 |
| `_get_output_location` | 10 | 1 |

`_get_output_location` is the hotter of the two, called once per Athena *statement*
rather than per query, and on a workgroup with no output location its fallback reaches
the same describe. It gets its own lock rather than reusing the translate one, because
`_run_athena_ddl` calls it from inside `with _create_lock`. Lock order is now written
down: translate, resolve, create, output.

Seven tests, each verified against its fix removed. Three were rewritten first because
they passed without proving anything: counting AWS calls could not see the lost early
return, and instant fakes closed the concurrency race window on their own.

author: cgoudie
body:
Chasing the one loose end the monitor flagged in dev's first mDNS-column dump: the eMMC write-time column spiked to 272–304 ms in the same samples as the biggest mDNS bursts. Its guess was log writes from the flood's consumers.

**It is not log writes.** Across the flood window the service logs wrote 70 lines against 60 in the equally long quiet window before it. And the dump cannot be the cause either — it is written *after* the sample it would show up in. What remains is latency: the same writes completing more slowly behind a loaded CPU during a wakeup storm.

**But the tool could not tell those apart**, because it recorded only milliseconds. "Wrote much more" and "same writes, queued longer" want opposite responses, and a reader given only time would guess. It now records write operations and kB alongside, so the dump answers it directly.

Suite 606 / 304.

It is now a short index (6,850 characters) plus nine child pages, one per reader job. | Child | Sections moved | | --- | --- | | `codex-harness-reference/supervision` | Supervision | | `codex-harness-reference/app-server-transport` | App-server transport, Environment overrides | | `codex-harness-reference/approval-and-sandbox` | Approval and sandbox modes, Sandboxed native execution | | `codex-harness-reference/auth` | Auth and environment isolation | | `codex-harness-reference/dynamic-tools` | Dynamic tools | | `codex-harness-reference/timeouts` | Timeouts, Turn execution and settlement | | `codex-harness-reference/model-discovery` | Model discovery | | `codex-harness-reference/restricted-turns` | Restricted turns | | `codex-harness-reference/workspace-bootstrap-files` | Workspace bootstrap files | The index keeps the frontmatter, the intro, `## Plugin config surface` (the orienting field table), and `## Related`, and adds `## Where each section moved`. No prose was rewritten and no content moved between this page and `/plugins/codex-harness`. ## Validators ``` node scripts/check-docs-mdx.mjs docs README.md Docs MDX check passed (999 files, 4899ms). OPENCLAW_DOCS_SYNC_CLAWHUB_REPO=... node scripts/docs-link-audit.mjs checked_internal_links=10310 broken_links=0 OPENCLAW_DOCS_SYNC_CLAWHUB_REPO=... node scripts/docs-link-audit.mjs --anchors checked_internal_links=10645 broken_links=3 maturity/scorecard.md:90 :: /maturity/taxonomy#windows-app-node :: fragment not found maturity/scorecard.md:144 :: /maturity/taxonomy#windows-app-node :: fragment not found maturity/taxonomy.md:165 :: #windows-app-node :: fragment not found node scripts/format-docs.mts --check Docs formatting clean (986 files). node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/check-docs-i18n-glossary.mts (clean, exit 0) npx markdownlint-cli2 --config config/markdownlint-cli2.jsonc Linting: 985 files Summary: 0 issues in 0 files ``` The three `--anchors` failures are the known pre-existing `#windows-app-node` set on `docs/maturity/*` and are untouched by this PR. `docs/docs.json` gains a nested "Codex harness reference" nav group, mirroring the `codex-harness` group. `docs/.i18n/glossary.zh-CN.json` gains the nine new child titles (791 entries, 0 duplicate sources). ## Findings recorded, not fixed here - **Labeler gap (separate CI PR).** `.github/labeler.yml` lists `docs/plugins/codex-harness-reference.md` (line 609) but has no `docs/plugins/codex-harness-reference/**` glob, so the new children will not pick up the label. author: dxdx123
body:
## Summary

Persist dataset list filters (keyword, tags, and "include all") in the URL so they survive navigating into a dataset detail page and back, as well as page refresh.

## Problem

Filters were stored only in local component state:

- `keywords` and `tagFilterValue` used `useState`
- `includeAll` used `useBoolean`

Entering a dataset detail route unmounts the `/datasets` page, and navigating back remounts it, resetting all filters.

## Solution

Move these three values to `useQueryStates` backed by URL query parameters, following the existing patterns in `app/components/apps/query-params.ts` and `features/skills/query-params.ts`:

- `keyword` — `parseAsString` with debounced URL updates
- `tag_ids` — `parseAsArrayOf(parseAsString, ';')`
- `include_all` — `parseAsBoolean`

The existing 500ms query debounce (`useDebouncedValue`) is preserved.

## Changes

- `web/app/components/datasets/list/index.tsx`
- `web/app/components/datasets/list/query-params.ts` (new)

Closes #42033

author: jxfuller1
body:
## Summary
- prune geometry candidates with bounded NumPy batches before the existing scalar attribute and structural scorers
- reuse fixed-radius distances, callout rectangle classification, compact glyph detection, and a conservative x-sorted leader-segment broad phase
- share an exact O(n log n) rectangle-union sweep across validation and reporting
- avoid repeated PyMuPDF page-coordinate work while preserving MuPDF float precision
- retain the SciPy benchmark backend for timing/output comparison

## PK531 benchmark
Three full, uncached comparisons on the same Windows/Python environment:

| Pipeline | Accepted main | This PR | Reduction |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Full comparison | 6.041 s median | 2.683 s median | 55.6% (2.25x faster) |
| Extraction | 0.846 s | 0.452 s | 46.6% |
| Callout reconstruction | 1.242 s | 0.476 s | 61.7% |
| Entity matching | 3.341 s | 1.413 s | 57.7% |
| PDF capability validation | 0.519 s | 0.175 s | 66.2% |

The accepted and optimized implementations produced the same complete serialized result hash and the same 6,610 changes for PK531_1 vs PK531_2.

## Safety
- no matching threshold, search radius, categorization rule, or alignment policy changed
- structural search radius remains 0.16
- existing scalar scoring remains authoritative; vectorized calculations only reject candidates that cannot reach the configured threshold
- large histogram combinations use a bounded fallback instead of allocating an unbounded matrix
- no new runtime dependencies

## Validation
- 227 tests passed
- Ruff formatting and lint checks passed
- added parity tests for optimized candidate filters, leader indexing, fixed-radius distances, bounded histogram fallback, and MuPDF coordinate precision

author: chocomintw
body:
Five follow-ups on top of `feat/ped-metadata-mounters`, all in `LoadStreamingFile.cpp`.

**Read the struct layout from the parser instead of hardcoding it**
Both mounters assumed a fixed memory layout (`CPedFacialOverlays` = 13 arrays back to back, `CPedSkinTones` = 3 arrays plus 4 more inside 112 bytes). We already ask the parser for the struct definition to allocate and load the file, so the field offsets now come from there too: a field is appendable when it's an `atArray` with 4-byte elements. If Rockstar moves or adds a field, we follow it instead of writing at the wrong offset.

**Unload removes the entries we actually added**
The old code remembered a count and trimmed that many off the end. Data files don't unload in reverse load order — stopping one resource unloads just its file. Resource A adds 5, B adds 3, A stops → the trim takes all of B's 3 plus 2 of A's. Now each file records the hashes it added and removes those by value. Safe because `AppendUniqueHashes` only reports hashes that weren't already present. Each file also records every hash it mentions, so a hash listed by two files survives until both are gone.

**Skin tones store lookup can retry**
The lookup lived in a function-local static, so it ran exactly once. It validates by checking the arrays hold 1–64 tones, which is only true after the game has loaded `pedskintones.meta`. Mount a `CFX_PED_SKIN_TONES` file before that and the store is null for the rest of the session. We now only cache the pointer once it's actually found. The scan also used to take the first plausible call site; when two distinct addresses both pass, it now says so and gives up rather than guessing and appending into unrelated memory. Multiple call sites pointing at the same store is normal and still fine.

**Nested hash arrays**
`CollectHashArrays` now walks nested struct members and fixed arrays of structs.

**OOB write guard + cleanup**
Bounds check when appending ped metadata hashes, plus removal of unrelated changes that had crept in.

author: kylianvo
body:
NotebookLM is no longer used. This removes it from every request path and keeps exactly one consumer: the operator script that re-sweeps curated doctrine.

## What changed

| Area | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Plan / Gear / Nutrition | Gemini primary, NotebookLM as a ~2-min fallback | Gemini only |
| Scheduler fallback | gemini → notebooklm → rule-based | **gemini → reduced-prompt gemini retry → rule-based** |
| `RAG_ENGINE` | Ordered the two engines | Deleted |
| `_nb_prompt` | ~120 lines of hand-synced paraphrase of the real prompt | Deleted |
| Principle sweeps | Admin endpoint + weekly Airflow DAG | **Script only** (`backend/scripts/distill_principles.py`) |
| Gear/nutrition web sweeps | endpoint + DAG | Unchanged |
| Knowledge Hub 8-topic sweep | `POST /api/knowledge/trigger` | Deleted (podcast pipeline already fills that table) |
| `workout_type_extractor` | NotebookLM sweep + 2 endpoints | Deleted |

## The two decisions worth reviewing

**1. Principle sweeps became script-only, and this is the point of the PR.**
`save_domain` *replaces* a `(domain, kind)` wholesale. A weekly unattended sweep that came back thin or refused would overwrite the 29 committed philosophy rows in `kb_seed/scheduler.json`. The insert-only web sweeps (gear/nutrition catalogs) can only ever add, so they keep their endpoint and DAG. Doctrine now changes when an operator runs the script, reviews the seed diff, and commits.

**2. A latent data-loss bug fell out of this.**
`sweep_domain("nutrition")` used to return principles + products. Now it returns products only — and the old `save_domain` would have passed that empty principle list straight to `replace_kb_chunks_by_kind`, **silently deleting every curated nutrition principle**. `save_domain` now refuses to replace principles when a sweep produced none, with a test covering it.

## Things I removed that have no replacement — flagging rather than quietly building one

- **`workout_type_extractor`** was the only way to regenerate the `workout_types` table. The existing rows are untouched and still serve the Planner's workout cards, but there is now no path to re-extract them. A Gemini-on-`kb_chunks` replacement is the natural successor; I did not build it here because it is a feature, not cleanup.
- **`source_label` still defaults to `'NotebookLM distillation'`** in `db.py:296` and the Alembic migration. Changing a column default needs a migration in both places, and the value is cosmetic metadata on existing rows — so I left schema and Python-side fallback consistent rather than half-cleaning it. Say the word and it's a small follow-up.

## Verification

- `848 passed`. The 5 failures are **pre-existing and identical on the base commit** (`google-genai` in this environment has no `ThinkingConfig`) — verified by stashing and re-running.
- Suite runtime **130s → 86s**: tests were previously making real NotebookLM auth attempts (`Run 'notebooklm login' to re-authenticate` appeared in baseline output).
- `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` clean; baseline was also clean, so the 4 reformatted files are mine.
- Frontend: `tsc --noEmit` and `npm run lint` show no new errors or warnings versus baseline.

## Test changes

`test_plan_generator_engines.py` was entirely about engine ordering and is deleted — but its cases that outlived NotebookLM moved rather than died:

- → `test_plan_generator_fallbacks.py`: Gemini grounded with KB context, `used`-counter attribution, course-context injection, plus new coverage for the retry tier and the rule-based fall-through.
- → `test_distill_principles.py`: the three `_query_with_retries` cases followed the code into the script.
- `TestNotebookLmCompactPromptContent` asserted that per-athlete facts survive alongside the schema. That bug (generic schema pushing athlete context off the end) is the kind that returns quietly, so the class was **retargeted at the Gemini prompt** instead of deleted.

No skipped tests.

author: gasvn
body:
## Summary

Fixes #564.

Adds `backend='serpbase'` to `web_search` / `web_api_documentation_search`: an opt-in real Google-SERP backend using SerpBase's API (https://api.serpbase.dev/google/search), for when DDGS's Google backend is unavailable or rate-limited.

## Root cause / motivation

DDGS's Google backend is unreliable/rate-limited in some environments. The issue proposed adding a real SERP API (SerpBase) as an alternative backend.

## Correction to the originally proposed request shape

The issue's proposed design didn't match SerpBase's actual live API. Verified directly against `https://api.serpbase.dev/google/search`:

| | Issue's proposal | Actual (verified live) |
|---|---|---|
| HTTP method | `GET` | `POST` (confirmed `GET` returns 405) |
| Results field | `organic_results` | `organic` |
| Result item fields | `position`, `url` | `rank`, `link` |
| Auth failure | (assumed non-2xx) | HTTP 200, with `error` in the JSON body |

Built against the verified-correct shape rather than the issue's description.

## Fix

- New `_search_with_serpbase()` method in `web_search_tool.py`: POSTs `{q, gl, hl}` (region split on `-` into country/language), checks the JSON body's `error` field explicitly (SerpBase returns 200 even on auth/quota failure), normalizes `organic` results (`link`→`url`, `rank`, `title`, `snippet`).
- Wired into `_search_with_fallback()`'s `serpbase` branch: falls back to the `auto` DDGS chain on any failure (missing key, API error, network error), mirroring the existing `parallel` backend's fallback behavior exactly.
- `run()` rejects non-default `safesearch` for `backend='serpbase'` (not supported by the API); `region` **is** supported (unlike `parallel`).
- `provider_notice` disclosure is attached whenever `serpbase` was attempted, same as for `parallel`.
- Added `SERPBASE_API_KEY` as an optional key in `web_search_tools.json` with `api_key_info`, and regenerated `.env.template` / `api_keys_catalog.json` via `scripts/gen_api_key_catalog.py`.

## Reproduction (before)

No `serpbase` backend existed; `backend='serpbase'` would have raised a schema validation error against the enum.

## Validation (after)

Live smoke test with no `SERPBASE_API_KEY` set (confirms clean fallback, no crash):

```
tu.run({"name": "web_search", "arguments": {"query": "test", "backend": "serpbase"}})
→ {'status': 'success', 'data': {..., 'backend_used': 'auto',
   'attempted_backends': ['serpbase', 'auto'],
   'provider_errors': {'serpbase': 'SERPBASE_API_KEY environment variable is not set...'},
   'provider_notice': "Query sent to SerpBase's hosted third-party Google-SERP API..."}}
```

Full `ToolUniverse().load_tools()` smoke test: 2716 tools loaded cleanly with `SERPBASE_API_KEY` unset (no regression from adding an optional key).

**Not yet verified**: an actual successful authenticated call. I wasn't able to complete SerpBase's account signup myself (no browser automation available on my end). Method, auth header, error-body shape, and field names were all confirmed live against the real (unauthenticated) endpoint plus their published docs — but a real search response has not been observed.

## Test coverage

13 new tests in `tests/tools/test_web_search_tool.py` (32 total, all passing): missing-key handling, response parsing against the documented shape, region splitting, `error`-field-with-200 handling, missing/malformed `organic` handling, truncation to `max_results`, `run()`-level success/fallback/safesearch-rejection, and that the `auto` chain never calls `serpbase` (matching the existing guarantee for `parallel`).

author: themudhaxk
body:
## Summary

Adds JS/TS SDK support for the backend's declared-relationship engine
(backend PRs `#103`/`#105`/`#108`/`#110`/`#113`, merged to `mudbase-server`
`main`). This SDK is JS/TS only; Python/Go/Java/PHP/C#/Dart/Ruby SDKs are
tracked as a separate follow-up (folders already exist under `mudbase-sdk/`
in the monorepo, this PR does not touch them).

- `DataApi.getData` / `DataApi.listData` gain a `populate` parameter (single
  key, comma-separated string, or array; a dot-path key such as
  `"comments.author"` resolves a nested relationship). Composes with the
  existing `sort`/`page`/`limit`/`filter` parameters.
- New `RelationshipsApi` client: `listRelationships`, `getRelationship`,
  `createRelationship`, `updateRelationship`, `deleteRelationship`,
  `getRelationshipOrphans` (owner/admin only, detection not repair).
- New `query.ts`: an opt-in fluent `DataQuery` builder -
  `.populate("author").populate("comments")` (repeatable, also accepts an
  array) chained with `.sort()/.page()/.limit()/.filter()`, terminal
  `.list()`/`.get()`. Includes a minimal `Populate<TBase, TRelations, TKeys>`
  mapped type that widens a populated field from its raw foreign-key id to the
  resolved type, for callers who declare their own per-collection interfaces
  (e.g. `Post.author` typed as `User`, not `any`).

## Relational-ergonomics item 16: fluent query builder (added in this update)

`mudbase-server` PR `#113`'s own description flagged item 16 - a fluent
query builder composing the backend's separate REST query-param mechanisms
into one chainable API - as "not landed anywhere as of this PR." This update
to the same PR closes that gap, extending `query.ts`'s `DataQuery` rather than
opening a competing PR, since a hand-written fluent layer over `DataApi`
already existed here on this branch:

- `.where(field, operator, value)`: filters the base collection's own
  fields, composing into the same `?filter=` JSON param as `.filter()`.
  `operator` is restricted to the exact subset of
  `utils/querySanitizer.js`'s server-side operator allow-list that has an
  unambiguous single-value comparison meaning: `==`/`!=`/`>`/`>=`/`<`/`<=`/
  `in`/`nin`. Repeated calls on the same field merge
  (`.where("price", ">", 10).where("price", "<", 100)` compiles to
  `{ price: { $gt: 10, $lt: 100 } }`).
- `.whereRelated(path, value)`: relationship-field filter (backend PR #105,
  `resolveRelationshipFilters`), composing into a dotted top-level query
  param (`?author.role=admin`), not `?filter=`. **Deliberately equality-only**
  - a deviation from the task brief's illustrative 3-arg
  `.whereRelated("author.role", "==", "admin")` sketch, made after reading
  the real backend code: a dotted query param can only ever carry one raw
  string value, coerced server-side by `coerceFilterValue` into
  bool/number/string, never a Mongo operator object - there is no `>`/`in`/
  etc. mechanism for a relationship-field filter today, so the client does
  not pretend to offer one.
- `.sortByRelated(path, direction)`: sort-by-relationship-field (backend PR
  #108, `resolveRelationshipSortKeys`), composing into the same `?sort=`
  param as `.sort()`. `.sort()` itself now accumulates/de-dupes across
  repeated calls instead of overwriting, so it composes with
  `.sortByRelated()`.
- `.filter()` now shallow-merges instead of overwriting, so it composes with
  `.where()`.

**Scope decision:** built for the JS/TS SDK only (this repo), matching the
existing hand-written-layer-over-generated-code precedent `query.ts` and
`realtime.ts` already established (frozen from OpenAPI regeneration via
`.openapi-generator-ignore`) - the other 6 generated-language SDKs are out of
scope for this pass, same as the rest of this PR's populate/relationship
surface.

**No new backend capability, no bypass.** Every method above only ever
composes REST query params `routes/data.js` and
`services/relationshipService.js` already parse, validate, and enforce
permissions on server-side (`RESERVED_LIST_QUERY_KEYS`, `hasUnsafePathSegment`
prototype-pollution guard, single-value-hop-only relationship sort
resolution). Nothing here invents a new backend capability or weakens/
duplicates that server-side enforcement - a malformed or unauthorized query
composed here still gets rejected or scoped exactly as if the caller had
built the query string by hand. Confirmed by reading the actual server-side
parsing code (`utils/querySanitizer.js`'s operator whitelist,
`relationshipService.js`'s `resolveRelationshipFilters`/
`resolveRelationshipSortKeys`/`coerceFilterValue`) rather than guessing the
param shapes.

- `RELATIONSHIPS.md` and `api.ts`'s `DataApiListDataRequest.populate` doc
  comment updated - both previously stated relationship-field filtering was
  "not supported server-side yet," which was stale as of PR #105/#108
  merging; corrected, with a new "Filtering, sorting, and paginating: the
  full fluent builder" section and a real composed usage example.
- `test/query.test.mjs`: 17 new test cases (`.sort()` accumulation,
  `.sortByRelated()`, `.where()` per-operator and merge behavior including
  the invalid-operator `TypeError`, `.whereRelated()` including the
  non-dotted-path `TypeError`, and a full combined chain) asserting against
  the exact request shape a fake-axios-injected `DataApi` receives.
- New `test/real-axios-merge.test.mjs`: the fake-axios harness above
  intercepts *before* axios's own `buildURL` step runs, so it can't
  demonstrate that `.whereRelated()`'s params (attached via the outgoing
  request's `options.params`) actually land on the final URL the way real
  axios merges them. This file proves that merge end to end against a real
  `axios` instance and a local HTTP server.

## Notes for reviewers

**Two deviations from a literal read of the original task brief, both
verified against the real backend code before implementing:**

1. **REST path.** The brief describes
   `GET /api/projects/:projectId/data/:collection?populate=`. The actual
   backend route (`server.js`, `routes/data.js` in `mudbase-backend`) mounts at
   `GET /api/data/projects/{projectId}/collections/{collectionId}/data`. This
   PR wraps the real, verified path.
2. **`.whereRelated()` is equality-only** (see item 16 section above), a
   deviation from the item-16 task brief's illustrative 3-arg
   `.whereRelated(path, "==", value)` sketch, justified by the real backend
   contract (dotted query params only ever carry one raw string value
   server-side, never a Mongo operator).

**Repo status.** This repo's own `README.md` (see commit `26a5606`) marks it a
retired, axios-based mirror - `npm publish` is explicitly forbidden here since
the maintained `mudbase-sdk` npm package is a separate fetch-based client
generated from `mudbase-docs`. This PR still implements the feature here per
the task's explicit instruction to work in this repo, but the hand-patches to
`api.ts` (the `populate` parameters and the whole `RelationshipsApi` class) are
commented as a stopgap: once the backend's `openapi.yaml` is updated for the
relational-ergonomics endpoints and the generator is re-run, they should be
replaced by generated output and this repo's `.openapi-generator-ignore` entries
for `api.ts` removed.

**CI.** This repo has no CI workflow configured (`.github/` has no workflow
files, `gh pr checks` reports "no checks reported"). Test evidence below is
from a local `npm test` run on this branch.

## Test plan

- [x] `npm run build` - clean, no new TypeScript errors
- [x] `npm test` - 46/46 passing (7 pre-existing realtime tests + 20
      pre-existing relationships/populate tests + 17 new item-16 tests + 2
      new real-axios integration tests)
- [x] Verified route/param/response shapes for `RelationshipsApi`, `populate`,
      and the item-16 filter/sort mechanisms directly against
      `mudbase-backend`'s merged `main`: `routes/data.js`,
      `services/relationshipService.js` (`resolveRelationshipFilters`,
      `resolveRelationshipSortKeys`, `co

author: bettercallzaal
body:
`validate.mjs` went from 4 check groups to **15** in one evening. Every one was added because a
real defect got through - and every one is worthless if the hook gets commented out for being slow.

**A permanently-red guard gets ignored. A slow one gets deleted.** Same failure, quieter door, and
the one nobody measures. The count is the number people quote; the runtime is the number that
decides whether the count still exists next month.

## No new tooling - it becomes a tracked label

obsidian's suggestion. The audit already tracks any recorded label, so:

```
zao-measure "zabalgamez hook runtime s" -- bash <abs>/scripts/measure-hook-runtime.sh
zao-measure --verify "zabalgamez hook runtime s"
```

The count and the runtime then sit side by side in the same report with HOLDS/DRIFTED, which is
exactly the comparison worth having: **a rising count with flat runtime is a lane getting safer; a
rising runtime is a lane about to lose its guards entirely.**

## Rounded on purpose

Three consecutive runs measured **3.65 / 4.06 / 4.13s**. A raw figure would DRIFT on noise every
single time, and the label would be trained to be ignored - the exact disease this exists to
prevent, reproduced inside the instrument that measures it.

So: whole seconds, from the **median** of three runs. Median rather than mean so one slow run - a
cold cache, another process - does not record as a regression.

Current value: **4s** (validate ~4.0s + test-all ~1.8s, measured separately).

Threshold to act on is **~10s**: split the hook, keeping fast structural checks at session start
and moving slow ones to pre-push, rather than accepting a hook people will disable.

`node scripts/validate.mjs` passes.

author: omkhar
body:
## Problem

`shared/session-commands` failed only on the **tmpdir** hostile-env axis (`passed=16 failed=1`). That axis points `TMPDIR` at a directory whose name carries a space, a literal `$HOME`, and a backtick `` `id` `` command substitution (`scripts/ci/run-validate-in-validator.sh:~83-91`), and the scenario roots its **entire** workspace tree under `TMPDIR` (`TMP_DIR=$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/...")`). Two earlier piecemeal fixes (#724 clean filter, #725 diff textconv) did not reach the remaining breaks because the full scenario only executes inside the Linux validator container (macOS takes a different launch path), so they were never reproduced.

## Method — reproduced in-container

Built the validator image and ran **only** this scenario inside it under the real hostile `TMPDIR` (uid 501, `HOME`/`GOCACHE`/`GOMODCACHE` mirroring the harness), iterating with `bash -x` until it ran to completion. Under `set -e`, running to completion is proof there is no remaining break.

## Hostile-path sites found and fixed (both test-side defects)

1. **Monitor env-file assertions (3 lines).** The product writes the monitor env file with `printf '%s=%q\n'` (`scripts/workcell` `write_session_monitor_env_file`). The assertions grepped the **raw** workspace path, which mismatched once `%q` escaped the hostile characters. Now match the `%q`-quoted form with `grep -qxF`.
2. **docker-desktop monitor fixture state file.** The fixture hand-wrote `session-monitor.env` with a raw-interpolated heredoc and then had the product `source` it — the unquoted hostile path broke sourcing. Now emitted with `printf "%q"`, mirroring the product's own format, so it is safe to source. (The intermediate single-quoted `printf '…\n'` was additionally nested inside a single-quoted `bash -lc` body, which collapsed the newlines into literal `n`; double-quoted formats — the existing pattern in these blocks — avoid that.)

## Why spot-quoting, not re-rooting

Sibling scenarios and this one deliberately root `TMP_DIR` under `${TMPDIR}` and pass under the axis — exercising real code under hostile paths is the axis's purpose. Re-rooting would defeat it. Both breaks were genuine test bugs that now match the product's real contract, and `%q` is a no-op on benign paths, so the normal axes are unchanged.

## Verification (in-container)

- Hostile `TMPDIR`: scenario **runs to completion, exit 0** (was the sole failure before).
- Normal `TMPDIR`: scenario exit 0 — no regression.
- `bash -n` clean; `shellcheck` (validator image) clean.
- The axis composition in `run-validate-in-validator.sh` is unchanged (space + `$` + backtick preserved).

## Why this is comprehensive

The fix was driven by an actual in-container run to completion rather than fixing the first error and guessing, so every hostile-path break the scenario can hit on this axis is covered in one pass.

author: efraimfeinstein
body:
The Birnbaum TEI in `opensiddur-projects` was authored by reading the scanned page, not by copying any transcription of it. The reading itself lived only in an untracked directory, so the text the TEI rests on could be lost while the TEI remained — leaving no way to check the encoding against anything but the images.

## What is here

`sources/birnbaum_siddur/scan_reading/`:

- **`readings/{printed}.md`** — what each page was read to say, in full. Fourteen pages: Hebrew 81–89, 91, 93, 95, 97, and the facing English in `english_90_98.md`.
- **`hebrew/{printed}.txt`** — the Hebrew lifted out of those readings, which is what the accuracy measurement actually diffs.
- **`transcription/{printed}.txt`** — the Wikisource side of that diff.

Nothing regenerates the readings; they are a transcription of the 1949 printing made by reading it.

## Two deliberate choices

**`transcription/` duplicates 12K of a file already in this repository** — it is a slice of `source/text/אשכנז/דפי יסוד/תפילת העמידה.txt` (153,830 bytes). That is worth it: the slice boundaries are a judgement, and without them the accuracy measurement cannot be rechecked against the words it actually compared.

**The images stay out.** A leaf is re-fetchable from the Internet Archive and the enlarged bands are cut from it by `opensiddur/importer/birnbaum_scan/pages.py`, so 63MB of the working directory earns nothing in git.

## Licensing

`LICENSE.md` gains section 4, because the two halves of this directory carry different rights and are meant to be laid side by side — a public-domain printing against a CC BY-SA edition of it. `readings/` and `hebrew/` are transcriptions of the section 1 printing; `transcription/` is Wikisource text and carries section 2's terms, so section 2's directory list now names it.

The downstream note telling readers not to describe the result as "Birnbaum 1949" is qualified for the same reason: it holds for the Wikisource layers, and `readings/` is precisely the material for which it does not — those pages were read off the 1949 printing itself.

## Downstream

`opensiddur-ai` [#119](https://github.com/opensiddur/opensiddur-ai/pull/119) points at `sources/birnbaum_siddur/scan_reading/`. That pointer resolves once this lands and the `sourcetexts` submodule moves off `eb0234f`.

body: # CDN bake-off results: jsDelivr is fastest — confirms main's CDN order **No behavioral change.** This PR carries the measurement evidence from the requested 3-CDN bake-off, plus the full E1–E10 experiment record that was missing from main's RESULTS.md, plus mechanical lint fixes for violations inherited from main (see "Inherited lint fixes" below). ## Bake-off (why there is no revert to make) #63 had reordered the CDNs to StaticDelivr-first based on a same-window A/B in which StaticDelivr ran 7.8–11.1 s vs jsDelivr's 15.5–24.5 s — measured **immediately after warming StaticDelivr's edge** for these files. The requested next-day bake-off of all three CDNs as sole source (identical code, only `TIF1_CDNS` varied, 5 interleaved rounds each, dedicated cold benchmark: full 2026 Monaco GP Race telemetry, fresh process + throwaway cache per run) shows that advantage does not persist: | CDN | runs (total_s) | median | |-----|----------------|-------:| | **jsDelivr** | 10.04, 11.72, 12.33, 9.10, 9.87 | **10.04 s** | | StaticDelivr | 32.42, 26.09, 26.46, 25.28, 24.45 | 26.09 s | | HuggingFace | 36.16, 36.73 — 2/5 valid; rounds 3–5 failed with `NetworkError` on `drivers.json` | 36.45 s | - jsDelivr beat StaticDelivr in **all 5 paired rounds** (−22.4, −14.4, −14.1, −16.2, −14.6 s) - StaticDelivr's edge decayed after ~12 h without traffic: 24–32 s for files it served in ~8 s the previous afternoon; its first-ever touch cost 97.6 s - jsDelivr's globally shared cache stays warm (~10 s) — the realistic experience for a new user's first fetch - HuggingFace is slowest and unreliable as a sole source; fine as a fallback **jsDelivr is the fastest option**, and main already ships jsDelivr-first (jsDelivr → HuggingFace → StaticDelivr) — the E9 reorder was not retained during the stack merges. So the correct order is already in place; this PR documents the data that confirms it. ## Contents - `tools/monaco_cdn_bakeoff.py` — interleaved 3-CDN bake-off harness (reusable for future re-measurement from any vantage point) - `.agents/perf-monaco/cdn_bakeoff.json` — full results - `.agents/perf-monaco/RESULTS.md` — complete E1–E10 experiment-series record (baseline, all ten hypotheses with kept/rejected outcomes and measurements, final-state summary, and the bake-off section superseding E9) ## Inherited lint fixes The required `lint` job runs prek over the whole tree, and main's `e571774` (F-series experiment log) landed with violations that fail it for every PR: ruff-format non-conformance (`tools/monaco_shard_probe.py`, `.agents/perf-fab5/proto_micros.py`), missing end-of-file newlines (`.agents/perf-fab5/*.json`), E402 on a deliberate late import (`profile_schedule.py` — noqa'd), a compound assertion (`proto_f4.py` — split), and an unused variable + import (`proto_micros.py` — removed). All mechanical and behavior-neutral; verified with `prek run --all-files` and `py_compile`. ## Verification - Docs/harness-only for this PR's own files; full unit suite passes on this head (1183 tests, CI-green on the test matrix 3.11–3.14) - `prek run --all-files` fully green after the inherited fixes - Benchmark integrity: 1452/1455 telemetry frames fetched in every valid run **Suggestion for the future:** re-run `tools/monaco_cdn_bakeoff.py` from other vantage points/regions before any future CDN reorder — the E9 lesson is that same-window A/B after self-warming an edge can invert overnight.

author: aethercontinuity
body:
## Yhteenveto

Kaksi entsoe-day-ahead-tapausta paljasti kaksi eri ongelmaa peräkkäin.

**Ensimmäinen: aikakatkaisu.** `entsoe-day-ahead` aikakatkesi oletusarvoisella 30 s:lla ensimmäisessä oikeassa ajossa. Suora testaus löysi syyn: ENTSO-E:n Transparency Platform on ajoittain aidosti hidas — sama pyyntö kesti 26,1 s 90 s:n budjetilla.

**Toinen: aito ylävirtakatkos.** Seuraavalla tarkistuksella kolme erillistä kutsua, kukin 90 s:n budjetilla, saivat kaikki 502:n takaisin 5–17 sekunnissa — nopeasti, ei aikakatkaisu lainkaan. Proxy välitti ENTSO-E:n omat HTTP 527/599 -yhdyskäytävävirheet. Ylävirta oli oikeasti alhaalla, ei hidas.

Nämä kaksi tapausta ovat vastakkaisia vikaluokkia samanlaisen "se virheili" -muodon alla, ja ne vaativat vastakkaiset reaktiot (odota pidempään vs. älä yritä uudelleen).

## Kolme muutosta

**1. Reittikohtainen timeout.** `entsoe` saa 90 s, muut kahdeksan pitävät 30 s:n oletuksen.

**2. Aikakatkaisu (nimenomaan, ei lopullinen tila) kertataan kerran kaksinkertaisella budjetilla.** Jos kertaus onnistuu, syy oli ylävirran hitaus: vastausta käytetään normaalisti, `upstream_slow: true` merkitään rinnalle, ei virhettä. Jos kertauskin epäonnistuu, se putoaa alla olevaan nelijakoon `retried: true`-merkinnällä.

**3. Neljä syytä kahden sijaan**, halvimmasta kalleimpaan todeta:

```
upstream_error   nopea 5xx — proxy vastasi, ylävirta ei
canary_route     nopea 4xx — proxy vastasi, oma pyyntö väärä
upstream_slow    aikakatkaisu, sitten 200 tuplabudjetilla
proxy_down       aikakatkaisu (kertauksenkin jälkeen) JA indeksi ei vastaa
```

Konkreettinen 4xx tai 5xx ohittaa tavoitettavuusproobin kokonaan — HTTP:n oma sopimus vastaa jo "onko proxy pystyssä" (se vastasi) ja "kenen syy" (4 vs. 5) ilman toista kutsua. Proobi käytetään vain kun tilaa ei ole lainkaan (kertauksenkin jälkeen) — ainoa tapaus jossa mitään lukea ei ole.

Todellista 4xx/5xx:ää ei koskaan kerrata — tuplattu aika ei voi muuttaa lopullista vastausta.

## Testit

28/28 läpi ilman verkkoa. Kaksi alkuperäistä luokittelutestiä, jotka käyttivät 500:aa merkitsemään "reitti väärin", kirjoitettiin uusiksi aidolla 4xx:llä (täsmää kaikkiin tänään havaittuihin oikeisiin `canary_route`-tapauksiin: fingrid 401, eduskunta 403), uusi testi kattaa nopean 5xx-polun suoraan, ja proobin-kerran-per-ajo-testi käyttää nyt pysyvää aikakatkaisua 500:n sijaan.

Prepares the NV oOS Complete checkout (Content Graph paid flow) for launch: legal documents, binding ToS consent at purchase time, and buyer-email collection for refund matching.

## Changes

**Legal docs (new)**
- `docs/legal/TERMS-OF-SERVICE.md` — full ToS for paid products, including the beta/testing disclosure and destructive-capabilities acknowledgement (referencing `WARRANTY.md`), license grant, no-warranty and liability-cap clauses, and refund summary.
- `docs/legal/REFUND-POLICY.md` — 30-day, no-questions-asked, money-back guarantee with processing, refund effects, fair-use/abuse, and chargeback sections.

**Checkout consent & buyer email (client — `plugins/nvoos-content-graph/`)**
- Purchase modal gains a required ToS/refund **consent checkbox** (links from the vendor `/session` response with client-side fallbacks) and a required **buyer-email field** (prefilled from the logged-in admin); the Pay button stays disabled until both are satisfied.
- The email is attached to the Stripe PaymentIntent via `confirmParams.receipt_email` so Stripe emails the payment receipt; Stripe's iframe is told not to double-prompt for email.
- `/payments/verify` sends `terms_agreed_at` and `buyer_email`; both are validated, forwarded to the vendor, and recorded in the local license record.
- New filters: `nvoos_content_graph/payments/terms_url`, `.../refund_policy_url`.

**Vendor (`addons/checkout-api/`)**
- `/session` returns `terms_url` + `refund_policy_url` (new storefront settings, with defaults).
- `/verify` accepts optional `terms_agreed_at` (plausibility-validated) and `buyer_email`; the intent's `receipt_email` is authoritative when present. Both are stored on the license row — fill-once, never overwritten — including webhook-issued licenses.
- Licenses table gains `buyer_email` and `terms_agreed_at` columns (DB version 3; `dbDelta` migrates automatically); admin table shows "Buyer email" and "Terms agreed".
- Pre-existing phpcs `PreparedSQL` errors in the license store fixed via the repo's `{$table}` interpolation + justified-ignore convention.

## Validation

- `php -l` on all changed PHP files; `node --check` on the modal JS: clean.

- `scripts/verify-commerce-fallback.js`: all checks pass.

- Publish the two docs at `nvdigitalsolutions.com/terms-of-service` and `/refund-policy` (the URLs wired as defaults).
- Review the legal docs with counsel before launch (this is a template, not legal advice).

author: aalzriqat
body:
## SCRUM-302 — organization-lifecycle economic gate

Suspended and destructively-purged organizations could still receive money postings through doors that never look at organization lifecycle. `requireTenantAuth` refuses a suspended org at the **authenticated** door, but `internalMutation`, cron and webhook entry points do not pass through it, and nothing substituted an org-state check at that trust boundary.

Reproduced: a suspended org whose purge had already drained `canonicalPayments` to zero had a canonical payment written straight back into that table by the payment webhook, while its authenticated twin `markSettled` correctly refused the identical request.

### What this PR does

Puts the lifecycle decision at the **economic chokepoints** rather than at the entry points. Gating only the four entry points known to be defective would fix four defects and leave the class open; a caller that reaches a chokepoint inherits the refusal without knowing the lifecycle exists.

- `convex/utils/orgLifecycle.ts` — `orgEconomicLifecycleBlock()` returns the decision as **data** (`ORG_NOT_FOUND` | `ORG_PURGE_HISTORY` | `ORG_SUSPENDED`, each with a `permanent` flag), so each call site chooses its own disposition. `assertOrgEconomicallyActive()` throws for chokepoints that want fail-closed behaviour.
- **Order is load-bearing:** purge history is checked before suspension. A purge leaves the org suspended too, and reporting that as the merely-temporary class is exactly the misclassification that would let queued work wait for a reactivation SCRUM-297 forbids.
- **Crons and the webhook classify rather than throw.** An uncaught throw inside a cross-org cron batch is a cross-tenant outage, not a single-tenant refusal. The payment webhook records a durable `webhookLogs` row in the same transaction as the refusal and answers 200, so the provider stops retrying and no economic state is created.

### R1 — the authority state-machine correction

The first version of this gate placed its early return **above** the `activeAttemptId` / `generation` guards in `performAuthoritySettlement`. That returned while the attempt was still the ACTIVE one, leaving `work.status === "DISPATCHED"`, `attempt.status === "SCHEDULED"` and the scheduled function reporting `state.kind === "success"` — the exact triple `observeAuthorityAttempt` throws on. The one-minute cron re-threw it forever and the car stayed held; `reactivateOrganization` touches neither table, so unsuspending could not repair it.

Corrected so execution identity is established **first**, and only then is lifecycle evaluated:

1. load work, require `DISPATCHED`;
2. require `activeAttemptId === args.attemptId`;
3. require `generation === args.generation` — a stale or superseded execution stays an ordinary no-op;
4. **only then** evaluate lifecycle for the genuinely active attempt;
5. if blocked: zero authority and zero economic effect, no active DISPATCHED/SCHEDULED claim left behind, and an atomically coherent transition.

**Temporary suspension** releases the claim and returns the work to `READY` with backoff, so a reactivated org mints a fresh generation and settles normally. **Permanent purge** terminalizes with its own outcome, `ACCOUNTING_REVERSED_AUTHORITY_ABANDONED_ORG_PURGED`, rather than borrowing one that would assert something never established.

`lifecycleHolds` refunds the retry budget for **temporary** holds, so repeated suspend/reactivate races cannot falsely terminalize a healthy car as `RETRY_EXHAUSTED` — an audit record claiming repeated failed attempts when not one settlement ever ran. A permanent refusal terminalizes instead and does not increment it.

The rollback boundary from SCRUM-208 is intact: no `try`/`catch` was added around `settleOneReversalSource`.

### Tests

- `convex/orgLifecycleEconomicGate.scrum302.test.ts` — failing-first reproduction across the economic surface, every negative case paired with a positive control on an active org in the same harness.
- `convex/authorityLifecycleRace.scrum302.test.ts` — drives the races through the real dispatcher and the real scheduler, so Convex records a genuine `state.kind` for the execution.
- `convex/authorityDispatchLifecycle.test.ts` — the "succeeded execution left the work claimed" invariant, with its former "unreachable in production" label corrected.

### Scope boundaries — read before extending

**There is no completeness ratchet in this PR, deliberately, by owner ruling.** An earlier revision added `scripts/ledgerCoreWriteGuard.test.ts`; it was **removed rather than repaired** because it asserted a property it could not measure — it scanned line-at-a-time so a multiline `insert(` was invisible, accepted a gate token appearing in a comment or after the write, compared sets rather than multisets, and resolved caller completeness from a hand-entered list seeded by a graph index that under-reported. A guard that asserts what it cannot measure is worse than none, because the next reader stops checking.

A direct source scan found **19 ledger-core insert sites across 7 files** at the certification SHA. That is a **measurement of one revision, not a standing guarantee** — nothing re-derives it on later commits, and **a new ledger-core writer will not fail CI**.

Follow-ups, none of them launch blockers for this merge: **SCRUM-308** broader lifecycle uniformity for non-ledger-core economic writers · **SCRUM-309** structural AST/symbol writer ratchet · **SCRUM-310** purge READY-row lifecycle behaviour (LIFE-1) · **SCRUM-311** test-suite flakiness investigation · **SCRUM-312** documentation residuals.

### Certification

Certified at `08812498c0bd3a31bf17952cd56ca3620036ec9b` against protected main `6db605071585305f0070c67515af22955c44e9a3`.

Required CI **11/11 success** (enumerated from live branch protection) · `unit-and-integration` **4298 tests, 0 failures** · both typechecks 0 · lint 0 errors · **Sonnet MAX APPROVE** · **Codex high APPROVE**.

Honest gaps: Playwright **UNAVAILABLE**, not among the 11 required and not counted as a pass. Codex's local Vitest was **UNAVAILABLE** (EPERM), likewise not counted. CodeRabbit `success` on the draft is a **skip, not coverage**.

Runtime remained **AST-identical to the reviewed R1 artifact** through every subsequent prose-only round.

author: orieg
body:
Multi-writer optimistic lock coupling (OLC) engine for `SyncExpanseSet` and `SyncExpanseMap` (Stage B), as specified in `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` §4.2 and pre-registered in `docs/benchmarks/concurrency/METHODOLOGY.md` §10 (Issue #568 PR 5).

Refs #568.

allow-regression: Stage B hand-over-hand OLC write path replaces single coarse mutex on SyncExpanseMap and SyncExpanseSet with optimistic lock coupling and ancestor version locks (sync_map_churn +110.24%, sync_map_insert +108.05%, sync_set_insert +94.98%, sync_map_remove +83.22%), measured in CI run https://github.com/orieg/expanse/actions/runs/34361400173

## Performance Trade-off Disclosure
- **Regressed Metrics**:
  - `sync_map_churn/random`: +110.24% (226,103,230 vs 107,545,838)
  - `sync_map_insert/random`: +108.05% (89,954,253 vs 43,237,094)
  - `sync_set_insert/random`: +94.98% (72,794,765 vs 37,335,140)
  - `sync_map_remove/random`: +83.22% (74,307,411 vs 40,556,821)
  - Smoke benchmark layout noise across unedited harnesses: `set_insert/sequential` (+1.89%), `judyl_insert/sequential` (+1.59%), `strmap_insert/routes` (+1.04%), etc.
- **Load-Bearing Rationale**:
  - Prior to Stage B, `SyncExpanseMap` and `SyncExpanseSet` writes acquired a coarse `write_root_covered` mutex and performed direct single-threaded operations.
  - Stage B replaces coarse mutex serialization with hand-over-hand optimistic lock coupling: epoch pinning, version sampling and validation, per-node version locking, bottom-up ancestor population maintenance (`bump_ancestor_pop0`), and version increment on unlock. In single-threaded Callgrind execution, this synchronization machinery adds instruction overhead per operation.
- **Net Win**:
  - Replaces global write serialization with concurrent multi-writer scalability across non-overlapping key expanses.
  - Concurrency scaling verified on benchmark harnesses: `SyncExpanseSet` (95% Read / 5% Write) achieves 7.12× throughput at W = 4 threads (471,154 ops/sec vs 66,354 ops/sec at 1T), and parallel disjoint progress passes full Wing-Gong linearizability (`test_multi_writer_parallel_disjoint_and_census`).

## 1. What changed and where

- **`crates/expanse/src/sync.rs`**:
  - Added `SharedTree::clear_path(&self)` method and wired `inner.clear_path()` into `write`, `write_root_covered`, and `read_locked` after operations, suppressing bypass conditions structurally by flushing acceleration path cursors (per `AGENTS.md §2.1.5`). Expanded safety rationale for temporary mutable borrow under reader fallback quiescence.
  - Implemented `olc_insert_set`, `olc_remove_set`, `olc_insert_map`, and `olc_remove_map` implementing hand-over-hand optimistic lock coupling:
    - Traverses root and branch nodes (`BranchL3`, `BranchL7`, `BranchB`, `BranchU`) validating node versions hand-over-hand.
    - Handles in-place modifications on `LeafB1`, linear leaves (`Leaf1`..`Leaf7`), and immediate representations under parent node locks.
    - Added `decode_matches(&edge, key, ...)` checks across all leaf and immediate types to prevent path-compressed prefix collisions on disjoint expanses.
    - Bottom-up ancestor population maintenance via `bump_ancestor_pop0`, acquiring per-node version locks for each ancestor frame to preserve census invariant S7 (`pop0(e) + 1 == |keys under e|`).
    - Hand-over-hand retry on concurrency conflict with bounded write-retry loop (`for _ in 0..MAX_RETRIES`), early gate-closure detection (`self.shared.gate.is_closed()`), and starvation-free fallback to serialized `write_root_covered` lock.
  - Added conditional target-specific atomic aliases (`core::sync::atomic::AtomicUsize` vs `loom::sync::atomic::AtomicUsize`) for full Loom race model compatibility.
  - Added dead-thread slot pruning in writer registry (`writers.retain(|s| Arc::strong_count(s) > 1)`) in both `enter_writer` and `quiesce_writers` to prevent unbounded memory churn from transient worker threads.
  - Kept `Shared::write` zero-overhead for non-OLC wrappers (`SyncExpanseStrMap`, `SyncExpanseBytesMap`, `SyncExpanseBlobMap`) by routing `Set`/`Map` `clear()` through `write_root_covered`.
  - Added `// SAFETY:` comments on all unsafe blocks to satisfy `clippy::undocumented_unsafe_blocks`.
- **`crates/expanse/src/occ.rs`**:
  - Added crate-private `version_try_lock`, `version_unlock`, `version_obsolete_locked`, `LockedTarget`, and `LockSet`.
  - Scoped `SeqVersion::try_lock` and `unlock` to `pub(crate)` with `#[allow(dead_code)]` for `#![no_std]` bare-metal builds.
  - Added ABA-prevention mutexes to `Collector` free-lists via `[Mutex<FreeListHead>; NUM_CLASSES]` to serialize concurrent multi-writer retirement and allocation recycling.
  - Added globally unique `id: u64` (atomic counter `NEXT_GATE_ID`) to `WriterGate` to eliminate memory-address recycling defects across tests and thread-local registries.
- **`crates/expanse/src/map.rs` & `crates/expanse/src/set.rs`**:
  - Added `root_top_ptr(&self) -> *mut Edge` on `MapCore` and `ExpanseSet`.
  - Added `set_tree_pop(&mut self, pop: u64)` on `ExpanseMap` and `ExpanseSet` (gated under `#[cfg(all(target_pointer_width = "64", feature = "std"))]`) to prevent dead-code warnings on `#![no_std]`.
- **`crates/expanse/src/node.rs`**:
  - Implemented crate-private `bits_eq(&self, other: &Self) -> bool` on `Edge` with `#[allow(dead_code)]` (placed after compile-time layout gate to preserve public API stability and line citations in `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md §10.8`).
- **`crates/expanse/tests/linearizability.rs`**:
  - Added multi-threaded Wing-Gong linearizability verification for `SyncExpanseMap` and `SyncExpanseSet`.
  - Added `test_sync_map_linearizability_tree_rooted` and `test_sync_set_linearizability_tree_rooted` at W = 4 over widened key sets on `Root::Tree` to exercise the full `olc_insert_*` and `olc_remove_*` concurrency path under Wing-Gong checking (addressing review item 2 and Table row S6).
  - Added Miri-safe single-threaded companion tests (`test_sync_map_linearizability_single_threaded`, `test_sync_set_linearizability_single_threaded`).
  - Added `test_multi_writer_parallel_disjoint_and_census` verifying parallel multi-writer progress across 4 threads on disjoint expanses with post-run census validation (`inner.validate()` and length checks).
- **`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` & `docs/ALGORITHMS.md`**:
  - Updated §4.2 in `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` to reference Stage B implementation in PR 5 (Refs #568), pending the benchmark campaign.
  - Added §3.6 to `docs/ALGORITHMS.md` detailing the 6-step Stage B OLC pipeline.
- **`docs/architecture_visualizer.html`**:
  - Added `sync_write` operation visualizing Stage B multi-writer optimistic lock coupling, and replaced prohibited "Lock-Free" phrasing with "Multi-Writer Optimistic Lock Coupling".

## 2. Verification

### Automated Suites [RUN]
- **Linearizability & Multi-Writer Census Suite:**
  ```bash
  cargo test -p expanse-trie --test linearizability
  ```
  Result: 7 passed; 0 failed.
- **10-Iteration Stress Loop [RUN]:**
  ```bash
  for i in {1..10}; do cargo test -p expanse-trie --test linearizability || exit 1; done
  ```
  Result: 10/10 iterations passed cleanly (100% green, 0 flakes).
- **Public API Snapshot Verification [RUN]:**
  ```bash
  python3 scripts/check_public_api.py
  ```
  Result: `check_public_api.py: the public Rust API matches its committed snapshot for expanse-trie` (0 diff).
- **Loom Concurrency Race Model [RUN]:**
  ```bash
  RUSTFLAGS="--cfg loom" cargo test -p expanse-trie --release loom_
  ```
  Result: 9 passed; 0 failed (all 9 model-checked interleaving tests passed).
- **Visualizer & Data Sync Tests [RUN]:**
  ```bash
  cargo test -p expanse-trie --test test_visualizer_sync
  ```
  Result: 20 passed; 0 failed.
- **Encoding Reference Sync Tests [RUN]:**
  ```bash
  cargo test -p expanse-trie --test test_encoding_reference_sync
  ```
  Result: 17 passed; 0 failed.
- **Full Workspace Tests (`scripts/gate.sh --quick`):**
  ```bash
  ./scripts/gate.sh --quick
  ```
  Result:
  - `cargo fmt --all --check`

author: einarjohnlagera
body:
Closes everything found by `v0.135.0`'s pre-signoff cold agent. It ran against the merged state, framed as falsification against eight claims plus the two structural questions, and re-ran the suites itself rather than trusting the implementing session.

**Seven claims upheld. One refuted. Two tests found that could not catch what they described.**

## C6 refuted — a curator is notified of their own publish

`adopt()` carries **no owner guard**, so a curator can self-adopt their own PUBLIC Review Set. `findReviewSetUpdateRecipients` had no self-copy exclusion, so publishing an update then told them about an action they had just taken themselves.

**The fix was already sitting eight lines above in the same file:** `countAdoptionsByCollectionIds` excludes self-copies with `adoption.ownerUserId <> source.ownerUserId` for the adoption *count*. The two queries now agree on what an adoption is, and `aCuratorWhoAdoptedTheirOwnSetIsNotNotifiedOfTheirOwnPublish` fails if they diverge again. Cosmetic in severity; real as a gap.

## Two tests passed for reasons unrelated to their claims

**This is the finding worth keeping, because one of them was written by the audit that went looking for exactly this shape.**

**1. `curatorEditsWithoutPublishingReachNoAdopter`** — added by this release's own audit to guard *"editing is not publishing"*, the release's boldest anti-drift claim. Its act phase inserted rows with `jdbcTemplate` and **called no service method**, so a producer wired to fire on a WRITE rather than on the publish call would have sailed straight through it.

Renamed to `unpublishedRowsAloneDispatchNoFanOut` — what it actually proves — and the real guard now lives on the real edit path as `NoteCollectionServiceTest.addItems_doesNotAnnounceAnUnpublishedEdit`, which drives `addItems` and asserts the event publisher is untouched.

**2. The `taskTransactionActive` assertion** captured `isActualTransactionActive()` in a wrapper running **on the test thread, after the publishing transaction had already committed and unbound** — so it read `false` whether or not `fanOut` was transactional, and could not see the regression its own `.as(...)` named.

The capture moved **inside `deliver`**, via a spy on the **Spring-managed** bean so the proxy is live. **Verified by mutation: `@Transactional` on `fanOut` now fails it, and previously did not.**

## Mutants

| Mutant | Killed by |
|---|---|
| Dedup key reverted to the audit's `<adoptedCollectionId>` | `dismissingOneRevisionAllowsTheNextPublishedRevisionToCreateANewRow` |
| `@Transactional` on the producer's `fanOut` | `FanOutTransactionBoundaryTest` — and **now also** the corrected runtime assertion |
| **Self-copy exclusion removed** | **`aCuratorWhoAdoptedTheirOwnSetIsNotNotifiedOfTheirOwnPublish`** |

## Upheld, and worth recording

The `LIKE` prefix cannot collide across sources (UUIDs are fixed-length and contain no wildcards). A same-millisecond key collision additionally requires a dismiss plus a lock-serialized round trip inside 1 ms. Adopted **child** collections point at their own child source, not the root, so a Goal adoption cannot multi-notify. `ACTION_REQUIRED` has zero references repo-wide, and **production still holds zero notification rows of any type — re-verified read-only at this audit rather than inherited**, since a stale row would break enum hydration.

## Also in this PR

Documented that an **unread and undismissed** `REVIEW_SET_UPDATE` never expires — it is badge-eligible, so retention keeps it, and suppression keys on `dismissed_at IS NULL`. A learner who never opens their inbox holds one row and a badge stuck at 1. That is intended, but only the dismissal path was written down.

**Known limitation, recorded not fixed:** no test exercises delivery on the real `ThreadPoolTaskExecutor` thread, and the mid-fan-out unique-index conflict is covered only with a mocked `NotificationService`.

## Verification

Backend 2,337 tests + the PostgreSQL harness; frontend 2,348 across 212 suites; `tsc --noEmit` clean; `npm run lint` 0 errors.

author: knoxio
body:
Stacked on #4591. Unblocks POPS-3222 (food) and POPS-3223 (inventory).

## What

`PageDescriptor` was flat — `{ path, index?, bundleSlot }` — and the loader built a flat list of routes from it. Every pillar migrated so far has a flat route table, so this held.

`pillars/food` does not. It nests eight tabs under a `data` layout whose element renders the tab chrome around an `<Outlet/>`. `pillars/inventory` has the same shape. Neither could be described by the wire, so neither could be loader-mounted.

## Why not flatten instead

Declaring `data/ingredients`, `data/aliases` … as siblings and having each tab render the layout around itself would make the transport dictate the app's route structure: the layout stops being a layout and **remounts on every tab switch, losing its state**, purely to satisfy a schema. So the wire carries the tree and the loader recurses into it.

## The two boundaries worth reading

**The depth bound is structural, not counted at parse time.** The schema for the last level has no `children` key at all and `.strict()` rejects one, so a hostile manifest cannot be walked to arbitrary depth before the depth is noticed. A `z.lazy` recursion would accept the input first and count afterwards.

**An index route with children is refused** — for a sharper reason than tidiness. React Router throws at *router construction* for that shape, and for a loader-mounted pillar that takes down the shell's whole router rather than one pillar's subtree. Refusing it at parse time makes it one manifest failing to parse and being skipped. The loader builds the two `RouteObject` union arms separately for the same reason, rather than assembling one shape and casting.

**Failure containment stays per node.** The error boundary is built per page, not per pillar, so a child whose slot the bundle does not carry degrades inside the layout — the layout and its sibling tabs stay mounted.

## Tests

- `libs/sdk/src/manifest-schema/ui.test.ts` — accepts a layout with children and nesting exactly at the bound; rejects one level past it, an index route with children, an unknown key at a nested level, and a non-kebab slot at a nested level.
- `pillars/shell/src/app/external-ui.test.tsx` — mounts the layout with its index child, mounts a named child under the same layout, and both halves of the containment claim: the broken child degrades, and its siblings and the layout stay up.

Verified the four loader tests go red when the recursion is removed.

Closes POPS-3256.

body: ## Summary Extends the hosted-quote backend (#38) with a tenant-scoped customer portal and recurring (subscription) quotes. Every existing route and response shape is unchanged; `GET /v1/quotes/{claim_token}` gains two additive fields (`billing`, `interval`). No new env vars; no frontend changes. **Migration:** `0014_customer_portal` — `customers`, `portal_login_tokens`, `portal_sessions`, `service_requests`, `quote_subscriptions`; `quotes.customer_id` (nullable), `quotes.billing` (default `one_time`), `quotes.interval`. Old quotes need no backfill: they are linked to a customer on the next approve for that address or on the customer's first portal login (`link_quote_customer` in `domain/customer_linking.py`). **New Stripe webhook events to subscribe:** `invoice.paid`, `invoice.payment_failed`, `customer.subscription.updated`, `customer.subscription.deleted` (plus `checkout.session.completed` now also handled for `mode=subscription`). ### Customers + magic-link auth - Identity is `(business_id, lowercased email)`; the same address at two businesses is two `Customer` rows, so nothing crosses tenants. - `POST /v1/businesses/{public_key}/portal/login` → always `202 {}`. When the address is a customer with a quote, `PortalService.request_login` stores `sha256(secrets.token_urlsafe(32))` (15 min, single-use) and enqueues a `portal_login_email` outbox command dispatched by `ResendPortalLoginEmailAdapter` (`Sign in to your account`, link `/portal/login?token=`). Throttled 5/hour per IP and per `(business, email)` (`429`, which reveals nothing about the address). - `POST /v1/portal/sessions` exchanges the token (`hmac.compare_digest` on the hash, marks it used) for a 30-day session token — also hashed at rest — and returns `{sessionToken, customer:{displayName,email}, business:{displayName,siteUrl}}`. `DELETE /v1/portal/sessions` revokes. All failures are a generic `401 {"detail":"unauthorized"}`. - `GET /v1/portal/me`, `GET /v1/portal/quotes`, `GET /v1/portal/subscriptions`, `POST /v1/portal/billing-portal` (`404` without a Stripe customer), `POST /v1/portal/requests` — exact field names in `docs/public_api.md`. Portal quote `id`/`status` are the same `gvq_…` public id and customer-facing status the public quote route uses; `claimToken` is included so the site can link to `/q/`. - Service requests persist a `service_requests` row (`source=portal`, `status=new`) and enqueue `New service request from (): ` through the existing owner-notice routing, anchored to the conversation of the customer's latest quote. - CORS on the public app now also allows `DELETE` and the `Authorization` header. ### Recurring quotes - `QuoteDraftProposal.billing: QuoteBilling` (`one_time` default) and `interval: BillingInterval | None` (required iff recurring, validated in the domain). - Structured parser: `billing: monthly|yearly` line (anything else is a deterministic rejection, no model fallthrough). Free-text: `written_recurrence(text)` finds literal owner wording (`per month`, `monthly`, `/mo`, `yearly`, `annual`, …); the model's schema/prompt is told the interval it may use (or `null`) and any model-invented interval is dropped — same never-invent rule as prices. Preview shows `Billing: monthly`. - `accept` on a recurring quote: `PublicQuoteService` creates a Stripe Customer once per `(business, customer)` via `BillingAccountPort.create_customer` (stored in `customers.stripe_customer_id`), then opens Checkout with `mode=subscription`, `customer=`, `line_items[i][price_data][recurring][interval]`. Same metadata and `Idempotency-Key` scheme as one-time payments. - Webhooks: subscription-mode `checkout.session.completed` marks the quote paid and inserts `QuoteSubscription`; invoice/subscription events update the row (status, `current_period_end`, `cancel_at_period_end`) and post owner notices (`Subscription for renewed $X` / `payment failed` / `cancelled`). Replay-safe via the existing `payment_provider_events` ledger; an event for a subscription that is not ours is recorded and ignored (`200`), one that races ahead of our own completion gets `503` for retry. - Stripe adapter (`infrastructure/stripe/api.py`): `customer_form`, `billing_portal_form`, subscription fields in `checkout_form`; still httpx form-encoded, provider bodies and keys never logged. ### Layout Ports (`BillingAccountPort`, `PortalLoginEmailPort`, repository protocols) and records in `domain/`, use cases in `application/portal.py` and `application/public_quotes.py`, vendor code in `infrastructure/`, routes in `interfaces/http/portal.py`, wired in `composition/production.py`. ### Tests `tests/test_customer_portal.py`: login flow (enumeration-safe, rate-limited, single-use, expiry), session auth/revocation, CORS preflight for `DELETE`, tenant isolation (same email at two businesses; two customers of one business), lazy linking of older quotes, service request row + owner notice, structured and free-text recurrence, subscription checkout form and Stripe customer/billing-portal forms, every new webhook event end to end (including replay and the racing-event `503`), Resend login-email payload, dispatcher. Existing hosted-quote tests unchanged and passing. `ruff check`, `ruff format --check`, `mypy src tests`, `pytest` (571 passed) green. Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/9a8786273e53413faf7b1e5e39169520 Open in Devin Desktop: https://app.devin.ai/desktop/session/9a8786273e53413faf7b1e5e39169520?variant=devin Requested by: @ckoutz ---

## 产地(第 9′ 条)

【skill 上下文: 无 skill,主循环派发 / 载体与分工: 候选出自 nyxid-oracle 搜题(GPT Pro,2026-09-09 r8,含对本仓 dev 的 REPO CHECK);数值验算与 dev/分支/PR 查重由 orchestrator(claude 主循环,session 523b4479)亲跑(predispatch CLEAR);Lean/Scribe/Library 由 codex-cli 实施席 `op-a397242` 完成,dossier/claim 由 codex-cli Stage-B 席完成;冻结、emit、门由 orchestrator 亲跑 / 混合方式: 评审三席 codex-cli 的判词由 orchestrator 在评审归位后以 PR 评论补记;同族无跨族独立性】

## 定理

模块 `D5/S1/Recurrence/Residue/ExponentialSquareWeightCatalanParity.lean`，命名空间 `D5.S1.Recurrence.Residue.ExponentialSquareWeightCatalanParity`。以下逐字列出三个公开定义及七个公开定理的声明；定理证明体省略。

```lean
noncomputable def d (n : ℕ) : ℤ :=
  if hn : 2 ≤ n then
    (n - 1 : ℕ) * d (n - 1) + ∑ j ∈ range n,
      if _hj : 2 ≤ j ∧ j < n then
        ((j : ℤ) ^ 2 - 1) * (n - j : ℕ) * d j * d (n - j) else 0
  else if n = 1 then 1 else 0
termination_by n
decreasing_by all_goals omega

noncomputable def a (n : ℕ) : ℤ := if n = 0 then 1 else (n : ℤ) * d n

theorem d_recurrence (n : ℕ) (hn : 2 ≤ n) :
    d n = (n - 1 : ℕ) * d (n - 1) +
      ∑ j ∈ Ico 2 n, ((j : ℤ) ^ 2 - 1) * (n - j : ℕ) * d j * d (n - j)

theorem a_eq (n : ℕ) (hn : 1 ≤ n) : a n = (n : ℤ) * d n

noncomputable def M : PowerSeries ℤ :=
  mk (fun n => if n = 0 then 0 else if n = 1 then 1 else ((n : ℤ) ^ 2 - 1) * d n)

theorem log_derivative_identity :
    coeff 0 (mk a) = 1 ∧ X * derivative ℤ (mk a) = M * mk a

theorem coeff_M_rat (n : ℕ) (hn : 2 ≤ n) :
    coeff n (M.map (Int.castRingHom ℚ)) =
      ((n : ℚ) ^ 2 - 1) * (a n : ℚ) / n

theorem generating_unique (b : ℕ → ℚ) (m : PowerSeries ℚ)
    (hb0 : b 0 = 1) (hm0 : coeff 0 m = 0) (hm1 : coeff 1 m = 1)
    (hshape : ∀ n : ℕ, 2 ≤ n → coeff n m = ((n : ℚ) ^ 2 - 1) * b n / n)
    (heq : X * derivative ℚ (mk b) = m * mk b) :
    ∀ n : ℕ, b n = (a n : ℚ)

theorem mod_two_catalan :
    X * mk (fun m => (d (2 * m + 1) : ZMod 2)) =
      Invariants.CatalanCompositionSquareParity.catalanSeries.map
        (Int.castRingHom (ZMod 2))

theorem hanna_conjecture (n : ℕ) : Odd (a n) ↔ ∃ k : ℕ, n + 1 = 2 ^ k
```

## 出处

Paul D. Hanna, OEIS [A397242](https://oeis.org/A397242), Jun 19 2026；bibkey `hanna2026a397242`，doi: null。下列原文来自 `Library/Recurrence/hanna2026a397242.md`，由 orchestrator 提供，Stage-B 无网络复核。

NAME:

> O.g.f. satisfies A(x) = exp( x + Sum_{n>=2} (n^2-1) * a(n)*x^n / n^2 ).

COMMENT（第一条猜想）:

> Conjecture: a(n) is odd iff n+1 is a power of 2.

条目另有两条模 3 分类猜想，不属于此项解决声明。dossier: `Problems/oeis-a397242-exponential-square-weight-catalan-parity.md`；唯一 `OpenProblemResolutionClaim` 绑定 `hanna_conjecture`，`ResolutionKind.Proved`。

## 证明

| 公开定理 | 证明路径 |
| --- | --- |
| `d_recurrence` | 展开 `d` 的递归分支，用 `sum_filter` 将受限 `range n` 改写为 `Ico 2 n`。 |
| `a_eq` | 正指标排除零分支，展开 `a` 得 `a(n)=n*d(n)`。 |
| `log_derivative_identity` | `convolution` 分离 `M*mk a` 的端点及线性项；`d_recurrence` 合并内部和，得到 `n^2*d(n)`，与 `coeff_derivative` 对齐；`a_zero` 给常数项。 |
| `coeff_M_rat` | `coeff_map -> coeff_M -> a_eq`，在 Q 中消去非零 n，得到精确的 `(n^2-1)*a(n)/n` 权重。 |
| `generating_unique` | 强归纳结合 `convolution_split` 与 `rational_identity` 比较两条微分方程；低次项经归纳相等，`coeff_M_rat` 和 `hshape` 确定顶次项，清除 n 后得系数唯一。 |
| `mod_two_catalan` | `reduced_recurrence -> even_pair -> odd_catalan`（使用 `sum_pairs`）`-> E_equation -> quadratic_unique`，与导入的 `catalan_equation` 比较，得 `X*E=mapTwo(K)`。 |
| `hanna_conjecture` | `a_zero` 处理零指标；`a_eq` 排除正偶指标；`odd_index_support -> mod_two_catalan + binary_catalan` 确定奇指标支撑，幂次平移给 `n+1=2^k`。 |

## 范围与诚实边界

第一层 OEIS 猜想（条目年份 2026）；KPI = open problems resolved，一份 dossier、一项第一猜想解决声明。所有自然指标均被量化，包括 `a(0)=1`，不是有限前缀结论。两条模 3 猜想未解决。

积分归一化 `d(n)=a(n)/n`（n>=1，`d(1)=1`）构造整数解。`M=X+sum_{n>=2}(n^2-1)d(n)X^n` 是整数级数。NAME 的形式化读法为 `A(0)=1` 与 `X*A'=M*A`；`coeff_M_rat` 明确给出指数的导数乘 X 后的有理权重。Mathlib API 检索未找到此形状的 PowerSeries exp/log 恒等式；此模块没有声称另证字面上的 exp 代入恒等式。`generating_unique` 在 Q 上证明满足精确权重形状的微分解唯一。模二 Catalan 递推是 `ZMod 2` 中的等式，不是整数 Catalan 系数等式。

目标 generality = I；直接导入冻结的 `D5/S1/Recurrence/Invariants/CatalanCompositionSquareParity`（其 generality = G）。实施席报告七个公开定理的 axioms 均为 std3：`[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`。原文归属、source-to-Lean 对应及优先权不属于内核证明。
