body:
Restructures the `<Route path="settings">` block so it no longer renders an intermediate `<Outlet />` that dropped `AppOutletContext`.

Before:
```tsx
<Route path="settings" element={<Outlet />}>
  <Route index element={<SettingsPage currentUser={currentUser} />} />
  <Route path="device" element={<DeviceInfoPage />} />
  ...
</Route>
```

After:
```tsx
<Route path="settings" element={<SettingsPage currentUser={currentUser} />} />
<Route path="settings/device" element={<DeviceInfoPage />} />
<Route path="settings/language" element={<LanguagePage />} />
<Route path="settings/appearance" element={<AppearancePage />} />
<Route path="settings/bookshelf" element={<BookshelfSettingsPage />} />
<Route path="settings/users" element={<UserManagementPage currentUser={currentUser} />} />
```

`SettingsPage` still receives `currentUser` as a prop and keeps its relative `navigate('device')` / `navigate('language')` / ... navigation. `DeviceInfoPage`, `LanguagePage`, `AppearancePage`, `BookshelfSettingsPage`, and `UserManagementPage` are now direct children of the `AppLayout` route, so `useOutletContext<AppOutletContext>()` resolves to the context provided by `AppLayout` and `currentUser` is no longer `undefined` for nested settings pages.

Verified end-to-end that `/settings/appearance` no longer throws `Cannot destructure property 'currentUser'`, and that `DeviceInfo`, `Language`, `Appearance`, `Bookshelf`, and `User Management` pages render without runtime errors. `pnpm --filter @bbbook/web typecheck` and `pnpm --filter @bbbook/web build` both pass.

author: cursor[bot]
body: ## Bug and impact Two meeting-lifecycle bugs that lose or corrupt session data: 1. **Quit while recording never ends the meeting** — Tray Quit, dashboard Quit, or Cmd+Q fired `audioManager.stop()` without waiting, then immediately `database.close()`. `endMeeting()` was never called. The last STT flush could not write (DB already closed), and the meeting row stayed open forever (`ended_at` / `duration_seconds` null). 2. **Overlapping `toggle-recording` ends the wrong meeting** — `stop()` sets `isRecording = false` immediately, then awaits STT (often 5–30s). The overlay still shows recording until that await finishes. A second click or shortcut enters the start path, creates a new meeting, and the first handler then `endMeeting()`s that new id and clears the session. Recording continues; later transcripts are dropped. ## Root cause - `will-quit` treated async stop as fire-and-forget and had no access to `MeetingSession`, so shutdown never persisted `ended_at`. - `toggle-recording` has no reentrancy lock, and stop is slow enough that a second invoke is a realistic user action. ## Fix - Ordered shutdown: wait for the final flush (15s cap), `endMeeting()`, then close the DB. `will-quit` uses `preventDefault` so this can finish. - Exclusive lock on `toggle-recording` so a second invoke is ignored until the first completes. ## Validation `node --experimental-strip-types --test electron/services/appShutdown.test.ts` — 5 passing (shutdown order, errors, hang timeout, lock). Full Electron quit/toggle runtime was not available in this environment.

author: madpatrick
body:
* Fix low-contrast graph range buttons on the base theme

.graphbuttons .btn dimmed the whole button to 50% opacity, which washes the white fill and grey icon toward the same backdrop color instead of just toning the button down, collapsing the icon-vs-fill contrast. On the base theme (no themes/*.css override) this left inactive graph range buttons barely visible. Ease the dimming to 75% opacity to keep the active/inactive distinction without erasing that contrast.

Fixes MadPatrick/dashticz#280

* Fix graph canvas not filling its block's width

.graphcontent relied on .block_graph's flex stretch (display:flex; flex-direction:column) to get its width, but that didn't reliably give the canvas Chart.js creates inside it the block's actual width - the canvas fell back to its browser-default intrinsic width instead, leaving the graph much narrower than its block. Set width:100% explicitly instead of relying on flex stretch.

Confirmed fix, reported by the user who filed MadPatrick/dashticz#280.

author: ciresnave-bot
body:
## What shipped to callers

`GGUFWriter::unimplemented_quant` returned this, verbatim:

```text
GGUF Q8_0 export is NOT IMPLEMENTED. Until 2026-09-09 it              returned
a correctly sized buffer of ZEROS and reported success,              producing
a file that loads with the right shapes and no              weights.
```

The message was written across several source lines. The line breaks and the
indentation that followed them were folded into the literal as runs of literal
spaces. **The source compiles, the value is wrong, and the wrongness is visible
only to whoever reads the error.**

## ⚠️ Why nothing caught it

| instrument | why it is blind |
|---|---|
| `rustfmt` | does not inspect string contents |
| `clippy` | has no lint for it |
| the test on that refusal | asserts `msg.contains("NOT IMPLEMENTED")` -- a fragment at the very front, which survives the folding intact |
| code review | `git log -S` finds ONE introducing commit and no earlier correct form: it was **born mangled**, so the diff showed the folded text as an addition, which reads as intentional prose |

A literal is the one region of a Rust file that every other instrument treats as
opaque, so a defect *inside* one is invisible by construction.

Measured separately: `cargo fmt --all` on the repaired tree does **not** re-fold
any of them, so for these instances rustfmt is not the cause and the authoring
path is.

## Repaired

**24 runs in 12 literals across 6 files.** One is user-facing (`gguf_export.rs`);
the other eleven are assertion and guard-failure messages -- the text a
maintainer reads at the exact moment a guard trips.

## The guard

`crates/mlmf-core/tests/literal_whitespace.rs` lexes every string literal in the
workspace and rejects a run of **>=4 spaces between two non-space characters on
the same logical line of the value**. Indentation that *begins* a line is not a
collapse -- an embedded TOML or JSON fixture is supposed to be indented -- so
escaped `\n` is decoded before the rule is applied.

### ⚠️ The one exemption is written against a property, not a category

`examples/onnx_import_example.rs` prints a comparison table padded with runs of
4 to 27 spaces. **No threshold separates that from a collapse, because the
padding is wider than the folding was.** The exemption tests that the line's
trimmed form begins with `|` -- the property that makes the spaces column
padding -- and not "it is under `examples/`", which is merely where the only
current instance happens to live.

Measured, so the exemption is sized rather than assumed: of the 14 runs it
admits, **14 are on table rows**, and **zero** runs anywhere in the workspace
are admitted for any other reason. Its cost, stated because an exemption without
one is a hole: **a genuine collapse inside a table row is invisible to this
guard.**

## ⚠️ My own census was 27 files short, and only widening caught it

The first scan ran over `src` and `crates` -- **115 files** -- and I was about to
report *"24 runs across the workspace"*. The workspace is **142 files**. The
missing 27 are `build.rs` and `examples/`, and they contained the one case that
**refutes the threshold I had just called "the strictest this corpus supports"**.

A census named after a subject and taken over a subset reads exactly like a
complete one.

## Non-vacuity

| quantity | measured | floor asserted |
|---|---|---|
| files walked | 142 | 110 |
| literals lexed | 5,790 | 4,000 |

The Python prototype that found the original 24 counted **5,790 across 142**
independently. They share an author and a design, so that agreement is a
cross-check on the two implementations, not on the idea.

## Sabotages

Each red on the named test, for the named reason. Every mutation asserts its
occurrence count before applying -- one of these was rejected as a no-op by that
check rather than silently "passing".

| mutation | goes red |
|---|---|
| re-introduce a collapse into `gguf_export.rs` | the corpus test |
| threshold beyond any run | the detector control |
| walk finds no files | the corpus test (floor) |
| lexer recognises no literals | both |
| line counter steps over a newline | the detector control, on its **line** assertion specifically |
| drop the escaped-newline decoding | both |
| drop the table-row exemption | the corpus test, **14** offences |

### ⚠️ The line-counter sabotage is a real regression, not a hypothetical

The Python prototype reported every hit **one line early** in any file containing
a lifetime: the char-literal branch scanned `&'static str` to end-of-line, found
no closing quote, and stepped over the newline. **The numbers stayed plausible.**
It surfaced only by disagreeing with `grep` on a line I already knew.

In the Rust port every advance goes through one `advance_to` that counts
newlines, so the omission is **structurally unavailable** rather than a thing to
remember.

## Verification

```
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features   exit 0
cargo fmt --all --check                                 exit 0
cargo test -p mlmf --lib                                97 passed
cargo test -p mlmf --doc                                29 passed
cargo test -p mlmf-core                                 132 passed, 18 binaries
```

97 and not 99: this branch is off `main`, which does not yet carry #62's two
routing tests.

## Not fixed here -- filed separately

Four test binaries each carry their own `.rs` file walker with **four different
populations**, and `common/mod.rs` -- the module that exists to stop exactly
this -- carries none. One of the four, `write_check_has_no_consumer.rs:59`,
silently `return`s on an unreadable directory: **the defect `empty_tests.rs`
documents having fixed in its own copy.**

This guard adds a fifth walker rather than consolidating blind, because a
consolidation that silently changes a guard's population is the same class of
defect as the one #60 just closed.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

https://claude.ai/code/session_01MdVuiraXRfDHQ227cjBt51

## Summary by Sourcery

Preserve intended string-literal text and add a workspace-wide guard against folded indentation defects.

New Features:
- Add a workspace-wide test that detects unintended interior whitespace folding in Rust string literals while preserving deliberate table alignment and line indentation.

Bug Fixes:
- Correct malformed user-facing and diagnostic messages whose source formatting had been folded into runs of literal spaces.

Enhancements:
- Make literal scanning non-vacuous by validating workspace coverage and the number of literals examined.
- Add detector fixtures covering normal and raw strings, escaped newlines, lifetimes, and deliberate indentation.

Tests:
- Add regression and sabotage coverage to verify the whitespace detector recognizes collapses, reports accurate lines, decodes escaped newlines, and enforces its corpus population.

author: koosie0507
body:
When composing attributes 2 problems exist:

1) while creating a LSTM cell, we need to preserve the order in which the records in a batch were processed. Otherwise, we end up partially learning randomness. This will definitely result in a lower performing matcher. The problem lies in how `nn.utils.rnn.pack_padded_sequence` handles batches when `enforce_sorted=False`. We can't use `enforce_sorted=True`, but we can read the unsorted indexes at the end and rearrange the output in the order of the input.
2) there's contamination across attributes when we append them all to the same state. The original DeepER paper does not state that we should combine state, only attrs. Which means that a simple `torch.stack` is closer to the original text of the paper. 

This PR fixes both and adds a test to ensure we have proper intra-batch ordering at the output of each call to `__compose_attr`.

author: fxlr8
body:
## Summary

Seeds `css/css-break` as a WPT phase, giving css-break-3 conformance a
measured ledger instead of hand-written geometry tests. Purely additive: one
new phase runner, one expectations file, and two matrix entries.

## Why

fulgur's css-break-3 coverage today is a handful of bespoke tests that encode
one engineer's reading of the spec. The WPT corpus is 1,168 tests written
against the spec text by the people who wrote it. Seeding it converts
"conformance work" from *inventing new tests* into *promoting FAIL→PASS in a
file*, which is reviewable, monotonic, and hard to fool.

## Changes

- `crates/fulgur-wpt/tests/wpt_css_break.rs` — phase entry, delegating to the
  existing shared `run_phase` runner. Same shape as `wpt_css_page.rs`.
- `crates/fulgur-wpt/expectations/css-break.txt` — the seeded ledger.
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` and `wpt-nightly.yml` — one matrix entry each.

## Baseline

Measured on this PR's base commit, not inherited from #719:

| | |
|---|--:|
| total | 1168 |
| PASS | 34 |
| FAIL | 971 |
| SKIP | 163 |

The seed as originally written on #719 declared **36 PASS**, because it was
measured against that branch's pagination work. Re-running it against `main`
surfaced two tests that pass there and fail here, so they are recorded as FAIL:

- `break-nested-float-in-table-001-print.html` — page count mismatch: test=1 ref=3
- `flexbox/multi-line-row-flex-fragmentation-080-print.html` — page 1 diff: 12096/138240 pixels exceed tol

Those two are a fair measure of what the walker work on #719 is worth in
conformance terms, and they become the first promotion candidates when it lands.
Recording them as FAIL here keeps this file an honest description of `main`.

## Not a CI gate

The `wpt` job is already `continue-on-error: true` — "WPT reftests are a
reporting channel, not a blocker on PRs." This phase inherits that, so it
cannot turn `main` red; regressions surface via the step summary and the
`target/wpt-report/` artifacts. The runner likewise never panics on a
regression, and skips silently outside the dedicated `wpt` matrix job (where
`FULGUR_WPT_REQUIRED=1` is set), so the `test` matrix, the coverage cell, and
local dev are unaffected.

## Related

Extracted from #719, which is blocked on a larger reconciliation with `main`.
This slice touches only files `main` has not changed, and is independent of
that branch's pagination work.

author: codetrust2025-spec
body:
### call the stages what they mean, and store exactly what they stored

"Failed" was being read as a system failure rather than a rejected candidate,
and "Completed" did not obviously mean the file is closed. Both are relabelled
in the editor's dropdown: fail now reads "Rejected", completed reads
"Closed / Completed".

Labels only. The stored values stay in_progress, completed, fail and dropped,
and that restraint is the point: `fail` and `dropped` are the values
_interview_rows_for_range and find_interview_slot_conflicts already exclude,
and `completed` is what stamps a closure date. Renaming a value means finding
every one of those sites, and a missed one quietly lets a rejected candidate
back into revenue or into a slot-conflict check.

No new stage was added. The four already existed and the dropdown already
offered all four; they had simply never been used, which is why closed and
dropped candidates were still sitting in the pending lists.

Pending Gmail and Pending Works both key on the stored value and both take only
in_progress, so a candidate leaves them the moment any terminal stage is set.
Tested with one candidate in each of the four stages, on both sides.

`v0.3.1` reached npm but was never listed on the registry. npm answers a publish with "Your package is being processed and may take a few minutes to become available", and the version stays 404 on the read API for about a minute. The registry resolves the package before accepting a listing, and the step ran seconds after `npm publish`.

- `.github/workflows/publish-registry.yml` — polls npm for the version, then publishes
- `.github/workflows/release.yml` — registry steps removed

The registry publish is now its own workflow so `workflow_dispatch` can re-run it. Rerunning Release cannot reach those steps: npm rejects a version it already holds.

author: cursor[bot]
body: ## Bug and impact After a WordPress site pairs to Cloud site A, visitor telemetry (Experience Slot impressions, add-to-cart, and `commerce.purchase` with order totals) is stored in `rwgc_cloud_event_queue`. Disconnect does not clear that queue. Pairing to Cloud site B immediately runs `run_maintenance()` → `flush()`, which POSTs the leftover events to `/sites/{site_B}/events/batch`. **Trigger:** pair + traffic on site A → disconnect (or copy a paired database) → pair site B. The first post-pair maintenance tick uploads site A’s anonymous visitor IDs, experience/variant ids, and purchase values into site B’s workspace. Same path as a staging clone of production that re-pairs to a different Cloud workspace. This is outbound leftover-state (not Gate D, and not #59). Disconnect without re-pair still keeps pending events for a same-site reconnect. ## Root cause The durable queue is not site-scoped. `pair()` stored new credentials but never discarded events; `flush()` uploaded whatever was queued to the current `site_id`. ## Fix - Stamp `site_id` on the durable queue when events persist - `discard_unless_site()` on successful pair (keep a queue already stamped for that site; drop foreign or unstamped leftover) - Drop foreign durable items on persist/flush so a credential change cannot POST another workspace’s events ## Validation ``` php tests/test-rwgc-cloud-events.php php tests/test-rwgc-cloud-connector.php php tests/test-rwgc-cloud-security.php php tests/test-rwgc-cloud-health.php php tests/test-rwgc-cloud-migration.php ``` All passed. New coverage: persist stamps `site_id`; disconnect keeps events; same-site reconnect flushes them; re-pair to another site discards the queue and does not POST leftover purchases; flush after a credential swap drops foreign items. Not in this PR: manifest leftover (#59), migration `is_imported()` site_id ignore (admin workflow).

## What changed

Dynamic Island enabled window focus when mouse interaction started. On macOS, Electron also allows a focusable panel to become the main window, which can make it a separate AltTab destination after a click. Keep the island non-focusable and continue to enable mouse events during interaction.

| State | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Mouse enters the island | Mouse events and window focus enabled | Mouse events enabled; window stays non-focusable |
| Mouse leaves, then returns | Window focus disabled, then enabled again | Window stays non-focusable throughout |

Affected surface: desktop main-process window control. Direct keyboard interaction with island buttons is no longer available; keyboard users can use the main OpenBot window. No IPC, renderer, persistence, or dependency changes.

Local smoke check: started a fresh isolated dev profile on macOS 15.3.1 with Electron 44.0.0. Used `bun run dev:automation` against the named worktree instance to inspect the main window and idle island and send an island button click. Stopped only that worktree's stack afterward.

Native AltTab exclusion is **not yet verified**. AltTab 11.6.0 is installed, but the available computer-control tool cannot send global shortcuts. The idle profile also had no pending approvals or questions. Before merge, manually check AltTab after expansion, clicks, collapse, and repeated interaction; approvals and suggested answers; opening the main window; minimized/hidden main-window switching; display reconnection and full-screen spaces. Other macOS versions and native Cmd+Tab remain untested. Mock tests do not prove native switcher behavior.

Model: GPT-6. Harness: Codex, Vitest, repository `dev:automation`, and Computer Use for AltTab inspection.

## Risk and security impact

No change to the renderer-to-main trust boundary, permissions, persistence, or network access. The intentional behavior change is that the island cannot receive keyboard focus. Native switcher and mouse interaction checks above remain required before merge.

## Rapportini — registrazione da admin
Prima solo gli `artigiano` potevano inviare un rapportino. Ora un admin può registrarlo dalla pagina Rapportini (pulsante **Registra rapportino**):
- **per conto di** un operatore con account, oppure di un **esterno senza account** (nome libero → nuova colonna `rapportini_operativi.operatore_nome`, Alembic 0019; le ore finiscono comunque nel registro e nei costi cantiere con `utente_id` NULL)
- **voce o testo** → stessa pipeline IA degli operatori
- **Valida subito** (default ON): crea diario + ore + registro all'istante (helper `_esegui_validazione` condiviso con `/valida`)
- rimosso il codice morto `VistaOperativo`/`FotoInput`/`BannerIstruzioni`

## IA rapportini — pipeline a 2 fasi + verifica ore
- **Fase 1** `_segmenta_cantieri`: quanti cantieri, racconto spezzato per cantiere
- **Fase 2** `_estrai_campi`: estrazione campi per UN cantiere (prompt senza logica multi-cantiere)
- **Fase 3** `_verifica_ore`: seconda passata dedicata che annulla le ore non giustificate da una durata reale (`8:30`→8.3, orari scambiati per durate)
- tutte fail-open, `_estrai_dati` ricompone la struttura legacy (nessun cambio a valle)

## Gantt operatori — ferie per admin/amministrazione
`GET /assegnazioni/operatori` ora include anche i ruoli `admin` e `amministrazione` (come `tipo: utente`), così è possibile segnare ferie/permessi/corsi anche per l'ufficio.

## Test
Backend: Postgres/sqlite usa-e-getta — registrazione esterno+valida subito, per_conto operatore, non-admin ignora i campi, admin per sé, migration 0019 idempotente, pipeline 2 fasi assembla primario+altri_cantieri. Frontend: `npm run build` pulito.

author: marc0olo
body:
Groundwork for #83, and it makes the manual local flow complete instead of dead-ending after payment.

## The https rule was ours, not Stripe's

Checked rather than assumed:

- **The API reference states no scheme requirement** for `success_url`/`cancel_url` — only *"The URL to which Stripe should send customers when payment or setup is complete."*
- **Stripe's own Checkout quickstart uses plain http on localhost:** `YOUR_DOMAIN = http://localhost:4242`, `success_url: ${YOUR_DOMAIN}/success.html`, with *"Go to http://localhost:4242/checkout.html"*.

The mechanism is why: `success_url` is a redirect target for the **buyer's own browser**. Stripe never fetches it server-side. Our reason for the rule — never send a buyer to a plaintext page after paying — holds for a public origin and is vacuous for traffic that never leaves the machine.

## The change

`Session.validateOrigin` accepts http for loopback hosts only: exactly `localhost`, `127.0.0.1`, `[::1]`, or a `.localhost` subdomain. The last matters because a local `icp network` serves the frontend at `http://frontend.local.localhost:<port>`. Everything else still requires https.

⚠️ **The host is parsed, not substring-matched** — that's the whole risk here:

| refused | why it would slip past a substring match |
|---|---|
| `http://localhost.evil.com` | contains "localhost", is not loopback |
| `http://evil.com/localhost` | "localhost" is in the path |
| `http://localhost@evil.com` | loopback-looking userinfo |

Both parsing steps are mutation-verified: replacing the parse with `contains("localhost")` fails the trap test (**in isolation** — the loopback test aborts the file first, so I removed it for the probe), and dropping the port-strip fails the loopback test.

Validation moved from the mixin to `Session.mo` so it's unit-testable without a replica. `OriginError` moved with it and keeps its Candid name — interface unchanged at 805 lines.

## The default

The seed set `https://<frontend-id>.icp0.io` — a mainnet-shaped URL for a canister that exists only locally, so paying dead-ended the browser. It now sets `http://frontend.local.localhost:${GATEWAY_PORT}` (read, not hard-coded — the gateway port changes per start). **Not a chosen domain**; #40/#23 decide the real one.

Two passages documented the dead end as expected behaviour and are corrected: `local-dev-seed.sh`'s closing notes and SANDBOX-TESTPLAN's "looks like a bug" list.

## Verification

- full gate green, 26 steps · candid signatures unchanged at 805 lines
- 6 new unit tests in `test/session.test.mo`, both parsing steps mutation-verified
- deployed and reseeded against the running local network: `stripe_origin` reads back `http://frontend.local.localhost:8000`


## Review fix — the parse missed userinfo when a port was present

⚠️ **`http://localhost:8000@evil.com` was ACCEPTED as loopback http.** A browser reads everything before the last `@` as credentials, so that host is `evil.com` — but `hostOf` stripped the port first, took the text before the first colon, and answered `localhost`. **Four of five userinfo spellings passed**: `localhost:8000@`, `127.0.0.1:80@`, `[::1]:8000@`, and the same with a path. Only the port-less `localhost@evil.com` was refused.

Userinfo is now dropped first, at the **last** `@` (userinfo may contain one). Both halves mutation-verified: removing the strip, and taking the first `@` instead of the last, each fail the trap test.

⚠️ **The test was the more valuable half of the fix.** It held exactly one userinfo case — and it was the single member of the family a port-first parse happens to refuse. A trap table that samples one member and finds it caught reads as coverage of the family. It now asserts all five spellings plus `user@localhost@evil.com`, and the complement: userinfo in front of a genuinely loopback host is still loopback.

Severity as the review stated it: the origin is `requireController`-set, so this was a validation gap rather than a live open redirect — but catching the odd thing a controller types is the check's entire purpose.

**The livemode gating is filed as #143** rather than folded in: `expected_livemode = ?true` with a loopback origin is representable, and the fix is the mutual-refusal pattern from `Config.mo:157` ("unrepresentable rather than discouraged"). It changes two endpoints' error types, so it wants its own PR — with the note that `?false` and `null` must keep working, since `?false` is what the local seed sets.



## Second review fix — the userinfo fix introduced a trap

⚠️ **`set_stripe_origin("http://")` TRAPPED instead of returning its declared `Result`.** `"".split(#char '@')` yields zero elements, so `parts.size() - 1` underflowed on `Nat`. The line it replaced was option-returning (`.next() ?? ""`) and could not underflow — swapping it for an array index is where it came from, in the commit that fixed the previous hole. Guarded, and the whole degenerate family is now tested (`http://`, `https://`, `http:///path`, `https:///`, `http://@`, `http://localhost@`); removing the guard fails that test.

⚠️ **`https://` answered `#ok("https:")`** → `success_url = https:/#/order/<id>`. Pre-existing on `main`, same family, and refused here as **`#noHost`** rather than `#notHttps` — it *is* https, so that reason would be a false explanation for a true refusal.

`validateOrigin` now decides **scheme → host → loopback** in that order, because deciding loopback first made `http://` answer `#notHttps` while `https://` answered `#noHost` for the same defect.

⚠️ **The interface gains one arm** (`OriginError.noHost`), so signatures move by a line — deliberate, on a `requireController` method the frontend never renders.

Same lesson as the userinfo family one layer down: I tested the member I thought of, and the family had five more.

author: pmoust
body:
Two nightly lanes filed their tracking issue from a step inside the job that
does the work, gated on a step-level failure condition, with issues write
granted at workflow level. That has two faults: a job killed by a timeout or a
runner failure files nothing, and every step of the work job, including the
checkout and the compose bring-up, runs with a token that can write issues.
Both now follow the shape fuzz-nightly already uses: the workflow default is
contents read, and the routing lives in its own job that depends on the work
job, runs when that job's result is a failure, and grants issues write to
itself alone.

All three lanes also had a race. The routing lists for an existing issue by
its deterministic title marker and creates one when the list comes back empty,
so two runs failing close together could both read empty and both create. Each
reporting job now carries a concurrency group keyed to its workflow, with
cancellation off so a second report queues behind the first instead of being
dropped, which is the opposite of the usual reason for a concurrency group and
is commented as such.

Every workflow was swept for all three faults. Eight others route no failures
to an issue and are unchanged. Two of them declare no workflow-level
permissions at all, which is a separate least-privilege gap and is reported
rather than fixed here.

No local gate compiles Actions YAML and the executor has no GitHub token, so
the verification here is a YAML parse of all eleven workflows and a mechanical
assertion of each changed file's job names, dependencies, conditions and
permissions against the intent. The lanes are unproven until they run on main;
each will be dispatched by hand after the merge.

Fixes: #1360
Fixes: #1322
Refs: #1313

author: vitbokisch
body:
`<PlotChart yDomain={{ min, max }}>` now lowers to iOS and Android.

It is a `ChartSpec` field the geometry engine already consumes, and its sibling `y2Domain` has lowered as a one-liner since the second axis landed — but `yDomain` sat in `PLOT_UNLOWERED_PROPS`, so a native chart warned and drew an auto-scaled axis instead. A fixed y-range is basic charting with nothing web-specific about it, and the gap reads as an oversight rather than a decision, since the sibling with the identical shape was already there.

## How it was found

By asking which **`ChartSpec` fields** the plot emit warns about, rather than which props exist. Exactly two:

| field | verdict |
| --- | --- |
| `yDomain` | pure geometry the engine already reads — no reason to be unlowered |
| `emphasis` | interaction state; the native host has its own selection path, so it stays warned |

## Position, not just presence

Swift's memberwise init takes arguments in **declaration order**, and `yDomain` is `ChartSpec` field 9 — before `yFormat`, not appended after `progress` where the batch-2 literal props go. The order is read off the generated struct rather than restated, which is the discipline this repo already has a scar for.

```swift
ChartSpec(… showGrid: true, yDomain: Domain(min: 0.0, max: 100.0), progress: pyreonEntrance)
```
```kotlin
ChartSpec(… showGrid = true, yDomain = Domain(min = 0.0, max = 100.0), progress = pyreonEntrance)
```

**Bisect-verified**: reverting the two emit lines and restoring the unlowered entry fails 3 specs — both emit assertions and the no-warning check.

## Two harness errors, caught before they became findings

Worth recording because each looked exactly like a product bug:

1. The first fixture used a String `x` accessor where the host wants Double. **Both toolchains rejected the *fixture* line**, which is indistinguishable from an emit failure until you read the line number.
2. The Kotlin probe's regex did not allow spaces around `=`, so it reported `yDomain` **ABSENT** while the emit was correct. I nearly reported a Kotlin-only bug that did not exist.

## Completeness context

While scoping this I re-checked the campaign's open list against current `main`. Several items were already closed and my notes were stale:

- **error bars to native** — already lower via `PLOT_MARK_ACCESSOR_OPTIONS`
- **`<Histogram>` / `<Scale>` natively** — both in `GRAMMAR_CONFIG_TAGS`
- **`shiftCmds` per-frame cloning** — measured at **9.8 µs/frame** on a 301-command draw list, 0.06% of a frame budget. The inherited "fine at these sizes" was right, and is now measured rather than assumed
- **zero TODO/FIXME** in the charts package

Genuinely still open, all warning by name rather than dropping silently: `MapChart` natively (the geo host reduces GeoJSON topology on the web side — a real port), `emphasis`, and the web host concerns (`locale`, `facet`, `toolbox`, `onSaveImage`, `accessibleTable`, `keyboard`).

## Checks

- `@pyreon/charts` 1156/1156
- `@pyreon/native-compiler` 4552/4552, including the `swiftc` and `kotlinc` compiles of this emit
- `validate-fast` 44/44

Auto-merge not enabled — `gh pr merge` is blocked in my session.

Dev-environment tooling change: **pin the Nix dev shell to Go 1.27** — no application code touched.

## What changed

- `flake.lock`: nixpkgs input `2026-06-29` → `2026-09-08` (unstable head `da39501`). Required because the old lock has no `go_1_27` attribute at all (default `go` was 1.26.4).
- `flake.nix`: `go` → `go_1_27` — **pinned** rather than floating, so future lock refreshes can't silently change the toolchain generation.

## Why 1.27

1. **RUN-155 needs it:** the upcoming `tailscale.com/tsnet` dependency declares `go 1.26.6` in its module directive; the current shell toolchain (1.26.4) can't satisfy it. Design doc flagged this as the one open implementation item (docs/26 §2, §9) — this PR resolves it before implementation starts.
2. **Consistency:** `Dockerfile.supervisor` already builds with `golang:1.27-alpine`; local and image builds now use the same toolchain generation.

## Side effects of the lock bump (intended)

The refresh moves *all* shell tools to current unstable, most notably golangci-lint **2.12.2 → 2.13.2** (itself built with go1.27.1). Everything else shifts minor/patch. If you rely on shell tools the gates don't exercise (gopls, air, sqlc, goose, buf/protoc), that's the human check below.

## Automated verification

Full gate suite green on go1.27.1: `make test && make test-scripts && make test-web && make lint && make lint-web && make vet && make build && shellcheck && shfmt -d && hadolint`.

## Human-check list

- [ ] `direnv reload` (or re-enter `nix develop`): banner shows `Go: go1.27.1`, and your daily flow still feels right — editor/gopls against the new toolchain, `air` hot-reload, `sqlc generate`, `buf`/proto tooling.
- [ ] CI remains green on this PR (CI images are unaffected — they don't use the flake — but the lock bump rides along in the repo).

author: jacobqvisth
body:
## The bug you hit

The duel board showed two duels as **"In the publishing queue"** with a *See it in the queue* link, a stat card reading **"2 in the publishing queue"**, and another reading **"0 live on the channel"**. Both were already live on YouTube, the queue was empty, and the link went nowhere.

One missing write-back caused all four wrong answers. The builder sets `duel_status` to `rendered` and hands the file to the queue. The publishing worker then writes the YouTube id onto the **asset** and its own queue row, and nothing ever told `diagnostic_videos`. So a published duel sat at `rendered` forever.

It hid a second wrong answer: one row's `our_youtube_id` was `425iyYzuRNA` while the asset and queue both said `L6tuiPgv-AY` — a stale id left from a replaced upload.

## The fix, in two places

**The worker** now marks the source row published when it finishes an upload, keyed on the asset. Both boards get updated (they key on the asset under different column names), and each update is a no-op for a video the other board owns. It cannot fail the run: the upload has already happened.

**The duels API** reconciles on load against the asset and the queue. That is how the forum-answer board has always read its publish state, and it is why that board never had this problem. Deriving cannot drift. The reconcile persists what it finds so counts and filters agree.

Verified against prod: 2 corrected on the first call, **0 on the second** (idempotent). Prod data is already correct.

## Also: related articles on the Catalogue

Answering "are these also articles on our website". **They are not.** Videos and articles are separate streams fed by the same thing — real diagnoses — and they overlap by fault code rather than one-to-one. There is no article about "four codes, one harness", and the three P0299 articles are all on different cars from the P0299 video.

So each catalogue row now offers **"Articles on the same code"** where a published article matches, worded as a code match rather than as *the* article for that video. 4 of 12 videos match; the planned "P0300 and the misfire family" picks one up too.

Matched on **title and slug only**. The body quotes other people's codes in passing, and matching it returned articles that merely mention a code.

**Not linked: the fault-code pages.** They are built (1,300+ Astro pages) but every Webflow item in the cluster is still a draft and `wrenchlane.com/en/fault-code/*` 404s today. A board full of 404s is worse than a board with no links.

## Verification

- `tsc --noEmit` clean, `eslint src/` clean (1 pre-existing unrelated warning), 82 tests pass
- `npm run build` passes
- Reconciler run against prod: 2 rows corrected, stale YouTube id replaced, second call a no-op
- Catalogue page rendered authenticated: 5 article links present, correct codes

author: kpostaagasi
body:
Implements a `--take-profit` flag for the `replay()` backtest engine that closes positions early when their recorded ask falls to a target profit level, freeing collateral for new entries.

## Summary

This adds a measurable early-exit rule to the portfolio backtester: when `take_profit` is specified (0..1), any open position whose recorded ask has fallen to `1 - take_profit` of the credit is bought back that day at that ask price. The freed collateral becomes available for new entries the same day. This answers a concrete question about the cost/benefit of taking profits early vs. holding to expiry.

## Key Changes

- **Core backtest logic** (`backtest.py`):
  - Added `take_profit` parameter to `replay()` with validation (0 < x < 1)
  - New `_close_early()` function to record early exits at recorded ask prices
  - Modified settlement flow to check for profit targets before computing free capital
  - Prevents same-day re-entry of closed contracts (paying ask then selling bid is just the spread)
  - Updated `peak_committed()` to use `exit` date instead of `exp` for collateral release timing
  - Changed trade sort order from expiry to resolution (`exit`) order, since cash arrives when positions close

- **Trade record structure**:
  - Renamed `exp` field to `exit` to clarify when cash is actually freed
  - Added `buyback` field (ask price paid) and made `settle` (expiry close) mutually exclusive
  - Both fields cannot be non-None; exactly one is None depending on how the position closed

- **Statistics** (`backtest.py`):
  - Added `early` count to `replay_stats()` (positions closed by profit target)
  - Fixed `assigned` calculation to only count settled positions
  - Changed `deployed` from sum of DTEs to sum of actual days held (matters for early closes)
  - Updated span calculation to use `exit` instead of `exp`

- **CLI and rendering**:
  - Added `--take-profit` argument with bounds checking (0 < x < 1)
  - Conditional header in trade table: `çıkış` (exit) column only appears when book has early closes
  - New `trade_line()` function to format rows with optional exit date and buyback indicator (`↩`)
  - Summary line reports count of early closes vs. held-to-expiry positions

- **Documentation**:
  - Updated README with examples and detailed explanation of the rule
  - Clarified that entry is at recorded bid, exit is at recorded ask
  - Noted that freed collateral funds same-day entries
  - Updated CLAUDE.md invariants to reflect resolution-order semantics

## Implementation Details

- **No free buybacks**: An ask of 0 means no offer on the tape that day—the position stays open. This keeps the backtest honest: every trade is a quote that actually existed.
- **Spread is real**: Entry at bid, exit at ask means the round-turn costs exactly what it should. This is why early exit gives up the spread and remaining time decay in exchange for collateral and tail risk.
- **Cash timing**: Collateral is freed on the `exit` date, not the `exp` date. This affects `peak_committed()` and enables same-day re-entry with the freed cash.
- **Equity curve**: Trades are now sorted by `exit` (resolution order) rather than `exp`, so the P&L sequence reflects when cash actually arrived—critical for drawdown calculations with overlapping positions.

author: shahmir811
body:
## Summary

This branch adds two related mobile-app entry points that didn't exist before: **staff sign-in via an embedded WebView**, and **customer self-signup with admin approval**. Both extend the existing token-based mobile auth pattern (`Api\AuthController`) rather than introducing a new auth mechanism.

## What's included

### 1. Staff Mobile Login (embedded WebView)

Staff (`admin`, `accountant`, `production_manager`, `creative_head`) can now sign into the mobile app through the same portal-token + email form customers use — without any native staff screens being built.

- `users.mobile_login_token` — a permanent per-user token, auto-generated on create (mirrors `customers.portal_token`), backfilled for existing users.
- `Api\AuthController::verify()` now tries `Customer::portal_token` first, then falls back to `User::mobile_login_token`. A staff match returns `{"account_type": "staff", "redirect_url": "..."}` — **no Sanctum bearer token is issued**, since staff never call another `/api/*` endpoint. A customer match now also returns `"account_type": "customer"` for the app to discriminate on.
- `staff_mobile_login_tokens` — a single-use, ~90-second handoff token (SHA-256 hashed at rest, never stored raw) generated for the redirect URL. Config-driven TTL (`STAFF_MOBILE_LOGIN_TOKEN_TTL`, default 90s) and app URL (`WEB_APP_URL`) via the new `config/casualite.php`.
- `MobileLoginController::consume()` (`GET /mobile-login/{token}`) — the WebView's actual landing page. Locks and consumes the token inside one transaction, marks it used *before* any further checks (so it can never be replayed even on a later rejection), verifies the staff account is still active, then starts a real Laravel session and redirects into the dashboard. From there it's just the normal website — existing Spatie role middleware governs what each role sees, with zero new permission logic.
- User management screen reworked to show the admin row with protected actions, plus surfacing each user's mobile login token/link for staff onboarding.

### 2. Customer Self-Signup (mobile app → pending admin approval)

Previously the only way for a customer to exist in the system was for admin/accountant to create the record manually. This adds a self-service path from the mobile app that queues a request for admin review rather than creating a `Customer` directly.

- `customer_signup_requests` table — a parallel table to `customers` (not a status column, since `customers.created_by` is a required FK and `Customer` has no approval concept). Fields: `name`, `contact_number`, `city`, `country`, `address` (optional), unique `email`, `status` (`pending`/`approved`/`rejected`), plus `customer_id`/`reviewed_by`/`reviewed_at` once reviewed.
- `POST /api/auth/signup` (public) — new endpoint on `Api\AuthController`, validated identically to the admin's manual create form (including the fixed `Customer::COUNTRIES` list). Three outcomes:
  - Email already belongs to a customer → `422`
  - A request for that email is already pending → `200`, idempotent (no duplicate row)
  - New or previously-rejected email → `201`, creates/reuses the row, status reset to `pending`
- `PendingSignupController` (admin-only) — new **Pending Signups** screen: a review queue with Approve/Reject actions plus a read-only history of past decisions.
  - **Approve** creates the real `Customer` (with `created_by` set to the approving admin, `portal_token` auto-generated exactly as on manual creation), logs an activity entry, and redirects straight to the customer's page so the admin can copy and share the portal link the same way they already do today.
  - **Reject** leaves no `Customer` behind. A later resubmission of the same email reuses the same row rather than piling up duplicates.
- No auto-login, no push notification, and no status-polling endpoint — approval and sharing the portal link stay a fully manual, deliberate hand-off, matching how every customer gets onboarded today.
- New "Pending Signups" sidebar link (System section, admin only) with a live pending-count badge.

## Testing

- `tests/Feature/Api/AuthTest.php` and `tests/Feature/MobileLoginTest.php` — **23 tests, 75 assertions, all passing**. Covers: staff branch of `verify()` (no bearer token issued, correct redirect shape, hashed-not-raw storage, inactive-user rejection, email mismatch), `consume()` (valid token logs in, reused/expired/unknown tokens rejected, account disabled between issuance and consumption), and signup (new request, duplicate email, already-pending idempotency, resubmit-after-reject, country validation).
- Both suites extend this project's existing hand-built-schema test pattern (`RefreshDatabase` is unsafe here due to MySQL-only raw `ENUM` migrations elsewhere).
- Backend manually verified end-to-end against the live dev server (`curl` + `tinker`) for both flows; test data cleaned up afterward.

## Notes

- The mobile-app (React Native) side of staff login — the embedded WebView and logout interception — is built in the separate `casualite-app` repo but not yet confirmed working on-device (EAS build still being debugged). This repo's backend contract is stable and independent of that.
- The mobile-app signup screen itself is being built separately in `casualite-app` against the `POST /api/auth/signup` contract above.
- `CLAUDE.md`/`AGENTS.md` updated in lockstep (rules 5.33 and 5.34, route tables, migration list, Implementation Status) — verified in sync aside from the intentional "Claude" vs "Codex" header wording.

## E2E journey: login form

Sixth (final) Playwright journey. Unlike the others, this deliberately does **not** seed a session — it drives the real login form, exercising the email+password form, client-side auth token storage, and the route guard that every other journey seeds past.

### Flow (`e2e/tests/login-form.spec.ts`)
- **Happy path:** `/login` → assert the form renders → fill a valid email + password → "Sign in" → assert navigation to `/links` and the authenticated shell (create-link trigger) is present. (Fixtures `/auth/login` returns a session for any credentials, so a valid-shaped email signs in.)
- **Negative:** an invalid email → "Sign in" → assert the user stays on `/login` and never reaches the dashboard (submission blocked by native email validation and/or the zod resolver — asserts the real invariant, no navigation, rather than a specific message layer).

### Not 2FA
A true 2FA-login journey is not yet possible — the login page has no TOTP challenge step. That gap is filed separately as [#377](https://github.com/DhananjayThomble/URL-Shortener-App/issues/377).

author: tuskan
body:
Closes #248.

CI has run benchmarks on every push to main for months and uploaded the numbers as a 90-day artifact. It caught nothing — because **a number in an artifact cannot be wrong**. It faithfully recorded `BenchmarkSwapOptimized_100 ... 149427883656 B/op` — 149 GB per operation — on every merge while #246 was live.

A benchmark-diffing gate would not have caught that one either: the defect was present *at the baseline*, so every run agreed with the one before it. Relative detection finds what you introduce. This was there from the start.

Three changes, in decreasing order of how much they can fail.

## 1. Allocation contracts — these gate

Ordinary untagged unit tests in `coord`, `time` and `atmosphere`. Exact `0` where zero-allocation is a design claim the repo already makes in prose, and a **bound** where a bound is the honest statement:

| path | contract | measured |
| :--- | :--- | ---: |
| cached `Context.ICRSToAltAz` / `GeocentricToObserved` | `== 0` | 0 |
| `ICRSBatchToAltAz` over 512 targets | `== 0` | 0 |
| `Time.TAI/TT/TDB/MJD/JD`, `Sub`, `Equal`, `Add` | `== 0` | 0 |
| `atmosphere` refraction (3 forms), `Airmass`, `AtAltitude` | `== 0` | 0 |
| `coord.NewContext` | `<= 8` | 1 |

`NewContext` gets a bound rather than an equality because zero would be a false claim — it materialises the SOFA astrometry parameters. The risk there isn't that it costs one allocation; it's that it quietly starts costing many, which is how a per-epoch cost becomes a per-target one.

**Why `allocs/op` is safe to gate on and `ns/op` is not.** `allocs/op` is deterministic across machines, and — measured rather than assumed — **unchanged under `-race`**, so these need no build tag and no short-mode skip. Timing on a shared runner is noisy, and a noisy gate gets muted; this repo already had one job failing every run for an unrelated reason, which is exactly how it went unread (#238).

**They are not vacuous.** Injecting a single allocation into `Airmass`, `Context.ICRSToAltAz` and `Time.TT` makes each contract fail, naming the path and the count:

```
allocs_test.go:56: Airmass allocates 1 times per call, want 0.
allocs_test.go:69: ICRSToAltAz allocates 1 times per call, want 0.
allocs_test.go:51: TT allocates 1 times per call, want 0; it is arithmetic over the epoch...
```

Deliberately **not** an alloc contract on the out-of-coverage EOP path: #247 already guards that more precisely by counting `Loader.Cached` calls, and a weaker duplicate would add noise rather than coverage.

## 2. The Benchmarks job now reports a delta

It installs a pinned `benchstat` and posts a comparison against the previous successful run into the **job summary**, where a reader sees it on the run page, instead of into an artifact nobody opens. It still cannot fail a build — that split is the whole point.

Verified end to end against the real API rather than written hopefully: the `gh run list --jq` query returns a run id, `gh run download` retrieves a real artifact, `find previous -name bench.txt -print -quit` locates it inside the `benchmarks-<sha>/` directory, and the pinned `benchstat` produces a table from it. Missing previous run, missing artifact and missing `bench.txt` each report into the summary and exit 0, since expired retention is the ordinary case.

Two corrections come with it:

- The package list read `./... ./coord/... ./plan/... ...`, which *looks* like "just these five" while actually benchmarking the whole module, since `./...` already covers them. Now `./...` alone, with a comment — whole-module is the right scope, since `remote/file`'s ReadAt strategy benchmark is one CLAUDE.md explicitly says not to lose.
- `-count` 3 → 6. With three samples benchstat cannot compute a confidence interval and prints `± ∞` for every row — observed on the real artifact, not assumed. Affordable now that #247 took the worst `plan` benchmark from ~68 s to ~1.5 s.

## 3. CLAUDE.md gains a Performance section

Recording the three-layer split and, importantly, **the two ways to misread a benchmark that both happened during this work**:

- A low `-benchtime` charges a one-time lazy load to every iteration. At `-benchtime=1x`, `BenchmarkUTCToUT1` reported 8.6 ms and 15.6 MB for a conversion that actually costs 67 ns and allocates nothing. The check is to raise the iteration count and confirm the *total* stays proportional; flat total with falling ns/op means a fixed cost.
- A benchmark's epoch is part of its subject. `plan`'s schedulers ran at `time.ZeroTime()` — JD 0, 4713 BC — so 99.88% of their allocated bytes were EOP handling (#246).

Profiling itself stays a **manual, periodic step, not a CI gate** — the same rule the Fuzzing section already sets, for the same reason: a flame graph can't be usefully diffed by a machine, and #246 was found by *reading* `pprof -top` and noticing `io.ReadAll` had no business appearing in a scheduler.

## Verification

Full gate: `gofmt`, `go vet`, `golangci-lint run --build-tags="integration,network,validation"` at 0 issues, `go test ./...`, `go test -race -short -count=1 ./...` — all clean, including the new contracts under the race detector.

The workflow YAML was parsed and its `benchmarks` job inspected programmatically (6 steps, in order) rather than trusted to review.

author: lkdvos
body:
## Summary

Replaces `execute!`'s tile-by-tile driver with a BLIS five-loop (`NC`/`KC`/`MC`) macro-blocking nest with packed-panel reuse, matching classic cache-blocked GEMM implementations. `execute!` beats the prior driver (kept, unexported, as `execute_tilewise!`, its correctness oracle) by 1.66x-10.5x across the measured shape/kernel grid.

- Root-caused and fixed a pre-existing, undiagnosed allocation in `execute!` (a `Union{AffineAxis,ScatterAxis}` value left `QSTile`'s type parameters unresolved, forcing heap allocation and a dynamic `execute_tile!` call).
- New `Blocking`/`default_blocking(kernel)`: tunable `mc`/`kc`/`nc` keywords on `plan_contract`, defaulting to hardcoded constants measured on this repo's reference machine (Cascade Lake) — deliberately not an analytical/cache-probing model (a sibling Rust project tried exactly that and it's a documented refutation there: 14-34% loss even on its own reference machine, and further failures on two other machine classes).
- `test/test_macro_driver.jl`: an independent oracle test suite written blind to the rewrite's implementation, against the frozen `plan_contract`/`Blocking`/`execute!`/`execute_tilewise!` contract.
- Two independent reviews (Fable, Sonnet-High) with all findings triaged and fixed; full disposition and design rationale in `docs/decisions.md`'s "Macro-blocking milestone" section.
- A final cleanup pass condensed the diff for review (comment/LOC reduction, duplicate-loop merges), with no behavior change — allocation invariants and the full test suite re-verified after.

## Test plan

- [x] `Pkg.test()`: 12903/12903 passing (verified independently after each integration step, including after the cleanup pass)
- [x] `execute!` vs `execute_tilewise!` vs a direct dense-matmul/nested-loop oracle agree to tolerance across randomized block-size grids, real `StridedView`s (permuted/sliced/negative-stride/zero-stride), and an irregular-sliver-at-nonzero-offset fixture
- [x] Allocation: `SIMDKernel` through `execute!` is 0 B (Julia >= 1.11), `ScalarKernel` bounded to its documented `zero_accumulator` cost — re-measured, not assumed
- [x] `@code_warntype execute!` shows no `Union`/partially-applied `QSTile` downstream of axis construction
- [ ] CI (Julia lts/1 x ubuntu/macos, FormatCheck) — pending on this PR

This PR adds comprehensive logging to the project

### LogRite coverage

_Two tables, two units. The app's "Log Coverage" figure counts **log statements** against the opportunities the analyzer found; the file table below counts **files**. They differ by construction and neither is wrong._

**Files.** A file counts once here, whether it gained one log or forty.

| Language | In repo | Cannot hold a log | Eligible | Instrumented | Coverage | Nothing to log | Recommended, none placed | Reverted by gate |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Java | 41 | 5 | 36 | 19 of 36 | 52.8% | 17 | 0 | 0 |
| JavaScript | 2 | 0 | 2 | 2 of 2 | 100.0% | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| Go | 1 | 0 | 1 | 0 of 1 | 0.0% | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| **Total** | **44** | **5** | **39** | **21 of 39** | **53.8%** | **17** | **0** | **0** |

_Why those 17 file(s) had nothing to log:_ **ALL_METHODS_FILTERED** 15, **ALREADY_LOGGED** 1, **NO_METHODS_FOUND** 1.

_Of the **22** eligible file(s) the analyzer found something to log in, **21** gained a log — **95.5%**. The Coverage column counts every eligible file, including the 17 with nothing to instrument._

> 1 eligible file(s) are neither instrumented nor recorded as having nothing to log. That is an accounting gap in this report, not something about your code.

**Log statements.** What the analyzer asked for, and what the diff contains.

| Language | Recommended | Placed | Not placed |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Java | 91 | 49 | 42 |
| JavaScript | 22 | 13 | 9 |
| Go | — | — | — |
| **Total** | **113** | **62** | **51** |

_**Recommended** already excludes statements recommended more than once for the same file: only one copy can be placed, so a duplicate is not an opportunity and is not counted as one._

> **51 recommended log(s) were not placed** (Java, JavaScript). Where they were lost, by stage:
> - **28** written, then removed individually by a syntax gate because the file did not parse with them in it
> - **13** skipped before the write with no guard claiming it — the placement walk never visited the line. If this number is large it is the one worth reporting: nothing turned these statements down
> - **8** the scope guard refused the position — a variable the statement reads is not in scope there yet, so placing it would not compile
> - **2** never got an insertion key — the analyzer named a line this pass could not resolve to a legal position in the file
> Files reverted by a syntax gate are counted separately, in the last column.

> **Note —** these languages were found in the repo but produced almost no logs: **Go**. Nothing was reverted by a syntax gate, so either those files declare no instrumentable constructs (a script of top-level commands with no functions, a file of type definitions), or the constructs they do declare were not recognised. The file list is worth a glance.

> **Not verified —** this run could not confirm everything it normally does:
> - 19 file(s) were instrumented but not syntax-verified: their checker type-checks one file at a time and cannot resolve the project's dependencies, so it can neither clear nor convict the injected logs. The project build covers them instead.

author: digitaldedication
body:
Op het TV-bord (RK3566) blijft de kiosk hangen op een grijs scherm met play-knop zodra een video afloopt en de volgende moet starten.

## Oorzaken

1. **Meerdere video's hielden de decoder bezet.** `hydrateAround` zette ook op buur-video's een `src` (met `preload="auto"`), en afgespeelde video's werden alleen gepauzeerd. Het bord heeft één hardware video-decoder; elke video met een `src` claimt die, dus de volgende kon niet meer starten.
2. **Een mislukte `play()` werd nergens afgevangen.** De Promise-rejectie ging verloren, er kwam dus geen `ended`-event en de kiosk stond permanent stil — precies het grijze scherm dat blijft staan.
3. **Geen bewaking**: een video die niet start of halverwege stokt, liet de kiosk stilvallen.

## Wijzigingen (index.html)

- Foto's worden nog steeds vooruit geladen, maar **alleen de zichtbare slide krijgt een video-`src`**; alle andere video's worden losgekoppeld (`removeAttribute('src')` + `load()`) zodat de decoder vrijkomt. `preload` staat nu op `none`.
- `play()` krijgt een retry, daarna een poging zonder geluid, en gaat anders door naar de volgende slide.
- Nieuwe **watchdog** schakelt door als een video niet start of vastloopt, met extra respijt zolang hij nog aan het downloaden is (eerste sync). Een slidetoken voorkomt dat een watchdog van een vorige slide de huidige laat doorspringen.
- Bij "terug naar home" worden alle video's losgekoppeld.

## Tests (Chromium via Playwright)

- Werkende video's: slidevolgorde 0 → 1 → 2 → 3 → 0, video's spelen volledig uit, **max 1 video-`src` tegelijk**, watchdog greep 0× in.
- Kapotte video ertussen: kiosk maakt gewoon rondjes door en de goede video blijft normaal spelen.

Geen nieuwe APK nodig — de app synct `index.html` zelf.

body:
## Description

An export that silently produced nothing (see #143) flowed straight into `import`, which reported "0 users created" and exited 0. Nothing distinguished that from a real migration, so the failure was only noticed much later.

Both import entrypoints now refuse empty input:

- `import` exits 1 when `--csv` has no data rows.
- `importPackage()` throws when every entity CSV in the package is header-only, including the SSO handoff metadata CSVs (`sso/custom_attribute_mappings.csv`, `sso/proxy_routes.csv`), which the plan previously didn't track at all — so a handoff-only package still imports.

`--allow-empty` on both commands (`allowEmpty` on `importPackage()`) opts back into the old no-op, for callers that legitimately run against a possibly-empty file.

Note this is a change in exit-code behavior for anyone scripting around an empty CSV: what used to exit 0 now exits 1 without the new flag.

`--plan` is unaffected — it still reports `Total rows: 0` and returns, since planning an empty file is a reasonable thing to ask for.

author: duqueom
body:
## The gates were never tested

This repository relies on **fifteen gates** to detect its own drift. `grep -rl "import scripts"` over both test trees returns **nothing**. Every control that catches a regression could itself regress, silently — including the eight added this week.

## It already happened, twice

| gate | what narrowed | how it reported |
|---|---|---|
| `check_control_claims.py` | two table rows gained a Jinja `raw` wrapper; the row pattern stopped matching them | `OK — 5 of 36` instead of 38 |
| `check_doc_coherence.py` C8 | matched `N overlays` but not `N overlay renders` | passed, while two documents kept the stale count it exists to catch |

Both are the exact shape those gates hunt: **a control narrower than the surface it guards.**

## The ratchet

The gates announce their scope in their success line — so the narrowing is *measurable*, if anything measures it.

`test_gate_scope_ratchet.py` runs each gate, reads the count it reports, and compares it against a **recorded floor**. A floor is a ratchet at the measured value, exactly like `fail_under` for coverage: it costs nothing today, and makes later shrinkage a failure rather than a smaller number nobody reads.

Growth passes. Shrinkage fails, and lowering a floor becomes a deliberate line in a diff someone reviews.

## Two gates had no scope to ratchet

`check_baselines_expiry` and `check_vendored_runtime_drift` printed a bare verdict. They now report:

```console
[baselines] OK — 27 entr(y/ies) across 3 baseline file(s), none expired or unannotated (as of 2026-09-09).
[vendored-drift] OK — 34 vendored file(s) and 1 vendored director(y/ies) match their canonical originals.
```

**A gate that reports "OK" without saying how much it looked at cannot be told apart from one that looked at nothing.**

## Details that matter

- The count is extracted **per gate**, not as "the first integer in the line" — `check_gitleaks_pin` reports the pinned version `8.30.1`, whose leading 8 is not a scope.
- The gate list is read from the **Makefile**, not retyped here.
- A new gate must declare a floor **or** a stated reason it has none. Otherwise adding one would silently opt it out of the ratchet — narrowing the registry exactly the way the gates narrowed.
- 31 tests, ~12s.

## Verified by removing the control, twice

```console
# 1. reproduce the historical narrowing
$ # revert the row pattern in check_control_claims
::error::AGENTS.md's anti-pattern table has rows up to D-38 but this scan matched only 36.
FAILED test_gate_scope_has_not_shrunk[check_control_claims]

# 2. a gate with NO internal guard of its own — the ratchet acting alone
$ # rglob -> glob in check_payload_test_scope, a plausible refactor slip
[payload-test-scope] OK — 36 payload tests are service-scoped.      ← still exits 0
E  AssertionError: check_payload_test_scope now reports 36 payload tests checked,
   down from a floor of 46. It is still passing — at a smaller size.
```

`make verify` → `✓ every gate green`.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

author: franciscocamellon
body:
> ## Base: `develop` (o `#24` já foi mergeado)
>
> Quando esta fatia foi executada o `#24` estava `OPEN` e o `P0.6` proíbe a crew de mergear, então
> ela foi **empilhada** sobre a branch do `#021`. **O `#24` foi mergeado desde então**
> (`develop` = `a8673c3`) e este PR foi **reapontado para `develop`**.
>
> Os commits que ele acrescenta são exatamente os do `#022` — **27 arquivos**, nenhum do `#021`.
> O registro de como a fatia foi produzida está na §0 do laudo.

## O que esta fatia faz

- **`D5` reaberto, fechado.** `Projeto sem título — QGIS [iman-distro]` → **`Projeto sem título -
  IMAN Terra`**. A âncora era `QGIS(\s*)$`; o QGIS pendura `" [<perfil>]"` quando há mais de um
  perfil, e a regex nunca casava.
- **O `A05` que deixou isso passar foi reescrito** para asserir **por região** — e agora reprova,
  provado nos dois sentidos.
- **Raio 2px em tudo**, **barra de menus densa**, e uma **guarda estática** que reprova o build
  (`exit 7`) se qualquer um dos dois sair do arbitrado.
- **Procedência do splash corrigida** — o documento dizia `IMAN.cdr`, e não é.

Laudo completo: `docs/verify/022-titulo-raio-densidade/README.md`.

---

## Critérios do briefing `#022`

- [x] **Entrega 1 · título** — sufixo vira `IMAN Terra` com `[perfil]` depois; o colchete sai; o
      separador é hífen; o nome do projeto continua vindo do QGIS; não realimenta (três travas,
      declaradas abaixo).
- [x] **Entrega 1 · os 7 títulos** — levantados, lista crua publicada: **7 janelas de topo, `0` com
      o sufixo do QGIS** além da principal. `iface.mainWindow()` basta; **não há fatia própria a
      abrir**.
- [x] **Entrega 1 · `A05` reescrito** — critério (a)…(g), quatro estados, com as duas ressalvas
      implementadas literalmente.
- [x] **Entrega 1 · os dois testes do oráculo** — adulteração inversa **e** falso positivo.
- [x] **Entrega 2 · raio** — as 12 declarações em `2px`. **+2 declarados** (ver abaixo).
- [x] **Entrega 3 · densidade** — `QMenuBar::item` `3px 4px`; cerca por seletor respeitada.
- [x] **Entrega 4 · guarda estática** — 5 asserções, no `build.ps1` como `exit 7`, com as duas
      demonstrações de que reprova.
- [x] **Entrega 5 · procedência** — corrigida nos quatro lugares que a afirmavam, com hash
      recalculado nesta bancada.
- [x] **Cerca zero** — a arte não foi tocada, e nenhuma asserção reprova por `v1.0` ou `CAUCAIA`.

---

## Entrega 1 — o título

**Antes → depois**, mesma janela maximizada:

```
ANTES   Projeto sem título — QGIS [iman-distro]
DEPOIS  Projeto sem título - IMAN Terra
```

**Não realimenta**, por três travas independentes: (1) a **forma da regex** — depois da troca o
título termina em `IMAN Terra` e a regex exige `QGIS` no fim, então a segunda passada devolve a
mesma string (verificado em 11 casos, todos idempotentes); (2) `_retitula` só chama
`setWindowTitle` **quando o valor muda**; (3) o guarda `_retitulando` continua no lugar.

### Os 7 títulos — a pergunta que não estava medida

| classe | é a principal? | tem sufixo do QGIS? | título |
|---|---|---|---|
| `QgisApp` | **sim** | **não** | `Caucaia — Setor 3 (QGIS) - IMAN Terra` |
| `QDialog` | não | não | `Configurações de aderência do projeto` |
| `QgsPluginManager` | não | não | `Complementos \| Tudo (0)` |
| `QgsMeasureDialog` | não | não | `Medir` |
| `QgsGpsToolBar` | não | não | `Barra de Ferramenta GPS` |
| `MetaSearchDialog` | não | não | `Metabusca` |
| `QgsCredentialDialog` | não | não | `Entre com as credenciais` |

O `"IMAN Terra — Boas-vindas (powered by QGIS) — QGIS [iman-distro]"` da evidência do `#24` **não
era uma sétima janela**: era a **mesma** `QgisApp` com o demo aberto, cujo *título de projeto*
começa com "IMAN Terra". **O gancho basta.**

### O `A05` por região — os quatro estados + o controle

| estado | título | (a) | (b) | (c) | (d) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| sem projeto (pouso) | `Projeto sem título - IMAN Terra` | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
| projeto aberto | `spike017-projeto-alfa - IMAN Terra` | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
| projeto novo | `Projeto sem título - IMAN Terra` | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
| modificado sem salvar | `*Projeto sem título - IMAN Terra` | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
| **CONTROLE — nome hostil** | `Caucaia — Setor 3 (QGIS) - IMAN Terra` | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |

As duas ressalvas, literais: **`powered by QGIS` é removida do texto antes** da busca de (b) —
nenhuma asserção reprova o produto por exibir o crédito que a licença exige; e **(b)(c)(d) rodam só
no sufixo** — o prefixo é o nome do arquivo do usuário.

### Os dois testes do oráculo

```
  referencia: 14 assercoes, 0 FAIL
  D1  -> A01 voltou a FAIL, e so ela
  D5  -> A05 voltou a FAIL, e so ela
  D8  -> A08 voltou a FAIL, e so ela
  3 de 3 reversoes acenderam a assercao certa, e so ela.
```

Com a âncora `$` devolvida, os **cinco** estados reprovam e **os quatro critérios acendem** —
`Projeto sem título — QGIS [iman-distro]` em todos. E o **falso positivo**: um projeto chamado
literalmente `Caucaia — Setor 3 (QGIS)` mantém o `A05` em `PASS`.

### ⚠ O harness precisou de DOIS perfis, e isso é o fecho do buraco

Na primeira execução do oráculo, com **um** perfil, a reversão saía `Projeto sem título — IMAN
Terra`: o `A05` acendia por **(a)** e **(d)** — o separador — e **nunca** por (c), porque o colchete
nem chegava a existir. A asserção reprovava por um **proxy** do defeito.

O QGIS só pendura `" [<perfil>]"` com mais de um perfil. A raiz do **produto** tem dois na bancada;
a do **teste** tinha um. **O teste era mais estreito que o produto, e a diferença era exatamente o
defeito** — a mesma causa que deixou o `A05` cego desde o `#017`. O orquestrador passou a montar um
perfil-vizinho vazio, que existe só para o QGIS **contar** mais de um.

---

## Entregas 2 e 3 — raio e densidade

**Raio:** as 12 declarações de `border-radius` (5, 6, 7, 8 px) → **`2px`**.

> **⚠ Extensão declarada — 2 a mais que a enumeração.** `QTabBar::tab` usa
> `border-top-left-radius` / `border-top-right-radius` (8px), que a contagem de `border-radius`
> **não alcança** — nomes de propriedade diferentes. Deixá-los em 8px poria **uma aba arredondada ao
> lado de um botão de 2px**. Foram para `2px`; são **uma linha** para reverter, e a guarda os assere
> **em separado** (asserção 5) para a decisão ficar visível.

**Densidade — medida, não impressa** (`QMenuBar::item`: `6px 12px` → `3px 4px`):

| | antes | depois | |
|---|---|---|---|
| folga média por item | **24,5 px** | **8,5 px** | −16 px |
| largura ocupada pela barra | **1002 px** | **794 px** | **−208 px (−20,8 %)** |

O sponsor estimou "~24px entre rótulos, com 4px cai para ~8px". É exatamente isso.

**Cerca por seletor, respeitada:** `QStatusBar` e `QDockWidget::title` **não tocados**;
`QMenu::item` fora de escopo. Nenhum outro `padding`/`margin`/`spacing`/`min-*` mudou.

---

## Entrega 4 — a guarda estática

```
  [1] border-radius : 12 declaracoes, 0 fora de 2px
  [2] QMenuBar::item : padding '3px 4px'
  [3] QStatusBar     : 0 declaracao(oes) de padding
  [4] QDockWidget::title : 0 declaracao(oes) de padding vertical
  [5] cantos da aba  : 2 declaracoes, 0 fora de 2px
  5 de 5 asse rcoes passaram.
```

As asserções **3 e 4** transformam a cerca de prosa em guarda: reprovam a **regressão do `D2` e do
`D4`** sem subir o QGIS.

**Prova de que reprova**, com arquivo e linha:

```
CASO A - um raio de volta a 6px
  style.qss:132  [1] border-radius: 6px  (esperado 2px)      exit=1
CASO B - padding de volta no QStatusBar
  style.qss:65   [3] QStatusBar voltou a ter padding (D2)    exit=1
```

**E o build inteiro reprova junto:**

```
  BUILD RECUSADO: a guarda estatica do tema REPROVOU
    Teste : tools\test-tema-qss.ps1   (exit 1)
EXIT DO BUILD: 7
```

*(A guarda de árvore suja, `exit 3`, vem antes e impede o teste com a árvore só editada — que é o
comportamento certo. A demonstração foi feita com a regressão **

author: lukaskorba
body:
Implements [MOB-1786](https://linear.app/zodl/issue/MOB-1786/seed-backup-prompt-should-take-priority-over-migration-and-error-state).

Three users lost funds because they never backed up their recovery phrase. The backup prompt sat at rung 6 — the bottom half of the ladder — so whenever migration or an error state held the banner slot, the prompt was not merely outranked: the walk short-circuits at the first match, so it was **never asked**.

### Stacked on #2107

Based on `MOB-1889-under-300` ([#2107](https://github.com/zodl-inc/zodl-ios/pull/2107)), so this PR shows only its own commit. It retargets to `main` automatically once #2107 merges.

### What changed

Both orderings had to move together, because the ladder decides the *initial* seat by walk position and *displacement* by rank — changing one leaves the other wrong:

- The rung is asked **first**, immediately after the account guard it already depended on, as `.evaluatePriorityWalletBackup`.
- It seats at **rank -1**, above everything including a lost connection.

`rawValue` deliberately stays 6, so the `next()` walk-down helper and its existing tests are untouched. Rung 6 remains as a pass-through, keeping the rest of the chain and its tests intact.

### What did not change

The gates are exactly as they were. A brand-new wallet cannot spend, so any transaction at all is a receive — which is why `transactions.isEmpty` is the right "has received funds" test, and why spending back down to zero must not retract the prompt. `hasUserPassedPhraseBackupTest` lives in the keychain and ends the prompt for good once the user has backed up.

The user's own **"Remind me later" is still honoured**. This ticket reorders; it does not override a choice the user made. Reminder cadence belongs to PRO-276.

### How the migration banner actually reaches production — and why it matters here

`featureFlags.migration` is `false` in every mainnet flavour and gates only the ladder's **pull** rung (`.evaluatePriorityMigration`), the foreground check, and the `.upToDate` recheck. In production the migration banner arrives by **push**: `.onAppear` arms `migrationStateStreamEffect` (no flag), the manager's state/snapshot events funnel through `.migrationStateChanged` / `.migrationReevaluationRequested` into `bannerVariant` (no flag), and `.migrationVariantUpdated` seats `priorityMigration` (no flag). The only gate on that path is inside the manager — `isIronwoodActivated()` plus funds to migrate.

So a displacement test that re-runs the ladder is not sufficient on its own. This PR also proves the **hold** direction against the production path: with backup seated, a pushed `.required` variant still fires `triggerPriority(.priorityMigration)`, and the rank guard in `.openBannerRequest` (1.5 ≥ -1) is what rejects it — `aPushedMigrationVariantCannotDisplaceASeatedWalletBackup`.

### Review-round fix: the first-receive hook (rung 6)

Field-caught by Lukas while testing this PR: a new wallet that received 1 TAZ to its transparent address got the **shielding** banner, never backup. Cause: `RootTransactions` re-enters the ladder at `.evaluatePriority6` whenever the transactions array changes — that hook is how a *new* wallet gets the prompt at all, since at init-done the head rung walked past an empty history. The first cut of this PR made rung 6 a pass-through to rung 7, so the hook landed on the shielding rung instead.

Fixed by extracting the backup decision into `walletBackupClaimsSlot(state:)`, used by both the head rung (declines continue at rung 2) and rung 6 (declines continue at rung 7, exactly as before). Rank -1 wins wherever it is asked, so a seated shielding offer is displaced. Pinned by `theFirstReceiveReasksBackupAtRungSixAndDisplacesShielding`, the empty-slot variant, and a nothing-owed walk-on test; the existing rung-6 test in the residual suite is unaffected.

### This supersedes two approved rulings

Both were pinned by tests that failed on the rank change. They have been flipped with the new reasoning recorded in the file's own convention, not quietly adjusted:

- **MOB-1749's residual dust at 1.75** (approved 2026-08-25) no longer outranks backup. It keeps 1.75 and still outranks shielding, Tor and currency conversion — `residualDisplacesTheInformationalBannersBelowIt` keeps that coverage, now against currency conversion instead of backup.
- **MOB-1853's terminal-stall Retry at 0.75** now yields to an unbacked seed holding funds. During a terminal stall the Retry is displaced until the user backs up or dismisses.

Neither moves relative to the other; only backup moves. Flagging both explicitly for @michal-fousek, since they were deliberate calls.

### Testing

Full suite green with the 5 pre-existing known issues unchanged. The existing suite was run *before* any test was touched, so the code identified what the reorder broke rather than the expectations being adjusted to fit — exactly two tests failed, both predicted.

New `SmartBannerWalletBackupPriorityTests` covers rank against every other rung, `rawValue` staying put, the ladder asking backup first, displacement of a seated migration banner and a seated stalled banner, the pushed-variant hold above, and the gates that must still hold — no transactions, and no account holding the ladder before backup is asked.

author: jkhartshorne
body:
POL-028 (revised) puts variant readings in both tiers, and the standard tier is machine-owned (POL-002) — so its variants must be derived from the original's. Before this, standardize.py had no concept of a variant: every operation used find("FORM[@kindOf='standard']"), the first match, so a variant was neither produced nor transliterated nor cleaned.

create_standard gains _sync_standard_variants (one standard variant per original variant, surplus removed); apply_standard, remove_null_units and apply_c012 iterate findall instead of find. The standard base now inserts after the last original-tier FORM so tiers stay grouped — for a node with one original FORM, which is every node in every unmigrated corpus, that is index 1, exactly where it went before.

Inert for existing data, verified not argued: running main's standardize.py and this one over the same input gives byte-identical output for WakelinTexts, UtrechtManuscriptWordList, Latham-1862, Huteson-Rukai-Survey and SEALS33. The deprecated kindOf="alternate" spelling is deliberately untouched — it names no tier, so standardize cannot know what to derive from it; that is the next PR.

4 new tests; 47 pass.
