author: eth3rnit3
body:
## Problem

`create_otel_span` creates root observations with:

```ruby
else
  # Create root span
  otel_tracer.start_span(name, start_timestamp: start_time)
end
```

`Tracer#start_span` implicitly parents the new span to `OpenTelemetry::Context.current`. That context is **process-wide and provider-agnostic** — it is not scoped to the `TracerProvider` the tracer came from. So this branch only produces an actual root span when nothing else is currently active.

In a host application that runs its own OpenTelemetry instrumentation (Rack, ActiveJob, Sidekiq…) on a separate provider — a very common setup — a root observation started inside an instrumented request or job silently becomes a **child of that ambient span**.

The consequence is only visible on the Langfuse side: Langfuse ingests the child, whose `trace_id` belongs to a root span that was exported to the application's own backend and never reaches Langfuse. The UI then renders an empty, unnamed trace wrapping the real observation. Grouping or filtering by trace name becomes unusable, since a large share of traces have no name at all.

This is distinct from the isolated tracer provider introduced in 0.8.0 (#77): that change isolates which spans are **exported** to Langfuse (and it works — thank you for it). This issue is about which span a new span is **parented to**, which context propagation decides independently of the provider.

## Fix

Reset to `OpenTelemetry::Context::ROOT` for the duration of the root span creation only:

```ruby
OpenTelemetry::Context.with_current(OpenTelemetry::Context::ROOT) do
  otel_tracer.start_span(name, start_timestamp: start_time)
end
```

Nesting is deliberately unaffected: once the span is started it becomes current again, so child observations keep attaching to it, and the caller's ambient context is restored on the way out. The child branch is untouched.

## Tests

Three specs under `.start_observation`, covering the fix and the two properties a naive fix would break:

- a root observation gets its own trace, not the ambient one (**fails on `main`**, passes with the change);
- child observations still nest under the root;
- the caller's ambient context is restored afterwards.

`bundle exec rspec spec/langfuse_spec.rb` → 100 examples, 0 failures. `rubocop` clean on both changed files.

Happy to adjust naming, comment length or spec placement to your preferences.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes core root-span parenting in mixed OpenTelemetry setups; incorrect detection of “foreign” vs Langfuse ambient spans could mis-nest traces, though the scope check and new specs narrow the blast radius.
> 
> **Overview**
> Fixes root Langfuse observations being **parented to the host app’s unrelated OpenTelemetry span** when Rack/ActiveJob/Sidekiq (or another provider) already has `Context.current` set. Those roots showed up in Langfuse as orphan children under **empty, unnamed traces**.
> 
> Root span creation in `create_otel_span` now **temporarily clears only the active span** (invalid span in context) before `start_span`, so a new trace_id is generated without wiping `propagate_attributes` context values. If the ambient span is **Langfuse’s own** (`ambient_langfuse_span?` via tracer instrumentation scope), behavior is unchanged so nested `observe` / `start_observation` calls still attach.
> 
> Adds specs for a foreign ambient span: own trace_id, nested children, restored caller context, nested Langfuse observations, and propagated `user.id` / `session.id`.
>

author: therealbithive
body:
## What changed

A screenshot pasted into the editor is inserted with no dimensions, so the image extension stores its 500x500 defaults with the node. The read-only renderer turned those into a bare `aspect-ratio: 500 / 500`, which overrides the image's own proportions once it has loaded, so every wide screenshot was squashed into a square in posts, comments, changelog entries and the widget. The editor never showed it, because it only sets a maximum width.

The renderer now writes `aspect-ratio: auto W / H`: the stored box is reserved until the image has loaded, then the image's own proportions win. Existing content is fixed without a migration, because the correction is in rendering.

## Verification

Headless Chromium, a 1000x250 image stored as 500x500, real serializer output through DOMPurify with the reader's configuration:

| markup | rendered |
|---|---|
| before, `aspect-ratio: 500 / 500` | 500x500 |
| after, `aspect-ratio: auto 500 / 500` | 500x125 |

- `content-html.test.ts` states the reader's promises about image dimensions as V1-V6, with a fast-check property over width and height up to the extension's maximum. Its first run failed at `[1, 4097]`: the reader trusts stored dimensions only up to 4096 px (`safePositiveInt`), a pre-existing bound that is now stated as V4 rather than excluded from the generator. The property keeps one unguarded assertion across both branches: never a ratio without `auto`.
- Coverage of the touched lines: 100 % (the one executable line changed ran 243 times; the rest are comments).
- Stryker over `content-html.ts` with the suites that reach it: on the image branch 21 killed, 8 survived before this PR's extra tests; both changed lines are killed; three survivors on the branch are killed by two added tests, each verified by hand mutation; the remaining five are equivalent (optional chaining behind the `src` check, ternaries with identical results). Whole file: 117 killed, 47 survived, 159 no coverage. The file is not in the mutation manifest and this PR does not add it, for the reasons in SELF-IMPROVE.md ("all-or-nothing per file").
- typecheck, oxlint, prettier: green.

## What this does not fix

The stored 500x500 defaults are still wrong data. In the browser that is now only a short layout shift while the image loads. Mail clients honour `width`/`height` attributes literally, so a changelog or conversation notification email can still show a squashed image. The fix for that is to read the real dimensions at insertion time, at the four insertion points in `rich-text-editor.tsx`.

Also bumps the SELF-IMPROVE counter on "the coverage and mutation gates read HEAD, not the working tree" to 2x.

author: kjgbot
body:
A local agent followed by more than 30 seconds of deterministic work fails with `journal client: closed by caller`. `step.complete` drives downstream steps before replying, but used the 30-second request timeout; the launcher also queued status reads on that same connection and hid the original worker error when closing it.

Give the worker its own connection, apply run-lifecycle timeout semantics to `step.complete`, drain its acknowledgement before publishing success, and retain the worker error on failure. The fix is independent of #249; the same failure was reproduced before and after integrating that PR temporarily for testing.

Validation and full captured commands/output are in [the evidence report](https://github.com/AgentWorkforce/flows/blob/4361ef6f946ab565ad78fbe32f6ead8dffd98473/docs/journal-close-0909-evidence.md). The real-daemon agent → 35-second verification → report reproducer exits 0 and exports a successful journal. Reverting either fix reproduces the corresponding timeout; restoring the exact bytes passes. Final standalone checks: SDK build and test typecheck, 18 SDK tests, and six launcher tests. Protocol rejection, disconnect, explicit close, journal pagination, and failed-command behavior are covered.

The exact checked-in `workflows/drive-local.yaml` still refuses at selection because its F8b change is already applied; its exit-1 transcript is included. This PR does not claim a completed live Claude drive tick. No kernel changes, gate changes, or #249 implementation changes are included.

body:
## Problem
The `site departures` table printed only the real-time `expected` time, and `State=EXPECTED` was easy to misread as "on time". `EXPECTED` is a data-state — it only means a live forecast exists for that vehicle. A departure running minutes late is also `EXPECTED`; its forecast time simply slides later. Nothing in the output related the forecast to the timetable, so lateness was invisible in the board.

## Changes
- **`Delay` column** in `site departures` output: `expected - scheduled`, rendered as `+4m` (late), `0m` (on time or early, sub-minute jitter tolerated), or `n/a` (no comparable pair). Computed from fields already in the API response — no extra requests.
- **Docs** (`references/api.md`, `SKILL.md`): `state` describes the data source, not punctuality; documents the `Delay` column and the odd-seconds-vs-round-minute distinction (fresh forecast vs timetable time).
- **Tests** for the delay formatting (full suite passes, 21 tests).

## Example

Line   Destination            Expected/Scheduled          Delay  State
--------------------------------------------------------------------
10     Town Centre            4 min (2026-01-01T12:04:00)   +4m  EXPECTED
10     Town Centre            16:00 (2026-01-01T16:00:00)   0m   EXPECTED

## Notes
- No version bump — left to the maintainer (observed that the `v3.7.0` tag already points at current master while `_meta.json` still reads 3.6.0).

author: cascapera
body:
Item 4 of the UI survey, entry (a) — opened by the PR-213 lesson review.

`htf_offset` is nullable and its `null` is not a setting: the semantics refuse it wherever `htf` is named. **Four controls decided whether to offer `off` by reading `nullable` on its own, and three of them got it wrong.**

| Control | What it did | Cost |
|---|---|---|
| The grid's axis hint | said `or off for none` | a line the API refuses |
| The grid's `off` button | offered it | one click, 422, the whole study fails |
| The builder's caption | said `empty = off` | since the clock shipped in #208 |
| The builder's `off` option | correct, by luck | no nullable enum declares the key yet |

## Where the rule goes

The model publishes the other half of the rule where the rule already lives: `json_schema_extra={"requiredWith": "htf"}`. It travels through the generated JSON Schema into `SchemaParam`, and `offIsASetting` answers the question once for all four controls.

Read off the **outer** node, because Pydantic emits `float | None` as an `anyOf` and hangs the field's own keywords beside it. A reader looking inside the branch finds nothing and reports nothing — no error, no key, every form back to where it started.

The alternatives, for the record: a hand-written list in `axes.ts`, which is the one thing that file exists to avoid; or repeating the semantics in TypeScript, which is the DSL invariant broken on purpose.

## The keyword is held to the rule

A parametrized test in `test_semantic.py` walks the setup union and, for every field publishing `requiredWith: X`, proves both directions — a document naming X with the field null must be refused, one with X absent must pass. Relaxing the rule without touching the key now fails a named test. That is exactly the drift the #213 review found sitting in an ADR.

## `params.test.ts`, and why it had to exist

The tests over the real schema prove the fact is *transported*. They do not prove it *decides*. Measured: rewriting `offIsASetting` as `nullable && name !== 'htf_offset'` left all 878 tests in the repository green. A hand-made node called `whatever` is what tells those apart, and it also reaches the enum branch, which no parameter in the DSL exercises yet.

Found by the lesson review, along with the fourth control and a caption that was false in half the states of the builder — `required with htf` is not true while `htf` is empty, so it now reads `empty only if htf is`.

One change is deliberately unseparated: the builder's `off` option on a nullable enum. `htf` is the only one and nothing is required with it, so no test can tell the two readings apart today. Kept for the failure mode, said out loud at the line.

## Scope

⚠️ **This does not close item 4.** `requiredWith` is a fact about one parameter; `htf` having to be coarser than the document's own timeframe is a relation between two, and no static fact expresses it. The backlog carries the candidate — a dry-run endpoint that expands and validates every point and returns *all* the refusals, with the warning that it must not reuse `points_for`: that one decides and fails closed on the first bad point, this one reports and has to keep going.

## Green

engine 1213, schema 79 ts / 77 py, api 371 (no integration), web 807, mypy strict, ruff, eslint, tsc, build. Mutants: the name-decision and the enum branch both die on named tests.

body:
接在 #17 之後（base 是 `fix/thinking-cue-variety`）。

## 問題

語音路徑的 prompt 和它實際擁有的工具**對不上**，而真正撐起人格的那幾塊反而一個都沒掛。

語音走 `answerInstructions()` 的 `streamReply` 分支，裡面有 `SERVER_MEMORY_INSTRUCTIONS`（叫她呼叫 `manage_server_memory`）——但語音路徑呼叫 `registerChatbotMcpSession()` 時只傳了 `resolveContext` 一個 handler，而 `mcp.ts` 裡的工具全部是靠 handler 有沒有傳來決定註冊與否。所以那個工具**根本不存在**，指令只是在浪費 token 並鼓勵她說謊。

同時 `chineseStyle`、`banter`、`scenarios` 和 `voice_anchor` 全部被跳過，等於 #7 到 #11 的人格工作在語音裡完全沒生效。

## 改了什麼

- **拔掉 `SERVER_MEMORY_INSTRUCTIONS`**（工具不存在）
- **拔掉 `NTHU_CAMPUS_INSTRUCTIONS`，並且不再為語音掛載校園 MCP**（`codex.ts` 的 `nthuCampusMcp` 加上 `!job.streamReply`）。校園工具在語音裡技術上是掛得到的，但語音只該留必要的工具。
- **新增 `BUILTIN_VOICE_TONE_INSTRUCTIONS`**：說明日文怎麼承載傲嬌——重點在**語尾**（わよ、じゃない、でしょ、んだけど、なさいよ）而不是加字。給的是範圍不是腳本（「はあ？」「べつに」「知らないけど」…），並且照 #9 的教訓明講「每次都要換開頭，重複同一句是最像機器的一件事」。可用 **`prompts-local/voice.md` 覆寫，改語氣不用重建**。
- **語音也加 `voice_anchor`**。原本那段寫的是「Her everyday Chinese, her punctuation」，對語音是錯的，所以另寫 `SPOKEN_VOICE_ANCHOR`，同樣刻意不提任何安全相關詞彙。

## 字元帳

| | 字元 |
|---|---|
| 拔掉 `SERVER_MEMORY_INSTRUCTIONS` | −325 |
| 拔掉 `NTHU_CAMPUS_INSTRUCTIONS` | −360 |
| 加入語氣區塊 | +846 |
| 加入 spoken anchor | +約 300 |
| **淨增** | **約 +460** |

換掉的是叫她用不存在工具的指令，換來的是真正影響語氣的東西。延遲影響可以忽略（約 140 token）。

## 驗證

- 418 pass / 0 fail，`tsc --noEmit` 乾淨
- 測試新增：語音 prompt 必須含 `sentence-final particles`、不得含 `manage_server_memory` 或 `nthusa tools`
- `prompt-plan.test.ts` 原本斷言語音**沒有**錨點，改成斷言它有 spoken 版本且不含中文那段

author: ctrl-maud
body:
Adds `core/NaturalLanguage/SlashYear-Historical-Events.yml`.

**What it is:** 86,902 dated historical event records spanning 3,078 years, from roughly 3000 BCE to the present. Every record is a single sentence quoted verbatim from a specific English Wikipedia revision, carrying that revision id, the article title and the section anchor — so a claim built on a row stays checkable against its source. Rows are tagged with year, day, subject, century, decade and theme.

**Why it is not just Wikipedia:** Wikipedia publishes prose per article. This publishes the rows underneath it, normalised into one schema with provenance attached, plus aggregates no single article holds — 366 calendar-day pages, 4,868 subject timelines, cross-century groupings.

**Direct download, no login, no purchase:**

```
https://slashyear.com/dump/events.ndjson.gz
https://slashyear.com/dump/years.ndjson.gz
https://slashyear.com/dump/entities.ndjson.gz
https://slashyear.com/dump/datapackage.json      # Frictionless descriptor
https://slashyear.com/api/openapi.json           # OpenAPI 3 for the JSON API
```

**Homepage points at the repository, per CONTRIBUTING item 2:** https://github.com/ctrl-maud/slashyear — the whole extraction pipeline, the schema, and the gates that verify every published sentence against the revision it cites. `scripts/bootstrap.sh` + `scripts/reproduce.sh` rebuild the corpus from a released snapshot and re-run those gates.

**Licence:** rows CC BY-SA 4.0 (inherited from Wikipedia), code Apache-2.0.

author: carlotestor
body:
## Summary

Minimal fix for #30344. `toArray` returned the **live** `IList<object>` reference for any non-`List<object>` input, so when the input was a WS cache (`ArrayCacheBySymbolById → ArrayCache → BaseCache → SlimConcurrentList<object>`), `filterBySinceLimit` read `getArrayLength` and then each `getValue(parsedArray, i)` under **separate** lock acquisitions. A trim by the receive thread between the length read and a later indexed read invalidated the index and threw `ArgumentOutOfRangeException` from `SlimConcurrentList<T>.get_Item`.

`SlimConcurrentList<T>` already exposes an atomic snapshot that takes the read lock once for both the length and the copy (`SlimConcurrentList.cs:161-174`), so live caches are routed through it. The hot `List<object>` REST path is untouched and stays allocation-free.

This is the same idiom `arraySlice` already uses for this exact hazard, comment included (`Exchange.cs:884-888`):

```csharp
// we need to make sure our implementation of ToArray is called, otherwise
// it will call the default one that is not thread-safe
```

### Note on the alternative fix

The issue also suggested re-enabling the commented-out `((IList<object>)a).ToList()`. That does **not** fix the race and makes the failure mode worse: `Enumerable.ToList()` on an `ICollection<T>` does not enumerate — it reads `Count`, allocates, then calls `CopyTo`, which is the same two-acquisition window (`GetEnumerator`, the only single-lock snapshotting member, is never called). When the cache shrinks in between, the tail stays `null`, those nulls fail the `value != null` guard in `filterBySinceLimit` and the entries are **silently dropped** instead of throwing. Measured over 6s of contention: 196,965 silently-dropped entries with `.ToList()` vs 0 with `.ToArray()`.

## Verification

A/B against the same harness driving the real `filterBySinceLimit` over a live `ArrayCacheBySymbolById` (3 writer threads + 3 reader threads, 8 cores):

| build | successful reads | `ArgumentOutOfRangeException` | null entries |
|---|---|---|---|
| master (`bcf0655`) | 28,818 | **15** | 0 |
| this PR | 5,720 | **0** | 0 |

- `dotnet build cs/ccxt/ccxt.csproj` — succeeded, 0 warnings (`netstandard2.1` + `netstandard2.0`)
- `dotnet run --project cs/tests/tests.csproj -- --baseTests` — `[C#] base REST tests passed`, including the multithreaded suite

Fixes #30344

author: benjben
body:
## Problem

The plain (non-distroless) image's launcher script is not executable, so the container exits **126** at `exec` before the JVM starts — [QA-1328](https://snplow.atlassian.net/browse/QA-1328).

`DockerPermissionStrategy.CopyChown`, set here in 0.7.0, emits a bare `COPY --chown` and no `chmod` at all, so the modes in the image are whatever they were in the build context. Apps that stage the context in one CI job and run `docker build` in another ship it through a GitHub Actions artifact, which does not preserve permissions — every file arrives mode 644.

Distroless is unaffected: its entrypoint is `java -jar`, so it needs no executable bit.

## Fix

`dockerAdditionalPermissions` already lists the files needing the executable bit, but sbt-native-packager only honours it under the `MultiStage` and `Run` strategies. Neither is usable here — both also `chmod -R u=rX,g=rX` the whole install location, breaking apps that write there (the Spark distribution's `/opt/spark/work`), and `MultiStage` emits a second `FROM`/`WORKDIR`/`USER` that `SnowplowSparkPlugin`'s `dockerCommands` transform keys off. So this applies just the `chmod` part, ahead of the `USER` switch:

```dockerfile
COPY --chown=nobody:nogroup 4/home /home
RUN ["chmod", "u+x,g+x", "/home/snowplow/bin/snowplow-stream-collector"]
USER nobody
```

## Testing

New scripted test `docker/launcher-permissions` strips the staged context's file modes, then shells out to `docker build`/`docker run` the way CI does. It fails with exit 126 without this change.

Verified against stream-collector `stdout` from a mode-stripped context: launcher is `-rwxr-xr--`, collector starts, `/health` returns 200. Full `sbt scripted` green, `spark/smoke` included.

Companion CI fix: snowplow/stream-collector-private#68

author: pschleger
body:
An async-search job whose executor node dies is now **claimed by a live node, its partial results cleared, and re-executed** as-at its stored point-in-time — so losing a node becomes invisible to async clients on engine-executed backends, the resilience the commercial backend already has via its own shard recovery.

Closes #509

## What changes

- **Re-execution replaces claim-then-FAIL.** The stale-job reaper (`ReclaimStaleJobs`) claims a stale or released `RUNNING` job, calls `ClearResults`, and re-enqueues it into this node's worker pool at the claimed epoch. The deposed executor's late writes are epoch-fenced, so the result set has exactly one author.
- **Graceful shutdown hands off, it does not fail.** `App.Shutdown` drains the pool within its budget, then *releases* whatever is still registered; those jobs stay `RUNNING` and are immediately claimable. A restarted node reclaims its own released jobs on a startup sweep.
- **The reclaim sweep runs on the heartbeat interval** (15s default) rather than the 5-minute snapshot-TTL ticker, which keeps the two sweeps on their own cadences. A crash hands off within `staleAfter` + one interval; a graceful departure within one interval.
- **Attempt cap bounds executor losses, not claims.** `CYODA_SEARCH_JOB_MAX_ATTEMPTS` (default 3, minimum 1) bounds the new `SearchJob.StaleClaims`, which counts only staleness claims. A rolling restart of any length therefore costs no attempt. A job that keeps killing its executor is failed after the cap with a distinct, non-revealing message. Setting `1` reproduces the previous claim-then-FAIL behaviour exactly.

No endpoint, status code, or error code changes. A client observes only a longer `RUNNING` span, and — past the cap — a `FAILED` status.

## SPI change (consumer action required)

`AsyncSearchStore` gains `Release(ctx, jobID string, epoch int64) error` and `SearchJob` gains `StaleClaims int64`. `Release` relinquishes a claim without finishing the job, epoch-fenced like the other executor-side writes and idempotent at the same epoch; it neither bumps `Epoch` nor counts as an attempt. A `SelfExecutingSearchStore` **may no-op** `Release` and leave `StaleClaims` at 0.

The commercial Cassandra backend is notified in `Cyoda/cyoda-go-cassandra#98`. This supersedes the earlier search-SPI wave's note that the deferred re-execution follow-up would need no further SPI change.

The pin advances to `cyoda-go-spi@v0.8.4-0.20260909025738-5ce242287a78` across all four `go.mod` files; plugin submodules are pseudo-pinned to the SPI-bump commit, so the root pin sits one commit behind HEAD as the coordinated-release window documents. No SPI tag is cut for this wave.

## Storage backends

All three in-tree plugins implement `Release` and the counter, guarded by new `spitest` conformance subtests so the backends cannot diverge. Postgres and sqlite gain a migration for the two columns; postgres's save-chunk transaction now sets a transaction-local idle timeout so a node dying mid-save cannot pin the job row until TCP keepalive notices.

## Verification

- `make test-full` green after the pin bump: root 9231, parity 1462, memory 494, sqlite 660, postgres 860 — zero failures.
- `make race` green: 8275 tests plus the parity suites, zero failures.
- New isolated e2e coverage for crash mid-scan, crash mid-save, single-node restart, the attempt cap, shutdown-release, and a deposed executor; plus a subprocess-cluster test that SIGKILLs a node mid-job and asserts a survivor completes every job with the correct count and no double execution.
- A whole-branch review returned no blocking findings.

Spec and plan: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-08-509-async-orphan-reexecute-design.md`, `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-08-509-async-orphan-reexecute.md`. Cloud contract: `docs/cloud-parity/async-job-node-failure-resilience.md`.

The port-of-entry page showed the four means of transport as a `govukRadios` group, every option visible at once. Design release 1 puts the same four options inside a dropdown whose first, selected entry reads "Select one". This swaps the control to a `govukSelect` to match.

This is a cross-repo increment. The companion PR is on **DEFRA/trade-imports-animals-tests**, on the same branch name, updating the E2E page object and flow to drive a select rather than a radio group.

**Merge the tests PR first, then this one.** CDP runs the tests repo's suite against the deployed frontend, so a frontend merged ahead of its own test changes would be exercised by specs that still click a radio, and CDP would go red. Both PRs must be green before either merges.

author: anilcancakir
body:
## What

`DioNetworkDriver`'s `BaseOptions` never set `preserveHeaderCase`, whose default is `false`. The IO adapter forwards that flag straight into `HttpClientRequest.headers.set(...)` (`dio-5.9.2` `lib/src/adapters/io_adapter.dart:109`), which lowercases every header key on the wire. A case-sensitive consumer (ExoPlayer's `User-Agent` lookup, in a downstream app) silently receives the wrong value instead of an error, because the wrong casing is not a request failure, it just ships the player's default agent instead of the caller's.

Setting `preserveHeaderCase: true` on the driver's `BaseOptions` fixes it: the flag is verified at the resolved `dio` version (`5.9.2`, not `5.11.1`) to default to `false` in both `Headers` (`headers.dart:11`) and `BaseOptions` (`options.dart:151`), and to be forwarded by the IO adapter at `io_adapter.dart:109`. The browser adapter (`dio_web_adapter`) has no equivalent: it writes headers via `XMLHttpRequest.setRequestHeader`, which is a browser API with no case-preservation hook at all, so this fix only reaches non-web targets. That is a platform limitation, not something this PR can close.

## Behaviour change for existing consumers

Every header sent through `Http` now reaches the socket with the exact casing the caller passed, instead of being normalised to lower-case. HTTP header names are case-insensitive by spec, so no consumer should depend on the previous lower-casing, but a consumer parsing raw header bytes directly (rather than through a case-insensitive header map) would see a different string.

## Testing

`test/network/preserve_header_case_test.dart` opens a loopback `ServerSocket` and asserts the raw request bytes contain `User-Agent: Watchools/1.0` rather than `user-agent: ...`. A `dart:io` `HttpHeaders`-based assertion on the receiving side cannot prove this: incoming headers are parsed without `preserveHeaderCase`, so they lowercase on receipt regardless of what the client actually sent on the wire.

Red phase confirmed before the fix: the same test failed with `user-agent: Watchools/1.0` in the captured raw request.

`flutter test` (full suite, 1441 tests), `dart analyze`, `dart format --set-exit-if-changed` all clean on the touched files.

## Not done in this PR

The `CHANGELOG.md` / `doc/` / `skills/` post-change sync this repo's `CLAUDE.md` calls for is not included; this PR's scope was fixed to the driver plus its test by the calling task, and the sync would need to be added before release regardless.

author: anthonygwalters
body:
## Summary & Motivation

When merged, this pull request will add `docs/tableau-xml/` — six topic files and five runnable scripts covering how to edit a Tableau workbook as XML. It changes no code and no models.

The material comes from editing the `Academic & Gradebook Health Suite` workbook directly as `.twb` XML over a multi-day build: publishing to a scratch project, rendering, and finding out what actually breaks. It is written for an agent to turn into a skill rather than for a person to read start to finish.

Not added to the `mkdocs.yml` nav, following the same precedent as `docs/superpowers/`. It is reachable by URL.

## Reviewer Notes

**The scripts are runnable and were tested, not sketched.** All seven `mutate.py` operations, both checkers, and the misuse paths were exercised against a real 1.9 MB workbook before commit. `check_twb.py` and `check_geometry.py` contain no workbook-specific values.

**One question is left open rather than papered over.** Two tooltip encodings exist in the workbook and it is not settled which is required. A hand-built tooltip in the form that demonstrably works elsewhere rendered its field references literally. That is written up as unresolved, with the evidence on both sides, so the skill does not inherit a confident wrong answer.

**The publish gate is a raise, not an assert.** Asserts are stripped under `-O`, and that check is the only thing standing between a scripted mistake and a corrupted production workbook.

## Self-review

### General

- [x] Review the **Claude Code Review** comment posted on this PR. Address valid feedback; dismiss false positives with a brief reply explaining why.

Dagster, dbt and Docs sections do not apply. No schedules, sensors, models or integrations are touched, and `reference/automations.md` is unaffected.

## CI checks

- [ ] **Trunk** — passes. All 13 files clean under `trunk check --force --no-fix`.

<details>
<summary>For Claude</summary>

Claude-assisted, human-directed. Written as a deliberate knowledge dump at the end of a long build, so the next agent starts from evidence rather than rediscovery.

**Structure:** `README.md` (orientation and the three rules that explain most of the lost time), `01-content-models.md`, `02-dynamic-text.md`, `03-layout-and-zones.md`, `04-formatting.md`, `05-build-workflow.md`, `06-failure-catalog.md`, plus `scripts/` with its own README.

**Claims are marked verified or inferred.** Two inferences failed during the build and both are documented as cautionary examples, because they share a shape worth teaching: structural similarity treated as behavioral proof. A parameter placeholder proven in a worksheet title was applied to mark labels and rendered blank. A tooltip form present in the workbook was assumed to work and did not.

**Scripts, with what each earned its place for:**

- `check_twb.py` — six checks, each corresponding to a real Desktop refusal on a file Server had already accepted: missing `simple-id`, missing `<aggregation>`, undeclared manifest features, dropped manifest entries including dotted names, unknown elements, and pane children out of content-model order. The pane-order check was added after error `D2E8DA72`.
- `check_geometry.py` — differential gap comparison against a baseline, plus pairwise overlap including at top level. Differential rather than tolerance-based because container gaps are per-container constants (0, 1, 586, 587, 888, 2636 in one dashboard) unrelated to child count; a per-child tolerance passed the exact 4,445-unit defect it was written to catch.
- `mutate.py` — text surgery, not ElementTree, because an ET round trip fails a regex assertion on an unmutated file. Control mode must produce a byte-identical copy or every mutant result is void. Seven operations, all tested.
- `repack.py` — asserts the packaged `.twb` is byte-identical to the source and that no bare LF appeared. The predecessor flattened 27,000 CRLF endings on every repack undetected, because the file on disk stayed correct.
- `tsc_session.py` — download, publish and render template. Documents that `tableauserverclient` appends the file extension and that `include_extract=False` yields a stub.

**Deliberate omissions:** dual-axis marks (folding works, the second axis drew nothing, abandoned) and number formats for table calculations (no worksheet-level `attr='number-format'` existed in the corpus to copy). Both are flagged in place rather than guessed at.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
</details>

body:
## Issue / tarefa de origem

Solicitação autorizada pelo mantenedor em 2026-09-09: implementar a direção mínima do Katherine Visual System V2 e abrir uma PR com comparativos antes/depois para avaliação. Nenhum número de issue foi fornecido. Branch criada a partir de `origin/main` (`3431ed7`), sem depender de outra PR.

## Problema e causa raiz

A face já era a identidade correta, mas o desktop não tinha uma manifestação própria de atividade. Enquanto aguardava uma resposta, a composição usava `animate-pulse` no status e `animate-spin` no ícone de loading, com a cópia “Katherine está digitando...”. Isso gerava movimento contínuo e afirmava uma atividade mais específica do que o runtime realmente conhecia.

## Solução e decisões

- Mantém a face bfce existente, incluindo disco, olhos, proporções, mapper de expressões e props do vendor.
- Adiciona um único arco SVG curto, externo, neutro, não focável e sem rotação.
- O arco aparece somente quando `isLoading === true`, não representa percentual nem cognição.
- O arco fica oculto abaixo de 48 px e usa stroke óptico responsivo.
- O desktop usa “Preparando resposta…” em vez de afirmar que Katherine está digitando.
- Os loops de pulse/spin são desativados apenas no companion desktop. O chat web mantém seu comportamento padrão.
- A entrada/saída do arco dura 140 ms; movimento reduzido elimina a transição.
- Não foram adicionados dependências, requests, timers, stores, estados emocionais, contratos de backend ou dados persistidos.
- O runner `scripts/presence_review.py` reproduz a aceitação GTK com SQLite isolado, provider offline explicitamente identificado, erro real sem provider, seis escalas e movimento reduzido.

## Arquivos / áreas afetadas

- `frontend/src/features/katherine-face/KatherineFace.jsx`
- `frontend/src/features/katherine-face/KatherineFace.css`
- `frontend/src/features/chat/components/CompanionLayout.jsx`
- `frontend/src/features/chat/components/CompanionLayout.css`
- `frontend/src/features/chat/components/MessageList.jsx`
- Testes da face e integração desktop
- `scripts/presence_review.py`
- `docs/design/presence-v2/` com README, JSON de observações e PNGs comparativos

## Comparativos visuais

A documentação completa está em [`docs/design/presence-v2/README.md`](https://github.com/Anakyklos/katherine-bot/blob/feat/katherine-presence-v2/docs/design/presence-v2/README.md).

### Idle, 1280×800

| Versão atual | Esta PR |
| --- | --- |
| ![Idle antes](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Anakyklos/katherine-bot/feat/katherine-presence-v2/docs/design/presence-v2/before-idle-1280.png) | ![Idle depois](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Anakyklos/katherine-bot/feat/katherine-presence-v2/docs/design/presence-v2/after-idle-1280.png) |

As duas capturas são idênticas pixel a pixel. A ausência de sinal em idle é intencional.

### Processing, 1280×800

### Processing, 800×800

| Versão atual | Esta PR |

As capturas de processing usam um provider offline de teste, pausado para tornar o estado observável. A UI, o shell, o bridge, o renderer e o SQLite continuam reais. A captura de erro usa o runtime real sem provider configurado.

## Testes executados

- `npm --prefix frontend test`: **159 testes Node + 114 testes de componentes, 0 falhas**.
- `npm --prefix frontend run lint`: passou.
- `npm --prefix frontend run build`: passou.
- `uv run --project backend python -m pytest backend/tests/test_desktop_api.py backend/tests/test_desktop_app_runtime.py backend/tests/test_desktop_build_resolver.py backend/tests/test_desktop_import_isolation.py backend/tests/test_desktop_navigation.py backend/tests/test_desktop_security.py -q`: **96 passaram**.
- `uv lock --project backend --check`: passou.
- `xvfb-run ... scripts/desktop_smoke.py`: **SMOKE_OK**, incluindo UI real, bridge, persistência SQLite, privacidade, navegação e fechamento do shell.
- `xvfb-run ... scripts/presence_review.py --scripted --verify-v2`: passou no entry real `desktop.html` em 1280×800 e 800×800, com composer visível, sem overflow, arco condicionado a busy, zero animações persistentes e zero mutações após estabilização.
- Mesmo runner com `--reduced-motion`: passou, com duração computada `0s`.
- Probes ópticos reais em 32/48/64/96/128/256 px: arco oculto em 32 px, visível a partir de 48 px, dois olhos em todas as escalas.
- `git diff --check`: passou.
- Detector Impeccable focado nos componentes alterados: `[]`.

## Riscos, migração e rollback

Não há migração, alteração de schema, contrato de API, autorização ou persistência. O rollback é reverter o commit `ecb95d7`. CSS container queries e `cqi` foram exercitados no WebKitGTK deste host, mas não em todos os ambientes Linux suportados.

A validação de resposta usa provider offline de teste e não comprova modelo remoto, percepção humana, uso por horas, Wayland, energia ou instalação do `.deb`. A preferência estética e a semântica do arco ainda devem ser avaliadas pelo mantenedor.

## Fora de escopo deliberado

- Janela flutuante compacta real.
- Conexões contextuais, nós e rede cognitiva.
- Novos estados de voz, sucesso ou bloqueio.
- Remoção da boca existente ou mudança do vendor.
- Teste com provider remoto, estudo com usuários, benchmark de CPU/RAM/energia e instalação do pacote.

body:
**Description of your changes:**

Repro: call the read-run-log endpoint (`/apis/v1beta1/runs/{run_id}/nodes/{node_id}/log`) for a run you can access, passing a `node_id` like `../../other/node` or `..`.
Cause: `GetLogObjectKey` joins the caller-supplied `node_id` into the object-store key (`logPathPrefix/executionName/nodeID/logFileName`) with no separator or `..` check, so the key can resolve outside this run's log prefix. `readRunLogFromPod` already validates a caller-controlled `node_id` (it confirms the pod belongs to the run) before streaming; the archive fallback `readRunLogFromArchive` skipped that guard.
Fix: reject a `node_id` that contains a path separator or a `..` component in `GetLogObjectKey`, before it reaches the artifact-key lookup or the key join. Legitimate Argo node ids are a single path segment, so this leaves valid reads unchanged. Regression test added.

lemuelvdm
body:
This PR consolidates and simplifies the native source release process while modernizing the Unicode data generation tooling.

## Summary

The release automation has been refactored from a complex multi-stage Python-based system into simpler shell scripts that integrate directly with the CI workflow. Additionally, the Unicode data generator has been ported from Python to C++ for better integration with the native build system.

## Key Changes

- **Removed complex release orchestration**: Deleted `tools/release-native.py`, `tools/release-native-test.py`, and the associated validation schema and gate logic (`tools/release-validation/`). These implemented a separate publication workflow that refused every release because it required external attestation files that do not exist for the Reporting 0.1.3 semantic input.

- **Removed source release preparation tool**: Deleted `tools/release-source.py` and its test suite (`tools/release-source-test.py`). Source bundle preparation is now handled by simpler shell scripts.

- **Moved the whole-boundary benchmark harness to the binding**: The Python driver under `benchmarks/e2e` is deleted; the worker and allocation probes now live in `kumwe/kumwe-engine` under `tools/benchmark/`, next to their PHP orchestrator. Historical evidence stays under `benchmarks/e2e/evidence`.

- **Added simplified release scripts**:
  - `tools/release-bundle.sh`: Assembles the immutable source release bundle (archive, SPDX inventory, metadata, checksums)
  - `tools/release-publish.sh`: Tags the commit and publishes the bundle as a GitHub release
  - `tools/release-notes.sh`: Renders release notes from the bundle metadata

- **Added version management**: `tools/version.sh` provides a single source of truth for version management, reading from and updating `resources/capabilities.json`. Supports getting, setting, and resolving versions for CI workflows, including automatic patch bumps and a `bump` workflow input.

- **Ported Unicode generator to C++**: Replaced `tools/generate-unicode-data.py` with `tools/generate-unicode-data.cpp`. The new implementation produces byte-identical output while integrating better with the C++ build system and avoiding Python runtime dependencies.

- **Updated CI workflow**: Modified `.github/workflows/ci.yml` to add a `version` job that resolves the tested commit and version, supporting both pull requests and default-branch releases, plus `release` and `notify-binding` jobs. Removed the separate `release.yml` workflow in favor of integrated release steps.

- **Updated documentation and metadata**:
  - Rewrote `docs/releasing.md` to reflect the new streamlined process
  - Updated `CHANGELOG.md`, `CHARTER.md` and `MIGRATION-HANDOFF.md` to document the new automated release approach
  - Updated `.gitattributes` to exclude release-related files from source distributions
  - Updated build configuration to read version from `resources/capabilities.json`

## Implementation Details

The new release process is fully automated on the default branch: every commit that passes the complete quality workflow is automatically published as an immutable source release. The version declared in `resources/capabilities.json` is the single source of truth, eliminating the complexity of separate version management systems. Each release dispatches `engine-release` to `kumwe/kumwe-engine`, which embeds the exact archive and publishes the PHP extension under the same version.

The C++ Unicode generator maintains exact compatibility with the previous Python implementation while reducing external dependencies and improving build integration.

author: kristofferremback
body:
## Problem

`createThreadOn` adds the anchor's author to a bot-created thread with the bot as the adder, but `processMemberAdded` in `activity/service.ts` resolved every adder as a user. The activity row for a `/spawn` thread read "bot_01KS… added you to …" because the bot id never matched a user.

## Solution

Record the adder's type on the `member_added` event and store the bot as the activity actor.

- `StreamService.addToStream` takes an `actorType` and writes `payload.addedByType` beside `addedBy`; `createThreadOn` passes `params.createdByType`.
- `processMemberAdded` reads `addedByType`, resolves the name through `resolveAuthorName` with that type, and inserts the activity row with `actorType` set to it.
- Events written before this change carry no `addedByType`; they were all user-added, so the read defaults to `user`. Stated in a one-line comment at the read.
- Dropping the row altogether was considered (Kris: "I'm also not sure it's needed?"). Kept: the row is how the user finds a thread they were added to from the activity feed, and this PR is the minimal fix.

## Files

| File | Change |
| ---- | ------ |
| `apps/backend/src/features/activity/service.ts` | Resolve the adder by `addedByType`, store it as the actor type |
| `apps/backend/src/features/activity/service.test.ts` | Bot-adder case: actor is the bot, name resolves to the bot's name |
| `apps/backend/src/features/streams/service.ts` | `addToStream` records `addedByType`; `createThreadOn` passes the creator's type |

## Test plan

author: kinminghao
body:
## Summary

`startup()` was called fire-and-forget at the top level of `packages/server/src/index.ts` — no `await`, no `.catch()`. If any step in the startup flow failed (DB connection, runtime initialization, etc.), the error was silently swallowed and the process continued running in a half-initialized state, leading to unpredictable 500 errors.

## Changes

Add `.catch()` to `startup()` that logs the error via `logger.fatal` and calls `process.exit(1)`, ensuring the process terminates cleanly on startup failure.

body:
## Summary

Adds general version installation and uninstallation to the native SwiftUI Versions screen while preserving the existing project-centric workflow.

### Included

- Typed `asdf uninstall <tool> <version>` operation in `AsdfService`
- Individual Install action for available versions
- Explicit destructive Uninstall confirmation for installed versions
- `VersionUsageInspector` that lists managed projects whose `.tool-versions` exactly references the selected tool/version
- Fallback references count as usage; prefix matches do not
- Live stdout/stderr task panel for general version operations
- Cancellation backed by the existing cancellable `AsdfCommandRunner`
- Global mutual exclusion between Project Install Missing and Versions install/uninstall tasks
- Post-success refresh of project runtime status and the selected plugin's installed-version state
- Shared 200,000-character in-memory log cap
- Unit tests for project usage/impact detection
- README and `docs/DEVELOPMENT.md` updated with version-management safety rules and Codex constraints

## Safety

- Uninstall always requires explicit confirmation, even when no managed project references the version.
- If managed projects reference the version, the confirmation lists them and explains that uninstalling may leave them with a missing runtime unless another fallback remains usable.
- `.tool-versions` is never modified by install/uninstall operations.
- Plugin installation/removal remains a separate future workflow.

## Validation

macOS GitHub Actions will run the complete `swift test` suite. Merge only after CI is green.

author: a5af
body:
## Summary
- PR #3100 documented but never fixed jekt-delivery failure: `ReactiveHandler`'s registry holds one key per block, and `input.rs`'s Register-tail re-keys it to the live, renameable display name on every turn -- evicting the stable `AGENTMUX_AGENT_ID` a spawn registered it under moments earlier.
- GitHub PR-body tags embed that stable ID specifically because it survives renames -- a jekt tagged with it had nothing left to resolve to after the agent's first turn.
- Reproduced live this session: `AGENTMUX_AGENT_ID=agentg` in env, but the live WAN subscription is `claude` (the current display name).
- Fix: a second, independent alias registry (`Handler::alias_to_block`) that `spawn_process` also populates with `AGENTMUX_AGENT_ID`, never evicted by the ordinary per-turn re-key. `inject_message_inner` falls back to it on a primary-registry miss. The existing #2695 recipient-identity check gets a matching `stable_agent_identity_confirmer` (backed by a new, write-once `Controller::stable_agent_id()`) so an alias-resolved delivery isn't rejected for legitimately not matching the live display name.
- Scoped to `PersistentSubprocessController` only (the stream-json/ACP agent path). No change to `ShellController` or the ordinary rename/#2697 behavior.
- See `docs/incident/INCIDENT_2026_09_09_JEKT_STABLE_ID_ALIAS.md` for full root cause. Also includes `INCIDENT_2026_09_09_JEKT_CASE_MISMATCH_SUBSCRIPTION.md`, a research-only doc from checking (and disproving) a case-sensitivity hypothesis along the way.

## Test plan
- [x] New unit tests: alias resolves via `inject_message`, alias survives a primary-key change, `unregister_block` cleans up the alias, dual-confirmer accepts a stable-only match, dual-confirmer still rejects a target matching neither identity.
- [ ] CI build
- [ ] Verify against a live GitHub PR-review jekt end-to-end once merged and deployed

author: ijoolaie
body:
## Summary
- reauthorize the Agent through the canonical policy kernel at the WorkItem -> Run hand-off
- prevent revoked, killed, expired, or governance-drifted Agents from creating new executable Runs after dispatch state is committed
- keep the Run-worker authorization as the final execution-time defense
- add regression coverage proving authorization occurs before employee resolution and Run creation

## Security rationale
The deferred side-effect boundary is now governed, and the Run worker revalidates authority before provider/tool execution. The remaining WorkItem -> Run adapter could still create and enqueue a Run after Agent authority changed, relying on the later worker denial. That is fail-closed for provider execution but leaves an unauthorized executable Run artifact and a RUNNING WorkItem hand-off. Reauthorization here closes that earlier mutable-authority boundary while retaining the worker check for defense in depth.

## Validation
CI should exercise the repository governance/security gate set before merge.

author: pcw7
body:
W4 의 프로젝터를 쓰려고 `order_key` 계산 경로를 들여다보다 발견한 **잠재 버그**다.
스키마 한 줄이지만 증상이 조용하고 늦게 나타난다.

## 무엇이 틀렸나

`fractional-indexing` 은 키를 `0-9 A-Z a-z` 의 **이진(코드포인트) 순서**로
비교한다고 가정한다. 그런데 이 DB 는 **ICU + `ko-KR`** 로 초기화된다
(CLAUDE.md: 한국어 검색 때문에 소급 변경 불가 축). 두 순서가 실제로 다르다 —
이 DB 에서 직접 측정한 값이다:

```
이진(C)    : Zz  a0  a1  a9  aA  aZ  aa  az  z0
ICU(ko-KR) : a0  a1  a9  aa  aA  az  aZ  z0  Zz
                       ^^^^^^^^          ^^
```

조용히 두 가지가 깨진다.

1. **`max(order_key)` 가 진짜 마지막 형제를 놓친다.** `page.ts` 의
   `nextSiblingKey()` 가 그 값 뒤에 새 키를 만들면 **이미 존재하는 키**가 나온다
   → `ux_block_sibling_order` UNIQUE 위반.
2. **`ORDER BY order_key` 가 에디터가 계산한 순서와 다른 순서를 준다**
   → "문단 순서가 이상하다". 데이터는 멀쩡해 보이고 재현이 어렵다.

## 실측 임계값: 형제 37개

순차 생성 키는 `a0..a9`(10) → `aA..aZ`(26) → `aa..` 로 간다.
**37번째에서 `aa` 가 생기는 순간** ICU 가 `aZ` 를 최대로 보기 시작한다:

| 형제 수 | 마지막 키 | ICU 의 max | 그 뒤 새 키 | 충돌 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 11 | `aA` | `aA` | `aB` | — |
| **37** | `aa` | **`aZ`** | **`aa`** | **있음** |
| 62 | `az` | `aZ` | `aa` | 있음 |

**36개까지는 증상이 전혀 없다.** 개발 중에는 멀쩡해 보이다가 문서가 커지면
터지는 종류다. 지금 잡은 게 다행이고, W4 프로젝터가 본문 블록 수십~수백 개를
한 부모 밑에 넣기 시작하면 바로 만났을 것이다.

## 왜 컬럼 단위 `COLLATE "C"` 인가

데이터베이스 collation 은 바꿀 수 없다 — 한국어 정렬·검색이 거기 달렸고
CLAUDE.md 가 "한 번 정하면 못 바꾼다"고 못박았다. 바꿔야 하는 건 **이 컬럼
하나**다. `order_key` 에는 사람이 읽는 텍스트가 들어가지 않으므로 언어별
정렬이 의미를 갖지 않는다 — 오히려 방해다.

TypeScript 쪽 비교(`compareBlockOrder`)는 UTF-16 코드 유닛 비교라 이미 이진이다.
이 마이그레이션으로 **DB 와 앱이 같은 순서를 본다.**

`live_block` 뷰가 `SELECT *` 로 이 컬럼에 의존해
`cannot alter type of a column used by a view` 로 막혔다. 같은 트랜잭션에서
뷰를 내렸다 0006 과 동일한 정의로 다시 만든다 — 뷰가 없는 순간이 밖에서
관측되지 않는다.

## "걸었다"가 아니라 "실제로 막는가"

HANDOFF §5 대로 동작을 확인한다.

- `scripts/verify-schema.mjs [6]` — 대소문자가 섞인 표본(`aA aZ aa az Zz`…)을
  넣고 `ORDER BY` 와 `max()` 결과가 JS 정렬과 **같은지** 확인
- `src/lib/block/order-key.db.test.ts` — 형제를 **70개 실제로 만들어**
  ① 키 중복 없음 ② 생성 순서 = JS 정렬 ③ **DB 의 `ORDER BY` = 생성 순서**
  ④ `max()` = 마지막 키

  이 테스트가 36개짜리였다면 버그를 못 잡는다. 개수 자체가 테스트의 일부다.

이 PR 이전 상태로 되돌려 확인한 결과, 70개 키에 대해
`ORDER BY x COLLATE "ko-KR-x-icu"` 는 생성 순서와 **일치하지 않는다**(측정함).
즉 위 ③ 이 실패한다.

## 확인

- `npm run check` 통과
- `REQUIRE_DB=1 npm test` → **245 tests / pass 245 / skipped 0** (243 → +2)
- `npm run db:verify:schema` 통과 (`[6]` 절 추가)

author: tomsauy
body:
La 4.1.5 est sortie le 6 septembre, pour les deux ans du pack. Côté langue, l'amont ne change que **3 fichiers et 7 lignes** — mais les mods, eux, ont bougé.

## Le pack — cinq gestes

Une clé nouvelle : le presse-papiers du gestionnaire d'étang. La description du **jeton de surplus** réécrite — l'objet a été retiré du jeu et son ancien texte décrivait un comportement disparu. Sa clé `.warn` devenue orpheline. Deux quêtes où l'anglais passe de *called* à *invited* en nommant le Marchand.

Et le **journal des modifications** en 4.1.5, avec sa ligne d'anniversaire et la 4.1.4 descendue en fin de fichier, comme l'a fait l'amont. Structure et nombre de puces vérifiés contre l'anglais.

Trois des six changements anglais ne demandaient rien : des fautes de frappe corrigées en amont (*poviding*, *Bottle*, *degreading*) que notre traduction rendait déjà correctement.

## Reliable EMI change d'identifiant

C'est le morceau qu'un diff des fichiers de langue ne montre pas.

Le mod passe de `emixx-forge-1.5.3` à `remi-forge-4.6.8` et devient **`remi`** — `modId` vérifié dans son `mods.toml`, espace de noms `assets/remi/lang/`. Nos **86 clés** sous `assets/emixx/` étaient donc mortes, et le mod n'embarque aucun français : la configuration d'EMI serait repassée en anglais.

| | |
|---|---|
| récupérées en renommant `emixx` → `remi` | **82**, dont 77 telles quelles |
| relues (le mod ne s'appelle plus « EMI++ ») | 5 |
| disparues du mod | 4 |
| **nouvelles traduites** | **114** |

Le mod a beaucoup grandi : mode défilement, préfixes de recherche, pages de tags par catégorie, panneau Poste de travail. Vocabulaire aligné sur l'existant — « barre latérale », « onglets du mode Créatif », « groupes de piles ».

Au passage, deux noms de panneaux d'EMI qui n'avaient pas de français alors que huit clés de REMI y renvoient : **Liste** et **Fabricables**.

## Les mods — 193 clés

**Create: Numismatics (163).** Le mod a gagné 170 clés : points de vente, sous-comptes, cartes autorisées, et toute une série de guides Ponder. Son français embarqué n'en couvre que 113.

Vocabulaire aligné sur le sien — *Boutique* pour Vendor, *Automate de dépôt* pour Depositor, *Liste de confiance* pour Trust List — **sauf sur un point** : il dit « compte bancaire » quand le pack dit « compte en banque », 9 fois contre 2. Une seule forme désormais, la majoritaire : les 3 clés du mod sont recouvertes et nos 2 écarts corrigés. Il n'en reste aucun.

**Every Compat (27) et Quality Food (3)** sur les moules établis : « X en %s », « Tige de X creuse », « … en %s écorcé ». Deux termes neufs pour le projet, tracés dans `provenance.json` : *Whispering* devient « murmurante », sur le registre de *Airy* → « ajourée » ; *Kitchen Cabinet* devient « Placard de cuisine », « Meuble de cuisine » étant déjà pris par `refurbished_furniture`.

**90 clés mortes retirées** — Every Compat 70, Create: Schematic Checker 19, Quality Food 1. Mesurées en diffant l'ancien jar contre le nouveau, seule méthode fiable : compter les clés absentes de l'anglais donnait 1 744 faux positifs, tous des noms dérivés de l'identifiant par KubeJS.

## Trouvé en chemin, sans rapport avec la 4.1.5

`item.society.villager` perdait son `%s`, qui reçoit le métier. Tous les villageois s'affichaient « Villageois », indistinguables. Même défaut que `item.society.invitation`, corrigé en août — relevé cette fois par le validateur.

## Vérifications

- 258 fichiers de langue relus, JSON valide partout
- aucun nom d'objet accentué, hors `item.utility.downgrade` dont la valeur est une phrase d'infobulle
- zéro ligature `œ`, zéro « compte bancaire » résiduel
- structure et nombre de puces du changelog identiques à l'anglais
- 2 939 alias EMI régénérés sur les jars de la 4.1.5, tous pourvus de leur texte
- les arbitrages non évidents sont dans `outillage/provenance.json` — 1 719 termes, 2 429 clés

## Ce qui n'a pas bougé, et que je craignais

`ShopScreen.class` est **identique** entre `society_trading` 1.2.6 et 1.2.9, `bipush 102` compris : la limite de largeur de la boutique n'a pas changé, et les 36 corrections de largeur d'août tiennent.

author: deanmarano
body:
## What

A `preflight` failure now stops the rest of the CI run on a pull request. Preflight names the failing check(s) in an error annotation and the job summary, then `POST`s `repos/{repo}/actions/runs/{id}/cancel`.

Today preflight only `needs: changes`, and so does every expensive lane — so a trailing-whitespace prettier failure caught in ~25s leaves the DB matrix, `rails-comparison` and the parity pipelines running for another 20+ minutes on a run that is already lost. The `concurrency` block cancels only a run superseded by a *newer push*; it has nothing to say about a self-inflicted failure.

## Option chosen: self-cancel (option 2), scoped to `pull_request`

**Why the others lost:**

- **`needs: preflight` on the expensive lanes (option 1).** It pays on every *green* run to save time on the rare red one — and preflight is no longer sub-minute: it does a checkout, a `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` and the closing-story-citation scan, so it serializes minutes, not seconds, onto the front of every lane's critical path. It also changes when each of those jobs' `!cancelled()` / `always()` guards fire, which would mean re-verifying every downstream gate against an aggregator whose skip allow-list is a hard failure by design. Large blast radius, permanent cost, for a case that only occurs when someone has already made a mistake.
- **Doing nothing / relying on the aggregator.** The `ci` job already reports the failure correctly — it just does so 20 minutes late, which is exactly the cost being complained about.

## Legibility

The concern with cancelling is a wall of ambiguous grey jobs. Three things address it:

1. Every check step in preflight now carries an `id:`, and a new `Report which preflight checks failed` step (`if: failure()`, runs **before** the cancel) reads `toJSON(steps)` and emits `::error::Preflight failed: prettier commit-attribution` plus a `### Preflight failed` job-summary block. Both are written before cancellation and survive it, so the run page's summary names the cause. An id-less setup step failing (checkout/setup-node) prints an explicit fallback rather than an empty list.
2. The failing step itself is still red in the step log — the per-step independent reporting that the ci.yml:383-397 consolidation comment protects is untouched. Each guarded step keeps its `!cancelled() && …` prefix, so a prettier failure still doesn't suppress the docs-freeze or attribution checks; the cancel only fires after all of them have had their turn.
3. That comment block was extended (not rewritten) with three lines pointing at the new terminal behaviour, and the two new steps carry the full reasoning inline, in the file's WHY style.

## Aggregator and allow-list

**No allow-list arm was touched or broadened.** Cancelling includes this job, so preflight's own conclusion becomes `cancelled` rather than `failure` — hence the annotation/summary ordering above. Downstream jobs report `cancelled`, which ci.yml:2013 already treats as a hard failure (`result == "failure" or result == "cancelled"`), and `ci` itself is normally cancelled before it starts. Branch protection reads a cancelled required check as not-success, exactly like a red one. The `preflight` arm of the skip allow-list (ci.yml:2035) is unaffected: nothing here makes preflight *skip*.

The visible change in reporting is that the run's final conclusion reads **cancelled** instead of **failure**. That is the deliberate trade; the annotation is what carries the diagnosis.

## Non-PR events

The cancel is gated `failure() && github.event_name == 'pull_request'`, mirroring `concurrency`'s own scoping and for the same reason: pushes to `main`, the Monday `schedule` sweep (where `changes` falls back to `prettier_files=__ALL__`) and `workflow_dispatch` exist *for* the full-suite signal and the timing report, and none is re-triggered by pushing a fix. Those runs stay red the slow way, with every lane's result intact. The report step is ungated by event, so the annotation improves those runs too.

## Permissions

`actions: write` added to the preflight job, with a comment saying it is required by — and only by — the cancel step. Declaring `permissions:` zeroes unlisted scopes, so `contents: read` and `pull-requests: read` stay listed.

### Scope: same-repository, non-Dependabot PRs

This repo is public, and GitHub caps `GITHUB_TOKEN` at read-only for a fork `pull_request` run and for every Dependabot `pull_request` run, *below* whatever the job declares — `actions: write` cannot raise it. Those runs 403 on the cancel and keep every expensive lane, i.e. today's behaviour. That limit is accepted rather than engineered around: a fork run cannot read secrets at all, so no PAT or App token reaches it, and the only mechanism that does work is a second `workflow_run`-triggered workflow running in the base-repo context to cancel its trigger — a parallel workflow with its own token and failure modes, for a repo with **zero forks and no Dependabot config**. If either becomes a real source of PRs, that is the design to reach for; the comment on the step says so.

What the fix does buy is that the 403 is **said out loud**: the step branches on the error and emits `::warning::` naming the read-only token as the cause, so a `continue-on-error` step cannot swallow it in silence and send someone hunting a phantom bug. A test pins that the message stays.

Failure of the cancel API (403, 5xx) is `continue-on-error: true`: it degrades to the pre-change behaviour rather than replacing a legible prettier failure with a confusing red on a step about cancellation.

## Verified vs. not

**Verified locally:**

- ci.yml parses (`yaml.parse`), the job graph has no cycles and every `needs:` names a real job (31 jobs walked). `actionlint` is not installed on this host.
- No `if:` expression contains a literal newline (the ci-suite-coverage invariant).
- Two new invariants in `scripts/ci-suite-coverage.test.ts` (the existing home for ci.yml pins): every preflight check step carries an `id:` the failure report can name — a check added without one would fail the run but vanish from the annotation — and the cancel step stays `pull_request`-scoped, `continue-on-error`, and backed by `actions: write`. A third pins that the read-only-token limitation stays announced. `pnpm vitest run scripts/ci-suite-coverage.test.ts` — 28/28 pass.
- `prettier --check` on the file.
- The report step's bash/jq replayed against a synthetic `toJSON(steps)` payload, in both the some-failed and no-id'd-step-failed cases.

**Only the first real red run can confirm:**

- That the runner's token, with `actions: write`, is accepted by the cancel endpoint on same-repo PRs (org policy could still restrict it; the `continue-on-error` fallback and the new warning are why that is neither fatal nor silent).
- Whether preflight's own conclusion lands as `cancelled` or `failure` — GitHub's grace period on an in-flight job is not contractual either way. Both are hard failures to the aggregator, and the annotation is written first regardless.
- The precise mix of `cancelled` vs. `skipped` on lanes that had not yet started when the cancel landed. `cancelled` is a hard failure; a lane GitHub happens to mark `skipped` instead would hit the allow-list — I have not seen GitHub do that on a run cancel, and it is the one behaviour worth watching on the first red run. If it happens, the fix is a narrow allow-list arm for it, not a broadened one.

author: acherukuri83-stack
body:
Two deferred-depth items from `docs/backlog.md`, in one small PR.

## 1. Prime Finance portal tab

`portal/src/PrimeFinanceView.tsx` — one **Prime Finance** tab with a domain
selector (Stock Loan / Margin / Cash / Corp Actions). Each choice routes to the
endpoint that already exists:

| Domain | Request |
|---|---|
| Stock Loan | `POST /investigate {loan_id}` |
| Margin | `POST /investigate {margin_call_id}` |
| Cash | `POST /investigate {cash_break_id}` |
| Corp Actions | `POST /corpaction {event_id, account_id}` |

The result is the standard `Finding`, rendered with the same shape the
Engineering tab uses: outcome, root cause, proposed / rejected actions, open
questions, and a click-through trace link. Sample ids are pre-filled
(`LN-5001`, `MC-9001`, `CB-8001`, `CA-7001` / `ACC-88213`).

`portal/src/api.ts` gains `primeFinance(kind, id)` and
`corpaction(eventId, accountId)`. **No schema change** — no `openapi.json` /
`api-types.ts` regen needed.

Wired into `App.tsx` `TABS` + `LIVE` between **Client** and **Engineering**.

## 2. Bounded Supervisor -> Developer hand-off

`agent_core/supervisor.py::_recommend_incident_review`, called after
`_carry_open_questions`: when **every** dispatched sub-finding is
`INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE`, the client `Finding` gets an `open_questions` note
recommending a platform incident review (`POST /diagnose` with the suspected
job / service).

This is a **recommendation only**. The Supervisor does *not* call
`developer.investigate_incident` itself — "which platform subject" (which job id,
which service) has no safe default to synthesise, so a human picks it from the
note. That remaining auto-dispatch step stays documented in `docs/backlog.md`
and `CLAUDE.md` as the open product question.

## How I validated

- `cd ai-platform && ./.venv/Scripts/python.exe -m ruff format --check . && ruff check . && mypy .` -> clean (164 source files)
- `./.venv/Scripts/python.exe -m pytest -m "not eval and not contract" -q` -> **127 passed**, 19 deselected
  - `tests/test_supervisor.py` +2: `test_all_insufficient_recommends_a_platform_incident_review`, `test_mixed_outcomes_do_not_trigger_the_incident_recommendation`
- `cd portal && npm run lint && npx tsc --noEmit && npm run build` -> clean
- Docs: `docs/backlog.md` — "Portal affordance" and "Supervisor hand-off" items marked done / narrowed to the auto-dispatch follow-up; `CLAUDE.md` "Landed so far" + "Still deferred" updated.

No eval sweep (paused for C+ by owner decision).

author: danbeckdev
body:
## `audit` was never red on 8 of 10. Six of those were cancellations.

`ci.yml` sets `concurrency: cancel-in-progress: true`, so every new run cancels the previous one on the same ref. **Measured on ten main commits at 14:2xZ, by conclusion:**

```
6  audit   cancelled     <- NOT failures
3  check   cancelled     <- NOT failures
2  audit   failure       <- real
```

**`audit 6 of 10` was six cancellations and two failures. `check 3 of 10` was entirely cancellations.**

## The change that made section 4 see everything is the change that made it over-count

**#740** moved this section's population from **PR heads** to **merge commits**, an hour before this fix — because PR heads structurally could not see `ready-label-audit`, which runs on the `issues` event against main's tip.

**A PR head stops moving, so it rarely carries a cancellation. A merge commit on a fast-moving main carries them constantly.** Widening a population without re-reading what its new members can say is the shape.

**And it inflates in the alarming direction**, which is the direction that gets acted on: *"audit red on 8 of 10"* went into three tables and a dispatch before anybody read a conclusion.

## The list existed twice

Section 4's tally and **section 2's per-PR red list** each carried their own copy of `["SUCCESS", "SKIPPED", "NEUTRAL", ""]`.

**Fixing one would have left the other reporting cancelled runs as red on open PRs** — a remedy applied at one call site when the behaviour reaches several, **in the commit fixing exactly that class.** Both now call `isRed`, and `NOT_RED` states the reasons once.

## Acceptance

```
npx tsx --test packages/lab/src/packaging/queue-table.test.ts
```

50 tests. `CANCELLED` (either case) is not red; a name that was only ever cancelled is not reported at all; an empty conclusion is in flight and now deliberately so rather than by accident. **`TIMED_OUT` stays red, asserted — a timeout IS a verdict about the commit**, and "never report" is the failure this fix must not become.

**Mutation**: the pre-fix list is written out and shown to count a superseded run as red — the six-of-ten that was quoted.

Closes: none — correcting #740 the same afternoon.

author: phillipmwaniki
body:
P2 of the Harbour MCP server (after #12): an agent can now **move files** over SFTP, not just run commands. Contract: `docs/mcp.md`.

## Tools (only with `--allow-write`)

- **`harbour_sftp_list`** `{ host, path? }` → directory listing (defaults to the login dir).
- **`harbour_sftp_read`** `{ host, path, maxBytes? }` → `{ path, encoding, content }` — `utf-8`, or `base64` when the file isn't valid UTF-8. Refuses a file larger than `maxBytes` (default 1 MiB) **without reading it** — large files are what the app's transfers are for.
- **`harbour_sftp_write`** `{ host, path, content, base64? }` → `{ path, bytesWritten }`, creating or truncating.

Same connection rules as command execution: keychain-only secrets, unknown host keys refused, **guarded hosts refused**. Each call opens a fresh connection for the operation and closes it after.

## Core additions (no app change)

Reaching a connection for SFTP needed a way to connect **without a shell**:

- `transport::start_headless` — drives channel-opening (SFTP subsystem, direct-tcpip, tcpip-forward) on a session with no pty, no reader, closing when the returned transport drops.
- `client::connect_headless` — establishes the chain and hands back that channel-only transport.
- `sftp::read_file` / `write_file` (size-capped read), and `SftpSession` re-exported so the headless consumer can name it.

Host resolution + the guarded/auth checks are now a shared `prepare` step behind both the command and SFTP tools, so they reach a host under one set of rules.

## Tests

18 crate tests total (3 new for SFTP): the SFTP tools appear only with `--allow-write` and are refused without it; a guarded host is refused before connecting; missing arguments are reported. The live SFTP path runs through the core's already-tested `sftp` module over the headless connection.

Gates green locally: fmt + clippy `-D warnings` on both crates (default and `--no-default-features`), `cargo test` (mcp), app suite. Docs: `docs/mcp.md`, CHANGELOG.

Next: P3, port forwarding — the last of the "full" scope.

author: valerielinc-ops
body:
## Implementato

- in questa PR — `scripts/ci/review-gate.mjs` ricostruisce gli Important ancora aperti dalla cronologia delle review bot, conservando gli anchor `path:Llinea`; una review successiva con `Important: 0` e `## LGTM` non può cancellarli per il solo riallineamento della base.
- in questa PR — gli anchor ereditati passano nello stesso classificatore fail-closed già usato dal gate: un finding ancora nel diff resta bloccante, mentre il percorso esistente registra `review-gate: DECLASSIFIED` solo quando tutti i file citati sono fuori dal diff corrente.
- in questa PR — la chiusura richiede una conferma path-specifica `Fix di \`path:Llinea\`: ok.`; la vecchia forma `Fix di L12: ok.` non può chiudere anchor su file diversi, e un Important senza citazione richiede il testo normalizzato esplicitamente confermato.
- in questa PR — il bundle e il prompt di `tests.yml` espongono gli Important storici, prescrivono le conferme per anchor e degradano in modo esplicito se la sezione storica non è renderizzabile; `REVIEW.md` documenta la stessa regola.
- in questa PR — la regressione riproduce Important su commit A, riallineamento a commit B e review LGTM: prima della correzione 18/19 test passavano e l’asserzione nuova falliva; dopo la prima correzione la suite passava 22/22, la suite finale precedente 65/65 e i test aggiunti sul feedback del reviewer passano 35/35.

## Non implementato (ancora)

- per scelta — questa PR non esegue dispatch o rerun di workflow, deploy, invii o purge: la correzione è verificata localmente e la produzione resta al ciclo normale della PR.
- by construction — `.github/workflows/enable-native-automerge.yml` — falso positivo: usa `PR_NUMBER` per abilitare il merge nativo, non per classificare review storiche.
- by construction — `.github/workflows/post-merge-followup.yml` — falso positivo: usa `CTX_DIR` e `PR_NUMBER` per il triage post-merge, non per il gate della review.
- by construction — `.github/workflows/pr-redflag-fixer.yml` — falso positivo: invoca il classificatore sul singolo evento 🔴, non implementa la selezione dell’ultima review nel gate.
- by construction — `scripts/ci/followup-has-candidates.mjs` — falso positivo: `latestReviewer` serve a decidere se fare triage follow-up, non a decidere il merge.
- by construction — `.github/workflows/issue-fix.yml` — falso positivo: `CTX_DIR` è solo contesto del fixer, non stato dei finding.
- by construction — `.github/workflows/pr-redcheck-fixer.yml` — falso positivo: `PR_NUMBER` identifica la PR del red-check fixer, non la cronologia delle review.
- by construction — `build-plugins/weeklyEmployersPlugin.ts` — falso positivo: `currentKeys` è un set di chiavi dati, non un’identità di finding.
- by construction — `scripts/ci/collect-followup-batch.mjs` — falso positivo: `PR_NUMBER` seleziona il batch post-merge, non il verdetto del gate.
- by construction — `scripts/ci/is-followup-fix-pr.mjs` — falso positivo: `PR_NUMBER` identifica la PR da classificare per il follow-up, non una review.
- by construction — `scripts/ci/lib/constants.mjs` — falso positivo: `review-gate` è una categoria di errore, non il percorso decisionale del gate.
- by construction — `scripts/ci/lib/hook-command-parser.mjs` — falso positivo: `PR_NUMBER` è parsing dell’ambiente del hook, non persistenza di finding.
- by construction — `scripts/ci/lib/jobFailureCategory.mjs` — falso positivo: `review-gate` è solo un’etichetta di diagnostica, non la selezione della review.
- by construction — `scripts/ci/lib/reopen-breaker.mjs` — falso positivo: `review-gate` è una causa del breaker, non una decisione di severità.
- by construction — `scripts/ci/pr-autorebase.mjs` — falso positivo: `review-gate` è una causa di riapertura, non il gate che valuta gli anchor.
- by construction — `scripts/ci/report-vitest-failure.mjs` — falso positivo: `PR_NUMBER` serve a riportare failure Vitest, non a valutare review.
- by construction — `scripts/lib/orphan-enriched-store.mjs` — falso positivo: `currentKeys` identifica record di arricchimento, non finding di review.
- by construction — `scripts/sync-gsc-orphans.mjs` — falso positivo: `currentKeys` identifica orfani GSC, non finding di review.
- by construction — `scripts/write-employer-traffic.mjs` — falso positivo: `currentKeys` identifica documenti di traffico, non finding di review.

Closes #8109

author: pcw7
body:
에디터의 입력 계층. **UI 는 다음 PR**이고, 여기까지가 헤드리스로 테스트된다.

## F-12-01 의 클론 대안을 그대로 했다

> 키맵을 **선언적 테이블 하나로 정의**하고 ProseMirror `keymap` 플러그인 +
> `inputRules` 에 위임한다. **OS 분기는 `event.metaKey || event.ctrlKey` 정규화
> 한 곳에서** 처리한다.

`Mod-` 접두사가 그 정규화이고 `prosemirror-keymap` 이 이미 플랫폼에 맞게
해석한다 — 우리가 `navigator.platform` 을 보지 않는다. 정본이 "Mac 은
`cmd+option+숫자`, Windows 는 `ctrl+shift+숫자`"라고 나눠 적은 것도
`Mod-Alt-<숫자>` 하나로 선언한다.

## 접두사 목록을 다시 적지 않는다

블록 규칙은 **레지스트리(`block/types.ts` 의 `markdownPrefix`)에서 생성한다.**
여기 다시 적으면 두 곳이 어긋나고, 어긋나면 *"슬래시 메뉴에는 있는데 마크다운으로는
안 만들어지는"* 타입이 생긴다. 테스트도 목록을 재선언하지 않고 레지스트리가
주는 13개 접두사가 모두 동작하는지 확인한다.

## `Backspace` — 순서가 동작을 정의한다

세 커맨드가 순서대로 걸린다.

| 순서 | 커맨드 | 언제 |
|---|---|---|
| ① | `undoInputRule` | 방금 마크다운 변환이 있었다 → **그것만** 되돌린다 |
| ② | `mergeBackward` | 블록 맨 앞 → 이전 줄과 병합 |
| ③ | (ProseMirror 기본) | 글자 지우기 |

**①이 ②보다 앞이어야 한다.** `# ` 를 쳐서 헤딩이 된 직후의 Backspace 는
"헤딩 취소"이지 "앞 블록과 병합"이 아니다 — F-01-17 엣지 케이스
*"마크다운 자동 변환 undo | 변환만 되돌리고 입력 텍스트는 유지"* 가 요구하는
동작이고, 이건 우리가 만들 필요가 없었다(`undoInputRule` 이 정확히 그것이다).

## 색은 토글이 아니다

`toggleMark` 로 표현되지 않는다 — 같은 색을 다시 누르면 꺼져야 하지만
**다른 색을 누르면 갈아타야** 한다. 그리고 `default` 는 마크를 **제거**한다.
계약에 `default_background` 가 없는 이유와 같다: "기본"은 색이 없는 상태이지
색이 아니다.

링크도 같은 이유로 `removeMark` 를 먼저 부른다. 겹쳐 쌓이면 어느 링크가
이기는지가 문서 순서에 달리고, RichText 계약(`text.link` 는 하나)으로
직렬화할 때 **하나가 조용히 사라진다.** 테스트가 마크 개수를 확인한다.

## 인라인 규칙 — 순서와 공백

- **`**` 를 `*` 보다 먼저 등록한다.** 뒤집히면 `**굵게**` 가 기울임이 된다
- **닫는 구분자 직전이 공백이면 매칭하지 않는다.** 그러지 않으면 `2 * 3 * 4` 를
  쓰다가 `* 3 *` 가 기울임으로 변한다
- 변환 후 `removeStoredMark` — `**굵게**보통` 에서 "보통"에 서식이 이어지지 않게

ProseMirror 에는 `textblockTypeInputRule`·`wrappingInputRule` 은 있지만
**마크 규칙이 없어서** 직접 만들었다.

## 테스트가 한 글자씩 타이핑한다

`handleTextInput` 을 직접 불러 실제 타이핑을 재현한다. 입력 규칙은 "마지막에
들어온 글자"를 트리거로 삼으므로 **텍스트를 한 번에 넣으면 규칙이 아예 돌지
않는다.** 정규식만 단위 테스트하면 "패턴은 맞는데 트리거되지 않는" 경우를 놓친다.

## `---` divider 는 텍스트를 버리지 않는다

빈 블록에서만 변환하고, 캐럿을 둘 자리가 없어지므로 뒤에 빈 문단을 만든다.
텍스트가 있는 블록에서는 **변환하지 않고** `---` 를 글자로 남긴다.

## 코드 블록 예외는 지금 해당 사항이 없다

F-01-14 는 "코드 블록 안에서는 입력 규칙을 전부 꺼야 한다"고 하지만
**MVP 12종에 `code` 가 없다.** 대신 규칙이 "이 타입에서 동작하는가"를
레지스트리의 `hasRichText` 로만 판단하게 해뒀다 — `code` 를 추가할 때
`if (type === 'code')` 를 심지 않고 레지스트리에서 끌 수 있다.

## 확인

- **396 tests / pass 396 / skipped 0** (368 → +28)
- 레지스트리가 선언한 접두사 13개 전부 동작 확인
- `Mod-k` 는 `promptLink` 를 준 경우에만 바인딩된다 — URL 을 묻는 것은 UI 의 일이다
