## Summary
- `SessionTail` (Core): one session transcript read incrementally. The first `advance()` takes the last 512 KB exactly as `SessionProgress.read` did; each later one reads only the appended bytes, waits for a torn last line's newline, keeps the window at 512 KB by dropping the oldest entries, and starts over if the file shrank. The head's goal is read once it exists.
- The session's recent sub-agent transcripts (touched within the 30 min login window) get the same treatment: one 128 KB tail each, advanced with the parent, dropped when they age out. Before, every progress recompute re-read all of them — one session with 18 recent agents cost 434 ms (2.3 MB of JSON) per read.
- `SessionProgressModel` keeps a tail per session instead of size+mtime stamps: an unchanged transcript is a stat, a streaming one (the watcher fires once a second) parses its new lines only. `MirrorExporter`'s six panel rows use tails too instead of six fresh 512 KB reads every 30 s.
- `SessionProgress.read` is unchanged in behaviour (`assemble` is shared); `goal` comes off the parsed entries (no second parse of the tail — was half of every read).

## Test plan
- [x] `swift test --filter "SessionTailTests|SessionProgressTests|AwsLogin|PastSessionsTests"` — 64 tests. New `SessionTailTests` (6): first read equals `read`; appends add only the new entries (tokens, nowDoing, lastActivityAt); a partial trailing line waits; the window trims the oldest and a big first read starts at the last maxBytes with the goal still from the head; a shrunk file starts over; a missing file appears later; a sub-agent's failure lands on an agent-only advance and clears when the agent ages out (result equals `SessionProgress.read`).

**Какво променя този PR / What this PR changes**

По искане на библиотеката: **името на библиотеката не се изписва никъде в
страницата за сканиране с телефон.**

Миналият кръг (v2.4.45) го сложи на три места — лентата под заглавието,
заглавието на раздела (оттам го взима и иконата на началния екран) и името на
файла. Заявката тогава беше за **файла**; на екрана името няма какво да каже —
библиотекарят знае в коя библиотека е, а телефонът се носи из читалището и между
хора.

- Махнати са лентата с името и името от заглавието на раздела: страницата пише
  само „Инвентаризация — сканиране“.
- Остава единствено в **имената на файловете** —
  `inventarizaciya-skener-<библиотека>.html` за страницата и
  `inventarizaciya-<библиотека>-<дата>.txt` за изнесения списък.
- Наръчникът, помощта в програмата и упътването в самата страница вече казват
  същото (дотук обещаваха името в заглавието).

**Защо / Why**

Заявка от библиотеката след пускането на v2.4.45.

## Как беше проверено

- Страницата е **генерирана с истински настройки** и проверена: в готовия файл
  няма нито едно споменаване на библиотеката — нито „Яворец“, нито името на
  читалището; заглавието на раздела е неутралното „Инвентаризация — сканиране“;
  елементът с лентата го няма.
- Проверена е и **в истински браузър** (Chromium, Playwright): страницата се
  зарежда без грешки в конзолата, предупреждението за камерата при отваряне като

- При непопълнени настройки: общо име на файла и същото заглавие.
- Тестовете за старото поведение не са махнати, а **заменени** с тестове за

author: freno10
body:
Closes FF-1405. Stacked on #26 (FF-1404) → #25 → #24 → #22 → #20 → #19 → #17 → #15.

## What changed
Every copy-to-clipboard string in the MCP setup said `https://api.midday.ai/mcp` — so a self-hoster following their own dashboard's instructions pointed their AI client at Midday's API and met somebody else's OAuth consent screen.

- The 15 `*-mcp` client configs and the dashboard's own `mcp-setup-instructions.tsx` build the URL through `getMcpServerUrl()`, which derives it from `getApiUrl()`.
- The 16 `installUrl` values pointing at `midday.ai/mcp/<client>` are deleted — those install pages only exist on midday.ai. So is the desktop app's `midday.ai/download`, which FF-1377 already replaced with a local build.
- The MCP server advertised `midday.ai` as its website and an icon on Midday's CDN. It advertises this dashboard, and no icon (there is no self-hosted equivalent).
- The remaining hardcoded `app.midday.ai` links in the Slack notifications and Slack app home go through `getAppUrl()`.

`@midday/utils/envs` gains `tryGetApiUrl()`: the same read as `getApiUrl()` but `null` instead of throwing. Setup instructions are display copy that ends up in a client bundle — a wrong instruction is recoverable, a bundle that throws at module load is not. Everything that routes a request or a customer keeps the strict version.

## Verified
A production build of `apps/dashboard` with `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL=https://api.example.com` bakes `api.example.com/mcp` into the bundle and leaves **no** `api.midday.ai/mcp` anywhere in `.next`. `apps/api` 398 + 14 pass, `packages/utils` 106 pass, `turbo typecheck` on app-store, api, dashboard, website, worker, utils.

## The live check is FF-1433, not this PR
FF-1405 also asked for an end-to-end verification against the real domain — adding the connector in Claude, completing the OAuth consent, listing transactions. That needs a deployed API and a browser, so it is split out as **FF-1433** under the deploy epic and blocked by this ticket. Merge this one freely; the verification is tracked separately and will not be closed with it.

author: zhiyongww
body:
Summary:
Grow each IBGDA peer from its published channel watermark to a canonical requested prefix. The shared PRIMS control path exchanges matching range geometry before allocation and a ready record after graph-external device publication, then advances the host watermark.

Allocate only the missing IBGDA QP groups, loopback QPs, send/recv staging and control MRs, and completion slots. Fixed-capacity descriptor tables retain stable addresses for existing kernels and CUDA graphs. Cold capture uses relaxed capture mode with synchronized nonblocking side streams, so graph replay performs no allocation or connection.

When lazy channels are disabled, preserve the legacy two-phase peer tags, combined per-peer send/recv allocation, bound eager channel layout, and full-capacity first use.

Differential Revision: D114917352

author: zhiyongww
body:
Summary:
Make `MultiPeerTransport::get_device_handle()` the single MCCL readiness boundary for batched per-peer IB channel demand. It validates the complete batch, max-merges duplicate peers in rank order, and prepares the requested peers before kernel arguments are built.

Migrate every MCCL-native PRIMS collective to this boundary: hierarchical AllGather, ring and tree AllReduce, ring ReduceScatter, and SendRecv. Each launcher declares the channel prefix its kernel indexes; SendRecv intentionally requests full capacity until matched per-edge geometry exists. Kernel ABIs remain unchanged.

Add default-off `MCCL_PRIMS_LAZY_CHANNELS` with an optional per-communicator override. Before subtransport exchange, ranks validate the requested mode, peer-channel protocol version, backend geometry and capabilities, plus the symmetric per-edge transport route matrix. Disabled mode retains eager full-capacity materialization and the legacy two-phase peer wire. Physical prefix growth follows in the backend diffs.

Differential Revision: D114917353

author: jather-code-ee
body:
## Summary
- Sets `enableReadyCheck: false` on both the standalone Redis client and the Cluster client's `redisOptions` in `buildRedisClient()`
- Silences the recurring `NOPERM ... 'info' command` warning ioredis emits on every connection against ElastiCache, since the ACL-restricted Redis user has no INFO permission. In this repo's `ioredis@6.0.0`, `_readyCheck` already catches this case and falls back to a `console.warn` ("Skipping the ready check because INFO command fails…") — the client still becomes `ready`. So this isn't a fix for a broken connection, it's removing a benign warning logged on every (re)connect.
- Trade-off: with the ready check disabled, a node returning `-LOADING` (a cold start after failover/restore) has commands sent to it immediately instead of waiting out the load window. `enableOfflineQueue` is on for the cluster nodes, so this should surface as transient errors rather than an outage.
- The ready check is otherwise diagnostic-only; disabling it does not affect functionality (see [ioredis docs](https://github.com/luin/ioredis/wiki/Disable-ready-check))

## Test plan
- [x] `enableReadyCheck: false` set on both Redis and Cluster client configs
- [x] `redis-client.test.js` updated with matching assertions, all tests passing
- [x] `npm run lint` / `npm run format:check` clean
- [ ] No `NOPERM ... info` error lines observed in logs after deploy

Ten options and their measured costs do not fit in a popover, and a popover cannot be read while dragging a slider — which is the only time most of them are interesting. The panel keeps the same content: a `branched | branchless` switch in its header, the three branch options with their measured cost, the rest of `SHADER_FLAGS` (cull weight, unroll limit, polygon / text / SubCurv variants) in a scrolling body, and the live branch census of the last compiled shader as its footer.

The bottom row is always present now (it used to appear only when the program had parameters or solve blocks): 26% of the column on its own, 34% once the other panels join it.

`src/components/GenOptions.tsx` lost its popover plumbing (click-outside / Escape) and is a plain panel.

author: mbroekhuizen-firda
body:
De resultaten van de run van 9 september (branch `resultaten/NVIDIA-RTX-PRO-6000-Blackwell-Server-Edition-600W-20260909-142908`) zijn opgehaald, geanalyseerd en uitgeschreven.

## Wat er gemeten is

De lesvalidatie van negentig minuten, opnieuw op dezelfde RTX PRO 6000, met het nieuwe gedragsmodel van twee assen (persona × werkprofiel), het uitgebreide corpus (`web` + `unity`) en een exacte tokenizer. Dat is precies de controlemeting die `OPZET-VERVOLGMETING.md §2` vraagt.

**De matrix is niet opnieuw gemeten.** De map `20260908-180708_matrix` in die push is op de regeleindes en één toegevoegd veld in `analyse.json` na byte-voor-byte gelijk aan wat er al in de repo stond; alleen de lesvalidatie is nieuw. Die map is daarom niet nog een keer toegevoegd.

## Wat eruit komt

| | Eerste lesvalidatie | Tweede lesvalidatie |
|---|---|---|
| Oordeel | groen | **oranje** |
| p90 doorlooptijd instructie | 69,0 s | **144,4 s** |
| Decodesnelheid per stream (p50) | 53,4 tok/s | 41,0 tok/s |
| KV-piek | 8,5 GB (15,4 %) | 14,6 GB (26,6 %) |
| Wachtrijpiek | 2 verzoeken | 9 verzoeken |
| Fouten / preempties | 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 |

Drie dingen die het rapport onderbouwt:

- **De kaart is niet trager geworden.** Per niveau van gelijktijdigheid decodeert de server even snel als in de eerste run — 113 tegen 116 tok/s bij één verzoek, 85,8 tegen 85,8 bij twee. De uitwijk naar `TRITON_ATTN` verklaart het verschil dus niet. Wat verschoof is waar de klas op die curve zit: de meettijd met acht of meer gelijktijdige verzoeken gaat van 11 % naar 38 %.
- **Vier studenten dragen bijna een derde van de belasting.** De vier op werkprofiel `doorspitten` doen 12 % van de agentstappen en verbruiken 29 % van de rekentijd; hun p90-doorlooptijd is 238 s, op zichzelf rood. Ook `klein` is niet meer groen (99,6 s).
- **De tokenizer bleek de kleinste van de drie wijzigingen.** De eigen telling zat er in beide runs 6,0 % respectievelijk 5,5 % naast ten opzichte van wat vLLM rapporteert — de oude schatting van 4,65 tekens/token was dus een half procentpunt van exact. Alle geheugenuitspraken uit de eerste meting blijven overeind.

## Wat er in deze PR zit

Toegevoegd:

- `results-van-de-gpu/20260909-125855_les/` — de meetgegevens, met LF-regeleindes zoals de rest van de repo
- `CONCLUSIES-TWEEDE-LESVALIDATIE.md` — de analyse
- `RAPPORT-TWEEDE-LESVALIDATIE.html` — dezelfde analyse als leesbaar rapport, met vier grafieken die uit dezelfde CSV's zijn getekend

Bijgewerkt:

- `RESULTATEN.md` — opnieuw gegenereerd met `python3 -m stresstest report` over beide fases (identiek aan wat de pod maakte, op de bronpaden na)
- `CONCLUSIES.md` — conclusie 1 aangemerkt als achterhaald, met verwijzing naar de nieuwe analyse; de rest van dat bestand gaat over de matrix en staat nog
- `OPZET-VERVOLGMETING.md` — §2 noteert dat route 1 half gedaan is en wat er nog openstaat, plus een nieuw punt 8 over het expliciet vastzetten van de attention-backend

## Wat hierna nog moet

De matrix onder het nieuwe gedragsmodel. Sweep, klifzoeker, engine-varianten en kaartvergelijking staan nog allemaal op de oude, lichtere klas, dus `RESULTATEN.md` draagt nu twee gedragsmodellen tegelijk. Draai die eerst op deze kaart (`ATTENTION_BACKEND=TRITON_ATTN scripts/pod.sh all --skip-lesson`, ± € 13) voordat er een andere kaart gehuurd wordt — anders is de 5090-meting opnieuw met niets te vergelijken.

## Controles

`python3 -m pytest tests -q` → 74 geslaagd, 3 overgeslagen. Er is geen code gewijzigd; `RESULTATEN.md` is door het harnas zelf gegenereerd, niet met de hand aangepast.

## Summary
- classify Prisma/Postgres health-check failures into safe coarse categories
- log only the category, never connection strings, hostnames, usernames, passwords, or raw driver errors

## Why
The production health endpoint currently proves the database is unavailable but intentionally suppresses the driver error. Preview does not necessarily share Production database secrets, so this needs to run in Production to identify whether the remaining issue is authentication, reachability, pooler mode, TLS, or general configuration.

author: icapitalan
body:
Fixes sc-19409

### Problem

The library's CI matrix and local runtime lagged behind current stable Elixir/Erlang releases, and several hex dependencies had minor and patch updates available. One pre-existing credo warning in `test_helper.exs` was also blocking a clean CI run.

### Motivation

Keeping the CI matrix current proves the library works against the latest stable runtimes before users upgrade their own apps.

### Proposed Solution

- Adds OTP 29.x + Elixir 1.20.x as the leading matrix pair in CI; advances the dialyzer job to the same
- Bumps local runtime (`.tool-versions`) to Elixir 1.19.5-otp-28 / Erlang 28.5.0.5
- Upgrades all hex deps: ecto 3.13.5 → 3.14.2, credo 1.7.14 → 1.7.19, decimal 2.3.0 → 3.1.1 (major, now required by ecto 3.14), ex_doc 0.39.2 → 0.40.4, plus patch bumps on dialyxir, erlex, jason, makeup, makeup_erlang, telemetry, earmark_parser
- Replaces `use ExUnit.Case` with `import ExUnit.Assertions` in `UserHelpers` — it never defined tests, so the case module was unnecessary and triggered a credo check

### Feedback

No behavior changes. The only non-obvious call is the `decimal` major bump: ecto 3.14 now requires `decimal ~> 3.0`, so that's a forced upgrade, not a choice. Worth a quick scan to confirm nothing in the library touches decimal directly (it doesn't).

author: downfallz
body:
## What

`Sides` is a blunt instrument, and it fails exactly where tuning happens: one declaration is enough to count a
side, so pushing a spell's cost through the roof leaves its sides untouched while nobody can afford to cast it
any more. This adds the numbers that do move, and shows them everywhere a spell appears.

**Per spell, per evaluation.** The combat recorder already saw every resolution; it now tallies them per spell
too. A spell outcome carries declarations that **landed** against ones that **fizzled** (`Resolve` is the column
a cost change moves), and the **damage, healing, energy, stuns, bleeds and buffs** those casts added up to.
`Won-cast` weighs the win correlation by use instead of by side.

**Per match.** A trace now opens on a box score: the most valuable creature, damage dealt per creature as a
chart, one row per creature — damage dealt and taken, healing, kills, casts, fizzles, crits, conditions, energy,
health left, and the spell it declared most — and one row per spell per side. All of it read off the trace,
which already carried every resolution.

**In a comparison.** The spell delta table gains before/after columns for casts, resolve rate and damage,
alongside the win share it already had.

Charts: damage by spell, landed against fizzled (stacked), and damage by creature. They reuse the two player
colours `viewer.css` already defines, which pass the CVD checks (worst adjacent pair ΔE 29.9 protan, 38.2
normal-vision) — no new palette.

## The domain change these numbers needed

`CombatExecution.Apply` discarded what `Creature.TakeDamage`, `Heal`, `GainEnergy` and `Apply` return — damage
capped at the health left, healing at the health missing, nothing at all on a dead creature, a condition its
stacking policy refuses — while `CombatResolution.Outcomes` carries what the action aimed for. Every per-spell
total added here was therefore the proposed size, so a spell that overkills every turn measured as if the health
it could not remove had been removed. Codex caught it.

`Apply` now answers with what landed: the same outcome types carrying the applied amount, an outcome that
changed nothing left out. `CombatActionResolved` and `CombatStep` carry it as `AppliedOutcomes` beside the
resolution, which still holds the attempt. Everything counting what a spell did reads the applied list — the
recorder, the viewer's box score, its side summary, its kill credit, and the console match log, which used to
print `Damage 7` beside a creature with two health dying.

`Applied outcome` is in the glossary, and the `EffectOutcome` and `DamageOutcome` doc comments — which said
"before it is applied" and "damage to deal" — now describe both uses, since the same shapes carry either.

## Two things stated rather than implied

Both would otherwise be read as something they are not, so the code, the console and the page all say them:

1. **A bleed is counted where it is applied, not where it hurts.** Its damage lands at upkeep, and a `Condition`
   does not remember the spell that put it there, so crediting it to a spell is not possible.
2. **`Won-cast` does not read against one half.** A winning side survives longer and therefore acts more, which
   pulls every spell's winner share up together; on a greedy-against-random run the baseline is 60%, not 50%. A
   reader given the number alone would take a spell sitting on the baseline for a winner, so the console and the
   page print the baseline next to the column.

## Checklist

- [x] `dotnet build`, `dotnet test`, and `dotnet format --verify-no-changes` pass locally
- [x] New behaviour has tests; bug fixes have a test that failed before the fix
- [x] Domain names match `docs/domain/glossary.md` (new terms added)
- [x] Hard-to-reverse decisions have an ADR in `docs/adr/`
- [x] `AGENTS.md` and docs still describe reality after this change

## Notes for the reviewer

**Three bugs found by reading output against the thing it described, not by a test failing.** They are the
interesting part of the diff:

- A creature's damage taken left out the bleed it took between rounds: the losing team read 15, 16 and 16 taken
  while each had 20 health and had died. Every row now reconciles at 20 taken, 0/20 left.
- A kill was credited to the actor of the entry a death showed up on. One creature bled out on the entry of its
  own action, and the guard against crediting a creature with its own death then dropped the death entirely —
  three deaths, two kills, nothing saying where the third went. A kill is credited only when the dead creature
  was struck by that very resolution, and deaths belonging to nobody are counted and named.
- The overstated totals above.

**On the test that matters most.** An end-to-end run where nothing overkills totals the same whether the
recorder counts the attempt or the result, which is exactly how counting the wrong list goes unnoticed — so it
is pinned where it is decided, in `CombatStatsRecorderTests`, by handing the recorder an event whose two lists
disagree. Reverting `CombatStatsRecorder` to `resolution.Outcomes` fails two of those tests. `CombatExecution`
has six tests of its own (overkill, overheal, a dead target refusing all four outcome kinds, a stacking policy
refusing a condition on a live one, what lands in full, a fizzle), and `MatchTests` pins that the aggregate
publishes the applied list rather than the computed one.

**On the viewer.** No JS test runner here, so it was driven in a browser against a real 618-event trace and two
real evaluations, with the chart configs asserted through a stubbed `Chart` so a malformed one throws.

**One thing I got wrong and fixed.** The sample trace is a single minified line; I rewrote it indented, which
turned a handful of added keys into 61,119 added lines. It is rebuilt from the file on `main` so nothing but the
new key differs, and the diff is back to its real size.

author: andybons
body:
## Problem

A `prefix_changed` chain refusal named the first differing input item by rendering `"input[<n>]"` into `provider.RequestMetadata.ChainRefusalDetail` (added in #266, commit 155ede5891d3). That locator does not survive the log pipeline. Live rows in the fleet's BetterStack `boxes` source read `chain_refusal_detail="input"`, so an operator can see THAT request assembly rewrote history the server already held, but never WHICH item — the only actionable half.

## Where the truncation happens

**BetterStack's ingest**, not harness and not the fleet's Vector collector.

Evidence, from source 2670209 over the last 14 days:

1. **Every** stored `prefix_changed` row carries a *pair* of fields — the index is not lost, it is moved:
   ```
   "chain_refusal":"prefix_changed","chain_refusal_detail":"input","chain_refusal_detail_json":[139]
   ```
   Grouped over all 20 refusal rows: `[139]`×8, `[101]`×6, `[0]`×2, `[85]`, `[79]`, `[2]`. So the ingest received the whole `input[139]` and read it as a path expression, splitting the base name from the subscript. Nothing upstream truncated anything.

2. **The `<field>` / `<field>_json` split is BetterStack's own convention, and it happens on rows that never touch Vector.** Querying every `_json` sibling in the source turns up `prompt_json` (14 rows, `resource.attributes.service.name=claude-code`) and `error_json` (2 rows, `boxes-control-plane`) — both shipped by the control plane's own OTLP exporter, with `json_parsed` absent, i.e. they bypass the log-collector DaemonSet entirely. A transform that also fires on the OTLP path cannot be Vector's.

3. **The Vector config is incapable of it.** `deploy/boxes/templates/logcollector-configmap.yaml` in `meetneptune/boxes` does `parse_json` → `merge(., object!(parsed), deep: true)` → assigns `.json_parsed`, `.namespace`, `.pod`, `.container`, `.node`, `.box_id`, `.service`. No operation there splits a string value, and none invents a `<name>_json` key. It also never rewrites `.message`, yet the split appears *inside* the nested `message` copy too.

4. **The producer was emitting the bracketed form.** The shipped binary (`go version -m` → `v0.0.0-20260909162629-155ede5891d3`, exactly the #266 merge) contains the literal `input[`.

**No consumer-side change is needed in `meetneptune/boxes`.** The collector is innocent.

## Design

The index travels as its own field, in a shape no pipeline can mangle.

- `ChainRefusalDetail` keeps the **NAME** cases — a wire property name for `property_changed`, and `input_shorter_than_prefix` for the prefix refusal that has no index — and stays free of the `[`/`]` that trigger the split.
- New `ChainRefusalItem *int` carries the **INDEX**, and only `prefix_changed` sets it. A pointer rather than a plain `int` because item `0` is a real and common answer (assembly rewrote the head of the input), so "no item" needs a value of its own; a bare `int` with `omitempty` would silently drop it.
- A number is also directly aggregatable — group `chain_refusal_item` within `prefix_changed` to find which assembly site is rewriting history — which the rendered string never was.

The `provider/AGENTS.md` rule holds: a refusal still carries no item content and no response ID.

## Semantic change

`turn_metrics` no longer emits `chain_refusal_detail` for an indexed prefix refusal; it emits `chain_refusal_item` as a JSON number. `property_changed` and `input_shorter_than_prefix` are unchanged. A chained call still emits none of the three keys.

`docs/design/codex-websocket-chaining.md`'s refusal table and `docs/engine-request-cycle.md`'s `turn_metrics` field list are updated to match.

## Verification

Red-verified against the exact mechanism: with the new field present but the old rendering left intact, the tests failed on `prefix refusal item = <nil>, want a reported 0` and `locator(139) detail = "input[139]", want empty`.

- `TestInputItemLocatorKeepsTheIndexOutOfTheDetailString` (new) pins the reported regression.
- `TestWebSocketChainRefusalMetadataNamesTheReason` (extended) drives a prefix refusal through the real pool and asserts the reported item is `0` with an empty detail; the property case asserts no item.
- `TestTurnMetricsReportsChainRefusal` (extended) asserts the emitted record holds `"chain_refusal_item":4`, holds `"chain_refusal_item":0` for item 0, carries no `"input["` and no `chain_refusal_detail` for an indexed refusal, and still names the property for `property_changed`.

`go build ./...`, `go vet ./...`, `gofmt`, and `go test -race ./...` all pass. The rebuilt binary no longer contains the `input[` literal and now contains `chain_refusal_item`.

Updates #266

author: lewing
body:
<!-- -->
Fixes browser-Wasm CoreCLR ReadyToRun failures introduced after #133218 while preserving shared `U`, `UG`, and `UM` unboxing stubs and almost all of their binary-size benefit.

## Corrected root-cause analysis

The initial version of this PR replaced `U`/`UG` with per-method managed thunks based on an ABI-mismatch hypothesis. That approach and its portable-prestub changes have been removed. The revised patch does not change the shared-stub calling conventions or lookup keys.

NESM inspection stopped immediately before the failing Test23 `call_indirect`: the call expected five `i32` parameters, but the selected table slot was zero (a null function reference). The expected parameter count alone did not establish a `U` versus `UG` mismatch. The observed delay-load fixup resolved to a non-unboxing shared target requiring a generic context, whose portable entrypoint lacked an R2R-to-interpreter adapter such as `IvTiS1p`.

Replacing a compiled per-method unboxing thunk with a structural assembly stub lost dependencies previously introduced by compiling the thunk's managed body. There are two distinct transitions:

- **Interpreter -> unboxing stub:** needs an `M` adapter for the full managed unboxing signature, for example `MS56Tp`.
- **Unboxing stub -> target:** needs an `I` adapter for the target signature, including its generic context where applicable, for example `IS56Tip` or `IvTiS1p`, so its portable entrypoint is callable before the target's native body is published.

Structural sharing also allows the runtime to find a shared stub for a generic instantiation Crossgen2 never compiled. A matching Wasm function shape does not imply that the exact managed transition cookie exists: different struct sizes can share the same structural stub but require different interpreter adapters. The actual `GitHub_19361` execution exposed this case with a missing `MS56Tp` cookie.

## Changes

- Add a per-target dependency node retaining the shared stub, compiled target, interpreter-to-R2R adapter for the unboxing signature, and R2R-to-interpreter adapter for the target signature.
- Keep these dependencies per managed target rather than on the structurally shared node, so signatures with the same Wasm shape but different managed layouts retain their distinct adapters.
- Before publishing a shared unboxing stub, require the exact incoming interpreter cookie and callable code in the target portable entrypoint. An installed R2R-to-interpreter adapter counts as callable code; this does not require a precompiled native target body.
- If either transition is unavailable, use the existing interpreted IL-stub fallback. R2R callers independently root their call-signature `I` adapters through the existing call-site recording machinery.
- Extend the existing Wasm generic-dispatch tests with a 56-byte struct return alongside the 16-byte case, checking distinct adapters while retaining the original shared-stub assertions.

## Evidence and validation

Browser-Wasm **Release CoreCLR under Node.js 26.4.0**, with explicitly regenerated and Wasm-validated CoreLib, LINQ, and test images:

| Runtime case | Actual execution evidence | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `LoaderClassloaderGenerics`, `DisplayName~genrecur.dll` | `Test23 OK`, matching `Passed test` line | Exit 100 |
| `Regressions`, `DisplayName~genrecur.dll` | `Test23 OK`, matching `Passed test` line | Exit 100 |
| `Regression_NoOptimize_r_1`, `Repro.Program.TestEntryPoint` | `Starting stress loop`, `Result: Completed Normally`, matching `Passed test` line | Exit 100 |

The earlier `GitHub_19361` name filter matched no test; earlier success claims using that filter were invalid. The results above use the actual fully qualified method name and confirm that the stress loop executed. Earlier stale CoreLib images were also replaced explicitly rather than relying on layout generation to refresh them.

Additional validation:

- Browser Release runtime and corerun build: succeeded.
- Wasm `ILCompiler.ReadyToRun.Tests`: 75 passed, 37 target-inapplicable skips.
- Host macOS arm64 generic-dispatch tests: 3 passed, 2 Wasm-only skips.
- Negative dependency checks: removing only `I(target)` fails on missing `IS16Tip`; removing only `M(unboxing)` fails on missing `MS56Tp`. Restoring both passes.

The full CI outer-loop matrix and a browser-hosted run have not been rerun locally.

## Binary size

Optimized browser `System.Private.CoreLib` images using `--optimize --generate-unboxing-stubs` in the local comparison:

| Variant | Bytes |
|---|---:|
| Earlier fully shared prototype | 26,991,640 |
| Revised shared stubs with transition dependencies | 26,993,234 |
| Superseded per-method `U`/`UG` fallback | 27,387,567 |

The revised image adds **1,594 bytes** over the earlier fully shared prototype and saves **394,333 bytes** compared with the superseded fallback, retaining approximately **99.6%** of the size reduction in that comparison. This supersedes the initial description's claim that the fix gives back nearly the entire saving.

Fixes #133491

> This pull request description and investigation summary were generated with GitHub Copilot.

author: ansavva
body:
## Why

`useNativeFocusRing()` gives a leaf a ring to spread. Spread it on the focusable
element and you are done — `outlineStyle: 'solid'` replaces whatever the
platform would draw there. Spread it on a **wrapper**, and the focused element
inside is untouched: under react-native-web it kept Chrome's own
`outline: auto 1px`, painted *inside* the owned accent ring.

Two rings, the inner one a browser default in a colour this package does not
own — it follows neither `tokens.json` nor a `ThemeProvider` override, and it
is the exact thing `native-focus.native.ts` was written in 0.18.0 to stop
("the web pane ringed in brass, the native pane in Chrome blue").

`PasswordInput` and `NumberInput` are the two leaves that ring a wrapper: both
draw the box on a row so a button can sit beside a bare `TextInput`.

### This is the other half of #20

0.21.2 gave a ring to native controls that had **none** — PasswordInput's own
Show/Hide toggle, and all of DataGrid. These two had one already, on the
wrapping row; what leaked was the focused element *inside* it. Keeping them
apart was deliberate, and it is the reason `native-focus.native.ts`'s header
gives: *"One control having the fix is worse than none having it, because it
makes the design look deliberate."* Each PR closes a whole class rather than
half of two.

### Rejected: `outlineWidth: 0`

The obvious cancel, and it does not work. Chrome ignores `outline-width` for an
`auto` outline and paints its ring regardless. It has to be
`outlineStyle: 'none'`, which RN 0.86's `ViewStyle` type does not admit
(`'solid' | 'dotted' | 'dashed'`) even though react-native-web forwards it to
CSS verbatim — the same platform/type gap the `aria-*` casts throughout these
leaves already document. Hence one contained cast.

### Rejected: fixing it twice, in the leaves

`suppressPlatformFocusRing` lives beside `nativeFocusRing` in
`lib/native-focus.native.ts` rather than as a literal in each leaf, for the
reason the ring itself lives there: a third wrapper-ringing leaf should have
something to reach for instead of re-deriving the cast and the reasoning. On a
real device it is inert — React Native paints no default ring to cancel.

## What

- `lib/native-focus.native.ts` — new `suppressPlatformFocusRing`, documented
  with why `outlineWidth: 0` is not it and why no jsdom test can see this.
- `password-input.native.tsx`, `number-input.native.tsx` — the inner
  `TextInput` spreads it, so only the row's owned ring paints.
- A permanent regression story on each, `No browser focus ring`. Named away
  from "one ring" on purpose: after #20 a PasswordInput row legitimately holds
  *two* rings, one per focusable control. The invariant here is narrower — a
  single focused **element** paints one ring, and it is ours.

**Version:** `@ansavva/design-system` 0.21.3 → **0.21.4, a patch**. Consumers on
`^0.21.0` take it on their next install; no range to widen.

Changelog entry written at the top of `packages/design-system/CHANGELOG.md`.

## How to review

**Before** — the native pane, focused, with the fix backed out. The browser's
ring nested inside the owned one, on both components:

![no-browser-ring-before.png](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6cebca3d-8b9a-41c0-887f-3317b0a93714)

**After** — one ring, matching the design, in both schemes:

![no-browser-ring-after.png](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3071898c-068d-4598-97de-af9dd57dcc47)

Both are the new `No browser focus ring` stories: the play leaves the native
field focused, so the capture *is* the focused state rather than a posed one.
The web pane is unfocused in both — the comparison to make is the native ring
against the design, not pane against pane.

The subtle part is **why a real click**. A programmatic `.focus()` does not
engage Chrome's `:focus-visible` heuristic and reports `outline-style: none`,
which would make the assertion pass against the very bug it exists to catch.
The plays click, and they assert the row's `solid` ring **first** — that is what
proves focus actually landed, without which the second assertion is vacuous.

## Verification

Re-run in full after rebasing onto `main` at 0.21.3 (#18, #19 and #20 all
landed under this branch).

- **The affected set was measured, not guessed.** A Playwright sweep tabbed
  through all **230 workbench stories × 2 colour schemes** with real key
  presses, recording every element computing `outline-style: auto` while
  focused and classifying by whether an ancestor painted an owned ring.
  Before: the wrapper-ring class was exactly 20 rows, 10 `forms-numberinput--*`
  and 10 `forms-passwordinput--*`, light and dark. After: **zero**.
- **The new plays fail against the bug.** Backed the fix out and ran them: both
  failed with `expected 'auto' to be 'none'`. Restored, both pass — in
  `test:a11y:light` and `test:a11y:dark`.
- `npm run ci` green on the rebased tree: token drift, skills, changelog,
  format, lint, all three typecheck programs + workbench + scripts, unit tests,
  and axe over every story in both schemes. **230 story tests pass per scheme**,
  the two new regression stories included.
- Looked at both components in the workbench, both panes, both schemes.

### What was NOT verified

- **On a real device.** There is no simulator in this loop. The change is inert
  there by construction — React Native paints no default focus ring, so there
  is nothing to cancel — but that is reasoning, not a measurement.
- **`outlineStyle: 'none'` against react-native-web's own types.**
  react-native-web ships no type declarations, so the cast is checked against
  RN 0.86's types and its *runtime* behaviour is what the browser assertions
  cover.

### Found and deliberately left alone

The same sweep turns up a **much larger** separate population, unchanged by
this PR: **28 components** whose focused native element has *no* owned ring and
shows Chrome's directly — Accordion, Alert, Calendar, Checkbox, Dialog, Field,
Switch, Tabs, Toast, Tooltip, Wheel and more. That is #20's class, and #20
covered two of its members (PasswordInput's toggle and DataGrid — both now
confirmed clean). Folding the rest in here would bundle two responsibilities
into one publish, so it stays out. Worth its own PR.

body:
## What

Lets the feature owner attach reference documents to a plan interview, and makes that the explicit trigger for an optional read-only run.

The interview's `plan_interview.round` / `.synthesis` / `.critique` passes run **no-tools** by default. Attaching one or more reference documents on the *Feature brief* step switches those passes to `HeadlessRunner::run_read_only`, so the interviewer can read the attached documents **and** the surrounding codebase while shaping questions and the plan. Nothing changes for an interview with no attachments.

## How it works

- **Attaching** — `Ctrl+D` on the brief step opens a `ratatui_explorer` file browser (`AppMode::PlanInterviewAttachDoc`, a deliberate sibling of `BrowsingPath` that stashes the live `PlanInterviewState` and restores it on confirm/cancel). `Ctrl+X` drops the last attachment. Cap of 4. Any readable text file anywhere on disk; `plan_interview::validate_attachment` rejects a directory, an oversize file (>512 KB), a binary sniff, a duplicate, or the cap — each with a stated reason.
- **Reachability** — `prepare_attached_docs(workdir, docs)` runs right before each pass. An in-workdir doc is referenced where it lies; an external one is copied into `<workdir>/.amf/interview-docs/` (gitignored scratch, via the existing `extension::generated_amf_subdir`) so a CWD-scoped read-only harness can open it. That folder is wiped at the start of every pass and by `App::clear_plan_interview_doc_staging` on interview accept/abort. A doc that has moved or gone unreadable is dropped and reported — never fatal.
- **Prompts** — the five interview input builders carry an `attached_documents` array (`path` + `origin`); `round` / `synthesis` / `critique` templates gained a `{{tool_access_note}}` token resolving to either `TOOL_ACCESS_NOTE_NONE` / `CRITIQUE_TOOL_ACCESS_NOTE_NONE` (historical no-tools wording) or `TOOL_ACCESS_NOTE_ATTACHED` (the read-only exception). The drift-guard sync test confirms byte-identical default rendering when nothing is attached.
- **Persistence** — `PlanInterviewRecord.attached_docs: Vec<String>`, `MIGRATION_035` (column backfilled `'[]'`). A resumed or re-run interview restores the list; paths are re-validated at dispatch, not on resume.
- **UI** — the brief step grows a `Reference docs · N/4 · interview runs read-only` panel (missing files flagged), footer hints gain `Ctrl+D` / `Ctrl+X`, and the optional-AI consent screen adds a line noting the passes run read-only and a token estimate is then only a floor.

## Files

New: `src/app/plan_interview_attach.rs`, `src/handlers/plan_interview_attach.rs`, `src/ui/dialogs/plan_interview_attach.rs`, plus a `plan-interview-attach-doc` screenshot scenario + seeds.
Changed: `src/plan_interview.rs`, `src/app/plan_interview.rs`, `src/app/state.rs`, `src/db/{migrations,plan_interviews}.rs`, prompt defaults, dashboard / dialogs / status / mouse / handler dispatch, `CHANGELOG.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `docs/backlog/plan-mode-interview-plan.md`.

## Testing

- `cargo test -j 2` — all 2532 pass, including the prompt drift-guard, migration count/idempotency tests, and 6 new tests (`validate_attachment`, `prepare_attached_docs` staging/cleanup, the round-prompt read-only switch, DB `attached_docs` round-trip through `finalize_draft`).
- `cargo clippy` — clean.
- Manual: captured from a throwaway AMF instance via the new scenario. Screenshot walkthrough is in the section below; it drives up to the optional-AI consent step and aborts before accepting (accepting spends real tokens).

author: paulohenriquevn
body:
Four commits hardening and de-duplicating the workflows. Everything below was measured against this repository's own run history rather than asserted, and both linters were re-checked against a deliberately broken file so that "clean" means checked rather than not-run.

## Security

- `postgres:15-alpine` pinned by digest. The tag is mutable and this is the job that asserts `SKIP LOCKED` race-safety, so a silent minor bump under it turns a real regression into "flaky CI". Digest read from the registry, not recalled.
- `backmerge.yml` no longer grants `pull-requests: write` at the workflow level; its only job already declares it.
- `codeql.yml` passes `repository.private` through `env:` instead of interpolating it into a shell script.
- A `release` environment now guards the publish job, restricted to `main`. `release.yml` carries `workflow_dispatch`, so before this anyone with write access could dispatch it from an arbitrary branch and mint a `theokit-release` App token there. No reviewer gate — `branch-protection.json` rejects that by name.
- `NPM_TOKEN` and `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` deleted. Unreferenced on all three branches, and no workflow uses `secrets: inherit`. The first was one careless `env:` away from silently disabling npm trusted publishing and provenance, exactly as `release.yml`'s own notes warn.

## Cost

Of the last 40 CI runs, **six commits ran the full workflow twice on the identical head SHA** — once from the push merging `workspace -> develop`, once from the `develop -> main` pull request opened seconds later. Four pairs started within 33 seconds of each other, at ~29 billed minutes each. `concurrency` could never collapse them: it keys on `github.ref`, which differs between the two events by construction.

The same tree was validated four times end to end — tree `007672610` by the workspace PR, the develop push, the develop PR and the main push.

So `push` now fires on `main` only, across the six workflows that shared the pattern. No verdict is lost: a commit reaching `develop` arrived through a pull request that ran these checks and immediately becomes the head of the one that runs them again, and a direct push to `develop` is forbidden by `rules/git-safety.md` and blocked by `validate-command.sh`. `main` stays because SonarQube measures new code against its analysis of the default branch.

`preview.yml` had the same duplicate on a ~1 minute bill and is now keyed on the commit rather than the ref.

**The cost, stated rather than discovered:** Actions caches are scoped per branch and pull requests read the base branch's cache. `develop` no longer writes one, so a `workspace -> develop` pull request may restore a colder pnpm store. Setup measured 30s of a 409s job with the cache warm; that step is the ceiling on the regression, against ~29 minutes saved per promotion.

## Measured and deliberately NOT changed

- The 97 Claude Code runs in three days are all `skipped` at 0s.
- The node matrix tests the floor and the ceiling of the supported range, not one thing twice.
- Setup is 30s of a 409s job — step-level caching had nothing left to give.
- `fetch-depth: 0` on the changelog gate costs 3 seconds over 2505 commits; trading a working, documented gate for two seconds is churn.

## What this pull request is for

Validating the trigger changes. A workflow that runs on a push uses the file on *that* branch, so these take effect only once merged — this PR is the first real exercise of them, and of the renamed `postgres-integration` check (safe to rename: PR #710 merged while that workflow never ran, which a required context could not have done).

author: rhprasad0
body:
## Summary

First of six sequential slices restoring the production delivery pipeline (refs #304).

- Add a fixed-target, explicitly approved baseline-adoption helper for the existing production pricing 1.3.0 / Oracle 1.14.0 schemas. Verify canonical application definitions, ownership, grants, versions, and route count; atomically establish pricing ownership and private baseline history.
- Add the production migration IAM prerequisite, scoped to the protected production environment, main ref, fixed reusable workflow, and exact production database user.
- Document the bounded adoption procedure and its approval boundary. No workflow or deployed infrastructure/database mutation is included in this PR.

## Validation

- 41 focused offline adoption tests and a test-owned local PostgreSQL 17/PostGIS 3.5 adoption/drift/rollback/rerun test, including production-equivalent constraint creation order, trigger/RLS/policy/rewrite drift, and two-session lock contention.
- 16 release-manifest verifier tests; the existing IAM input digest is refreshed, with all other input and package hashes, permissions, and mutation contracts unchanged.
- Ruff check/format, full `v2` pyright, delivery IAM rendering contracts, Terraform formatting and backend-disabled validation, and diff whitespace checks.
- Independent project-graph checker passed; concurrent security review reported no findings.
- Bounded read-only production comparison matches all 36 canonical application-definition fingerprints. No production adoption or database mutation was run.

## Delivery boundary

Live adoption currently fails closed on confirmed production PostGIS type-permission drift: `geometry` and `geography` grant `PUBLIC USAGE` and lack explicit `oracle_owner USAGE`. The owner approved adding a separate reviewed prerequisite repair slice; live execution still requires explicit approval. This PR neither performs nor silently includes that repair.

This PR does not itself restore production. The owner retains merge and protected production approvals. After merge, subsequent slices add immutable development evidence, release admission/private production planning, protected migrations, exact-plan apply/health, and live restoration proof. No arbitrary production migrations, reset, application-agent changes, or automatic adoption invocation are added here.

Live adoption still requires fresh production evidence and explicit human approval under the runbook. Existing production state must satisfy the checks; drift fails closed.

## PR feedback repairs

- Reject unexpected triggers, policies, row-security flags, and rewrite rules both before and after adoption; retain canonical view rules and enabled internal constraint triggers.
- Hold fixed application-relation locks through commit; validate competing DDL timeout and rollback with a deterministic, binary-pipe subprocess handshake.
- Isolate mocked tests from ambient CA and AWS endpoint overrides while retaining production rejection checks.
- Correct the stale IAM input digest that failed trusted development release verification. No workflow change or gate bypass is needed.
- GitGuardian's original synthetic-fixture finding was marked false positive by the owner; the fixture now generates its dummy value at runtime.
- Correct stale OIDC documentation without altering existing deploy/planner trust contracts or weakening the migration role's exact workflow restriction.

This is a test-only refactor that centralizes Duco's repeated scheduled coordinator update sequence.

Several Duco platform tests need to verify behavior after the normal polling interval elapses. Each of those tests previously repeated the same three operations:

- Advance frozen time by `SCAN_INTERVAL`.
- Fire Home Assistant's time-changed event.
- Wait for background tasks so the scheduled coordinator update has completed.

The sequence is now represented by `async_fire_coordinator_update()` in the shared Duco test module. The helper deliberately uses the real integration polling interval and waits for background tasks, so each caller continues to exercise the same public, time-driven coordinator path as before.

The helper replaces only literal copies of that complete sequence in binary sensor, fan, setup, number, and sensor tests. The surrounding setup, mocked client responses, state assertions, error handling, and recovery assertions are unchanged. This keeps the test scenarios independently readable while making the shared transition explicit and reducing the chance that one future test changes the polling trigger incompletely.

The diff touches six files because that polling transition was duplicated across those platform suites, not because the integration behavior or its coverage is changing. All existing Duco test cases remain collected and passing.

author: necco-c
body:
Adds `sqlsnoop`, an eBPF SQL statement monitor for Postgres and MySQL. It reads every statement any process on the host sends off the socket, with the parameter values the driver actually bound, and opens on a ranked list of the ones worth looking at.

## Reviewer action items - [x] ~~Apply the About description~~ — applied at repo creation - [x] ~~Apply the topic tags~~ — applied, all 15, verified unmangled - [x] ~~Add a LICENSE file~~ — Apache-2.0, byte-identical to exectop's - [ ] **Resolve one flagged claim:** the README says "Verified on 6.1, 6.6, 6.12 and bpf-next". Only 6.12.105 arm64 was verified directly by hand; the other three are what this PR's CI run covers. If the matrix goes green this claim is grounded and the box can be ticked as-is. - [ ] Decide whether the four GIFs (9.7 MB) stay committed. Currently committed, matching every sibling, so the README renders on GitHub with no external hosting. - [ ] Review the remaining flagged claims in the reviewer notes (10 of 11 are grounding 1, measured directly). ## What it does Three views. **findings** opens first, because a live feed at forty statements a second is twenty rows of routine lookups with one real problem somewhere in them, and spotting it is work the tool should do rather than delegate: ``` WHEN WHAT COST STATEMENT ▸ 11:55:52 check ORDER BY with no LIMIT — sort… 19.0ms SELECT o.status, count(*), avg(o.total) FROM orders o… 11:55:50 n+1 ×19 worst of 5 bursts 10.8ms SELECT id, status, total FROM orders WHERE customer_id = ? 11:55:52 check SELECT * fetches every column 1.37ms SELECT * FROM inventory LIMIT ? ``` **feed** is one line per statement with values inline and repeated shapes folded; **top** collapses by shape and ranks by total database time. An N+1 is the bug this exists to find, and it is invisible to almost everything else: each of the two hundred lookups is fast and correctly indexed, so a slow-query log stays empty and an APM shows a slow endpoint with nothing to blame. ## How it works One BPF program covers both wire protocols. They frame messages differently but both are length-prefixed and tag-then-payload with the statement text at a shallow offset, which is the shared seam. The kernel decides only "is this a SQL frame and where does the text start", copies a fixed window, and stops. All parsing, normalization and parameter decoding happens in JS, where it can be unit tested. Three facts about real client behaviour shaped the design, each found by running against live traffic rather than reading the specs: - **Clients prepare once and execute many times**, so most executions carry only values. Attribution goes through the prepared-statement name in the Bind message. A workload issuing 84 lookups sent 36 statements and 99 parameter blocks, and those unattributed executions *are* the N+1 — a model needing a statement per execution cannot see what it exists to find. - **Clients do not wait for replies**, so the kernel keeps a per-socket ring of send timestamps rather than one slot. With one slot, 120 of 135 replies had no timestamp to pair against and were dropped in the kernel. - **Pipelining clients send values before their statement**, so orphaned parameter blocks are held briefly, guarded on placeholder count and age. ## Verification - **43 unit tests** over the analysis layer, needing no kernel and no database (`node --test test/lib.test.mjs`). They caught two real bugs on their first run: `verbOf` classified `WITH x AS (…) DELETE FROM t` as a *read*, so a CTE-wrapped write was never counted as a write nor checked for a missing `WHERE`; and the leading-wildcard `LIKE` check could never fire, because its condition reduced to a test of the normalized shape where the `%` has already been replaced. - **All 6 BPF programs verify** on 6.12.105 arm64. `on_sendmsg` sits at 345,443 instructions, 35% of the 1M ceiling — down from 686,652 (69%) after cutting the Postgres frame loop from six frames to four, which is the change this PR's CI matrix is most worth watching. - **`make clean && make` is silent.** No warnings. - **Live capture verified** against PostgreSQL 17 and MySQL 8 with psycopg2, psycopg3, MySQLdb and both command-line clients, on plaintext and inside TLS. Note for anyone reproducing locally: run `make veristat` with `sudo`. Unprivileged it reports every program as `failure` with zero instructions, which is `-EPERM` from the loading probe rather than a verifier rejection, and it is a convincing false alarm. ## Known limits, stated in the README - Go and Java clients over TLS are invisible: neither exposes a C symbol to hook. Plaintext works for both. - Clients on a Unix socket are invisible; the probes hook `tcp_sendmsg`. This is the most common cause of an empty first screen. - Latency is socket-paired rather than exact, since neither protocol carries a request id. - Statements are captured to 256 bytes, parameter blocks to 192, and truncation is marked. - An 8-byte binary parameter is ambiguous (`int8`/`float8`/timestamp) because the Bind message does not carry the type. Ambiguous values are marked and the runnable-statement form refuses to build rather than handing you SQL that runs against the wrong row. Reviewer notes with the full flagged-claims table live in `~/code/yeet-scripts-readmes/sqlsnoop/notes.md`.

body:
# Description

The core's 0.7.0-rc.2 takes the reply destination from the reply type instead of the mount site,
and this crate no longer builds against rc.1, so the dependency floor moves with it.

Both scaffolds declare the confirmation subject on `Confirmation` itself and mount the handler with
the bare `publish` clause. That is the form the core guide teaches first, and it is the right one
here: for a starter service the confirmation subject is a property of the message, not a decision
one mount makes. Rendered and compiled both scaffolds locally; the generated AsyncAPI document
reports `confirmations` as the resolved destination.

The crate had no test of the reply form at all, so the two new harness tests are fresh coverage
rather than a port: one reply type that fixes its own destination, one that leaves it to the mount
site, both asserted through the publish log.

The documentation change is deliberately narrow. The broker page stops spelling the clause with an
argument and says nothing about where a reply lands, because that rule holds on every broker and
the core's publishing guide owns it. The full style pass on this page is a separate pull request.

Found on the way and not fixed here: the `.out(Reply, ..)` paragraph on the broker page is followed
by a snippet that publishes from a startup hook instead, and no `.out(Reply, ..)` call is compiled
anywhere in this crate.

- [x] Bug fix (a non-breaking change that resolves an issue)

## מה זה

**תיעוד בלבד** — `CLAUDE.md` בלבד, +24/−2. אין שינוי בקוד האתר.

## מה השתנה

**המשימה האחרונה מרשימת החוסמים נסגרה.** הכתובת הוסתרה ואזורי השירות הוגדרו ב‑GBP, אומת מול צילום מסך של הממשק.

מיקום העסק מוגדר כ**"ללא מיקום; רק משלוחים ושירותים בבית הלקוח"** — צורה חזקה יותר מהסתרת כתובת בלבד: זו הצהרה מפורשת של Service‑Area Business, המודל הנכון למורה נהיגה שנוסע אל התלמידים. ביאליק 4 נשארת אצל גוגל לצורכי אימות ואינה מוצגת לציבור.

**אזורי שירות:** ירושלים, מעלה אדומים. השני לא הופיע בפרופיל כלל עד עכשיו — חצי מהשוק היה בלתי נגיש דרך ה‑Local Pack.

## ✅ התאמת שעות מלאה בין הפרופיל לאתר

כל שבעת הימים תואמים. הטבלה המלאה נכנסה לתיעוד.

⚠️ **זה מאשרר החלטה מהבוקר.** בעל העסק אמר בעל פה "8 עד 17" אבל הוסיף "כמו שגוגל רשמו", ולקחנו מה‑GBP מילולית — כולל **שני ב‑09:00** ו**שישי עד 12:00**. לו היינו מיישרים ל"8 עד 17" באופן גורף, האתר היה סותר את הפרופיל בשני ימים.

**הכלל שנרשם: כשהוראה בעל פה מסכמת מקור כתוב, המקור הכתוב מנצח.**

`areaServed` באתר תואם לאזורי השירות בפרופיל, וה‑`address` ב‑Schema מכיל `addressLocality` בלבד בלי `streetAddress` — בדיוק כמו הפרופיל. ההחלטה המתועדת מ‑14/04/2026 מחזיקה ואומתה מול המציאות.

## הערה תפעולית שנרשמה

PR #76 מוזג ב‑**squash**, כך שהיסטוריית ענף הפיתוח התפצלה מ‑main. הענף יושר ל‑main ב‑`--force-with-lease` **רק אחרי** ש‑`git diff origin/main origin/<branch>` החזיר ריק — כלומר אומת שאין תוכן שלא מוזג. שווה לבדוק את זה לפני כל יישור ענף בריפו הזה.

author: cryppadotta
body:
## Thinking Path

> - Paperclip manages AI agents and their work.
> - The native runner receives provider events and saves task answers.
> - A task completion tool reports the task result.
> - That tool does not end the provider turn.
> - The old grace timer could stop the stream before the final answer arrived.
> - This change keeps the stream open until the provider ends the turn.

## Linked Issues or Issue Description

**What happened?**

The completion-tool grace timer could interrupt a provider after five seconds.
The task could lose the final answer even though the provider was still working.

**Expected behavior**

Save the completion result and continue receiving events. Save the final answer
before response selection. Let the provider turn-end event end the normal stream.

**Steps to reproduce**

1. Start a native task.
2. Have the provider call paperclip_finish.
3. Delay the final assistant answer for more than five seconds.
4. Observe that the old timer can stop the answer.

**Paperclip version or commit**

Reproduced on the implementation branch before this fix. Replayed onto master
at 6abeb6733. Related provider authority work: Refs #13092.

**Deployment mode**

Local source checkout with the native runner and Codex.

## What Changed

- Remove the completion-tool interrupt timer.
- Drain pending event persistence before selecting the visible response.
- Keep task completion validation, provider errors, cancellation, waits, and goals.
- Add delayed-answer, slow-persistence, replay, failure, and cancellation tests.
- Add a browser regression through the production native persistence path.
- Document the distinction between task completion and provider turn end.

## Verification

- Focused native runtime, controller, and response-selection tests passed on the implementation checkout.
- Repository typecheck and build passed. Repository test groups passed after the documented fixture and resource retests.
- A fresh deterministic browser task kept a delayed final answer after refresh and used one provider run.
- Fresh real Codex tasks also returned and saved their full answers.
- After replay onto current master: 165 native transport tests passed using the release runner. The full native runtime tests also passed.
- The production browser regression passed with a 31-second final-answer delay, refresh, one saved answer, and one provider run. Test-drive teardown was verified for graceful exit and forced termination.
- All GitHub checks passed on the final PR head. Greptile is 5/5 with no unresolved review threads.

## Risks

- A provider must still send its terminal event. Existing execution timeouts and cancellation remain active.
- Completion reports must not hide later provider errors.
- No new task state, recovery policy, or database migration is included.

## Model Used

OpenAI Codex, GPT-6 (`gpt-6-astra`). Used for reasoning, code edits, tool use,
and test execution. The exact context-window limit is not exposed in this
session. Real-provider acceptance used Codex CLI 0.153.4 with `gpt-5.6-sol`.

author: mobeenabdullah
body:
The changeset added by #1667 opens its frontmatter and never closes it — the file carries one `---` where it needs two, so the parser reads the whole document as unterminated frontmatter and rejects it.

**This is not local to that file.** `getReleasePlan` parses every entry in `.changeset/`, so one unparseable file fails `pnpm changeset status` for the whole repository and the release train stops behind it.

## What was measured

```
# before, on main
pnpm changeset status  -> exit 1
  error could not parse changeset - missing or invalid frontmatter.

# every changeset, through the real parser
parsed ok: 1097   invalid: 1
```

The `1097 ok / 1 invalid` line matters: it says the defect is one file rather than a convention the repository has drifted away from.

## The fix, and one wrong turn worth recording

The closing `---` after the last package entry. That is the whole defect.

I first read the blank line on line 2 as the cause and removed it — the parse error names frontmatter, and a blank line inside it looks like the problem. It was not: restoring that blank line and re-parsing still succeeds, so it was never required. Only re-running the gate after the first "fix" caught it, and the diff here is what prettier settled on once the file became parseable.

## Verification

- `pnpm changeset status` exits **0**, and lists 25 packages to bump at patch.
- The parsed result carries 25 releases and the original summary, so the entry keeps the meaning #1667 gave it.
- No changeset of its own: this changes no published package, it makes an existing one readable.

author: tfufuz1
body:
This change hardens DiskANN's `pending.wal` file format against corruption and allocation DoS attacks:
1. Adds a 5-byte header (`PWAL` magic + version 1) to `pending.wal`.
2. Computes and appends a 32-byte HMAC-SHA256 over `(id || dim || embedding)` using `DISKANN_INTEGRITY_KEY` for every appended vector.
3. Performs defensive parsing on recovery by checking `dim <= MAX_PENDING_WAL_DIM` (65,536) before buffer allocation to prevent out-of-memory allocator aborts.
4. Verifies per-entry HMACs using `subtle::ConstantTimeEq`. Corrupted entries log an error with byte offsets and doc IDs, skip the bad entry, and continue processing valid entries in the file.
5. Adds test coverage for roundtrip serialization/deserialization, bit corruption skipping, allocation DoS mitigation, and clean rejection of legacy unversioned files.

author: avyayv
body:
## Summary

Task generation now supports every sandbox the backend already implements — Docker, Modal, Vercel, and E2B — instead of only Docker and Modal, and all empty-state boxes use one consistent dashed style.

- Sandbox options come from the shared execution backend registry, so the UI, API schema, and worker can no longer drift apart.
- Cloud (E2B/Vercel) generation requires its runtime artifact and an explicit Docker/Modal Harbor verification environment, since Harbor supports neither as a verification environment.
- Vercel credentials store token, team ID, and project ID encrypted; the API never returns secret values.

## Design

### Generation settings and provider registry

- `src/providers.ts` — adds `executionBackendLabels` so UI labels stay in sync with the backend list.
- `src/site/generation-settings.ts` — sandbox enum now uses `EXECUTION_BACKENDS`; `superRefine` requires a sandbox credential for non-Docker providers, a prebuilt non-base E2B template or digest-pinned Vercel image (`isDigestPinnedOciImage`), and an explicit `harborEnvironment` (Docker/Modal) with its own Modal credential for cloud generation. Docker/Modal payloads reject cloud-only fields, keeping existing settings valid.
- `src/site/generation-config.ts` (new) — single source for the generation execution/Harbor environment/image variables, shared by submission and runtime.

### Credential storage

- `src/evaluation/credentials.ts` — adds the `vercel` kind with required, provider-specific `teamId`/`projectId` fields; secrets persist the new fields alongside token IDs.
- `src/evaluation/account.ts` — `CredentialInfo.kind` accepts `"vercel"`.
- `src/site/generation-credentials.ts` — one `sandboxCredentials` helper validates and resolves credentials for the generation sandbox and, when relevant, the Modal verification environment; clears all provider variables before applying saved secrets so host credentials cannot leak in.

### Submission and runtime

- `src/site/task-start.ts` — resolves the execution backend, image, and timeout cap through `loadConfig` with the generated environment instead of special-casing Modal.
- `src/temporal/activities/generation-runtime.ts` — uses `loadWorkerConfig`, verifies the run matches its saved configuration, caps hosted timeouts by the submitted value, and closes the sandbox executor after the activity.
- `src/site/pr-routes.ts` — `/generation-options` advertises all backends.

### UI

- `review/src/web/GenerationFields.tsx` — sandbox select from API options with shared labels; runtime image/template field and Harbor verification selector appear only for cloud sandboxes; credential pickers filter to the exact provider.
- `review/src/web/evaluation/CredentialEditor.tsx` — Vercel token, team ID, and project ID fields.
- `review/src/web/ui.tsx` — `EmptyState` primitive (dashed border, centered muted mono text) reused by `RepoPage`, `ReposPage`, and `ConnectRepoSheet` for every empty/no-match box.
- `review/src/web/generation-fields.test.tsx`, `review/src/web/empty-state.test.tsx`, `tests/site-generation-cloud.test.ts` — new coverage for provider labels, conditional fields, credential filtering, schema validation, runtime execution, secret hygiene, and empty-state markup.

## Validation

- `bun test` — 488 pass, 0 fail (2377 expect calls), including 20 new cloud-generation and empty-state tests.
- `bun run typecheck:review` and `bunx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` — clean.
- `bun run build` — production build succeeds.
- `bunx biome check src tests review/src` — clean except two pre-existing warnings in files this PR does not touch (`src/cli/dev-proxy.ts`, `src/viewer/archived.ts`).
- Verified the deployed review preview serves the new generation fields and dashed empty states; no cloud provider API was called, so no charges were incurred.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> New Postgres service, OAuth/session configuration, and schema migrations (including dropping `repo_runs`) affect deployments and upgrades; credential encryption keys must be set consistently on API and worker.
> 
> **Overview**
> **Expands local and packaged operations** so several checkouts can run isolated stacks, with a documented `.env.example`, per-project Compose names/ports/images, optional GitHub OAuth on the API, and a shared **dev proxy** (Caddy + CoreDNS, plus the `avyayv` helper) for subdomain routing on a tailnet.
> 
> **Adds `site-postgres` to Compose** for users, repos, tasks, and evaluation metadata; ships `drizzle/` in the API image; and applies new migrations (`evaluation_records`, soft-delete on `tasks`, drop `repo_runs`). author: epilogos
body:
`the_installed_alt_a_opens_the_real_surface_and_ctrl_t_switches_modes` was reported flaky locally: it hung for the full 10s timeout and failed, chalked up to "tmux 3.6a" since that was the obvious difference on the machine it failed on. That diagnosis was wrong. It reproduces identically regardless of tmux version and is not fixed by upgrading tmux — it fails on any shell with no `LANG`/`LC_ALL`/`LC_CTYPE` exported, which is exactly the shell it was run in.

Two independent, ambient locale reads both have to agree before this test's Unicode markers ("AIKit · Workspace", "Relations · Tree") ever reach the captured PTY output:

1. The popped-up `aikit ui` process picks Unicode vs. its own documented ASCII-safe fallback from its `LC_ALL`/`LC_CTYPE`/`LANG` (`aikit_tui::layout::Glyphs::from_env`). With none set, it correctly renders the ASCII fallback ("AIKit - Workspace") — the app working as designed, not a bug — which the test's Unicode assertion then never matches.
2. Separately, tmux decides *per attached client* whether that client can take UTF-8 output, from the locale the attaching process had when it ran `attach-session` — independent of what the popped-up pane's own process sees. A client tmux believes is not UTF-8-capable gets any wide character it's sent replaced with a placeholder (`~`, `_`) on the way out, garbling the same markers even once (1) is fixed alone.

Confirmed both mechanisms directly: instrumented the test to dump the popup's real process environment (`ps -E`) and the raw captured bytes at the moment of timeout, saw `LC_ALL`/`LC_CTYPE`/`LANG` genuinely absent and the rendered text genuinely ASCII, fixed one mechanism at a time and watched the failure mode change (ASCII hyphen, then a `~`/`_`-garbled partial-Unicode render) before both were pinned and it passed cleanly.

**Fix:** pin `LC_ALL=en_US.UTF-8` in both places, the same way `TERM` is already pinned there rather than trusted to be ambient — once on the private tmux server's global environment (covers the popped-up process's own choice), once on the attaching client's `Command` (covers tmux's per-client UTF-8 decision). No product code changed; this is test-only, and the app's ASCII fallback behavior is correct and untouched.

**Found in passing, filed separately:** `scripts/verify` excludes this exact test from the enforced gate under `legacy_pty_journeys`, with a comment saying it targets "the retired legacy palette/tree interaction" pending a V2 rewrite. Git history shows that rewrite already happened three weeks after the exclusion (`d4a1dac`, "finish the unified-surface test — markers match rendered text") — the test now asserts on current V2 markers and its own doc comment says the V1 choreography no longer exists. The exclusion's stated reason no longer describes this test. That's a separate call from this fix (it changes CI enforcement, not just test correctness, and I haven't audited the other four excluded names), so it's filed as its own follow-up rather than folded in here.

**Proof:** the fixed test passes repeatedly and fast (~0.8–1.8s instead of hanging to the 10s timeout and failing) run standalone, 5 consecutive runs all green. All 14 tests in `mux_install.rs` pass. The real-tmux suites in `aikit-adapters` (`tmux_real`, `working_environment_tmux_real`) pass unchanged. `scripts/verify quick -p aikit-cli -p aikit-adapters` (878 tests under nextest) passes with clippy `-D warnings` clean and `git diff --check` clean.

author: 3uzbcqje
body:
Chart 0.11.0 dropped the `-app` suffix from the fullname template, so **every resource is renamed**:

```
star-server-app  →  star-server     Deployment, Service, Ingress, ServiceAccount, PDB
```

This is `bettervoting.com`, so worth being deliberate about.

## Nothing that carries traffic or identity changes

Rendered both versions against this repo's `values.yaml`:

| | 0.8.2 | 0.11.1 |
|---|---|---|
| host | `bettervoting.com` | `bettervoting.com` |
| TLS secret | `star-server-tls` | `star-server-tls` |
| TLS hosts | + `www.bettervoting.com` | + `www.bettervoting.com` |
| image | `bettervoting:sha-12e6a3a` | `bettervoting:sha-12e6a3a` |
| replicas | 2 | 2 |
| env vars | 20 | 20 |
| service port | `5000 → http` | `5000 → http` |

The TLS secret name is set **explicitly** in values.yaml rather than derived from the release name — so cert-manager doesn't reissue, and there's no Let's Encrypt rate-limit exposure.

## PruneLast changes the procedure entirely

This is the first rename to run since #62 enabled `prune: true` with `PruneLast=true`. Confirmed live on the app:

```
automated={"prune":true,"selfHeal":true}
syncOptions=["CreateNamespace=true","ServerSideApply=true","PruneLast=true"]
```

Previously the old resources would have been orphaned and needed manual deletion — and under the old RollingSync would have stalled the whole pipeline. Now:

1. ArgoCD creates the new set (`star-server`)
2. Waits for it to become healthy
3. **Only then** prunes the old set (`star-server-app`)

While both Ingresses exist for `bettervoting.com`, ingress-nginx resolves the host conflict in favour of the **older** one — so traffic stays on the old pods until the old Ingress is pruned. There's no window where the hostname points at pods that aren't ready.

## Capacity

The transition runs 4 pods instead of 2. At 256Mi each that's 512Mi extra, against ~1.6Gi free on the tighter of the two nodes. Checked because if the new Deployment can't schedule, it never goes healthy, PruneLast never fires, and you'd be left with both sets running.

## Nothing external depends on the old names

Checked Ingresses and Services cluster-wide — only the starvote objects themselves reference `star-server-app`.

## Also: three more broken README queries

`README.md` had three more Loki examples using `{pod=~"star-server-app-.*"}`. #64 fixed one; these three were missed. They were **already broken** — fluent-bit sets no `pod` label, because `Auto_Kubernetes_Labels` promotes the pod's Kubernetes labels rather than its name — and the rename would have made them wrong twice over. Replaced with `{app_kubernetes_io_instance="star-server"}`, which is verified to return results and survives the rename.

The repo now has zero references to `star-server-app`.

## Watching the rollout

```sh
kubectl -n starvote get pod -w        # 2 new star-server pods should become Ready
kubectl -n starvote get deploy,svc,ing,sa,pdb    # old -app set should disappear after
curl -sI https://bettervoting.com | head -1
```

Worth watching this one rather than merging and walking away — it's the first PruneLast-driven full-resource rename in this cluster, and `discord-bot` and `alaska-rcv` have the same migration behind it.

author: danwilliams201302-max
body:
## Purpose
Stop the TMS UI and operational endpoints from independently calling RoadTech/TachoMaster and triggering provider rate limits.

## Changes
- Adds a single immutable RoadTech live snapshot refreshed only by `DotTrackingIngestionService`.
- Existing operations, wallboard, ETA, tracking diagnostics and Tacho enrichment callers now read the same snapshot via `DotTrackingClient.GetLatestVehicleEventsAsync` instead of contacting RoadTech.
- Diagnostics report the central snapshot capture time and age.
- Adds a one-minute shared TachoMaster HTTP response cache so duplicate duty/member/metric/login requests across screens are served from the same provider read.
- Stops immediate retries when RoadTech/TachoMaster returns HTTP 429.
- Keeps the last successful RoadTech snapshot when a subsequent refresh fails.
- Adds regression tests for snapshot consistency, Tacho response caching, and 429 suppression.

## Operational result
All live sections consume the same RoadTech batch/time, while provider polling remains controlled by the background ingestion cadence. A provider outage/rate limit no longer causes every screen refresh to create more upstream login/telemetry calls.

# 存储实测与 SmolLM-135M 先例方向相反：本 checkpoint 的 model.safetensors 真存
# bf16（272 张量全 BF16，HANDOFF 实测更正），importer 的 fp32 load 是保值
# bf16→float32 上转，arg0 blob 打包约定不受影响。模型面：hidden 576、30 层、
# 9 q-heads / 3 kv-heads（GQA）、SwiGLU MLP 1536、RoPE theta 100000（SmolLM-135M 为
# 10000）、max positions 8192、vocab 49152、tie_word_embeddings。host 侧数值期望

# 已在 workload 轮以 host 载体实证（SmolLM2/HANDOFF.md + reference/；jit 与官方
# aten 路径逐位置 argmax 全同）。

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- 预期测试（bind 轮序列，bbdev_plan 为权威生成器）
- 预期应跑的测试：
  - `nix develop -c bbdev workload --build '--chip pebble --model smollm2'`（workload 侧
    构建；MODEL_LAYOUT / layout / _MODELS 三源齐备后的模型织入）

    封闭 lane）
- probe 取证配对：上述 model stem 走 sim + analysis 成对步骤（`probe:` 声明 5 分钟）

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- ball 落点期望：本轮不声明（决策与推理）
# 决策：不声明 ball-expect 行。layout 采用经 CI 验证的 Pythia / BertMedium / SmolLM
# 同款 host-linalg 形态——全部 op 降 riscv64 host 循环、构造上不产生任何 buckyball
# dialect op。若在此形态上声明 ball-expect，probe 零事件即按「ball 未执行（layout
# 管线断点）」判 FAIL——该信号断言的是本写集有意不走的路径，是自证失败而非管线缺陷；
# 零事件 trace = PASS + host-fallback 形态注记（哨兵行
# probe-evidence: buddy-buckyball-smollm2-run cycles=none (instrument-not-applicable)）。
# 本轮核心观察点（layout 管线能否把 silu/transpose 落进 ball）已在 bind 会话用 pebble
# per-chip 工具链（compiler/thirdparty/buddy-mlir/build/pebble/bin/buddy-opt）对
# subgraph0.mlir 真跑取证（tosa→linalg→bufferize → -convert-linalg-to-tile
# --target=pebble → -convert-tile-to-buckyball → -lower-buckyball-to-bank-ssa
# -assign-physical-banks，全部 exit 0），结论逐条钉精确：
#   - 复证对象的一致性声明：本地 build 重跑 importer 后 subgraph0.mlir 与 workload
#     轮 S1 清点存在轻微重 trace 差异（tosa.transpose 332→334、tosa.add 365→366、
#     其余计数全同；arg0.data 仍 538,060,160 B bit-exact）——Dynamo 重 trace 方差，
#     本会话对两个版本各跑一遍观察链：S1 版计数与 phase9 SmolLM 逐位相同，重产版
#     多出的 2 个 transpose 位点是 i64 输入 ids 张量（1×16）上的（见 D-p-3）。
#   - SiLU：不可达（D-s-1 复证，两版图同型）。30 个 silu 语义站点（1x16x1536 f32，
#     图内以 negate→exp→add(1.0)→reciprocal→mul 五原子链存在于 linalg.generic）从未
#     变成 tile op：-convert-linalg-to-tile 只 raise 751 tile.matmul + 334
#     tile.transpose（S1 版 332），math.exp ×90 / math.rsqrt ×61 / math.log ×30 /
#     math.fpowi ×61 全留 linalg.generic；-convert-tile-to-buckyball 产出
#     buckyball.mem_transpose ×334、buckyball.silu = 0（grep 计数 0，C 段 IR）。
#     SiluBall funct7 59 / ballId 11 自 PR #33 在册，但 midend 无 elementwise/silu
#     fusion 模式、tile→buckyball 只挂 transpose/quant/matmul/mega 模式，五原子链
#     无触发路径；n≤256 分片发射（每站点 96 次调用、2,880 次/前向，s2 brief §4 #7）
#     因根本无 op 产生而悬空。派生规格 D-s-1（phase9）原文复证。
#   - Transpose（f32 权重/拆合头 332 位点）：编译层可达但载体不可交付（D-p-1 复证）。
#     332/332 f32 站点经 tile.transpose → buckyball.mem_transpose，bank-SSA + 物理
#     bank 分配 exit 0；但该 lane 把这张 134M-param host 常驻参数图展开到 3,046,468
#     行 bank-SSA IR（S1 版 3,046,453）、266,180 个 memref.alloc（S1 版 266,177）、
#     131,449 对 mvin/mvout、525,796 mset、263,230 fence——phase8 D-p-1 结论在
#     SmolLM2 图上复证（与 phase9 SmolLM 数字逐位一致，同架构同编译器故）。
#   - Transpose（i64 输入 ids 位点，本轮新断点）：重产图新增 2 个 tile.transpose 于
#     memref<1x16xi64>（输入 ids / 因果掩码索引路径），-convert-tile-to-buckyball
#     将其降成 buckyball.mem_transpose（memref<1x16xi64>），违犯 TransposeBall 的
#     8/32-bit 元素契约——-lower-buckyball-to-bank-ssa 段的 verifier 报
#     "transpose only supports 8-bit or 32-bit elements"（Cr.mlir:150/185），进程仍
#     exit 0（诊断非致命），该 2 个 op 未被降成 bank 级 op 而是残留于 D 段 IR
#     （D 段 grep 实据 2 个 i64 buckyball.mem_transpose）。派生规格 D-p-3
#     （tile 管线对 i64 索引张量无元素宽度闸门，把 TransposeBall 契约外的位点 raise
#     成 mem_transpose；core-compiler 领地）。
#   - RMSNorm：不可达（phase8 D-p-2 同型）。61 个 rsqrt 站点在两个 pass 中均未离开
#     linalg.generic（无 LN 模式触发；且 LayerNormBall 的 C∈{4,64,256,512}/ε 契约
#     本就不覆盖 C=576、ε=1e-5 的 RMSNorm，s2 brief §5 已冻结该边界）。
#   - 归口统计与 s2-brief §4 结论一致：现成 ball 2（TransposeBall、SiluBall——
#     模型路径触发不成立/载体不可交付，见上）；派生新 ball 0；其余全部 host fallback。
#     主机形态下 bank 池闲置（s2 brief §3(d)「本轮无任何算子对 bank 池提出承载承诺」）。
# 「模型落 ball」在任何 chip 上都没有上游先例——本轮不声称任何未经 probe trace 观察的
# 落点；若 probe trace 意外出现 ball-op 事件，将作为正向事实照录（届时 D-s-1 之外的
# 那条路径即被实证）。
