Public names stay the same (`APP_CSS`, `SYMPHONY_COLORS`, per-surface `*_CSS`, `themed_markdown`, …). Chrome `$` variables are generated from color tokens. Copy the packaged file to `~/.symphony/theme.toml` to edit. Default dark appearance is unchanged.

author: bcollard
body:
## The problem

`vm.imageDisk` sizes the Lima data disk mounted over `/var/lib/containerd` — which is where images **actually** live. Docker in the klimax VM runs the containerd snapshotter (`driver-type: io.containerd.snapshotter.v1`), so both image layers and container writable layers land there, not on the VM root disk. Measured on a live VM:

| | Size | Used | Holds |
|---|---|---|---|
| `/` (`vm.disk`) | 58G | 4.8G | OS, `/var/lib/docker` (metadata, volumes) |
| `/var/lib/containerd` (`imageDisk`) | 30G | 13G | content store 3.7G + overlayfs snapshots 9.1G |

`EnsureImageDisk` only ever **creates** that disk — it returns early when the directory exists. So raising `vm.imageDisk` in the config had no effect on an existing VM, **silently**, and the only way to get a bigger one was to delete the disk, discarding the image cache it exists to preserve.

Observed in the wild: a config reading `30GiB` while the disk sat at 10GiB and 95% full.

## The command

```sh
klimax down
klimax disk resize-image 30GiB
klimax up
```

Grows the backing file and syncs `vm.imageDisk` in the config. Refuses to shrink, and refuses to run while the VM holds the disk — Lima locks it, and resizing underneath a running guest would corrupt it.

**The guest side needs nothing.** Lima's own `05-lima-disks.sh` already runs `growpart` + `resize2fs` for additional disks, before klimax's mount unit, so the partition and ext4 grow on the next start. I initially added a `growpart` call here on the assumption that `resize2fs` alone couldn't grow past the old partition table — then the resize worked without it. Removed; Lima had it covered.

## The warning that was missing

`klimax up` now warns when the live disk and the configured size disagree, in either direction, quoting the fix:

```
WARN Image disk is smaller than vm.imageDisk in the config — the size in the
     config only applies when the disk is first created
     live=30GiB configured=60GiB
     fix="klimax down && klimax disk resize-image 60GiB && klimax up"
```

That silent mismatch is the entire reason this was hard to notice, and it's the part I'd argue matters more than the command.

## Verification

End to end against a live VM: **10GiB → 30GiB with the 8.8G image cache intact**, nothing re-pulled. `df` went from 95% full / 498M free to 32% / 20G free.

The warning fires on a drifted config (tested with a copied config, not the real one) and stays quiet when the two agree.

Tests cover the config rewriter, including that it leaves the adjacent `vm.disk` line alone — the two keys sit next to each other and `disk:` is a loose enough pattern to be worth pinning.

## Docs

README, CLAUDE.md, SKILL.md and `config.example.yaml` all updated. The config example and SKILL now say outright that `imageDisk` applies only at creation, and that `/var/lib/containerd` — not the root disk — is where images land, since that surprised even me.

## Locked acceptance 1. **Cash walk-in:** PDV cash **without a customer must sell**. Schema already allows `sales.customer_id` NULL. This PR relaxes prod-only `assert_store_sale_settings` (it was raising `customer_required_on_sale` when Centro `store_settings.require_customer_on_sale=true`) and stops the API/UI from blocking checkout. HTTP still maps `customer_required_on_sale` if a stale RPC raises it — **never** opaque `sale_processing_failed`. 2. **Card chain:** `inventory_movement_chain_mismatch` is inventory/ledger, not Stripe. Append-only reconcile (`reason=inventory_ledger_reconcile`) + `BEFORE UPDATE` on `inventory_balances` heals BEV-001-style drift (stock 226 vs last movement 176) so Log2 authorize ≠ confirmed → capture → `saleConfirmed=true` can succeed. Chain CHECK is **not** weakened. Capture without confirmed sale stays fail-closed (`unknown`, specific `error`). 3. **PIX stays dead.** **`CARD_CHECKOUT_ENABLED` stays unset/false** until smoke. No livemode. Zero opaque `sale_processing_failed`. Does **not** rewrite `process_sale_core` (that body has diverged and must keep `sale_items`). Does not enable card/PIX. ## How to verify **Cash (Centro, after migrations `193000`–`193200`)** 1. Open caixa on this terminal. 2. Sell 1× BEV-001 **without** customer → HTTP **200 / confirmed**, not 422, not `sale_processing_failed`. 3. If an old RPC still raises `customer_required_on_sale`, HTTP is **422 `customer_required_on_sale`** (mapped token) — PDV keeps the cart and shows the message. No silent fail / fake receipt. **Card (Log2, testmode only — hold until smoke)** 1. Leave `CARD_CHECKOUT_ENABLED` unset/false in prod until this is deployed and cash walk-in is green. 2. After opt-in + service role + Stripe testmode: authorize ≠ confirmed, then capture → `process_card_sale` **`saleConfirmed=true`** (ledger catch-up if BEV-001 still drifted). 3. If confirmation fails: status `unknown`, specific `error`, **not** captured. **PIX** — still not_configured / button disabled. No livemode. ## Tests `pnpm test` 329 passed. `pnpm typecheck` + `pnpm lint` clean.
  
## Resumo por Sourcery Impor políticas de venda para clientes da loja, expor erros específicos de processamento e reconciliar divergências no livro-razão de inventário sem enfraquecer a integridade da cadeia de movimentações. Novos recursos: - Adicionar a recuperação de políticas de venda no nível da loja e impor o comportamento de checkout com cliente obrigatório nos fluxos de pagamento em dinheiro e cartão. - Adicionar mapeamentos acionáveis de erros HTTP e voltados ao usuário para erros de processamento de clientes, inventário e vendas com cartão. Correções de bugs: - Impedir que capturas de cartão sejam reportadas como bem-sucedidas quando a confirmação da venda falhar, exibindo o erro mapeado subjacente. - Reconciliar divergências no saldo do inventário com ajustes somente de acréscimo no livro-razão antes de registrar movimentações de vendas em dinheiro ou cartão. Melhorias: - Propagar as informações do cliente pela captura de cartão e aprimorar a validação do PDV e as mensagens de conflito. Testes: - Adicionar cobertura para a imposição de políticas de clientes, mapeamentos de erros acionáveis, comportamento de captura de cartão com falha segura e migrações de reconciliação da cadeia de inventário.
Original summary in English ## Resumo pelo Sourcery Aplicar as políticas de venda da loja, retornar erros de processamento específicos e preservar a integridade do livro-razão de inventário em vendas à vista e com cartão. Novos recursos: - Adicionar a recuperação das políticas de venda no nível da loja e aplicar o comportamento de checkout obrigatório para clientes em vendas à vista e com cartão. - Expor mapeamentos acionáveis de HTTP e voltados ao usuário para falhas de cliente, inventário, pagamento e processamento de vendas. Correções de bugs: - Impedir que capturas de cartão sejam reportadas como bem-sucedidas quando a confirmação da venda falhar, exibindo o erro mapeado subjacente. - Reconciliar o saldo do inventário e divergências na cadeia de movimentações com ajustes somente de acréscimo no livro-razão antes de registrar as movimentações da venda. Melhorias: - Propagar as informações do cliente durante a captura do cartão e aprimorar a validação do checkout, o tratamento de conflitos e as mensagens de erro. Testes: - Adicionar cobertura para a aplicação das políticas de clientes, o mapeamento acionável de erros RPC, o comportamento de captura de cartão com falha segura e as migrações de reconciliação da cadeia de inventário.
Original summary in English ## Summary by Sourcery Enforce store sale policies, return specific processing errors, and preserve inventory ledger integrity across cash and card sales. New Features: - Add store-level sale policy retrieval and enforce customer-required checkout behavior across cash and card sales. - Expose actionable HTTP and user-facing mappings for customer, inventory, payment, and sale-processing failures. Bug Fixes: - Prevent card captures from being reported as successful when sale confirmation fails, while surfacing the underlying mapped error. - Reconcile inventory balance and movement-chain drift with append-only ledger adjustments before recording sale movements. Enhancements: - Propagate customer information through card capture and improve checkout validation, conflict handling, and error messaging. Tests: - Add coverage for customer policy enforcement, actionable RPC error mapping, fail-closed card capture behavior, and inventory-chain reconciliation migrations.

author: villasboasbernardo-hub
body:
## Identificador de origem

**CIAARA-14.2** (autorização de 08/09/2026) · **spec 004** (checklist de origem) · **FR-006**

Origem concreta: `specs/004-auth-convite-e-rbac/checklists/security.md`,
itens **CHK014**, **CHK015**, **CHK016** e **CHK001**. Os três primeiros reprovaram já na redação da
lista; o quarto continua aberto e este PR entrega o **modelo** que ele pede.

## O que muda

O documento 22 deixa de afirmar coisas vencidas sobre fatos decididos fora dele, e o `FR-006` passa
a dizer **quem impõe** o mínimo de senha em vez de apenas exigir o número.

⚠️ **Nenhuma regra de negócio muda. Nenhum `RN-` foi tocado, reinterpretado ou reescrito.** São os
mesmos 12 caracteres, a mesma verificação contra vazamento, a mesma recusa de composição e de
expiração. Mudou **onde a exigência está escrita** e **o que o documento afirma sobre o mundo**.

## Destino do requisito na v2.1

- [x] **[PRESERVADO]** — mesma regra, mesma implementação
- [ ] **[PRESERVADO — nova implementação]** — mesma regra, mecanismo diferente
- [ ] **[ABSORVIDO PELA PLATAFORMA]** — o motor passa a garantir o que o código garantia
- [ ] **[REVOGADO — v2.1]** — motivo e substituto declarados abaixo
- [ ] **[NOVO — v2.1]** — não existia na v2.0

**Preservado, e a marcação importa.** Este PR não altera comportamento de nada. É correção de
documentação normativa: três afirmações que descreviam um estado do mundo que a autorização da
CIAARA-14.2 e o Épico 3 já haviam mudado, mais uma redação de requisito que não nomeava o
impositor.

## Definition of Done (BRIEF §7) — todos, sem exceção

- [x] 1. `tsc --noEmit` sem erro e `eslint` sem aviso novo
- [ ] 2. **Unidade (Vitest):** toda função de `lib/dominio/` tocada, com casos sintéticos
- [ ] 3. **Invariantes (pgTAP):** asserção nomeada por `RN-` de _Risco: Alto_ (stub rastreável é
      aceito e melhor que cobertura fingida — Princípio VIII)
- [ ] 4. **RLS (teste negativo):** para cada perfil, o que ele **não** pode ler/escrever é negado
      pelo banco. Só o caminho feliz **não** vale.
- [ ] 5. **E2E (Playwright):** percurso principal da fatia, incluindo a rota `/print/*` quando houver
- [ ] 6. Migration aplicada no preview e **revertível** (script `down` ou plano descrito abaixo)
- [x] 7. Commits no padrão `feat(RF-…): …`

**Os itens 2 a 6 não têm objeto, e desmarcá-los é a resposta honesta.** Este PR toca **três arquivos
Markdown** e **zero linhas de código, SQL ou configuração**:

```
docs/fase-2/22-Seguranca-RLS-e-Autenticacao.md
specs/004-auth-convite-e-rbac/spec.md
specs/004-auth-convite-e-rbac/checklists/security.md   (novo)
```

Não há função de domínio tocada, nem regra `RN-` nova, nem perfil novo, nem percurso de tela, nem
migration. Marcar esses itens seria cobertura fingida, que o Princípio VIII recusa.

O item 1 vale e passa: `pnpm verificar` sai **0**. `docs/` e `specs/` estão em `.prettierignore` —
são escritos e alinhados à mão —, então o `format:check` não os reformata.

## Fronteira servidor/cliente

- [x] Nenhum `"use client"` novo em `page.tsx` ou `layout.tsx` (só em folha — risco R-01)
- [x] Nenhum `await` dentro de laço em `app/**` (risco R-02 — N+1)
- [x] `lib/dominio/` continua sem `import` de supabase/next/react (risco R-10)
- [x] `lib/tipos/database.ts` regenerado se houve migration (risco R-04)

Os quatro são verdadeiros **por vacuidade**: `git diff --stat main...HEAD` não lista um único arquivo
fora de `docs/` e `specs/`. Não houve migration, então não há contrato de tipos a regenerar.

## Plano de reversão da migration

**Não se aplica.** Não há arquivo em `supabase/migrations/` neste PR.

Para o caso de alguém precisar desfazer a correção documental, a reversão é `git revert` dos três
commits, que são separados por assunto exatamente para permitir isso:

| Commit | Desfaz |
|---|---|
| `c8c76f9` | as três (mais uma) correções factuais no documento 22 |
| `d86f7d1` | a redação do `FR-006` que nomeia o mecanismo |
| `e0820ac` | a inclusão do checklist de segurança |

⚠️ **Reverter o primeiro devolve ao documento 22 três afirmações que hoje se sabe falsas** — entre
elas a de que a hospedagem de dado pessoal segue pendente na CIAARA-14.2. É desfazer um registro,
não uma implementação.

## Como validar no preview

**Não há o que validar no preview: nenhuma tela muda.** O deploy da Vercel vai subir idêntico ao da
`main`, e isso é o resultado esperado.

A validação deste PR é **leitura do diff**, e são quatro pontos:

1. **Documento 22 §1.2, linha da ameaça A-3.** A defesa deve citar a autorização da CIAARA-14.2 de
   08/09/2026 e o recorte do `FR-028`, e a descrição da ameaça deve nomear CPF, RG, telefone e
   endereço — o que está em risco cresceu no Épico 3.
2. **Documento 22 §9.** A lista de dado pessoal deve trazer as 12 colunas de identificação civil e
   residência, com a migration que as trouxe. A frase sobre "a única pendência" deve ter saído da
   citação e da linha da tabela, **sem levar junto** o raciocínio da urgência, que fica como
   registro de por que a decisão precisava vir antes do Épico 2.
3. **Documento 22 §11, ponto 1.** ⚠️ **Confira este com atenção: não estava nos três itens
   autorizados.** A mesma afirmação vencida aparecia numa quarta ocorrência, como "Pendente na
   CIAARA-14.2". Corrigi seguindo a convenção já usada nos pontos 2 e 3 da mesma tabela. **Emendar
   três e deixar a quarta manteria exatamente a contradição que a emenda desfaz** — mas se a
   preferência for tocar só o autorizado, é um `git checkout` de uma linha.
4. **`FR-006` na spec 004.** Cada uma das três exigências deve nomear mecanismo e ambiente. O
   parágrafo marcado com 📐 declara que este requisito é o modelo para os próximos `FR-` de
   segurança.

## O que este PR deliberadamente NÃO faz

| Não fez | Por quê |
|---|---|
| Tocar em código, migration ou qualquer `RN-` | Restrição explícita da tarefa |
| Reabrir ou comentar no **PR #5** | Ele foi mesclado em 09/09/2026 (`5848213`); este trabalho nasce da `main` já atualizada |
| Mexer em `NEXT_PUBLIC_URL_APLICACAO` | Fora desta tarefa. Continua com Bernardo, nas T003 e T062.1 |
| Corrigir o **título** do §9, que ainda diz "pendência formal, não detalhe" | Não estava na autorização. Fica anotado no **CHK015** |
| Fechar os outros 23 itens do checklist | Nenhum é bloqueante isolado, e vários pedem decisão, não redação |

## O que fica aberto no checklist, em ordem de alcance

| Item | O que pede |
|---|---|
| **CHK001** | Passar os demais `FR-` de segurança pelo modelo que o `FR-006` inaugurou. É o de maior alcance |
| **CHK002** | Nenhum requisito diz **quando** as migrations alcançam o preview. O `SC-002` cobra o percurso funcionando lá, e o banco de preview não tem as duas do Épico 3 |
| **CHK008** | O `SC-003.1` **não pode falhar**: exige o limite "conferido e registrado", e registrar qualquer número satisfaz. Falta a faixa aceitável |
| **CHK012** | O `FR-027.1` exige que **toda** escrita chegue com identidade autenticada, e o convite usa `service_role` por desenho. A exceção não está declarada |

author: flerpharos
body:
Fixes #327

Two low-severity networking fixes in `src/labapi/client.py`:

1. **Proxy TLS bypass**: `_313HTTPAdapter` only overrode `init_poolmanager`, so the relaxed SSL context (`strict_cert=False`, which drops `VERIFY_X509_STRICT`) was never applied to requests routed through an HTTPS proxy — `proxy_manager_for` built its pool manager with default strict verification, silently ignoring the setting. Fixed by storing the built `ssl_context` on the adapter and overriding `proxy_manager_for` to pass the same context through to the parent implementation.

2. **Loopback callback SO_REUSEADDR on Windows**: the auth callback `TCPServer` unconditionally set `allow_reuse_address = True`. On POSIX this is the benign TIME_WAIT-reuse behavior. On Windows, `SO_REUSEADDR` instead permits another local process to bind the same `127.0.0.1:<port>` while the listener is up, letting it race for the `auth_code`/`email` callback. Fixed with a platform conditional: on Windows, `allow_reuse_address` stays `False` and a `server_bind` override sets `SO_EXCLUSIVEADDRUSE` instead; POSIX behavior is unchanged.

## Testing

- Added `test_strict_cert_false_relaxes_ssl_for_direct_and_proxied_requests`, which asserts the adapter stores `ssl_context` and that `proxy_manager_for` injects the same context into its pool manager.
- Added `test_collect_auth_response_blocks_concurrent_bind_on_windows` (skipped off Windows), which binds the loopback listener via `client.collect_auth_response()` and asserts a second socket (even with `SO_REUSEADDR` set) cannot bind the same port. Verified this reproduces the pre-fix vulnerability directly at the socket level (two `SO_REUSEADDR` sockets can share a port on Windows) and that the fix blocks it (`PermissionError`/`WinError 10013`).
- Ran the full suite (`uv run pytest --ignore=tests/test_integration.py`) five times in a row on Windows to check for rebind flakiness from disabling `SO_REUSEADDR`: consistently 432 passed, 1 skipped, no flakes.
- `uv run ruff check .` and `uv run ruff format --check .` pass; pre-commit's pyright hook passes on the changed files.

## What this is

Stratus v3: **authorization without authentication**, and a **rider-operations desk** whose coverage rule cannot be waived.

- A "Signed in as" picker in the header switches between fifteen personas grouped by app role (requester · coordinator · authority · trainer · crew · observer). The persona is state, not identity: switching it never resets the plan, it changes what the plan allows. No passwords, nothing persists.
- **R9** — every mutating transition in `rules.js` takes the actor first and calls `authorize()`; the matrix is data in `src/lib/auth.js` and the tests are generated from it (every role × every action). Refused controls stay on screen, disabled, with the R9 message as the tooltip.
- **R10** — a rider-facing sortie needs a qualified rider operator covering its window, at or under the desk ratio. R2 extends to the desk (nobody flies in a window they cover). The desk's ratio and minimum are bounded settings; there is no waiver.
- Separation of duties: nobody assigns their own request (I1, even a coordinator), nobody grants their own rating (I2), coordinators consume priority and authority sets it (I3). I4 (every actor's role permits its event) and I5 (every rider-facing sortie covered) are asserted on the seed.
- The board gains the rider desk row (cover · release · settings), crew get **My day** with Acknowledge, the trainer edits the rating matrix effective-dated, authority edits program priority and targets, every timeline event names its actor, Capacity shows desk load against the ratio and actions by role, the EOD report gains the desk and who did what.
- **Arc D4, the desk shortage**: the showcase run lands while the swing-shift rider operator is on leave; the third P0 showcase of the day is refused `R10 · desk at 3:1, ratio is 2` while a Levant and a rated crew were free (the note names them, and asks the PM to waive a ratio that has no waiver); the trainer's desk qualification for an operator adds a second coverer on Jun 17 and the backlog flies.

## Commits, in build order

1. `feat(data)` personas, rider desk, rider-facing flags, actor stamps, arc D4
2. `feat(rules)` R9 authorization matrix + R10 coverage + invariants I1–I5
3. `fix(data)` arc D4 on the ratio; the showcase run draws nothing from the planner (from an adversarial review: the plan before Jun 15 is now byte-identical to main, and the report asserts D1–D3 still hold)
4. `feat(ui)` persona switcher, disabled-with-reason controls, footer
5. `feat(ui)` rider desk row, desk.cover, my-day view, trainer editing, authority cards
6. `feat(loop)` actors in timelines and reports; capacity desk charts
7. `docs` README, sql 09–10, CLAUDE.md
8. `fix(rules)` releasing a coverer cannot leave riders uncovered (`checkUncover`)
9. `fix(review)` the branch review's must- and should-fixes: triage through the rules, the R10 note on the rail, one program transition, refusals shown in every picker, grants from tomorrow, the audit table's range filter and withdrawn column

## Verified

- `npm test`: 173 tests (was 36) — 102 generated matrix cases, R10 and the desk row and its release, every transition's refusal, I1–I5 on the seed, arc D4's refusal note.
- Two adversarial review workflows: eight agents and four lenses after the data commit (its must-fixes are commit 3), and five lenses on the whole branch (its must-fixes are commit 9).
- `npm run data`: every invariant check and every arc assert passes; tomorrow still holds exactly two unscheduled P0.
- Walked in the browser as coordinator, PM, trainer, crew, rider operator, requester and observer: assign, cover, release, desk settings, program edit, grant, acknowledge, withdraw, triage and its undo, and every refusal tooltip; the header fits a 375px viewport.

## Numbers that moved (quoted in the README from the report)

North star 85% (70% for P0); the tell 16 of 24; the Harmattan crew-deferral drop is now about two-thirds rather than ~80%, because the showcase run borrows the two Harmattan-rated day pilots. D2 and D3 read as before.

author: dasabhinaba34
body:
Two health models, **five** renderings, **four** sets of thresholds — and two of the five used the same two words for different questions.

## The conflict

| where | said "At risk" when |
|---|---|
| `/sales/leads` | score < 40 |
| owner's reports | 1.25 cycles overdue |
| handset pill | *(coloured at a hardcoded 70/50)* |
| handset `customerStage` | score < 60 — and an **unscored** customer fell through to "Active" |
| manager's journey book | fetched `health_score`, rendered nothing at all |

A manager and an owner could each read "At risk" about one shop on one afternoon and mean different things. That is what B3-16 was raised about, and it is worse than "two models".

## The resolution — not deleting one

They answer different questions and both are worth asking:

- the **band** — *has this customer stopped buying?* One fact: cycles past their own rhythm. It already governs `customers.status`, the Call Log and the owner's retention report.
- the **score** — *how is this relationship doing?* Five weighted components.

**The band owns the retention word; the score stops borrowing it.** A customer buying perfectly on time whose score is 30 is not at risk of leaving — they are paying late with two complaints open. Saying *that* is both truer and tells somebody what to do.

`lib/customer-health.ts` is the one place either becomes words — pure and client-safe like `account-types` and `seat-labels`, because three of the surfaces are client components. A low score says `watch` and **names the components dragging it**, reading `healthComponents`, which the engine has stored since it shipped and nothing had ever read.

There is a test asserting a score can never produce the phrase "at risk".

## Shown in both places, as asked

- **MBOS app** — band + score on the customer list and card; `customerStage` reads the real band instead of guessing from a score.
- **Manager console** — the leads table, and a band dot on the journey planner's book, which showed no health at all.

## Thresholds are configuration now

`mbos.health.strongAtOrAbove` joins `mbos.health.atRiskBelow`, replacing the hardcoded 70/50 in the handset pill. `checkConsistency` refuses a strong threshold at or below the watch one — a score between them would be both at once. The old key keeps its name so no stored setting needs migrating; its **label** changed, which is what a manager actually reads.

## One more thing

**CI now typechecks and tests the handset.** `mbos-app` had `typecheck` and `test` scripts that nothing ever called — CI ran only its lint. So its engines were tested when somebody remembered, and its types only on a laptop that happened to have the native packages installed. That matters most for native modules: a local tree usually cannot resolve them, so `tsc` silently skips every call and a wrong argument reaches an APK that cannot be recalled.

## Checks

- `npm run test` — 784 pass
- `tsc --noEmit` + `eslint` clean on **both** projects
- No migration on the server; one additive handset column (`healthBand`), and `mbos-wire.test.ts` confirms it has somewhere to land

author: deathemperor
body:
## What
A 65 s \`sample\` of the release bundle (678f6cc4, four live sessions) caught the Stats refresh at ~4 s of CPU per pass: 1.6 s decoding \`stats/transcripts.json\` (24 MB) with \`JSONDecoder\`, 1.4 s re-encoding and rewriting it. \`StatsModel.refresh()\` made a fresh \`CacheHandle\` per loop, so every 5-minute refresh decoded the cache again, and because some live session had always moved (\`filesTouched > 0\`) the whole corpus was written back every time. The decode churned hundreds of MB of small dictionaries per pass: \`heap\` showed 10,942 live \`[String: Stats.Day]\` + 31 MB of Int arrays, and \`vmmap\` 451 MB of MALLOC_SMALL against a 156 MB live heap — RSS sat at 587–615 MB.

- \`StatsModel\` holds one \`CacheHandle\` for its lifetime (\`scanning\` already serializes the loops that use it); \`CacheHandle\` is \`@unchecked Sendable\` for that.
- \`StatsScanner.scan\`: with a handle, a caught-up corpus is rewritten once when it catches up, then at most every \`settledWriteInterval\` (10 min); mid-backfill checkpoints stay at 30 s. The handle tracks \`dirty\` so held changes still reach disk on the next due pass even when nothing else moved. A quit in between loses only the watermarks since the last write; the next launch re-reads those bytes.

## Tests
\`testCacheHandleCarriesThePassesAndWritesTheFinishedCache\` extended: after the finished write, the transcript grows, the cache file is removed, and a settled pass off the held handle parses the new lines without touching disk; past the interval it is written and differs from the earlier file. \`StatsTests\` 74/74.

## Verify after the rebuild
\`infinitusctl perf\` rss over 30 min should stay near the launch value instead of climbing to ~600 MB; a 65 s \`sample\` should show no \`StatsScanner.Cache.init(from:)\` frames after the first refresh.

author: rem7474
body:
## Summary

This PR implements the optimizations identified during the full-stack performance audit following the merge of PRs #369, #370, and #371.

### 1. Frontend: Bundle & Hydration
- **Remove `manualChunks` in `vite.config.js`**: Grouping chunks by node_modules bucket previously pulled Vue runtime, Tabler, etc. into the ApexCharts chunk (1.4 MB) and marked it `modulepreload` at entry. Removing it restores Rollup dynamic code-splitting: entry JS is reduced from **3 126 KB uncompressed (779 KB gzip) down to ~458 KB (~150 KB gzip) — an ~80% reduction in blocking entry JS**. ApexCharts, Cytoscape, and xterm.js are now strictly async.
- **Dashboard REST hydration (`GET /api/v1/dashboard/init`)**: The dashboard now requests `/dashboard/init` on mount, allowing initial metrics and hosts to render without waiting for the WebSocket handshake, token validation, and initial frame. The shared `applySnapshot` function ensures whichever arrives first renders cleanly.
- **`shallowRef` on `summaryChartSeries`**: Eliminates deep reactivity overhead across the large chart data arrays.

### 2. Backend: WebSocket & DB Fan-out
- **Single JSON serialization**: `snapshotChanged` in `internal/ws/base.go` now returns `([]byte, bool)`. Sockets write raw bytes via `safeWriteRaw`, removing duplicate JSON marshaling per connected client.
- **Eliminate N+1 in APT snapshot**: `sendAptSnapshot` used to issue 3 DB queries per host sequentially (3N queries). Replaced with batch methods `GetAptStatusAll`, `GetUUStatusAll`, and `GetAptHistoryAll` (3 set-based queries total).
- **Host-filtered version comparisons**: `sendHostSnapshot` now calls `buildVersionComparisonsForHost`, scoping Docker containers to the specific host instead of scanning the full fleet inventory.
- **Alert engine O(1) lookups**: Preloads maintenance windows (`GetHostsInMaintenance`) and active incidents (`ListAllOpenAlertIncidents`) in bulk before rule evaluation loops, replacing per-rule/per-host database queries.
- **Pool & Caching tuning**: Set DB connection pool `SetMaxOpenConns(50)`, increase `dashboardCacheTTL` from 1s to 3s.
- **Metrics approximate count**: `CountMetrics` now uses TimescaleDB `hypertable_approximate_row_count('system_metrics')` with fallback to `COUNT(*)`.

### Verification
- `go build ./...` & `go vet ./...` passed
- Go tests (`internal/ws`, `internal/alerts`) passed
- `vue-tsc --noEmit` passed (0 type errors)
- `eslint` passed
- Vitest passed (17/17 tests passing)
- `npm run build` passed, verifying entry chunk sizes and modulepreloads in `dist/index.html`

body:
## The finding

`subscription_projection` is **empty across the entire production database**.
Nobody is subscribed, and nothing in the product could change that.

`createSubscriptionForContractor` is called from **exactly one place**:
`persistContractorSetup`. SUB-1 shipped **6 Sep**; every contractor in production
completed setup before it — the newest 1 Sep, the rest July and August. The only
trigger had already fired for all of them before the code existed, there is no
other entry point, and no backfill.

Not the missing env var it first looked like, and **not** a missing checkout
page — I said that earlier today on a grep for `checkout.sessions.create` /
`billing_portal` and was wrong. Creation goes through `subscriptions.create`.

## Why this is safe

- **It charges nobody.** The subscription carries SUB-1's open-ended trial
  (1 Jan 2100). Only `endTrialIfAllowanceExhausted` ends it — on the third
  completed job, per D18. A backfilled trade starts paying exactly when a trade
  who signed up today would.
- **Re-running is safe.** `createSubscriptionForContractor` checks for a
  projection row first and keys both Stripe calls on the contractor id, so a
  retry returns the original customer and subscription rather than double-billing.
- **Dry-run by default**, `--confirm` to write, matching
  `delete-voice-note-objects.ts`. The production write stays with a human.

## What it deliberately does not do

**It does not write `subscription_projection`.** The
`customer.subscription.created` webhook does, from Stripe's own state, which is
what keeps the projection honest. So rows appear *after the webhook lands*, not
immediately — and **if they never appear, the webhook is the next thing to look
at**, not this script.

## Runnable, and tested as runnable

```
RUNNABLE: npx tsx scripts/backfill/create-missing-subscriptions.ts --confirm
```

Per `AGENTS.md`: two money backfills previously shipped as library functions
with no entry point — every gate green, nothing invocable. So the test **spawns
the command** rather than importing the function behind it, and runs without
credentials because the script's first act is to refuse an incomplete
environment.

The entry point is guarded on `process.argv[1]`. Without that guard, importing
the module for its pure selection function executed `main()` and killed the test
runner with *"process.exit unexpectedly called with 1"* — caught on the first
run, and exactly what the guard now prevents.

It **refuses loudly** without `STRIPE_SUBSCRIPTION_PRICE_ID` — the variable whose
absence puts the entire subscription block in `persistContractorSetup` behind a
silent `if`. A backfill that repeated that silence would be worse than none.

## Two things for you

1. **Run it** — dry-run first to see the list, then `--confirm`.
2. **Confirm `STRIPE_SUBSCRIPTION_PRICE_ID` is set in Vercel production.** If it
   isn't, new signups have the same gap and the backfill will refuse rather than
   quietly do nothing.

- [x] All tests pass (`npm test`) — 412 files / 5135 tests
- [x] TypeScript compiles cleanly (`npm run typecheck`)
- [x] Lint passes — 0 errors
- [x] No new secrets or production credentials added to code
- [x] No migrations

## Why and outcome

Usage-period acquisition issued an idempotent insert, a lock-only query, and a separate row read. Read the period fields in the locking query and delete the redundant helper, reducing acquisition from three database statements to two.

Reconciliation diagnostics now report `work_pending` when a projected workspace wake is due, including when there is no mailbox backlog. Scheduling and billing decisions retain their existing owners.

## Product UX

- Effort: Not applicable — internal database access and operational diagnostics.
- Result: Ready.
- Walkthrough: Allowance admission, billing transitions, exhaustion, and group funding retain their existing behavior. No member-facing interface, reply, or scheduling change.

## Evidence

- Direct: Eight focused Web suites passed: 295 tests across allowance policy, usage recording, group funding, reconciliation facts/timing, and PostgreSQL period acquisition, plan resets, and operator resets.
- Coverage: The new real-PostgreSQL proof verifies creation/reuse, bigint/date decoding, two-statement acquisition, and committed spending visibility after actual row-lock contention. It fails on the original source with three statements and passes on the patch with two. Synthetic data ran against an isolated migrated loopback database.
- `pnpm --dir apps/web typecheck:prepared`: passed after final TypeScript edits; full Web typecheck generated prerequisite artifacts first.
- `pnpm docs:drift` and `git diff --check`: passed.
- ReviewGPT Round 1: **PASS**, zero findings, on `ee6c2f559a181ca226589eee04120b2d460f6497`. [Review conversation](https://chatgpt.com/c/6aa1b997-7920-83e9-8f5b-2a93606be5f1). Full sensitive snapshot; all nine changed postimages matched. Apollo lane, `gpt-6-pro` verified by response metadata and response hash; approximately 326 seconds from send to captured completion. Exact user/assistant turn binding and `REVIEW_COMPLETE` verified. The review substantively traced period locking, billing/settlement callers, transaction handling, and every changed logging path. No accepted or rejected findings, remediation, or tooling retries.
- CI: **PASS** on `ee6c2f559a181ca226589eee04120b2d460f6497` — all required checks, Web tests/builds/typecheck, package coverage, billing, and Temporal compatibility. [Release verification](https://github.com/cobuildwithus/murph/actions/runs/34397538958). Current-base mergeability verified with `git merge-tree --write-tree HEAD origin/main`; working tree clean.

## Non-obvious affected surfaces

The shared usage-allowance owner also serves billing resets, usage settlement, and group funding. Focused suites cover those paths alongside the real PostgreSQL contention proof. Due-work classification affects logs only.

## Architecture and reuse

- Existing systems reused: The existing allowance transaction, beneficiary-before-period locking, idempotent creation, generated Prisma model types, and reconciliation request clock.
- New logic: Select period fields under the existing row lock; derive diagnostic pending status from existing mailbox and due-work facts.
- New abstractions: None; the lock-only helper is removed.
- Complexity intentionally avoided: No cache, queue, service, state, dependency, pool configuration, scheduling jitter, or existing/missing fast-path split.

## Complexity impact

- Guard: pass — `pnpm complexity:diff`.
- Hotspots: `ensureHostedAiUsageAllowancePeriodTx` remains 22; its existing billing-policy branches are preserved. `readHostedRuntimeReconciliationFacts` remains 33; the change only passes its existing clock to logging. Unchanged allowance hotspots are `matchHostedAiUsageGeminiVideoAnalysisRecord` (31), `resolveHostedAiUsageAllowancePricingDecision` (26), `matchHostedAiUsageRetellPhoneCallRecord` (22), and `matchHostedAiUsageXaiSearchRecord` (22); provider matching and pricing are outside this correction. No new hotspot is introduced.
- Agent judgment: Allowance complexity debt is unchanged; reconciliation debt decreases from 16 to 13. Further billing-policy restructuring would expand this focused correction without evidence of need.

## Hot reply path impact

- Path status: Touched — shared usage admission can run before hosted processing.
- Database calls: No added calls. Each period acquisition uses two sequential statements instead of three inside the same transaction. The beneficiary lock still precedes period acquisition. No new collection fanout, transaction, or concurrent connection; one existing transaction connection per invocation.
- Network/provider calls: None added or moved into the transaction.
- Other awaited latency: None added; timeouts, retries, fallback, and authority checks remain unchanged.
- Before/after proof: Real PostgreSQL query counting proves 3 → 2 period statements for creation and reuse. Contention proof verifies the committed spending decision. Production latency improvement is not claimed.

## Murph initial provider input impact

Not applicable for individual and group Murph: no prompts, tools, schemas, messages, provider wrappers, or input builders change.

- Assembled instructions: Unchanged.
- Tool/schema/generated guidance: Unchanged.
- Other provider-visible input: Unchanged.
- Measurement method: Not run — no provider-input surface changed.

## Deployment concerns

- Deployment: applicable
- Supported skew: Old and new Web instances use the same existing tables, columns, transaction locks, and response contract; diagnostic keys and schema remain unchanged.
- Safe order: Web-only release; no Worker deployment or migration prerequisite.
- Rollback floor: Existing schema and protocol remain compatible with the previous Web implementation.
- Expected exposure: Calls served during a mixed Web rollout may use either two or three acquisition statements and either diagnostic classification; billing and scheduling authority are unchanged.
- Reversibility: Reverting the code requires no data conversion or repair.
- Convergence proof: Both implementations exercise the same PostgreSQL schema and locking contract; the baseline regression run confirms the original acquisition shape. Live rollout convergence has not been exercised.
- Post-deploy checks: Confirm the deployed Web revision, inspect bounded pool-pressure/error aggregates, and verify due-work diagnostics.

Classification rule: production TypeScript is source; test files are tests; Markdown is docs. No binary or generated files.

author: choikh0423
body:
## Summary

Migrates **S-08 TransactionTypeManagement** (`app/app-transaction-type-db2/`) end to end into the consolidated app: CICS **CTLI** (`COTRTLIC`) and **CTTU** (`COTRTUPC`) as REST + React screens, and the three JCL jobs (`MNTTRDB2`/`COBTUPDT`, `TRANEXTR`, `CREADB21`) as Spring Batch jobs. Backend lives entirely in `com.carddemo.trantype`; persistence is JPA against the existing `db2_transaction_type` / `db2_transaction_type_category` tables via `com.carddemo.common` entities (boundary **B-08**, decision **D-7**) — **no schema change, no new Flyway migration**.

Both online programs are pseudo-conversational state machines, so the services are modelled the same way: the client returns the previous `state` with every keystroke and the service reproduces the COBOL `EVALUATE EIBAID` / flag dance, rather than exposing CRUD endpoints.

```
POST /api/admin/transaction-types/list    { aid, typeFilter, descFilter, rows[7], state } -> { rows, infoMessage, errorMessage, state, nextProgram }
POST /api/admin/transaction-types/update  { aid, typeCode, description, state }           -> { typeCode, description, infoMessage, errorMessage, state, nextProgram }
```

Every message string, label and PF-key line is copied verbatim from the BMS maps and COBOL literals (`TranTypeMessages`), including SQLCODE suffixes (`Deadlock. Someone else updating ? SQLCODE:-911`).

Quirks preserved deliberately (each noted in the FR):
- CTLI's first F8 past the last page says `No more pages for these search conditions`; a **repeat** F8 says `No more pages to display` (`COTRTLIC.cbl:1536-1549,1674-1701`).
- CTLI's type-filter message claims "2 DIGIT" but the program only enforces numeric.
- CTTU pads `7` to `07`, and treats `*`/spaces as not-supplied.
- CTTU saves with UPDATE first and only INSERTs on SQLCODE +100 — so the "add" path is an update that missed.
- `COTRTUPC` sets `Delete of record failed` and then immediately overwrites the return message with `Delete failed with message: …`; the migrated code emits the second one, which is what the screen actually shows.
- `COBTUPDT` sets RC=4 and **keeps processing** later records, so the maintenance job is a tasklet running each record in its own `REQUIRES_NEW` transaction and finishing with exit status `4`.
- `COTRTUP.bms` paints `F6=Add` but the COBOL never tests F6 — the React screen has no F6 control.
- `CREADB21` uses plain INSERTs, so a second run against populated tables fails on the unique index (test asserts this).

DB2 plan/package operations (`FREEPLN`, BIND, `RUN PROGRAM(...) PLAN(CARDDEMO)`) have no target-side equivalent and are documented as not applicable; `FREEPLN` is a no-op step so the Job keeps one Step per `EXEC PGM=` (**D-3**).

## FRs covered and tests

Full matrix in `TransactionTypeManagement_functional_requirement.md` (§ traceability). Summary:

| Area | FRs | Tests |
|---|---|---|
| CTLI browse, filters, 7-row paging, U/D actions, F10 confirmations, error paths | FR-L01…L27 | `TranTypeListServiceTest` (19), `TranTypeLockFailureTest` |
| CTTU lookup / add / update / delete state machine and validation | FR-U01…U24 | `TranTypeUpdateServiceTest` (17), `TranTypeValidatorTest` (9), `TranTypeLockFailureTest` |
| Endpoints + admin-only gate | FR-L01, FR-U01 | `TranTypeControllerTest` |
| MNTTRDB2 fixed-width 53-byte records, A/U/D/`*`, RC=4 continuation | FR-B01…B10 | `TranTypeMaintenanceJobTest` |
| TRANEXTR 60-byte unloads, ordering, backup/GDG generations | FR-X01…X04 | `TranTypeExtractJobTest` |
| CREADB21 seed load, duplicate-key rerun | FR-C01…C05 | `CreateDb2TablesJobTest` |

`mvn -B test`: **858 tests, 0 failures** (whole module, after rebase). `CI=true npm run build`: green.

## Boundary decisions

- **B-08 / D-7**: `EXEC SQL` → JPA/`JdbcTemplate` on the same PostgreSQL target; the `-911`/`+100`/`-532` branches map to `PessimisticLockingFailureException`, empty `Optional`, and a child-row pre-check respectively, so the legacy messages stay reachable.
- **D-3**: one `Job` per JCL job, one `Step` per `EXEC PGM=`; jobs are launched only through `BatchJobLauncher` (`inpfile` parameter for MNTTRDB2, `hlq` for TRANEXTR).
- CTLI/CTTU keep the legacy `XCTL` targets in the response (`COADM01C`/`CA00`, `COTRTUPC`) rather than hardcoding React paths.
- Shared frontend files touched: only the two import lines and two `element` entries in `src/routes/registry.js`.

## Deferred / notes for the integrator

- `DataLoadJobTest` needed `jobLauncherTestUtils.setJob(dataLoadJob)` once a second stream registers `Job` beans; the same fix landed upstream during my rebase, so I took the upstream version — no change from me in that file.
- Legacy control member `CREADB21` seeds `REVERAL` where the foundation seed has `Reversal`; the batch job loads the legacy spelling from its control member and does not rewrite the foundation seed data.
- Inventory lists `TRANEXTR`/`CREADB21` under S-19 but they operate solely on TRNTYPE/TRNTYCAT and are executed here, per the task scope; the inventory's package layout for this module also differs from the source tree layout (recorded in the migration plan).

author: macodocious
body:
## Problem

With `display.interim_assistant_messages` disabled (the Discord default), assistant text written in the same turn as tool calls is captured on `_last_content_with_tools` but never transmitted. When the model's next `final_response` is non-empty but **different**, the captured content is silently orphaned.

Concrete bug (production, Sep 09): the agent posted only:

> Plan presented above — awaiting your go-ahead

— the actual 3,338-character plan sat in the dropped tool-call turn and the user never saw it. The DB shows the plan row (`finish_reason=tool_calls`) with no `platform_message_id` and no `delivery_obligation`: the claim shipped, the content did not.

## Fix

After `run_conversation` in `gateway/run.py`, if `_last_content_with_tools` holds content that was never delivered and the final response is non-empty but different, ship the captured content as its own message first — mirroring the existing clarify-path delivery (`_clarify_callback_sync`):

- same scrub (`strip_think_blocks`), same secret redaction, same interim dedup (`_interim_text_was_delivered`), same thread metadata
- skips when the final response already contains the captured text (no duplicate)
- always clears the capture afterward (no stale reuse on later fallbacks)

Two related status-rail leaks fixed on the same coin:

1. **Scratchpad retry-exhaustion bail** (`agent/conversation_loop.py`): `"Incomplete REASONING_SCRATCHPAD after 2 retries"` no longer ships verbatim as the user-facing `final_response`. The user gets a clean reply; the raw diagnostic stays in the `error` field for operators.
2. **Empty-after-tool-calls nudge** (`gateway/run.py` `_TELEGRAM_NOISY_STATUS_RE`): `"⚠️ Model returned empty after tool calls — nudging to continue"` is now filtered from chat (stays in logs), like the other recovery nudges.

## Tests

- New `tests/gateway/test_orphan_pending_content_delivery.py` (modeled on `test_clarify_pending_content.py`; uses the same `run_agent`/`dotenv` fakes):
  - captured content ships as its own message when the final response differs
  - no duplicate when the final response already contains the captured text
  - no duplicate when content already went through the interim rail
  - thinking blocks stripped before delivery
  - no captured content → no extra message
- Extended `tests/gateway/test_telegram_noise_filter.py` with the nudge string in `NOISY_STATUS_MESSAGES` (parametrized across chat surfaces).

Results: new + clarify + noise-filter suites — **233 passed**. Full gateway suite: 9,876 passed; the 15 failures (telegram adapter/model-picker/network-reconnect files) are pre-existing and order-dependent — they pass in isolation and their files are untouched by this diff (3-file diff verified against `origin/main`).

## Caveats

- None known. Interim assistant messages remain disabled; this fix delivers dropped content without turning on interim streaming.

author: menodk
body:
## O que entra

Integração completa com o ChatPro e a tela de cadastro que o paciente abre ao clicar no
link do WhatsApp — da BeHemp ou da Greens, que envia este mesmo endereço.

**O caminho do paciente:** manda mensagem no WhatsApp → o bot pergunta nome completo e
e-mail → confirmamos quem ele é numa chamada autenticada de volta ao ChatPro → nasce a
solicitação com protocolo e token de 7 dias → o corpo da resposta vira a mensagem com o
link → ele abre `/cadastro/{token}` já preenchido → cria a conta (e-mail é o login) →
agenda a teleconsulta.

### Estrutura

| camada | onde |
| --- | --- |
| lógica do ChatPro | `lib/chatpro/` — cliente, telefone, segredo, solicitação, diretório, processador, token |
| rotas | `app/api/chatpro/` — bot-link, intake, start, webhook, processar, solicitação |
| a tela | `app/(auth)/cadastro/[token]/` |
| gravação | `app/_actions/cadastro-por-link.ts` |
| tabelas | `solicitacoes_cadastro`, `chatpro_eventos`, `chatpro_diretorio`, `chatpro_sessoes` |
| decisões | `docs/adr/ADR-0015` |
| configuração manual | `docs/chatpro/COMO-CONECTAR-NO-PAINEL.md` |

## 🔴 Um defeito que este PR corrige e que valia para todo o repositório

O middleware do Clerk protege tudo por padrão e declara *"sempre roda para API routes"*.
Nem `/cadastro/{token}` nem `/api/chatpro/*` estavam na lista pública. Em produção isso
significaria: o paciente cai no login para poder criar conta (laço fechado), o servidor do
ChatPro recebe redirect e o bot marca falha, e **o log da aplicação não mostra nada** —
porque a requisição nunca chega à rota.

Os 31 testes locais passaram verdes porque o `.env` de desenvolvimento está sem as chaves
do Clerk, e sem elas o middleware não bloqueia. Foi preciso ler o middleware para achar.

As rotas não ficam desprotegidas: o token de 64 hex é a credencial do `/cadastro`, e as do
ChatPro têm autenticação própria (segredo em tempo constante, token no caminho da URL,
`CRON_SECRET`). O guarda tem um caso de **controle** que fica vermelho se alguém "resolver"
liberando `/medico`, `/admin` ou `/paciente`.

## Migrations — 10, todas aditivas

Este PR carrega `0025`–`0027` (ChatPro e cadastro), mas o journal da `main` está em 18 e o
da branch em 28: as `0018`–`0024`, do trabalho anterior, também sobem.

Auditadas uma a uma: **nenhuma é destrutiva** (só `CREATE TABLE`, `CREATE TYPE`,
`ADD COLUMN`, `ADD VALUE`), **nenhuma tem coluna obrigatória sem default**, e a única FK
nova aponta para tabela criada na migration anterior. O `ALTER TYPE ... ADD VALUE` rodou em
PG 15.17.

⚠️ O deploy roda `pnpm db:migrate` contra o banco de produção, sem rollback.

## LGPD

Conteúdo de mensagem nunca é gravado nem registrado: `message`, `alt_message`, `title` e
`url` de mídia são removidos antes do insert, e mensagens viram contador. Telefone, e-mail
e CPF saem mascarados em log. A auditoria registra que o cadastro aconteceu e sob qual
protocolo — não o conteúdo, que já está na ficha com controle de acesso. Conversa de
paciente de canabidiol é dado sensível pelo art. 11.

## Como foi verificado

- **31 testes ao vivo** contra o servidor local, com o banco conferido a cada passo
- **451 casos em 13 guardas**, verdes — os três novos somam 129 casos
- **31 sabotagens**, todas acusadas
- `pnpm typecheck` exit 0 · `pnpm test` verde · baseline verde · `pnpm build` exit 0 —
  rodados **depois** do merge da `main`

## ⚠️ Depende de configuração para funcionar

Nenhuma variável nova é obrigatória, então o deploy não quebra sem elas — mas a integração
sobe inerte até o `.env` da VPS receber `CHATPRO_INTAKE_SECRET`,
`CHATPRO_WEBHOOK_PATH_TOKEN`, `CHATPRO_INSTANCE_ID`, `CHATPRO_INSTANCE_TOKEN` e
`CRON_SECRET`, e até o painel do ChatPro e o cron serem ligados.

`NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL` precisa estar correta **com esquema**: errada, o endpoint responde 200
e o link dentro da mensagem não abre em lugar nenhum — e nenhum teste de backend pega isso.

## Ponto em aberto para o time

O hotfix #35 (mesclado hoje) manda paciente **sem autorização ANVISA** para
`/paciente/anvisa` no login. Esta tela, por decisão do dono, termina em
`/paciente/teleconsulta` — porque quem chega pelo WhatsApp não tem receita e precisa da
consulta. Os dois fluxos não colidem tecnicamente (o cadastro não passa pelo `/redirect`),
mas o paciente que sair e voltar cai na ANVISA. **Vale alinhar qual é a primeira tela do
paciente novo.**

author: nzbman
body:
## Summary

Upgrading to 0.19.14 backfills a `download_cleanup` row for every historical terminal download (1461 on one production install) and works through them at 100 per tick. Each legacy row spent three attempts failing the same way before settling, logging a warning per attempt plus a settle warning, and every policy-retained row logged at info. The result was a few thousand warn/info lines in the first minutes after upgrade.

## Changes

- An absent client entry with nothing left to verify now settles on the first observation. Absence is the adapter's authoritative answer, so retrying could never change it. Rows with no payload checkpoint settle at debug; a row whose host cleanup was actually planned keeps its single warning.
- Rows that can never be attributed (no title/facet, unreadable tracked state) are abandoned at once at debug instead of after the retry budget. Manual import re-attributing such a row reopens it so its cleanup actually runs.
- Policy-retained, recovered-absence and unresolved-client settles log at debug. A removed client stays at info.
- "terminal cleanup remains pending" warns on the first failure and then once per hour of backoff.
- Each reconcile tick that did cleanup work logs one summary line: settled outcomes by kind plus the count still pending.
- The absent-source reconciler follows an adapter's `Unknown` history cursor for up to eight pages before proving absence (PR #206 review finding). Without this a job behind the first history page on an adapter without exact lookup could never release its binding.

## Tests

- `durable_cleanup_settles_an_absent_entry_without_a_payload_checkpoint` and `durable_cleanup_abandons_unattributable_rows_at_once` replace the retry-budget variants.
- `durable_entry_only_cleanup_recovers_absence_but_not_unknown_or_reused_identity` now asserts the recorded outcome (a mismatched checkpoint settles as unverified, never as recovered).
- New `authoritative_absence_follows_the_history_cursor_past_the_first_page` (advancing cursor is followed; a stalled cursor preserves the binding).
- New store test `attribution_reopens_an_abandoned_cleanup_row`.

author: trroev
body:
## Summary

Resolves the vitest security advisory (CVE-2026-47429 / GHSA-5xrq-8626-4rwp) by bumping to **3.2.7** — staying on the v3 line, no v4 migration.

## Why not v4 (closes #121)

Renovate proposed jumping `^3.2.4 → ^4.0.0`, but the advisory is patched in **3.2.6+** as well, and our catalog range already permitted it. The vuln (arbitrary file read/exec via the Vitest UI server) only affects a **networked UI server** or **Windows browser mode** — neither applies to our headless CI on Linux — so there's no urgency to force the v4 migration. #121 should be closed in favor of this.

## Changes

- `pnpm-workspace.yaml`: catalog `vitest` and `@vitest/coverage-v8` bumped `^3.2.4 → ^3.2.7` (they're version-locked, so both move together).
- `pnpm-lock.yaml`: re-resolved + `pnpm dedupe`d so the vulnerable `vitest@3.2.4` is fully collapsed out of the tree (a naive single-dep bump left it behind via the coverage plugin's peer).

## Verification

- `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` passes (catalog snapshot consistent).
- No `vitest@3.2.4` package entry remains in the lockfile.

author: zen0bit
body:
Fixes the autobump workflow failing at the "Open PR" step (`autobump: not found` / `xdistdir can't find your void-packages tree`), so automatic update PRs can't be created.

**Root cause:** the PR body in `Create branch  push`... wait, it's in the `Open PR` step (`.github/workflows/autobump.yml`) contains unescaped backticks:

```
Generated by the `autobump` workflow using `xxautobump` in the oco-builder image.
```

GitHub Actions writes each `run:` block into a shell script, and backticks perform command substitution even inside double quotes. So the shell tried to execute `autobump` (→ `autobump: not found`) and `xxautobump` (→ exit code 1 with the `xdistdir` error) before the `curl POST /pulls` ever ran. With the workflow's `set -e`, the step died instantly.

**Fix:** escape the backticks (`\``）so they render as literal characters in the PR body.

Verified: the escaped snippet now prints the backticks literally in a shell, and the YAML still parses cleanly.

## Summary

Progresses #396. Keep the issue open after merge. This PR does not accept release thresholds, representative consumer scale, or a candidate disposition.

- Adds fresh-generation and primed-driver edit benchmarks at 25, 100, and 500 entities.
- Adds real consumer clean/edit builds and an identical emitted-source control without the analyzer.
- Retains twelve ShortRun measurements, 45 build samples, asset hashes, and report checksums.
- Researches Dapper AOT, Mapperly, EF Core, and Roslyn primary sources to propose useful comparisons without inventing an industry latency budget.

The proposed primary tier is 100 entities, with 25 small and 500 stress cases. It is not yet accepted. Matched Dapper AOT comparisons, representative consumer validation, and approved candidate limits remain pending. Larger generator restructuring stays in #182. #393 remains open.

## Validation

- Release benchmark project builds on .NET 8 and 10 without warnings or errors.
- All twelve .NET 10 ShortRun cases produced latency and allocation statistics.
- All twelve Dry cases executed successfully on .NET 8 and .NET 10; these are execution checks, not performance claims.
- All 45 real .NET 10 consumer build/control samples succeeded. Every analyzer-enabled build's generated source matched fresh-driver output outside measurement.
- Existing evidence destination was rejected without overwrite.
- Whitespace formatting, style verification, and diff checks passed.

## Standards

No findings. Report checksums, counts, medians, source links, and diagnostic limitations verified.

## Spec

No fix-required measurement findings. Two release requirements remain intentionally incomplete: representative consumers with accepted numeric thresholds, and candidate evidence or an explicit accepted disposition. The issue remains open after merge.

Livrer, en configuration Home Assistant, le premier lot runtime **Arsenal**
du chantier C51 (Lot 5 — backend d'émission de commande), restreint à
l'opération `AUDIT` pour ce premier lot pilote : générer une commande MQTT
d'admission NAS transactionnelle (`request_id`/`ts`/`expires_at`/`source`),
la publier sur le canal fixé par le contrat, et exposer la corrélation puis
un diagnostic de l'état de la transaction `AUDIT`. `RELEASE_DIFF` reste
explicitement hors périmètre (Lot 6, non commencé).

## Domaine(s) concerné(s)

Transverse — chantier
[`C51`](00_documentation_arsenal/audits/04_chantiers/transverses/c51_commandabilite_nas.md)
(§12.3, nouveau), contrat
[`contrats/nas_transactionnel.md`](00_documentation_arsenal/contrats/nas_transactionnel.md)
v1.2.1 (implémenté, **non modifié**).

## Couche(s) touchée(s)

- [x] **Décision** (template sensors, helpers, admissibilité) — helper d'ancrage, capteurs de corrélation/diagnostic
- [x] **Action** (automatisations, scripts souverains, exécutants bornés) — `script.nas_admission_demander_audit`
- [x] **Diagnostic / observabilité** — `sensor.nas_admission_audit_etat_transaction`

- [x] Documentation / contrat — mise à jour du chantier C51 et du registre

Nouvelles entités uniquement, aucune modification d'entité existante :

Aucune entité existante, aucun contrat NAS, aucune UI Lovelace modifiés.

## Déploiement

**Cible du déploiement :** dépôt `/homeassistant/` (alias runtime `/config`).

**Fichiers / composants concernés :**

`14_mqtt_sensors/system/nas_admission_result_raw.yaml`,
`12_template_sensors/system/nas_admission/`.

**Mode d'application Home Assistant** — reloads ciblés, aucun redémarrage complet requis :
- [x] Reload d'un domaine ou d'une intégration — préciser lequel : `input_text` (reload générique), `script.reload`, `mqtt` reload (recharge les sensors MQTT déclarés en YAML), `template.reload`.

**Précondition(s) éventuelle(s) :** identité MQTT dédiée `nas_admission` déjà

hors UI (Outils de développement > Actions), vérifier que

| `js-yaml` | 4.3.1 | 4.3.2 | #108 | high, `maxTotalMergeKeys` nao limita uso de CPU |
| `sharp` | 0.35.2 | 0.35.4 | #109 | high, vulnerabilidades no libheif |

O `vitest` e subida de **major** (3 para 4), entao a suite foi **exercida, nao suposta**.
`js-yaml` e `sharp` sao transitivos e entram por `override`, no padrao que o worker ja usava para
`undici`.

## Nota de metodo, porque quase virou erro

Eu quase classifiquei os alertas de `vitest` como falso positivo, porque `vitest` esta **ausente
do lockfile da raiz**. Ele nao estava ausente: estava em **outro manifesto**.

Num repo com dois lockfiles, `grep` na raiz responde pela raiz, nao pelo repo. O campo
`manifest_path` do alerta e quem diz de onde ele fala, e precisa ser lido antes de concluir
qualquer coisa.

## Exercido

- `npm test` no worker: **3 arquivos, 26 testes, 26 passando**, sob vitest 4.1.11
- `npm run typecheck`: exit **0**
- lockfile do worker varrido contra os quatro pisos, incluindo copias aninhadas

author: iskandr
body:
Fixes #310, #311 and #312 — all regressions in work I shipped in 3.37.0–3.38.0. Thanks for the reviews; all three reproduced.

## #310 — Pfeature cleanup could delete files in the installation (P1, destructive)

Confirmed at the upstream source: `pfeature_comp.py` ends with

```python
filelist = glob.glob("sam_allcomp*")
for file_2 in filelist:
    os.remove(file_2)
```

unscoped and relative to the working directory, and it scatters intermediates (`sam_allcomp.*`, `sam_input.csv`) there along the way. The sidecar ran it with `cwd=pfeature_home`, so it **required a writable installation, deleted any pre-existing `sam_allcomp*` file a user happened to have there, and let concurrent calls race over shared intermediate filenames.**

Each extraction now runs in its own `TemporaryDirectory` with a copy of `Data/` (~600 KB). The installation is only ever read; the wildcard cleanup can only reach the invocation's own scratch. Copy rather than symlink, deliberately — a symlinked tree would let the cleanup reach back into the installation.

Predictions are unchanged byte for byte (`3.157266404183623`, `3.7934723194625297` before and after).

The regression tests need no real Pfeature: a stub extractor reproduces the three behaviours that matter — relative `Data/` reads, intermediates in cwd, and the wildcard cleanup. Verified they fail against the previous code:

```
FAILED test_pfeature_cleanup_cannot_delete_files_in_the_installation
FAILED test_pfeature_leaves_no_intermediates_in_the_installation
FAILED test_pfeature_works_with_a_read_only_installation
```

plus a concurrency test running four extractions against one shared installation.

## #311 — PlifePred2 published an inference as established fact (P1)

You're right, and the internal contradiction you point at was real: the docstring said the transform was "established rather than assumed" while also admitting the training set is unknown, and it asserted an ex-vivo mammalian-whole-blood assay inherited from a paper whose dataset this model demonstrably does not use.

**`value` is now withheld by default.** `score` carries the model's native output — monotone in half-life, so ranking is unaffected — and a duration in hours requires opting in:

```python
PlifePred2().predict([pep])[0].blood_half_life.value                          # None
PlifePred2(assume_log10_seconds=True).predict([pep])[0].blood_half_life.value  # hours
```

The docs now separate three tiers explicitly:

- **Verified** — both models are `RandomForestRegressor`, so the output is not a class probability and upstream's `predict_proba` branch is dead code.
- **Inferred** — `log10(seconds)`, resting on the round-number leaf extrema (7.000 days, 95.0 days, ~7 significant figures) where log2 and ln invert the whole training range to seconds-to-minutes. The 20-second floor agreement is now described as **corroboration, not proof**, exactly on your reasoning: once the dataset differs, the old filter cannot establish the new target.
- **Not established** — species and assay matrix, inherited from a dataset this model does not use.

The derived QC column is renamed `hours_if_log10_seconds` so a QC frame can't be read as measured, and the tests that read as validating the transform now state they pin the arithmetic behind an inference rather than confirm it.

I did not withhold the typed endpoint entirely, taking your first option (gate) rather than the second. Say the word if you'd rather it not ship at all until the authors confirm.

## #312 — half-life leaked into the legacy affinity field (P2)

Reproduced, and my "no existing output changed" claim in #309 was wrong. `value_index` filled `Prediction.value` *by way of* `BindingPrediction.affinity`, so Thalf(h) reached a field documented as an IC50 and surfaced through `predict_peptides` and `to_dataframe`.

The parser plumbing is reverted — `affinity` is `None` for NetMHCstabpan again, as before #309 — and the hours are resolved in `to_pred` instead, which is the single conversion point and the one place the kind is known. Tests now cover the legacy object, dataframe and serialization paths alongside the typed one, plus `best_by_value(Kind.pMHC_stability)` and the zero-half-life case.

## Not addressed here

#313–#317 are queued behind these three, per your prioritization. Your per-bond note — that an enzyme field alone won't preserve site coordinates and context — is taken; I haven't started that design and won't until the shape is agreed.

Full suite: 798 passed, and the PlifePred2 end-to-end tests were re-run against the real forest.

body:
## Summary

`garry-starr-classic-penguins-off-broadway-2026` sat in `status='previews'` with `openingDate=null` for 6 days after it actually opened (2026-09-08, reviews live at 7 outlets by 2026-09-09), because `opening-night-poller.yml`'s auto-discovery filter required `openingDate` to already be set. That's a deadlock: `openSignalFromDiscovery()` (`scripts/lib/opening-signal.js`) is supposed to backfill `openingDate` from discovered review-publish dates, but discovery only ever runs via the poller, and the poller would never run without `openingDate` already set. At least 7 other off-Broadway shows are in the identical stuck state right now.

- `opening-night-poller.yml`'s "Find shows to poll" step now admits a `previews`-status show with no `openingDate` once `previewsStartDate` is 5–30 days old, via a new `isStuckPreviewsPollCandidate()` helper in `scripts/lib/opening-signal.js` (colocated with the file's other named thresholds). Bounded window: old enough to have plausibly opened, capped so a genuinely undiscoverable show doesn't re-enter every orchestrator run (5x/day) forever.
- Fixes a latent bug the new branch would have hit immediately: `runAggregators()` in `scripts/opening-night-poller.js` computed `year` from `new Date(show.openingDate)` unguarded — a null `openingDate` produced the epoch (1970), which `validatePageMatchesShow`'s year-mismatch check then used to reject every real 2025/2026 DTLI/Show Score page. Guarded like every other `openingYear` call site in the codebase.
- 5 new unit tests for `isStuckPreviewsPollCandidate()`; all 19 tests in `opening-signal.test.mjs` pass.

Reviewed per CLAUDE.md §18 (shared-infrastructure gate) via `/second-opinion` before the first edit — findings (1 correctness blocker, 2 design blockers) addressed inline; verdict recorded in `.claude/review-verdicts.jsonl`.

Explicitly out of scope (smaller follow-ups, not bundled here): `audit-opening-dates.js`'s SERP-based date discovery is `category === 'broadway'`-only (off-Broadway/West End get no equivalent daily audit); `enrich-off-broadway-dates.js` runs weekly and recent runs have an unrelated push-race failure in its audit-trail commit step.

author: raphael
body:
Dedicated pagination tools let the model request the next page with `{}` while the runtime restores the original query and page cursor. Their generated tool specification already described that smaller model input, but its decoder still required the complete execution input. An authored `{}` example therefore failed tool-definition registration with a missing-query error, before a model call could run.

## Match each decoder to the input it accepts

`ToolSpec.Payload.Codec` now matches the model-facing schema and example. A required `ExecutionPayloadCodec` matches the existing `ExecutionPayloadSchema`: it decodes and encodes the complete arguments after the runtime restores the query and cursor. Ordinary tools share the same codec implementation when both input shapes are identical.

The generator establishes hidden fields and cursor requirements in the Goa attributes before producing both schemas and decoders. This removes the separate schema-only cursor adjustment. It reuses the existing public typed execution payload and generates a private model decoder only where needed; no new model-visible fields or public payload types are added.

The separate MCP generator also supplies both contracts. MCP forwards model arguments unchanged, so its generated registrations share the existing codec and schema between model and execution inputs.

Execution, result previews, and restoration of saved work use the execution codec. Registration rejects handwritten specifications missing either execution codec function. Dedicated model inputs still reject query/cursor fields, and execution inputs still reject missing required query/cursor data. The runtime's exact empty-object rule for generated continuation actions is unchanged.

## Upgrade and compatibility

Regenerate tool specifications before starting workers on this version. Handwritten specifications must supply `ExecutionPayloadCodec`, sharing the existing codec when appropriate. Application code decoding complete executed or saved inputs through `Payload.Codec` must use `ExecutionPayloadCodec` instead. Generated typed payload codecs and typed tool descriptors retain their execution meaning. For dedicated pagination, the initial codec now enforces the already-declared no-cursor contract. Decode later-page requests with their actual continuation tool codec, without relabeling them as initial requests. Previously accepted initial requests containing a cursor were outside that contract and are not preserved. Provider-injected fields remain absent from transported JSON and are filled by the provider.

This changes the in-process Go contract, not model schemas, registry messages, stored payload formats, continuation identity, or correlation between parallel queries. No database migration or data rewrite is required. Update the framework and generated code together; do not start an upgraded runtime with old handwritten/generated specifications. No service-wire cutover is required. Repository runtime documentation includes these steps; the public website companion is [goa.design #249](https://github.com/goadesign/goa.design/pull/249).

## Verification

- A real generated-package regression constructs dedicated continuation definitions with authored `{}` examples and registers them through the runtime.
- Generated tests cover retained queries, cursor-only continuation, canonical JSON field naming, rejected unknown/missing fields, ordinary model-owned paging, and provider injection.
- Runtime tests distinguish model and execution codecs, preserve original model arguments, restore saved execution payloads, and keep independent continuation chains separate.
- Generated MCP checks cover no-argument tools, typed and located payloads, colliding tool names, and preservation of every JSON control character.
- Full `make test` passed after updating both generator paths and the Temporal test fixture: race/coverage across all non-integration packages, followed by quickstart tests.
- CI build and integration tests passed on the complete code head `bfb603e7`; the documentation-only follow-up reruns CI.
- `make lint` and `git diff --check` passed.

Review `runtime/agent/tools/spec.go`, `codegen/agent/specs_builder_plan_types.go`, and `codegen/agent/tests/continuation_input_codecs_test.go` first for the public contract, generation ownership, and actual registration regression. These checks prove the framework behavior, not downstream model-answer quality.

body: ## Summary - Skip the ancestor warm-cache scan when the current render episode is newer than every attached cache. - Advance one numeric maximum at the existing cache attachment point. Older retries remain eligible; root retry caches and held/promoted transition harvests keep their existing lookup paths. - Add behavioral regressions, a production benchmark guard integrated into recursive-context work checks, and an `octane` patch changeset. Partially addresses #981's parallel-use warm-plan item. This targets irrelevant adoption scans after prior warming; complex warm-plan allocation and other active-plan traversal work remain separate follow-ups. ## Performance evidence Baseline: merged main `7804852be69a78d11f3dc160f44d3bd358bedfc1`. Same production fixture, Node 26.4.0, and Chromium 149.0.7827.55. Detailed Chromium coverage observes the parent-property read in the actual emitted runtime helper, without source probes. ```sh BENCH_JSON=/tmp/warm-adoption.json node benchmarks/recursive-context/warm-adoption-work.mjs ``` | Scenario | Memo misses | Parent reads before | After | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | Depth 32 mount after unrelated warming | 33 | 1,089 | 0 | | Depth 32 update after unrelated warming | 33 | 1,089 | 0 | | Depth 128 mount after unrelated warming | 129 | 16,641 | 0 | | Depth 128 update after unrelated warming | 129 | 16,641 | 0 | Adoption calls remain 33/129, all memo values and surviving DOM nodes match, and the no-warming control remains at zero adoption calls. A real pending retry retains one adoption, one cache probe, and two parent reads; parent and child resources each start once. The final zero-parent-step guard fails on the untouched baseline. Both compiler files then passed **51/51** with two workers, and all **15 browser files / 130 tests passed** with Chromium permissions and two workers. No code changes were needed for these reruns. - [x] `pnpm typecheck:files packages/octane/src/runtime.ts` - [x] Scoped `pnpm format:files:check` for all changed files and `git diff --check` - [x] `pnpm sync` (no generated changes) - [x] Standalone warm-adoption benchmark and complete integrated recursive-context work pass for TSRX/TSX - [x] Production async-composition: initialization and transition update each retain eight network starts, eight creators, seven first-wave resources, two dependency waves, and zero mixed states. Existing resource retention, dependent-owner ordering, and lazy-module/node identity gates passed. - Full repository `pnpm test`, `pnpm typecheck`, and `pnpm format:check` were not run locally; the core suite and scoped checks above cover the local change. [Current-head CI](https://github.com/octanejs/octane/actions/runs/34397388909) passed **all 26 jobs** on `c176cd00e2fdc01647a3488929003652e1b2efcf` (attempt 2). The first attempt hit the same five-second Volar compiler-test timeout; that shard and one canceled shard passed unchanged on rerun. Cursor Bugbot completed successfully with no findings, and there are no review threads to resolve. ## Risk / follow-ups The maximum is never reset or reduced, including when an older root resumes. An outdated maximum can only permit extra scanning; it cannot hide a matching cache. This adds no per-block fields, allocations, retained trees, or cache invalidation hooks. SSR has a separate runtime; client hydration and native resource adoption retain their existing semantics. Independent source review found no correctness issues. The tests use a retained outer boundary around dynamic content so a root retry cache cannot hide a broken ancestor lookup. Active-plan recording stays intact because earlier completed siblings must still be remembered before later siblings suspend. ## Provenance - [x] An agent produced this diff (`agent-authored`) --- Need help on this PR? author: ecomrodrii
body:
Octava pasada. Abrí por primera vez la **hoja de compra** — la última pantalla antes de pagar, y la única de la app que no había mirado nunca.

## El fallo

El escaparate y la hoja decían **precios distintos del mismo plan**:

| | |
|---|---|
| tarjeta de la tienda | Mensual ilimitado — **89 €/mes** |
| hoja de compra | Mensual ilimitado — **89 €** |

Y la hoja es la que se lee con el dedo ya en «Continuar al pago». Ahí, un cobro que se repite cada mes se presentaba como un pago único, sin el periodo por ninguna parte.

## Por qué pasaba

El escaparate ya sabía hacerlo (`familia === 'suscripcion'` → `/{nombrePeriodo}`). La hoja simplemente **no preguntaba**: imprimía `euros(plan.precio)` a secas, en sus dos precios — el titular y la fila «Precio» del resumen.

La regla pasa a estar en un solo sitio (`esSuscripcion`, exportada de `lib/student/tienda.ts`, que es donde ya vivía `familiaDePlan`) y la usan las dos pantallas. Ese fichero ya defendía este criterio para el periodo: *«el nombre del periodo lo decide un solo sitio para el panel y para el escaparate»*.

## Lo que NO cambia

- Un **bono** sigue sin periodo: se paga una vez.
- Una **trimestral** dice «/trimestre», no «/mes» — el periodo sale de `nombrePeriodo`, igual que en la tienda. No se da por hecho que toda suscripción sea mensual.
- El estudio **sin pagos activados** sigue diciendo por qué no se puede comprar, y no ofrece pagar.

## Verificación

- 4339 unitarios en verde (el único rojo, `billing-rules`, falla igual en `main` limpio).
- `tsc` y eslint limpios.
- 13/13 en los e2e de compra (`student-descuento`, `student-hoja-compra`, `comprar-productos-fisicos`).
- Falsado: quitando el periodo otra vez caen **los dos tests de suscripción**, y los del bono y el estudio sin pagos siguen verdes — que es exactamente lo que deben hacer.
