author: smoralesm07-source
body:
## Qué cambia

La vista **Cobertura** publicaba la brecha SII↔UAF en agregado: 79.449 RUT observados, 34 gatillantes, la razón por sector. Todo cierto y nada que un analista pudiera abrir, porque la línea base llegaba declarada y sin RUT — la pantalla decía **cuántos** faltan y jamás **quiénes** son.

El dato entidad-por-entidad ya existía en la base y nunca había llegado a la interfaz: `aml_v_uaf_potential_screening_current_v0812` resuelve 74.087 observaciones y califica **115 con hipótesis de registro accionable**, con índice desglosado, materialidad, coherencia de tipo, territorio, escala, estructura societaria y estado de revisión.

*(El rediseño del Pulso en cuatro lentes conmutables que abrió este trabajo ya está en `main`; este PR trae únicamente el rediseño de Cobertura que lo continúa.)*

## Qué hace ahora la pantalla

- **Embudo de cuatro pasos**: 74.087 observadas → 44.799 con constitución verificable → 115 accionables → 5 revisadas, con la caída declarada en cada tramo y escala logarítmica (lo dice: entre 74.087 y 5 hay cuatro órdenes de magnitud).
- **Cuatro cifras de mando**: cola accionable, sin revisar, IVO medio, materialidad media — cada una con lo que *no* mide escrito debajo.
- **Paneles que además filtran**: de dónde salen los candidatos (observadas vs. calificadas por sector) y el perfil de la cola (banda IVO, forma societaria, tamaño) — son criterios de triage, no adornos.
- **Una ficha por entidad**, con el desglose del IVO como argumento central: cada segmento vale lo que pesa en el índice y se llena con lo que aporta, de modo que el tramo vacío de evidencia regulatoria dice, sin texto, que ninguna de las 115 tiene hoy un acto de un regulador que la respalde. Debajo: giro coincidente con su concentración en el sector, territorio, tamaño, dotación, antigüedad, estructura, materialidad y el pronunciamiento de quien ya la revisó.

## El read model

`obs_uaf_potential_total`, `_sector` y `_candidate`, materializados por `obs_refresh_uaf_potential()` y publicados por `obs_uaf_potential()` (migración `0022`, ya aplicada a la base). Los 115 accionables viajan enteros; las 73.972 observaciones no calificadas quedan en agregado y nunca se presentan como cola de trabajo.

## Límites que la pantalla publica

El candidato es una **hipótesis de registro**: no acredita que reúna los elementos que activan la obligación de inscribirse ni que incumpla. El IVO ordena revisión — no es probabilidad de obligación ni de LA/FT — y su credibilidad se imprime junto al puntaje. La materialidad mide el costo de incorporar, no la gravedad de nada. Ausencia del corte público UAF no equivale a no estar inscrita.

## Verificación

- `tsc --noEmit` limpio y build ok contra el estado real de `main` (probé un merge local antes de abrir este PR: sin conflictos de archivos, sin errores de tipos).
- El arnés `tests/render.mjs` incluye la comprobación `cobertura` con fixtures reales, y pasa.

body: ## Summary Closes #10 This PR adds an exported `selectTier()` function that allows users to predict which tier a set of inputs will qualify for before generating a full proof. ## Problem Issue #10 reported that the SDK's `selectThreshold` could select a tier at boundary values that the circuit would not satisfy, leading to confusing `meets_threshold=0` errors. ## Solution While the core formula fix was already applied in previous PRs (the SDK now correctly mirrors the circuit's integer arithmetic), this PR: 1. **Exports a new `selectTier()` API** that provides a clean, testable interface for tier prediction: ```typescript const tier = selectTier({ txCount: 50, disputeCount: 0, monthsActive: 12, avgBalance: 5000, }); // Returns: 3 (Gold) ``` 2. **Adds 8 new boundary tests** that directly test the exported `selectTier` function at all critical score boundaries: - Score 39 → Unverified (below Bronze) - Score 40 → Bronze (at Bronze boundary) - Score 69 → Bronze (below Silver) - Score 70 → Silver (at Silver boundary) - Score 84 → Silver (below Gold) - Score 85 → Gold (at Gold boundary) - Plus edge cases for maximum and zero scores 3. **Updates test documentation** to reference issue #10 ## Circuit/SDK Formula Verification Both the circuit and SDK use identical formulas: - `score_proxy = tx_capped*480 + clean_txs*480 + age_capped*1000 + bal_capped` - `threshold_scaled = threshold * 700` - Tier is satisfied when `score_proxy >= threshold_scaled` ## Test Results ``` Test Suites: 1 passed, 1 total Tests: 35 passed, 35 total (27 existing + 8 new) ``` ## Acceptance Criteria - [x] `computeScoreProxy()` exported from SDK for independent testing - [x] Dedicated unit tests for tier selection at boundary scores (39, 40, 69, 70, 84, 85) - [x] No regression in `generateReputationProof`

author: posthog[bot]
body:
## Problem

- Everyone who opens the login page or the password reset page sends a 2FA capability request that the server rejects with a 400.
- A person whose second factor is a passkey can then reach the 2FA step with no passkey button, because the rejected answer stays cached and nothing asks again.
- `login2FALogic` asked for the methods in `afterMount`. The endpoint answers only for a pending 2FA session, which neither of those pages has.
- Kea mounts a logic alongside anything that references its actions. The login funnel telemetry added in [#92064](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/pull/92064) references this logic's actions, so both pages mount it.

## Changes

- The 2FA step is now the only page that asks which methods exist, so the login and password reset pages send no request.
- Every arrival at the 2FA step asks again, so a cached rejection cannot hide the passkey button.
- `urlToAction` keyed on the 2FA route replaces `afterMount`, which makes the route rather than the mount decide when to ask.
- The endpoint keeps returning 400 without a pending session. That is the correct answer to the request, and relaxing it would leave a pointless request on every login page view.

Nothing looks different on the 2FA screen in the normal case: its markup is unchanged. The fix restores the passkey button in the case where the cached rejection hid it, verified through the logic value that gates the button rather than through a render.

## How did you test this code?

- New `login2FALogic.test.ts`, four cases. They catch three regressions no existing test covered, since the logic had no test file.
  - Mounting the logic through the telemetry logic on the login or password reset page must send no request. Guards against the rejected request returning.
  - Reaching the 2FA step must ask again. Guards against a cached `passkeysAvailable: false` hiding the passkey button.
  - Mounting while the router already sits on the 2FA route must ask. Guards a refresh or hard load against a later move to a navigation-only trigger.
- The first three cases fail against the previous `afterMount` version and pass after the change. The refresh case passes both ways, and locks in behavior a refactor could silently drop.
- The backend is unchanged. `test_passkey_2fa_methods_endpoint` already covers a user with TOTP only, a passkey only, and both, and `test_passkey_2fa_methods_endpoint_requires_session` covers the 400.
- Not run: the dev stack, so the flow was not exercised in a browser. The repo-wide frontend typecheck reports 435 pre-existing errors from the unbuilt `@posthog/quill` workspace, none in the touched files.

## Automatic notifications

- [ ] Publish to changelog?

## Docs update

None. No user-facing behavior is documented for this endpoint.

## 🤖 Agent context

**Autonomy:** Fully autonomous

Claude Code, from an inbox report about a burst of 400 responses on the passkey methods route. Skills invoked: `/writing-tests`, `/writing-pr-descriptions`, plus the repo `simplify` pass and `hogli ci:preflight --fix`.

The route was traced from the report's normalized path to `/api/login/2fa/passkey/methods/`, then to the two client callers. A scratch Jest probe confirmed that mounting the telemetry logic on `/login` mounts `login2FALogic` and fires exactly one request, and a second probe confirmed the cached `false` survives a navigation to the 2FA step with no retry. Both probes were deleted; the committed test file covers the same two properties.

The first draft carried a four line comment that narrated the old behavior. It was cut to two lines stating the invariant, per the repo rule against recording change history in code comments. Fixing the endpoint to return 200 instead was considered and rejected, for the reason given under Changes.

No open PR fixes this: `gh pr list --state open --search` over the endpoint, the logic name, and the telemetry found only unrelated passkey and 2FA work. No customer or session material appears in the diff or this description.

body:
## Thinking Path

> - Paperclip shows agent work in task feeds.
> - Native tools and provider notices appear in that feed.
> - A routine completion call adds no useful action for the user.
> - A provider notice needs readable text to explain its warning.
> - This change hides the completion call and displays the notice summary.
> - Saved run events remain available for inspection.

## Linked Issues or Issue Description

**What happened?**

The feed showed paperclip_finish as a normal tool call. Provider notices showed
a generic name or a large key-value table instead of a clear warning message.

**Expected behavior**

Hide the routine completion call from the task feed. Show a warning icon,
a short severity heading, and the full notice summary across the row.

**Steps to reproduce**

1. Open a native Codex task that calls paperclip_finish.
2. Inspect its tool activity in the task feed.
3. Inspect a run with a repository-trust provider notice.

**Paperclip version or commit**

Reproduced on the implementation checkout. Replayed onto master at 6abeb6733.
The search found no duplicate PR for this display change.

**Deployment mode**

Local source checkout with native task feeds.

## What Changed

- Hide paperclip_finish calls and results in task-feed adapters.
- Preserve the raw events for run-log inspection.
- Carry provider-notice text into the transcript.
- Render notices with an icon, severity heading, and full-width summary.
- Cover the display and transcript mapping with regression tests.

## Verification

- The affected UI tests and the token gates passed on the implementation checkout.
- Browser inspection confirmed the warning text is readable and completion calls are hidden.
- Repository typecheck and build passed. Repository test groups passed after resource retests.
- On this PR branch, 123 focused UI tests and the token gates passed. All GitHub checks passed; Greptile is 5/5 with no unresolved threads.

## Risks

- The task feed hides one known internal tool. Raw run events remain unchanged.
- Long warning text must wrap within the available width.
- No provider warning classification, accounting, or recovery behavior changes here.

## Model Used

OpenAI Codex, GPT-6 (`gpt-6-astra`). Used for reasoning, code edits, tool use,
and test execution. The exact context-window limit is not exposed in this
session. Real-provider acceptance used Codex CLI 0.153.4 with `gpt-5.6-sol`.

author: bjmeetsfo
body:
The cap binds under a budget, and the fill stops there

mx#1379 made a token budget OVERRIDE the slot cap, and shipped a test asserting
exactly that. A production-corpus run showed what it costs.

  packs           3,627 - 4,358 refs
  retrieve p50    9,769 ms
  proxy RSS       787 MB, peaking at 1.44 GB
  gateway RSS     587 MB, peaking at 1.03 GB

A default of 1000 refs is not a default if a budget silently lifts it. The cap
binds again and the budget narrows it further -- a pack holds whichever is
SMALLER -- and the fill now stops once the cap is reached instead of pricing
thousands of refs it can never return. On the corpus above that was most of the
fill: tokens_of and layer_of ran for every candidate past 1000.

The test that asserted the old behaviour is renamed and reversed rather than
deleted, so the record shows the behaviour changed and why:
a_budget_overrides_the_slot_cap becomes
a_budget_narrows_the_pack_but_does_not_lift_the_cap, and its control -- the same
store and cap with no budget returning exactly one ref -- still stands, because
that half was always right.

The measurement above came from a gated run: ingest returned 202, killing the
proxy made ingest 500 (so the gateway was really on the native backend rather
than the local adapter), and the encoder's own tick counter moved (so vectors
were the encoder's 1024 dims and not the 32-dim hash fallback).

108 tests pass in the proxy binary.

### Public website (/, /services, /about, /contact)

- **Abstract background animation** — custom canvas scene (slow-drifting emerald gradient orbs + rising micro-bubbles) on the hero and dark CTA bands; capped DPR, paused off-screen via IntersectionObserver, static frame under `prefers-reduced-motion`

Session-authenticated (scrypt hashing, hashed session IDs, httpOnly cookies, middleware gate, login throttling). Enables managing **without touching code**:

Zod validation on every input, honeypot + per-IP rate limiting on the contact form, sanitised media serving (no path traversal), login rate limiting, security headers.

## 1. The avatar builder is worth using, and it now saves

30 icons (up from 6), 16 colours (up from 8), three shapes, six textures and an optional outline — all on the **client side** as well as the teacher marks, since they share one enum.

**No human figures.** The first cut had six dancers — arabesque, grand jeté, handstand, breaker's freeze — and they were rejected on sight. The contact sheet shows why: these render at ~15px of actual ink on a teacher mark, and a figure at that size is a smudge with a dot over it. Styles are named by the thing you wear or carry instead: pointe shoe, snapback, tap plate, jazz hands, tutu.

Eight icons carry their detail as **cut-outs** under `fill-rule="evenodd"` — the mirror ball's facets, the medal's star, the ribbons across the pointe shoe, the hatband on the bowler. Each was an unreadable blob until the detail became the tile showing through.

**It used to save nowhere.** `IdentityCard` held everything in `useState` and wrote it to no table — it rendered, validated and previewed, and forgot you on reload. New `portal_avatar_prefs` table, own-row-only RLS. Deliberately not columns on `portal_household_members`: that table decides whether a login sees one dancer or a whole family, and Postgres won't split one table's columns across two policies.

## 2. Teacher photos — staff app only

New **private** `staff-photos` bucket, readable only by `is_active_staff()`. Not `portal-documents`, whose read policy lets anon SELECT so a parent on a studio code can sign a URL. Not `authenticated` either — every parent has an account, so that would have put staff photos one signed URL from the portal.

The portal is untouched; `TeacherAvatar` still draws coloured marks. `avatar_path` stores the object key and signs on read, because a stored signed URL rots in an hour.

Upload obeys the slow-tap rule: disabled button *and* a busy ref, striped indeterminate bar, live status line that carries the meaning without the animation.

## 3. "Your teachers" on the dashboard

Costs no request — `instructor_name` was already in `ENROLLMENT_COLUMNS`, and the marks come from the looks `PortalContext` already fetches. Splits multi-teacher fields (one mark for "Chill Kerney, Ky'ree Nevels" gives the initials CN — an invented third person beside their real names), groups by `normalizeName`, sorts by how many of the family's classes each teacher takes.

## The bug this fixes

`portal_instructor_looks` constrained `icon_key` and `palette_key` with enum CHECKs listing exactly the 6 icons and 8 colours from v46. The picker now offers 30 and 16, so **every save of a new one would have been refused with 23514** — the UI outgrew the constraint. v53 replaces both with a format check; the reasoning for reversing that v46 decision is in the migration header.

## Migration

`supabase-migration-v53-avatars-and-staff-photos.sql` — **already applied to production and verified**: the three stored teacher looks are byte-identical, RLS is on with two policies, the bucket is private with four storage policies, and Supabase's security advisor reports no new findings.

Build clean, 770 tests pass, verified at 375px and 320px in light and dark.

body:
## Summary

Device Key Custody now says what a device holds beyond the Master Key, what counts as activity for the idle lock, and how a secret is entered at a device. `DK-7`'s zeroization claim reaches the whole **secret-bearing inventory** — everything a device holds that carries the Master Key, is derived from it or wrapped under it, or unlocks it — and names the one test that asserts membership over the whole list. `DK-4` defines activity as the span of a keyed operation rather than the arrival of a request. A new `DK-10` states that a Passphrase or Recovery Code is taken from a non-echoing prompt, or from one explicitly selected line of standard input, never from a command-line argument. The concept documents carry the vocabulary those rules assume, and the register states the citation convention its two documentation trees already follow. Documentation only; no behaviour changes.

## Changes

- `docs/spec/device-key-custody/README.md`: two sub-items under `DK-7` (the inventory and its `Form: test` half), a sub-item under `DK-4`, and `DK-10` with two sub-items — one on the two-line stdin order, one stating that only the Recovery Code has a length bound (a Passphrase has no form to check against; `coffret-shell`'s Passphrase reader reads a line with no ceiling).
- `docs/spec/README.md`: the "Rule IDs" section now states that inside the register a rule cites a sibling bare, and everywhere else a citation carries the `spec:` prefix; the DK row's coverage mentions how a secret is entered. The Rust and TypeScript trees still mix both spellings; normalizing them is not part of this change.
- Concepts: `master-key` gains the `lock` collocation, a lock rule (`DK-3`, `DK-4`, `DK-7`) and the inventory rule, with the same definition as the register; `passphrase` gains the rule that a Passphrase is spent by the one unlock that needs it, with the no-route-back-through-a-browser sub-bullet; `recovery-code` cites `DK-10`; `container/entry` says "the Entry Path the file had at the moment the Container was written" instead of "Library name", which the Library concept reserves for the device-local name.
- Comment-only citations: `DK-10` from the Recovery Code reader's module doc and its four tests and from the two CLI setup cases that check `--help` and the round-trip scripts; `DK-4` from the four idle-lock cases; `DK-7`'s test half from the two zeroization assertions. The idle-lock doc no longer claims it never fires mid-operation: it defers rather than interrupts, and the moment between reading the clock and emptying the cell is deliberately unfenced because whoever took a handle first finishes on it. Five `coffret-device` sites now say "device-local Library name".
- Fixed while refining: the inventory definition initially read "carries it or is derived from it", which excluded the Passphrase (it unlocks the key) and the Container Keys (`KD-2` says they are never derived, only wrapped) that the enumeration lists; "the device as wanted" became "the Library as wanted", the object `want` takes throughout the lock module; a bare `(DK-4)` in a new test comment became `(spec: DK-4)` per the convention this change writes down.

## Review notes

The acceptance criteria live in the accompanying `docs/tasks/2026/0909-1507-carry-key-custody-past-the-master-key.md`. Every item is automated and ticked by the canonical check (`make check` plus grep gates over the register, the concept documents, and the cited test files, including two guards that keep `docs/spec/` free of `spec:`-prefixed citations and `docs/concepts/` free of bare ones); the task has no manual items. Worth a close read: the `DK-7` sub-items and the master-key concept's inventory rule, whose definition was revised across three refine rounds.

Recommended order: merge kabo-sh/kabo-plugins-internal#226 first, then this PR, so the two `main` branches carry the same plugin tree.

author: mikenedry
body:
Repeated equation-row copies, diffusion-array allocation, temporary query BVHs, and full polygon-adjacency rebuilds add overhead to remeshing. This patch reuses scratch storage, visits the existing source BVH directly, and updates only changed polygon incidences after accepted pentagon merges.

Accepted for merge after visual review. The measured full-suite total is lower; the default-thread geometry and runtime limitations documented below remain follow-up work.

## Implementation

- Reuse one equation-row vector during reduced-system assembly and one destination array per diffusion loop. Bound diffusion scratch lifetime to the loop, before subsequent energy assembly.
- Preserve curve-query intersection tests, traversal order, chain ties and endpoint selection while removing the temporary query tree and hit vector.
- Maintain edge incidences, vertex neighbors and boundary flags locally after accepted pentagon merges. Preserve sorted face IDs and repeated edge occurrences, and detect index normalization outside the immediate collapse neighborhood.

Sampling, geometry arithmetic, feature classification, integer rounding and recovery acceptance rules are unchanged. The patch changes four source files, with 119 insertions and 59 deletions. No mesh assets, benchmark binaries, generated reports or new test infrastructure are included.

## Validation and performance

- Release build and existing CTest suite pass (2/2).
- Targeted research proofs: 19 exact polygon replays and 1,539 independently reconstructed adjacency states; 497,532 curve-query differential comparisons plus 201 targeted comparisons and 103 analytic assertions; 86 solver systems, 827 state comparisons and 737 controlled solves; 100 randomized diffusion cases.
- Fresh paired full-suite runs: 682.46 to 626.62 seconds, an 8.18% reduction. One model process at a time, alternating before/after order between models, no timeout, with rendering outside the timing window. External machine activity was not controlled.
- All full-suite outputs are finite, have valid faces and no nonmanifold edges. Magnified bust face/ear views and recent cap/base checks preserve visible detail. The box boundary measurements match the baseline.

These are not universally byte-identical full-pipeline results, nor a claim that every model is faster. Targeted correctness proofs do not resolve all default-thread numerical and recovery variability.

## Observed limitations

- A visible, localized wrench jaw-tip notch appears in two of three candidate runs; all three default-thread baseline runs are closed. A controlled baseline reproduces the notch and its full output matches the controlled candidate byte-for-byte, proving existing susceptibility but not unchanged default-mode defect frequency.
- The keyboard bracket chooses different recovery layouts. Both binaries vary substantially between repeats, but the candidate's sampled fitting range extends beyond the observed baseline range. Its three-run median is 58.53 versus 42.17 seconds, with overlapping ranges of 35.27–59.74 and 40.20–59.31 seconds. A controlled full-pipeline comparison still differs.
- Quality-only isolation runs do not identify a clean single-change rollback: removing row reuse gives one open and one closed wrench, removing curve-query changes gives two closed outputs, and removing both still gives two open outputs. These small concurrent samples are not defect-rate estimates or speed measurements. Do not change geometry acceptance rules to make this performance patch pass.

The visual results were accepted for this merge. Default-mode geometry variability and recovery-sensitive runtime remain unresolved; this PR does not claim to fix them.

author: breezyslasher
body:
Two follow-ups to the wrong-match repair added in #52, both about the moment a person is looking at a list and deciding.

## The move is now a choice

Applying a match rewrites the tags and files the track where those tags say it belongs. That is right for the usual case: a wrong match is not only wrong tags, since the folder and filename were built from them too, so the track is sitting under the wrong artist and album and fixing only the tags half-fixes it.

It is wrong for a library whose layout is not this one. Several collections under a single mount — `/music/ALL`, `/music/Kids` — have no room in `{albumartist}/{album}/{track}`:

```
/music/ALL/98 Degrees/Revelation/03 - track.mp3
  ->  /music/98°/Revelation (2000)/Give Me Just One Night.mp3
```

That carries the file out of the collection it belongs to, and out of any folder-scoped scan of it. So the move is a checkbox, **on by default**. Unticked, the file is re-tagged where it stands and its `.lrc` is left alone, since nothing moved for it to follow.

## Cover art where it settles the question

Songs, Albums and Videos have always had artwork on the cards. The two searches added since — Lyrics, and the MusicBrainz candidate list — did not, and they are the two where it helps most, because both ask a person to tell near-identical rows apart.

**MusicBrainz candidates** are the ones that earn it. Two recordings with the same title and artist are usually the studio cut and a live or compilation version, and the sleeve settles it at a glance where reading the release name does not. Art comes from the Cover Art Archive by release id, loaded by the browser — so a release with no cover costs nothing server-side, and plenty have none, so an image that fails is hidden rather than leaving a broken icon on every row.

**Lyrics results** get Apple's artwork. Apple hands the url back as a template with `{w}` and `{h}` in it, so it is not a link until those are filled; filled at 160 it matches the thumbnails the other modes already show.

author: peatey
body:
Fixes #238.

## The bug

A failed Cloudability connection test at startup left the agent running with an empty `StorageServices` slice for the life of the process. `uploadData` iterated that empty slice, fell through to `os.Remove`, and deleted every tarball as if it had been uploaded — so samples were silently discarded until the pod was restarted.

## Reported bugs

- **Startup failure permanently disabled the uploader.** Storage services are now built through `ensureStorageServices`, which rebuilds them lazily when the slice is empty instead of only once at startup. The cooldown is stamped *after* the build finishes, not before, so a build that outlasts `UploadFrequency` cannot defeat its own gate.
- **Empty `StorageServices` silently discarded tarballs.** `UploadData` returns `ErrNoStorageServices` before any `os.Remove`, so the tarball survives and is retried on a later cycle.
- **`testUpload` backoff was nanoseconds.** `time.Duration(math.Pow(2, i))` made the three retries fire ~2ns, ~4ns and ~8ns apart. Now seconds-scale, with no sleep after the final attempt, behind an injectable seam so tests stay fast.

## Defects those symptoms were hiding

- **`doWithRetry` had the identical nanosecond backoff**, and never closed the response body of a failed attempt — leaking a connection per retry.
- **The presigned S3 PUT could not be retried at all.** This is the request in the issue's `connection reset by peer` log. `doWithRetry` re-issues the same `*http.Request`, and `Client.Do` consults `GetBody` only for redirects and its own internal rewind — never for a caller's retry loop. Attempt 1 sent the file, the transport closed it, and **attempt 2 put a 0-byte body on a live presigned S3 URL**; only the `Content-MD5` header prevented a truncated object being stored. The body is now rebuilt from `GetBody` before each attempt, and a request carrying a body without `GetBody` is attempted once rather than retried with a broken one.
- **Retaining tarballs exposed a wedge in `set.operateAndRemove`.** It discarded its progress list on the first error while those files had already been removed, stranding phantom entries that failed every subsequent cycle. It now retains partial progress and joins the errors.
- **Retrying every retained tarball each cycle made the pass O(queue depth).** A small backlog outran the tick, and dropped ticks stalled the rest of the loop. A pass now starts no new entry once its budget is spent, and abandons the batch when the destination as a whole is unavailable.
- **`MetricsCollectorServiceImpl.testUpload` was a line-for-line twin** carrying both original defects, on a live production path. Both call sites now share one `uploadProbe` loop so they cannot diverge again.

## Tests

Tests no longer reach `frontdoor.apptio.com` — a suite-level fake serves the login, presign and probe endpoints. That took the package from **~100s to ~4s** while keeping every spec.

Every new spec was mutation-checked: the bug it covers was reintroduced, the spec confirmed to fail, and the bug reverted. 66/66 specs green; `-race` reports zero data races.

Three specs fail under `-race` (`should only login once`, `should log back in if required`, `should emit each time emission interval is satisifed`). These are pre-existing and timing-sensitive — verified failing identically on a clean `develop` worktree. CI runs `go test ./...` without `-race`.

## Follow-ups, deliberately not in scope

- `UPLOAD_RETRY_COUNT` is still discarded by `NewApptioClient` (`maxRetries: 3` is hardcoded). Plumbing it needs a backoff cap first: `1<<i` is uncapped, so the documented default of 5 would mean ~330s per request and ~990s per upload.
- `doWithRetry`'s terminal error does not wrap the transport error, so callers cannot classify a connection failure via `errors.As`.
- Upload failure still does not reach `Healthy()` — the third suggestion in #238, which lives in the emitter rather than `cldy/`.
- The drain budget is checked between entries, not during one, so a single slow entry can still overrun the tick. Bounding that properly needs a `context` deadline plumbed through the client.

## Review

Three adversarial review rounds, each of which found real defects in the previous round's fixes. The final round found no correctness regression versus `develop` and cleared it to ship.

- Make sure that test_replication_xdcr fronts two separate clusters with one load balancer correctly. cbl-js uses js websocket library which can't send headers, so disable this test.

Ran the test_high_availability.py with the standard topology and the test_replication_xdcr.py with non jenkins topology.

author: yogthos
body:
Five things, in the order they were found.

**The TUI could not start a run.** With nothing selected Enter went to
`:submit`, which answered "no run selected" and dropped what had been typed, so
a harness with an empty database had no path to its first run from the UI.
Enter now means `:start` while nothing is selected and `:submit` once
something is; `state/enter-action` holds the rule so it is testable rather than
a branch in a click handler. A `start` button does it either way. Only
`:problem` goes up — the rest of what `POST /v1/runs` takes is left to the
server's config — and it runs off the UI thread, since that endpoint waits for
the beam to open every branch.

Abort and resume did receive their clicks; they did nothing and said nothing
with no run selected, which from the outside is a button wired to nothing.
Both say so now. Two toolkit tests press them for real, one on the widget and
one inside the whole shipped layout, since the container FTXUI hit-tests is
built out of the layout rather than the widget.

The STEER panel spent two rows captioning a single input line whose own
placeholder says what it takes. The row is bare; `{:title "STEER"}` brings the
caption back.

**A config file that named a provider did not get that provider.** The
provider came from `detect-provider` alone and the file layers were merged on
top of the preset that choice had already expanded, so
`{:llm {:provider :glm}}` set the `:provider` key and nothing else: DeepSeek's
endpoint, DeepSeek's key and deepseek-v4-flash, dispatching the GLM adapter,
silently. Files are now read before the preset is expanded. A provider spelled
as a string is the provider it names; one no table knows is an error rather
than a fall back to whatever the environment had.

`glm-uses-the-coding-endpoint` had bound the loaded values, ignored them and
asserted the static table instead, with a comment about key-env detection. It
asserts the loaded config now.

**proc/run leaked two descriptors per subprocess.** `:out :string` reads the
child's output into a string and left the pipe fds open — 30 spawns cost 60,
60 cost 120, never released. This is the leak behind provenance A-3, where the
suite "holds ~260 fds at peak" and the test task raises `ulimit -n` to 1024.
Three new git-spawning tests crossed even the raised limit and it surfaced
nowhere near the cause: eleven errors in store-test's ledger tests reading
"sqlite step failed: unable to open database file", all of which passed in
isolation. Not test-only — the `shell` tool runs through here, so a run that
shells out a few hundred times exhausts its own descriptors and then cannot
open its database.

**The footer and a GIT box, ported from dirge.** The status line said the run
id and the base URL, nothing about which project, branch or model — the things
that say whether the harness is pointed where you think it is. It now reads
`project:branch │ model │ used/window (pct%) │ turns │ status │ run`. The
denominator is the context window rather than the fold-trigger budget, so the
percentage reads 0-100 and an imminent fold is a `fold`/`fold!` marker;
`project:branch` collapses to the project alone on a detached HEAD. The
connection dot stays leftmost and is ours: dirge's UI is the process doing the
work, this one is a client that can be pointed anywhere.

`:widget/git` is dirge's left-panel GIT box — branch, `+staged ~unstaged
?untracked`, last commit subject. Both read a new `GET /v1/harness/project`,
served because only the harness process is bound to the project: a TUI
shelling out to git itself would caption whichever directory it was started
from whenever it is pointed elsewhere. The server caches the git side for
`:git-snapshot-ttl-ms`, since the poller asks every 1.5s and dirge froze its
own UI reading `.git/HEAD` per frame before it cached.

GIT sits in the wide CLAIMS/GATES row rather than a gutter. A fourth box in
the right column put 20 pinned rows against a `:grow` MODIFIED that may not be
squeezed, so on a 28-row terminal it drew as a titled box with nothing in it —
the squeeze tui.edn's own warning is about, one panel further along. The
toolkit test asserts the box's content now, not its title, which is what let
the bad placement pass.

**Both workflows pin jolt.** linux-sandbox.yml took the latest release; it
builds no binary so it never hit the 0.8.5 boot-image abort, but it runs on
every push and had no reason to track whatever shipped this morning.

`docs/tui.md` covers the footer, the endpoint and the two layout traps.

2222 tests / 9760 assertions green, plus 8 toolkit tests / 35 assertions
(`jolt tui-test`). The baseline at the previous commit was confirmed green
before trusting that the eleven store-test errors were mine.

Not in here, and worth knowing: a `jolt serve` process left running since
Sep 6 answers /health normally and 503s every `POST /v1/runs` at 30s, creating
no run row, because it predates both the ebb adoption and the deadline raise
in karamazov-iev2. That is karamazov-uk77, and restarting the harness is the
fix.

author: flemingss
body:
**Stacks on #58 and #59.** Merge those first.

Tomorrow is the first full session on the consolidated feeds, and it can be watched open to close. `live/shakedown.py` is that day in five phases pinned to the session clock.

| Phase | Window | What it settles |
| --- | --- | --- |
| pre-open | 07:30-09:29 ET | Whether the feed quotes before the open, realtime and delayed, plus entitlements at the new day boundary |
| open | 09:30-10:30 ET | Fifty minutes of realtime spread inside the window ADR-0019 charges from history |
| order-window | 10:30-11:30 ET | Controlled order, the type matrix during regular hours, and a round trip that measures commission |
| midday | 11:30-15:15 ET | Failure injection, strand recovery, subscription interference |
| close | 15:15-16:30 ET | The closing spread contrast, then the sweep |

**Each phase refuses to run outside its window.** That is the `warmup` lesson: a check that is wrong at the hour it is used trains you to ignore it. `--force` overrides and the record says it was forced.

**It is a command rather than a checklist** for the reason the corporate-actions scan taught. A tool that exists is not a tool that runs, and the fix is that a command owns the sequence. `--plan` prints the whole day first and marks every step that places an order.

**Reference prices come from the catalog's last close**, which is what the probes document that flag to mean. Deterministic, needs no node to prepare, and the limits sit at half the reference so they rest rather than fill.

**Twenty-five tests.** The one that earns its keep scans every step's flags against the flags its target probe actually registers, following the shared argument helpers. It exists because the first draft handed `--account` to `subscription_interference`, which opens a data client only. That mismatch would not have failed until mid-session, once, with the window gone.

**Commission research, filed not applied.** IBKR Lite is disqualified and not on cost: it has no API access, which this system is end to end. So the choice is Fixed against Tiered inside Pro, and the account is measurably on Fixed, since the stage-five trips paid USD 2.01 and 2.02 on one and three shares.

| At USD 20 risk per trade | Round trip |
| --- | --- |
| Pro Fixed, measured | 0.100 R |
| Pro Tiered, estimated | ~0.04 R |
| AAPL holdout net expectancy | 0.035 R |

The shakedown's `round-trip` step measures it rather than assuming it. Changing `COMMISSION_MIN` moves every verdict's cost basis, so it is a roadmap row wanting its own ADR, the way ADR-0011 and ADR-0019 did for spread. Nineteen items, fourteen ready to build.

author: decapent
body:
Le frontend n'arrivait pas à joindre l'API : deux groupes ACI distincts obligeaient le web à repasser par l'IP publique de l'API, ce qu'ACI ne garantit pas. Le relais `/api` expirait en **504** alors que l'API répondait normalement depuis l'extérieur.

Container Apps règle le problème à la racine, et coûte moins cher.

## Ce que ça change

| | ACI (avant) | Container Apps (après) |
|---|---|---|
| Réseau interne | IP publique, hairpinning → 504 | Nom court `http://archipelago-api`, jamais sur Internet |
| API exposée ? | Oui, port 8080 public | Non, entrée interne uniquement |
| HTTPS | Non, HTTP en clair | Fourni par Azure sur le FQDN |
| Coût au repos | Facturé 24/7 | `min-replicas 0`, dans le quota gratuit Consumption |
| Déploiement | Supprimer-recréer, avec coupure | Mise à jour en place |

## Fichiers

- **`deploy/creer-container-apps.sh`** — création initiale de l'environnement et des deux applications. Les workflows utilisent `az containerapp update`, qui exige que l'application existe.
- Les deux `deploy-job` passent de `az container` à `az containerapp`.
- Les secrets sont reposés à chaque déploiement, pour qu'une rotation se propage sans intervention.

`API_URL` cesse d'être une variable GitHub : il vaut toujours le nom interne de l'API. C'est aussi ce qui évite le piège du port manquant rencontré sur ACI.

## À faire avant de fusionner

```sh
REGISTRE=noresetspeedrun.azurecr.io \
REGISTRE_UTILISATEUR=... REGISTRE_MOTDEPASSE=... \
./deploy/creer-container-apps.sh
```

Container Apps n'est pas disponible dans toutes les régions. Si `canadaeast` est refusé, relancer avec `REGION=canadacentral`.

Une fois les applications créées, les anciens groupes ACI peuvent être supprimés :

```sh
az container delete -g archipelago -n archipelago-api --yes
az container delete -g archipelago -n archipelago-web --yes
```

Les variables `API_DNS_LABEL`, `WEB_DNS_LABEL` et `API_URL` deviennent inutiles côté GitHub.

## Note

Je n'ai pas pu valider ces commandes contre Azure — ma session `az` est expirée depuis le début de la session. Le YAML des workflows est validé syntaxiquement, mais le premier déploiement reste la vraie vérification.

## Summary

The migration upgrade fixture could not detect two corruptions: a migration that deactivates every seeded repository (the `active` column was never read back), and a widened `UNSETTLED` limb of `settlements_materialized_status_check` that accepts `settled_points = 0` (no case probed that boundary). This pins both, so the fixture fails when the shipped migration SQL stops being correct.

## Related Issues and Pull Requests

Fixes #126

## Changes

- `tests/db/migration-upgrade.test.ts`: the seeded repository shape, the seed insert, and the post-upgrade readback now carry `registered_repositories.active` (explicitly `true`), so an upgrade that flips it fails the row-preservation comparison the way `owner_name` already does.
- `tests/db/migration-upgrade.test.ts`: new refusal case `unsettled work carrying a zero settled amount` (`UNSETTLED`, `settled_points = 0`, `credits = 0`) beside the existing UNSETTLED cases, so a widened UNSETTLED limb that stores such a row is caught behaviourally.

Mutation proof, both defects planted into the real migration path and watched:

- Baseline (issue repro): with `update registered_repositories set active = false;` appended to `db/migrations/013_immutable_github_identity.sql`, the unmodified fixture passed 58/58 — the gap. After the change, the same mutant failed the 11 boundary cases that seed a repository, on the `active: true` → `false` readback.

The frozen-check rendering comparisons also fail under this mutant on main today; the new case adds the behavioural pin the issue asks for.

author: arena-ai-coding-agent[bot]
body:
## What this does

Cleans the repository out and replaces the `RMS/` + `restaurant_site/` skeleton with **Lumière**, a 3D restaurant management system on Django 5.2 + SQLite + vendored three.js — no bundler, no Node, no CDN at runtime.

**Deleted (nothing from the old code survived):** `RMS/` app (models/views/urls/admin, 7 templates, `background.jpg`), `restaurant_site/` project package, the committed `db.sqlite3`, every `__pycache__`/`.pyc`, `.idea/` — all 38 tracked files replaced or removed. Ignore rules fixed so runtime uploads and WAL sidecars can never be committed again.

## The headline feature: add food with 3 fields

`/studio/` asks for **name, price, stock** — that's it.

- a dish that already exists → **no duplicate row**: it becomes *restock to par (+N)* at the last-known price, recorded as a ledger movement
- **an image never has to be added twice**: twins inherit the photo (`post_save` propagation + backfill), and a byte-identical upload is SHA-1 matched in the browser and **re-linked instead of uploaded** (`menu_photo.checksum` is UNIQUE; the server de-dupes again)
- blank price / chapter / stock → inferred from that dish's history, the chapter median, the house default, and name tokens
- `GET /api/menu/suggest/` returns the whole plan (with the reason for every number) *before* you commit

## Schema

11 domain tables across 4 apps: venue singleton + append-only activity journal · staff profiles with role-derived permissions · menu chapters, **shared photo library**, dishes, price ledger, stock ledger · floor tables with real x/y/rotation · tickets, lines, payments, guest notes.

Real constraints, not conventions: `UNIQUE (category_id, match_key)` `uniq_dish_per_chapter`, `CHECK (price >= 0)`, `CHECK (seats >= 1)`, `PROTECT` on `Item.category`, `SET_NULL` on `Item.photo`, named indexes for every dashboard query, SQLite `WAL` + `foreign_keys=ON`. Money is snapshotted per order line, stock/price changes are ledger rows with `balance_after` — history can't be rewritten by editing a dish. `/vault/` is a live ERD + column explorer generated by introspection; `docs/SCHEMA.md` is the prose copy.

## Interface

WebGL landing scene (lathed ceramic plates, procedural PMREM environment, gold dust, raycast labels pinned to real 3D positions, damped orbit, off-screen pause, adaptive pixel ratio, CSS fallback), a 3D extruded floor plan on the dashboard, ink + champagne-gold design system, guest ordering, four-lane service board, kitchen display, re-skinned Django admin. `prefers-reduced-motion` respected everywhere.

## Verification

- `manage.py test` → **45 tests OK** (models, venue caching, template filters, smart-add contract, ledgers, guest visibility, order lifecycle, login rails, schema API, admin skin)
- `scripts/smoke.py` → **All smoke checks passed** (40 end-to-end assertions against the seeded dev database)
- every page, static asset, media file and JSON endpoint returns 200 on the preview host; all 10 JS modules parse; every cross-module symbol resolves

## Run it

```bash
python3 -m venv .venv && .venv/bin/pip install -r requirements.txt
.venv/bin/python manage.py migrate && .venv/bin/python manage.py seed_demo
.venv/bin/python manage.py runserver 0.0.0.0:8000
```

Sign in: `bithi / Bithi@2026` (owner). Seed: 22 dishes, 8 chapters, 10 photos, 14 tables, ~295 tickets, both ledgers populated.

## Two dishes are photo-less on purpose

*Truffle Parmesan Fries* and *Lamb Rogan Josh* keep the plate-medallion placeholder — the image budget for the session ran out, and they double as the "needs a photo" state the studio filter and the dashboard counter are built around.

author: scottxxxxx
body:
Prerequisite for switching GhostPour's ContextQuilt calls from the public hostname to the internal container network (Scott's decision relayed by CQ, awaiting his word to me directly). Safe and useful on either path.

**Why.** Bifrost read three weeks of edge logs: on the public hostname nginx re-proxies a failed upstream connect for up to ~49 seconds, which absorbed every CQ container swap (113 hairpin 502s, none reached a phone). GhostPour has no retry of its own: three httpx clients, all bare `AsyncClient(base_url, timeout)`. On the internal network the edge leaves the hop, so a CQ deploy would surface instantly as connection refused. Docker's embedded DNS can also NXDOMAIN briefly while the new container attaches.

**What.** One shared `connect_retry_transport()` (3 retries) on the shared client in `context_quilt.py` and both ad hoc clients in `cq_proxy.py`. httpx retries connection establishment only, never a request that was sent, so POST is safe. Verified in the installed httpcore source that OSError (which includes gaierror) maps to ConnectError and the retry loop catches ConnectError and ConnectTimeout, so NXDOMAIN is covered.

**Proved the tests can fail** (each in isolation, cache cleared, reverted between):

| Sabotage | Red |
|---|---|
| retries set to 0 | the behavioural attempt-count test only |
| shared client drops the transport | the shared-client test only |
| one proxy site drops the kwarg | the two-sites test only |

The behavioural test swaps httpcore's network backend for one that refuses every connect and counts attempts (1 + 3). The third test is a source-reading assertion, labelled as such in its docstring; the sites are inside request handlers and the property is literally that each passes the kwarg.

Existing ContextQuilt tests: 187 passed, 1 skipped.

author: ro31337
body:
## JIRA Issue(s)

https://coreweave.atlassian.net/browse/WB-39821

## Description

A project that already holds `calls_complete` rows rejects the legacy `/call/upsert_batch` route with a 400.

The hand-written client knows that error. It switches to the pairing processor and resends.

The generated client had no `calls_complete` support at all. Nothing caught the error, so the whole batch was dropped. On a local stack the ClickHouse row count did not move.

This is a port, not a new design. The TypeScript SDK already does the same thing in production (`sdks/node/src/weaveClient.ts`).

Four pieces. Start the pairing processor when the setting is on. Send paired calls through `v2_calls.complete`. Send unpaired ones through the v2 single-call routes, which are hidden from the spec, so we use raw `post`. Map the server's error code onto `CallsCompleteModeRequired`.

One more fix comes with it. The client no longer snapshots the call processor in its constructor. That snapshot left `flush()` restarting the retired processor after an upgrade. It fixes the hand-written client too.

Two notes before approving.

`WEAVE_USE_CALLS_COMPLETE` already defaults to true. So turning `WEAVE_USE_STAINLESS_SERVER` on also moves you to `calls_complete`. Non-eager call starts then stop appearing until the call finishes.

This is a faithful copy, so it keeps the hand-written client's existing weakness. A process that exits right after an upgrade without flushing can still lose in-flight calls.

Stacked on #7851.

## Testing

Eight new tests in `test_http_behavior_stainless.py` drive the vendored client over an `httpx.MockTransport`. Two more pin the batch re-parse and that `flush()` drains the live processor. Each fails on master.

Existing tests: one test and one fixture now pin `WEAVE_USE_CALLS_COMPLETE=false`. Four access-log tests lose two `get_call_processor` entries.

Locally: 1941 passed in `tests/trace/` and `tests/utils/`, 184 in `tests/trace_server_bindings/`, 178 with `--remote-http-trace-server=stainless`.

body:
## The witness

A triangle whose apex sits **exactly on a circle**, so four piece-ends meet at
that apex and the answer is two lobes pinched there:

```sql
SELECT ST_Difference(
  geometry 'CURVEPOLYGON(CIRCULARSTRING(0 2,2 4,4 2,2 0,0 2))',
  geometry 'TRIANGLE((0 0,4 0,2 4,0 0))');
```

Before this commit the overlay welds the two lobes into **one ring that visits
the apex twice**, the ring bounds no surface, and the answer comes from the
fall-through as a chain of chords. It now answers the two lobes with their arcs
kept: `5.657189742` kept and `6.909180872` shared, partitioning the disc to
`4*pi` exactly.

## Why the walk could not decide

A boundary piece arrives in the direction its **own** geometry happens to be
written in, and the two operands are written independently. A walk that crosses
from one boundary to the other therefore reverses the side the answer sits on
halfway round, and the ordering rule — turn as sharply as the node allows — is
applied in two different frames within one ring. Where exactly two piece-ends
meet that costs nothing, because there is no choice to make. At a node four of
them share, it decides the answer.

**This is a frame problem, not an ordering one**, and the measurement that says
so is that the *same* triangle against a **square** already answers correctly,
because both operands then arrive as segments in one frame:

| | |
|---|---|
| square minus triangle | `MULTIPOLYGON(((4 0,4 4,2 4,4 0)),((2 4,0 4,0 0,2 4)))` — correct |
| disc minus triangle | one self-crossing ring, no surface, GEOS strokes it |

Two orderings were tried against those two rows and **each satisfies exactly one
of them**: taking the last piece round answers the disc and regresses the
square; the standard planar face traversal answers the disc and breaks the
square's own assertion. No ordering can be right in both frames at once.

## What it does

The selection already knows the side: near a kept piece the answer coincides
with that piece's own geometry on one side, and `buffer_piece_interior_side()`
reads which. The exception is a piece of the **subtracted** geometry in a
difference, where what the subtrahend encloses is exactly what the answer does
not. So each selected piece records whether the answer lies to its left **as it
is stored**, each ring reads its frame off the first piece it takes, and a
candidate that would cross to the other side loses to one that does not. The
ordering then chooses among the candidates that hold the frame, unchanged.

**The pieces are not reversed, and that is deliberate.** Reversing them answers
the same question and rotates the start vertex of every ring assembled from
them — a spelling change across the whole areal surface for a defect that lives
at pinch nodes alone. Reading the frame off the ring instead leaves every start
vertex where it is: the union of two overlapping squares still spells
`POLYGON((1 2,0 2,0 0,2 0,2 1,3 1,3 3,1 3,1 2))`, byte for byte.

The sibling this mirrors is `lwgeom_force_clockwise`, the normalisation that
makes a direction comparison mean a *side* comparison elsewhere in the engine.
It cannot be used here: it handles `POLYGON`, `TRIANGLE`, `MULTIPOLYGON` and
`COLLECTION` and returns without touching a `CURVEPOLYGON` or a `MULTISURFACE`,
which are exactly the operands this reaches.

## Measured, and what did not move

| | |
|---|---|
| the four pairs a 225-pair type sweep finds | **4 of 4** now answer natively with their arcs kept |
| against an arc-exact area and exact circle-segment Booleans | **0 mismatches**, the new pair reading `6.909180872` / `5.657189742` |
| what a pair shares where it shares no area | `POINT(2 1)`, `POINT(1 1)`, `LINESTRING(1 0,1 1)`, `POLYGON EMPTY` — unchanged |
| ring spelling | unchanged, checked on the union whose expectation pins it |
| two builds over 42 instruments | 3 lines move: the 2 this commit's own test prints, plus a timestamp |
| `pg_regress` on PostgreSQL 18 | all tests passed |
| `libmeos` under MSYS2 UCRT64 | clean |
| cppcheck | 152 findings on both arms, **0 new** |

**The projected regime, which this was not aimed at and closes anyway:**

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `6.4e6`, 10 mm feature | `-2.18e-06` | **`-4.27e-14`** |
| `180 89`, 0.1 mm feature | `-1.23e-10` | **`-3.37e-20`** |

7 of 7 configurations now partition, where 5 of 7 did. Those two residuals had
no named cause; it is the same frame ambiguity, showing up as a tiny area error
rather than as a broken ring.

## On the test

It asserts the arcs survive — which the fall-through cannot do — and bounds the
partition sum on top of that. It is a **bound rather than an identity** because
`geom_area()` strokes each *part* separately, and the chords it lays across two
half-arcs are not those it lays across the whole circle, so the two sides differ
by `2.3e-05` where the *subject* itself carries arcs. Under an area that
integrates the arcs they sum to `4*pi` exactly. The assertion aborts at the
parent commit on the arcs.

## Summary
- rebuild Behavioral Intelligence as a standard FSFFL product surface using the shared panel/metric/dashboard components instead of a visually separate mini-app
- show all currently available observed owner history in a compact, readable dossier
- collapse unavailable advanced Behavioral outputs into one clear evidence-gated section rather than presenting a field of blank/waiting cards
- install a route guard that restores the shared generic surface scaffold before navigating away from Behavioral Intelligence
- preserve the governing rule that raw completed-action counts are descriptive evidence, not acceptance probability or universal Value
- add regression coverage for navigation recovery, shared styling, and evidence-gated inference

## Root cause
Behavioral Intelligence replaced the shared `#generic-screen` markup. Other product routes expect the generic scaffold to exist before their renderers run, so leaving Behavioral could leave the navigation flow in a broken state. Its bespoke CSS also made the surface look disconnected from the rest of FSFFL NEXT.

## Authority
Presentation-only repair. No Behavioral inference, Value, Decision, Search, Forecast, or Simulation authority changes.

author: omeganetwork-source
body: ## Problem On mobile MetaMask's in-app browser at https://chaos.omeganetwork.co, users experience the following: 1. Tap Connect 2. MetaMask connect prompt appears 3. User approves 4. UI briefly looks connected, then shows **"Connection cancelled"** 5. Wallet is not actually connected Desktop MetaMask and WalletConnect work correctly. ## Root Cause The `handleConnect` function in `Header.tsx` had a race condition: 1. **`connect()` was not awaited** - The wagmi `connect` function was called but the code continued immediately without waiting for the connection to complete 2. **Modal closed immediately** - `setShowConnectorModal(false)` fired before connection was confirmed 3. **Fragile timeout** - `setTimeout(() => ensureArcChain(), 400)` triggered `wallet_addEthereumChain` and `switchChain` calls while MetaMask mobile was still processing the connection request 4. **RPC calls during pending connection** - Issuing `wallet_addEthereumChain` while the connection is settling causes MetaMask mobile's in-app browser to cancel/reset the session, surfacing a "user rejected" error even though the user approved ## Fix - Use wagmi `connect()` `onSuccess` callback to sequence chain operations - Only call `ensureArcChain()` after connection is confirmed successful - Make `ensureArcChain()` async and await `wallet_addEthereumChain` before calling `switchChain` - Add small stabilization delay (200ms) for MetaMask mobile compatibility ## Testing - Build passes (`npm run build` - TypeScript compiles successfully) - Preserves behavior for desktop MetaMask and WalletConnect - Fixes the mobile in-app browser race condition by ensuring chain operations only occur after connection is confirmed ## Changes ```diff - const handleConnect = async (selectedConnector) => { - connect({ connector: selectedConnector }) - setShowConnectorModal(false) - setTimeout(() => ensureArcChain(), 400) // Race condition! - } + const handleConnect = (selectedConnector) => { + setShowConnectorModal(false) + connect( + { connector: selectedConnector }, + { + onSuccess: async () => { + await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, 200)) // Stabilization delay + await ensureArcChain() // Now safe to add chain + }, + onError: (error) => { + console.error('Connect error:', error) + }, + } + ) + } ```

This PR adds a complete example demonstrating how to use **Supabase + pgvector** as a persistent memory backend for AI agents. It includes a fully documented README and a well‑commented Python example.

This pattern helps developers build agents with **long‑term, cloud‑hosted memory**, which is one of the most requested features in agentic AI workflows.

README.md
example.py

author: amanthosadmin
body:
## Was ist neu

`www.amanthos.com` war in der GEO-Prüfung vom 10.09.2026 (Abschnitt 3.5) die schwächste der fünf
Domains, obwohl sie inhaltlich die reichste ist: null strukturierte Daten, kein Canonical auf
keiner Seite, keine Open-Graph-Tags, eine unvollständige Sitemap und Preise, die der eigenen
Betreiberseite widersprechen. Dieser PR schliesst diese fünf Lücken.

### 1. Organization-Block als JSON-LD (die grösste Einzellücke)

Die Domain trug bisher keinen einzigen JSON-LD-Block. Neu steht im `<head>` der Startseite ein
`Organization`-Block mit Name, Logo, `foundingDate` 2019, `foundingLocation` Stuttgart,
`PostalAddress` aus dem Impressum, Telefon, E-Mail, `areaServed` CH und DE, `sameAs` und
`subOrganization` für die vier Marken:

| Marke | URL im Block | Belegte Angaben |
|---|---|---|
| Prize by Radisson | `radissonhotels.com/de-de/hotels/prize-by-radisson-affoltern-am-albis` | 102 Zimmer, Affoltern am Albis (ZH) |
| Hotel Chalet Swiss | `https://chalet-swiss.ch/` | 52 Zimmer, Interlaken (BE) |
| Hotel Mulin by Amanthos | `https://hotelmulin.ch/` | 15 Zimmer, Breil/Brigels (GR) |
| Amanthos Living | `https://www.amanthosliving.com/` | drei Standorte |

Alle sieben im Block verwendeten externen URLs liefern HTTP 200 (heute geprüft). Der offizielle
Name des Radisson-Hauses lautet laut Titel der Betreiberseite „Prize by Radisson, Zurich
Affoltern am Albis"; er steht als `alternateName` drin, `name` bleibt „Prize by Radisson" wie
auf unserer Seite.

Jede Zahl im Block steht so auch im sichtbaren Text der Seite (Zimmerzahlen, Gründungsjahr) oder
im Impressum (Adresse). **Kein `aggregateRating`**: die Bewertungen auf der Seite (4.0, 8.0+,
9.3) stammen von OTA-Portalen, nicht von uns.

**`sameAs` enthält nur, was auf der Seite wirklich verlinkt ist:** YouTube `@Amanthos`, der
Podcast auf Spotify und auf Apple Podcasts. Eine Unternehmensseite bei LinkedIn oder Instagram
ist auf amanthos.com nirgends verlinkt (die fünf LinkedIn-Links im Team-Bereich sind persönliche
Profile, die gehören nicht in das `sameAs` der Firma). Siehe „Was mir gefehlt hat".

### 2. Living-Preise auf die Betreiberseite gezogen

Selbst geprüft auf `https://www.amanthosliving.com/` am 10.09.2026, die Zahlen stehen im
ausgelieferten HTML im Abschnitt „Our Locations":

| Standort | amanthos.com vorher | amanthosliving.com (heute gemessen) | amanthos.com nachher |
|---|---|---|---|
| Zürich Airport | ab CHF 129/Nacht | `Zurich Airport from CHF 109/night` | ab CHF 109/Nacht |
| Solothurn / Grenchen | ab CHF 105/Nacht | `Solothurn from CHF 49/night` | ab CHF 49/Nacht |
| Nyon / Duillier | ab CHF 99/Nacht | `Nyon from CHF 99/night` | ab CHF 99/Nacht (unverändert) |

Geändert an sechs Stellen: in der Säulen-Liste je DE und EN, und auf den drei Apartment-Karten.
Sonst wurde kein einziger Preis angefasst.

### 3. Canonical, Open Graph, Meta-Descriptions

`images/og-image.jpg` (1200x630) lag bereits im Repo, war aber nirgends eingebunden. Ein
geteilter Link zeigte deshalb weder Bild noch Titel.

### 4. Sitemap

`/imprint/en/` ergänzt, `lastmod` auf 2026-09-10.

**Hier weiche ich vom Auftrag ab, bewusst und sichtbar:** `/agb/` und `/agb/en/` sollten laut
Auftrag ebenfalls in die Sitemap. Beide Seiten tragen aber seit Commit `04595d0` (21.05.2026)
`<meta name="robots" content="noindex, follow">`. Eine `noindex`-URL in der Sitemap ist ein
Widerspruch, den die Search Console als Fehler meldet („Gesendete URL als ‚noindex' markiert").
Ich habe die beiden Seiten deshalb draussen gelassen und den Grund als Kommentar in
`sitemap.xml` geschrieben. Zwei Wege, der Entscheid liegt bei dir:

- **Variante A:** `noindex` bleibt, die AGB-Seiten bleiben aus der Sitemap. Nichts zu tun.
- **Variante B:** `noindex` fällt (AGB-Seiten sind rechtlich unbedenklich indexierbar, die
  Schwesterseiten indexieren ihre AGB auch), dann kommen beide URLs in die Sitemap. Zwei
  Zeilen entfernen, vier Zeilen ergänzen, sage Bescheid und ich hänge es an diesen PR.

### 5. llms.txt

Neu im Wurzelverzeichnis, rund 50 Zeilen Markdown: was die Gruppe ist, seit wann, die vier
Marken mit URL und je einem Satz, die Kennzahlen der Seite (3 Hotels, 169 Zimmer, 57+
Apartments, 40+ Deals, >50k m², Stand März 2026), Kontakt, Podcast. Nur belegte Angaben, die
Living-Preise mit Datum und dem Hinweis, dass amanthosliving.com massgeblich ist.

---

## Vorher → Nachher

| Merkmal | Vorher | Nachher |
|---|---|---|
| JSON-LD-Blöcke | 0 | 1 (`Organization` mit 4 `subOrganization`) |
| Canonical | auf keiner Seite | auf allen 6 Inhaltsseiten |
| Open Graph Startseite | keine Tags | 11 og-Tags plus 4 Twitter-Tags |
| Meta-Description `/imprint/`, `/privacy/` | fehlt | vorhanden |
| Meta-Description `/agb/`, `/agb/en/` | fehlt | vorhanden |
| hreflang | nirgends | `/imprint/` ↔ `/imprint/en/`, `/agb/` ↔ `/agb/en/` |
| Sitemap-URLs | 3 | 4 (`/imprint/en/` neu), `lastmod` 2026-03-09 → 2026-09-10 |
| llms.txt | HTTP 404 | vorhanden |
| Living Zürich Airport | ab CHF 129 | ab CHF 109 |
| Living Solothurn | ab CHF 105 | ab CHF 49 |

---

## DB-Migrationen

Keine. Statische Seite auf GitHub Pages, keine Datenbank.

---

## Geänderte Dateien

| Datei | Änderung |
|---|---|
| `index.html` | Canonical, 11 Open-Graph- und 4 Twitter-Tags, `Organization`-JSON-LD, sechs Preiskorrekturen |
| `imprint/index.html` | Meta-Description, Canonical, hreflang DE/EN/x-default |
| `imprint/en/index.html` | Meta-Description, Canonical, hreflang DE/EN/x-default |
| `privacy/index.html` | Meta-Description, Canonical |
| `agb/index.html` | Meta-Description, Canonical, hreflang DE/EN/x-default |
| `agb/en/index.html` | Meta-Description, Canonical, hreflang DE/EN/x-default |
| `sitemap.xml` | `/imprint/en/` ergänzt, `lastmod` 2026-09-10, Kommentar zur AGB-Entscheidung |
| `llms.txt` | neu |

---

## Breaking Changes

Keine. Es wurde kein einziges Element entfernt oder umbenannt, keine URL geändert, kein
Skript angefasst. Alle Ergänzungen liegen im `<head>` oder sind neue Dateien. Die einzige
Änderung am sichtbaren Text sind die drei Preisangaben von Amanthos Living, und die machen die
Seite mit der Betreiberseite konsistent statt inkonsistent.

---

## Testplan

Dieses Repo hat **keine Tests**. Der Workflow `quality.yml` prüft die deployte Seite (tote
Links, Web Vitals, axe, Search-Console-Datei) und läuft bei Push auf `main`, wöchentlich und von
Hand, nicht auf Pull Requests. Es gibt also keine Testzahl und keinen CI-Exit-Code zu zitieren.
Stattdessen lokal geprüft, alles heute in dieser Session gelaufen:

- [x] JSON-LD parst: `json.loads` über den extrahierten Block, 1 Block, `@type` `Organization`,
      4 `subOrganization`, 3 `sameAs`
- [x] `sitemap.xml` wohlgeformt: `xmllint --noout sitemap.xml`, Exit-Code 0
- [x] Alle 6 Inhaltsseiten tragen genau ein Canonical, genau eine Description, genau ein
      `</head>`, und der HTML-Parser meldet null Fehler
- [x] Alle 7 externen URLs aus dem JSON-LD liefern HTTP 200 (chalet-swiss.ch, hotelmulin.ch,
      www.amanthosliving.com, radissonhotels.com-Deeplink, YouTube, Spotify, Apple Podcasts)
- [x] Living-Preise gegen `https://www.amanthosliving.com/` gegengelesen, Zitate oben in der
      Tabelle
- [x] `gitleaks` beim Commit: „no leaks found"
- [ ] Nach dem Merge: `https://www.amanthos.com/llms.txt` liefert 200 (heute noch 404, korrekt)
- [ ] Nach dem Merge: Rich-Results-Test von Google über `https://www.amanthos.com/` zeigt die
      `Organization` ohne Warnung
- [ ] Nach dem Merge: Link-Vorschau prüfen (LinkedIn Post Inspector oder eine Testnachricht),
      Bild und Titel müssen erscheinen
- [ ] Nach dem Merge: Sitemap in der Search Console neu einreichen

---

author: regyssilveira
body:
Active source includes previously contributed no declarations, references or imports to analysis, and missing includes could pass unnoticed. The parser now resolves includes relative to the containing source, supports explicit search paths, records parent/path/SHA-256 provenance, and fails explicitly for missing files and cycles. Imports originating in includes preserve the consumer with a reason until source-aware editing is available.

The shared root/include reader also fixes multiline normalization deleting the following semicolon; regression tests cover both locations.

This PR is cumulative on #52 and #53; merge those first. The focused increment is commit ee2f20a. The fork branch cannot use another fork branch as the upstream PR base.

Validation: full documented quality gate passed with Delphi 12/compiler 36: 209 DUnitX tests on each of Win32 and Win64; CLI/VCL Release builds; simulated, representative console/VCL and rollback smoke tests. Coverage is 92% overall, 100% for DelphiSource and 98% for SourceIncludes; every required unit meets its floor. Probe runner checks and documentation checks pass.

Research results on both platforms: 101 PASS, 33 FAIL, 0 ERROR, 18 BLOCKED. Only include-declaration, include-reference and missing-include change from FAIL to PASS against #53. Recorded baselines include source hashes. No expectations were relaxed. include-uses and include-nested still FAIL because their oracle expects removal while the new source-provenance guard preserves them.

Limitations: project-derived defines/include paths and immutable snapshot validation remain follow-ups. Hashes describe read content but do not yet guard writes. Recursive includes are conservatively rejected even with guards; repeated nonrecursive guarded includes work. No interactive VCL behavior was manually exercised; automated builds and smoke tests passed.

author: sheikh-musa
body:
## What / why
Fixes the silent singleton-recycle failure that hit **cai** on 2026-09-09 (P1). cai's self-recycle fired `--reset boot_cai.sh` (a **cold-boot launcher**) instead of `reset_cai.sh`. `self_recycle` fires the reset **detached** (nohup, `env -u TMUX_PANE`, **no controlling TTY**); `boot_cai.sh` execs a fresh interactive `claude`, which with no TTY auto-selects `--print` and instant-exits (`Input must be provided ... when using --print`). cai never reset (same ~71% session); the only trace was a detached log 60s later + a 3-min false-offline. Root cause validated end-to-end: cai then recycled cleanly via `reset_cai.sh` (73.9% → 7.8%).

**The enabling bypass:** the reset→session derivation `case` — the *only* place a bad `--reset` was rejected — runs **only when `--session` is empty**. Passing `--session` skipped it, so a non-recycle script went through unvalidated and silently detached-failed.

## The guard
An unconditional allowlist check right after arg-parse: reject any `--reset` whose basename isn't one of the 5 in-place recyclers (`reset_{nazim,cai,fleet_health,orch,lane}.sh`) **loud at schedule time**, **even with `--session`**. Only an in-place `reset_*.sh` (which `send-keys /clear` into a live pane) survives the detached fire; a cold-boot launcher cannot.

## Nazim's gate conditions — each met
- **Fires even with `--session`** (the exact bypass) → `test_a_cold_boot_launcher_is_refused_even_with_session`; wet-proven.
- **Rejects `boot_*.sh` loud at schedule time, not a detached 60s-later fail** → exits 2 immediately, no `SCHEDULED`/`NOTHING scheduled` in output.
- **Keeps all 5 legit resets working** → `test_the_five_in_place_recyclers_pass_the_allowlist` (parametrized); `reset_lane.sh` stays allowed so worker lanes self-recycle.
- **Composes with GATE 3** → GATE 3 (`reset_nazim.sh`-scoped, runs later, guards the reviewer draft queue) is untouched; branched from fable HEAD `ee8d8ea` (has `39c9e66`). Different concern, both fail-loud.
- **Wet-prove of the reject path** → against the shipped script: `boot_cai.sh --session cai --dry-run` → `REFUSED ... not a recycle script`, exit 2, nothing fired; `reset_cai.sh --dry-run` → `gates passed, NOTHING scheduled`.

## Verification
- `tests/test_self_recycle.py`: 21 passed (16 existing + 5 new). 51 passed / 1 skipped across `test_self_recycle` + `test_reset_gates` + `test_reset_self_fire_guard` (no regression).

author: shturmill
body:
## Что изменено

Backend переписан с Python/FastAPI на Java/Spring Boot. React-фронтенд не менялся: файлы `src/**`, API-клиент, типы и используемые эндпоинты остались прежними.

HTTP-контракт сохранён:

* те же `/api/v1/...`, `/health`, `/uploads/...`;
* те же query/path-параметры и snake_case;
* те же JSON-поля и enum-значения;
* те же статус-коды;
* тот же формат ошибок:
  `{"error":{"message":...,"details":...}}`.

Совместимость со старым backend сохранена:

* существующие bcrypt-хеши работают;
* ранее выданные JWT принимаются;
* база после Alembic-миграций принимается Flyway через baseline без удаления данных.

Стек: Java 21, Spring Boot 4.1.1, Maven, Spring MVC, JPA/Hibernate, Spring Security, Validation, Redis, PostgreSQL, Flyway, Nimbus JWT, `RestClient`, JUnit 5, MockMvc и Testcontainers.

Код находится в `backend/` и разделён на `controller / service / repository / domain / dto / security / integration / config / exception / seed`.

### Изменение конфигурации

`JWT_SECRET` теперь должен быть не короче 32 байт из-за требований HS256/Nimbus.

Если текущий секрет уже достаточно длинный — ничего менять не нужно. Если нет, потребуется новый секрет, после чего старые JWT перестанут работать и пользователям понадобится войти заново.

## Связанный Issue

Closes #<!-- issue -->

## Тип изменения

* [ ] Feature
* [ ] Bugfix
* [x] Рефакторинг
* [x] Инфраструктура / CI
* [x] Документация

## Чек-лист

* [ ] PR небольшой
  Миграция неделима без нерабочих промежуточных состояний. Изменения разбиты на 8 логических коммитов.
* [ ] CI зелёный
  Локально проходят:

  * `./mvnw verify` — 247 тестов, 0 падений;
  * `spotless`;
  * `npm ci && npm run lint && npm run build`.
* [x] Соблюдено разделение слоёв
* [x] DTO оформлены через records, без `Map`/`JsonNode`
* [x] Доменные ошибки корректно преобразуются в 400 / 403 / 404
* [x] Добавлена Flyway-миграция
* [x] Добавлены и обновлены тесты
* [x] Нет закомментированного или временного кода

## На что обратить внимание при ревью

* `V1__baseline_schema.sql` — вручную восстановленная итоговая схема Alembic. Перед merge желательно сравнить её с `pg_dump --schema-only` существующей БД.
* `PostgresEnumJdbcType` — биндинг PostgreSQL enum `taskstatus` через `Types.OTHER`.
* `ReadBack.flushAndDetach()` — detach перед повторным чтением после записи.
* `TaskService.changeStatus` — блокировка строки задачи при начислении XP.

## Проверка

### Docker

```bash
cp .env.example .env
docker compose up --build
```

В другом терминале:

```bash
docker compose run --rm -e SPRING_PROFILES_ACTIVE=seed api
curl localhost:8000/health
```

Ожидаемый ответ:

```json
{"status":"ok"}
```

Тестовый пользователь:

```text
test@example.com
password123
```

Frontend запускается как раньше:

```bash
npm install
npm run dev
```

### Тесты

```bash
cd backend
./mvnw verify

npm ci
npm run lint
npm run build
```

Интеграционные тесты используют PostgreSQL через Testcontainers.

Для существующего PostgreSQL:

```bash
./mvnw verify \
  -Dtest.datasource.url=jdbc:postgresql://localhost:5432/app_test
```

## Проверка совместимости со старой БД

1. Взять БД после старых Alembic-миграций.
2. Запустить новый backend.
3. Flyway должен выполнить baseline версии `1`, не применяя `V1`.
4. Hibernate `validate` должен пройти.
5. Старые пользователи должны логиниться существующими паролями.

Совместимость bcrypt и JWT также проверяется автоматически в `LegacyCredentialCompatibilityTest`.

## Проверенный функционал

Проверены основные сценарии:

* авторизация и `/api/v1/auth/me`;
* создание и изменение задач;
* сохранение snake_case и формата timestamp;
* workflow `todo → in_progress → review → done`;
* запрет `done` без `review` и approve;
* однократное начисление XP;
* загрузка и выдача attachments;
* формат ошибок 400 / 401 / 403 / 404 / 503;
* запуск на БД, созданной Alembic;
* логин со старым passlib bcrypt-хешем;
* приём JWT, созданных старым backend.

## Известные ограничения

* `POST /api/v1/tasks` по-прежнему принимает `title` до 255 символов при колонке `varchar(200)`. Это существующее расхождение старого API и БД, в рамках миграции контракт не менялся.
* `{"difficulty": null}` при создании задачи теперь приводит к использованию значения по умолчанию вместо ошибки валидации. Frontend такой запрос не отправляет.
* `docker compose up` локально не запускался из-за отсутствия container runtime в окружении разработки. Docker-образ собирается в CI.

author: malpractis
body:
## What broke

Renovate **44.63.0** introduced an `apk` datasource that does a top-level
import of `tar`, a package that is declared in `package.json` but is not
present in the published runner image's runtime `node_modules`. The ESM
resolution fails at startup:

```
ERROR: unhandledRejection
       "code": "ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND",
       "message": "Cannot find package 'tar' imported from
                   /usr/local/renovate/dist/modules/datasource/apk/index.js"
```

This happens during tool init, **before any repository is cloned**, so
Renovate does no work at all.

## Why it went unnoticed for six days

The runner pin auto-merged `44.61.4 -> 44.64.0` in #1652 on 2026-09-04
14:27. The scheduled run at 14:23 (44.61.4) was healthy; the very next run
at 18:28 (44.64.0) crashed, and every run since has crashed.

Critically, **the job still exits 0 and the workflow reports success.** The
only external symptom is runtime dropping from minutes to ~40 seconds. All
~35 runs since the bump are green in the Actions tab and did nothing.

Because `RENOVATE_AUTODISCOVER_FILTER` covers all six repos, this silently
stopped dependency updates for home-ops, azerothcore-image, raidscope,
materia-core, wow-panel and wow-realmchat simultaneously.

## What changes on the cluster

Nothing reconciles from this PR — it is CI-only. The effect is that
Renovate starts opening dependency PRs again.

The backlog includes **authentik 2026.8.1 -> 2026.8.2**, which carries two
HIGH advisories published 2026-09-09:

- [GHSA-qgqp-xh8r-v73r](https://github.com/goauthentik/authentik/security/advisories/GHSA-qgqp-xh8r-v73r) — MFA bypass via recipient override in the email authenticator
- [GHSA-cxwx-9x59-28qm](https://github.com/goauthentik/authentik/security/advisories/GHSA-cxwx-9x59-28qm) — denial of service via malformed SAML messages

41 other updates are also queued.

## Validation

Dry run on 44.74.0 — [run 34417388855](https://github.com/materia-ops/home-ops/actions/runs/34417388855):

| | broken runs (44.64.0) | dry run (44.74.0) |
|---|---|---|
| duration | ~41s | 2m53s |
| `tar` errors | 3 | 0 |
| repos processed | 0 | all |
| updates detected | 0 | 42 |

44.74.0 is the exact version validated here, so it is pinned rather than
floated.

## Rollback

Revert the one-line pin. Nothing stateful; no cluster impact.

## Follow-up worth considering (not in this PR)

The runner pin auto-merges minor/patch **daily with no `minimumReleaseAge`**
(`.renovaterc.json5`, "Auto-merge the Renovate runner pin daily"). Renovate
is the one component that cannot recover from a bad self-update — it merged
itself into a broken version and then could not open the PR to fix it. A
soak window there, and/or a CI assertion that a run actually processed a
repository, would turn this class of failure from silent into loud.
