author: ro31337
body:
## JIRA Issue(s)

https://coreweave.atlassian.net/browse/WB-39823

## Description

The generated client let the vendor SDK build its own httpx client. So `WEAVE_INSECURE_DISABLE_SSL` and our request timeout never reached it.

That blocks anyone on a self-signed or internally-issued certificate. The handshake fails, and `weave.init` reports it as the server not having Weave.

We now build the httpx client ourselves. It goes through the vendor's own `DefaultHttpxClient`, so connection limits and redirect handling are preserved.

Two consequences. Our timeout is a single number, so read and write go from 60s to 30s, and connect from 5s to 30s. That matches the hand-written client. Both settings are also read when the client is built, not per request.

Vendor retries stay on deliberately. Our `with_retry` covers only the write paths, so turning them off would take every other route from three attempts to one.

Stacked on #7852.

## Testing

New test: `verify=False` under `WEAVE_INSECURE_DISABLE_SSL=true`, and the client timeout comes from `WEAVE_HTTP_TIMEOUT`.

Locally: 1941 passed in `tests/trace/` and `tests/utils/`, 184 in `tests/trace_server_bindings/`, 179 with `--remote-http-trace-server=stainless`.

author: fumingpower3925
body:
Fixes #484

## The defect

The WebSocket backpressure pause submits an `ASYNC_CANCEL` for the armed recv and marks the connection paused. The cancel has not landed yet. A handler that drains below the low watermark before it does makes `drainDetachQueue` take the resume branch, which called `prepareRecv` unconditionally — leaving **two recvs in flight on one socket**.

Both target `cs.buf`, the per-connection buffer, so the kernel's second write lands on top of the first one's unread bytes. The WebSocket parser then reads a length field at the wrong offset and reports a garbage connection index:

```
invalid conn index in payload: 2478706466968590878
1 frame parse error(s) observed — frames were corrupted
```

Multishot is immune, which is why the bug only ever showed on the default single-shot path: each completion carries its own provided-ring buffer, so two in-flight recvs cannot overwrite each other.

## How it was found

A detector in `prepareRecv` that logs whenever it is asked to arm a recv on a connection that already has one:

```
LEDGER double-arm fd=71  gen=33 bufring=false paused=true needsRecv=false inflight=2
LEDGER double-arm fd=164 gen=57 bufring=false paused=true needsRecv=false inflight=2
```

`paused=true` while the arm is in progress pins the call site to exactly one place: the resume branch assigns `cs.recvPaused = desired` *after* arming, so the log still sees the old value. The SQ-ring-full path that skips the cancel fired **0** times in the same runs, so a full submission queue is not involved.

## The change

- `prepareRecv` declines the second arm and reports **success**. "A recv is armed for this conn" is the postcondition every caller acts on, so returning false would make them set `needsRecv` and retry from the dirty list forever. The driver path at `engine/iouring/driver.go` has carried the same guard since it was written.
- The dirty-list retry gets an explicit `recvArmed` check of its own, because it calls `pickRecvTarget`, which **mutates** `cs.recvIntoBody`. Computing a target for an arm that is about to be declined would route the in-flight recv's CQE through the direct-body path.
- New `connState.recvCancelPending`. A pause withdrawn before the cancel lands used to leave `-ECANCELED` arriving with `recvPaused` already false, so `handleRecv` fell through to the generic negative-result path and closed a healthy connection. The flag marks a cancel this worker asked for so that CQE re-arms instead. Every other `cancelConnOps` caller nils `w.conns[fd]` or sets `closing` first, so no other cancellation can reach this branch.

## Measurement

io_uring single-shot variant run on its own, which reproduces far more readily than the three-variant test. 24 runs each, 4 workers, `memlock` 128 MiB, `seccomp=unconfined`.

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| runs reporting frame corruption | 2 of 24 | **0 of 24** |
| total single-shot failures | 8 of 24 | 4 of 24 |
| double-arm detector firings | 6 | 1 |

The four remaining failures all report `parseErr=0`. They carry `closeTimeout` and per-connection protocol errors, plus one frame-count mismatch — a different signature from the corruption this PR removes. Those are being characterized separately and will get their own issue; this PR does not claim to address them.

`engine/iouring/recv_arming_test.go` fails on a control build with the guard removed (`ring pending 1→2`) and passes with it.

author: yschimke
body:
Everything this repository owes the UI-builder cutover, in four commits. After this, picking up the fixed plugin is the only step left here.

## 1. Plugin 2.4.1 → 2.5.0

Picks up the discovery fix that follows a preview through the project's own composables ([yschimke/compose-ai-tools#5350](https://github.com/yschimke/compose-ai-tools/pull/5350)). `:catalog`'s record goes **104 → 108**, purely additive — `TimePicker`, `TimeInput`, `HorizontalMultiBrowseCarousel`, `MaterialExpressiveTheme`.

`TimePicker` and `TimeInput` are the pair whose absence made `m3/time-picker` one of the three components the published catalog cannot offer (#317). **Verified against the server's equivalence test: with this record it composes, so the known-absent set drops from three to two.**

The other two stay, for different reasons worth keeping apart:

- **`m3/date-picker`** — a discovery gap. `DatePickerModalSticker` reaches `DatePicker` through `Sticker → KeyboardNavigable → InlineDialogHost → DatePickerDialog`, and the walk follows the accessor call rather than the `GETSTATIC` read of the private `lambda$<key>` field that actually links one singleton lambda to the next.
- **`m3/snackbar-host`** — not a gap. There is no `SnackbarHost` preview, on purpose: `Snackbar.kt` says the host is a dispatcher and the catalog composes snackbars directly.

## 2. Three explicit builder ids

A component's builder id is derived from its own symbol, and for almost every sticker here that is already what the builder publishes — `m3/button`, `m3/horizontal-divider`, `m3/list-item`. Three disagree, and a saved design stores the string:

| Symbol | Published as | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `AlertDialog` | `m3/dialog` | what the shelf has always called it |
| `LinearProgressIndicator` | `m3/progress-indicator` | the builder offers one progress component with the shape as a property — a coarser cut than this catalog's Linear/Circular split |
| `SearchBarDefaults.InputField` | `m3/search-input-field` | `InputField` alone says nothing about the search bar it belongs to |

Editorial decisions, so stated beside the sticker rather than left to a derivation that would quietly re-key every design referencing them. `SearchBar` needs no entry — it derives `m3/search-bar`.

## 3. The vocabulary

The components a saved design names, each with the properties it takes, what every one accepts, its slots and its modifiers. This is the half of a published catalog that **cannot be derived**: the record knows a component's Compose parameter list, and a design does not want that — `onClick` is a required parameter and not a property any design sets; `style` is a property with four allowed values and not a parameter at all.

Everything else stays derived from the annotations, so this is not a second place to rename anything. **Eighty-five of the 108 components carry no entry** and are shelved straight from the record.

## 4. The shelves the builder actually sees

Three fixes, all found by composing this catalog's generated `ui-builder.json` against the frozen builder catalog in [yschimke/compose-preview-server#673](https://github.com/yschimke/compose-preview-server/pull/673), which is where they are now pinned.

**`menu.groupOrder` named nothing.** It held the seven `section` words, and a component is filed under its `@file:CatalogGroup(name = …)` **shelf** — so the list named none of the twenty-nine shelves in use. An unnamed group sorts alphabetically after every named one, which means the stated order governed nothing and the insert panel a person saw was A-to-Z. It now lists all thirty-seven declared shelves, grouped by section and alphabetical within one.

**`m3/time-picker` had no vocabulary.** It only became reachable in commit 1 and a saved design names it, so it is authored like the other twenty-two — `mode` spelling *dial* and *input* the way `m3/progress-indicator` spells linear and circular. That is what takes the composed catalog from 22 of the frozen 25 to **23**, all of them matching the frozen vocabulary field by field.

**Seven components were on the wrong shelf.** One component is one **symbol**, and a symbol several stickers draw is filed under whichever catalog id sorts first: `Text` on Badges, `Switch` on Lists, `IconButton` and `FloatingActionButton` on Bottom app bar, `HorizontalDivider` and `ListItem` on Dialogs. Each now states its shelf outright.

Four more (`m3/icon`, `m3/surface`, `m3/sticker`, `m3/material-expressive-theme`) and six components no sticker declares are deliberately left alone and filed as #323: the catalog has no section they belong to, so placing them means choosing a new shelf rather than correcting a derivation.

## Verified end to end

Through a composite build of [yschimke/compose-ai-tools#5354](https://github.com/yschimke/compose-ai-tools/pull/5354):

```
attached vocabulary        23 of 23
component.policy.orphaned   0
component.id.collision      0
shelved components        102 of 108
```

Every diagnostic that remains is `component.canvas.unclaimed` — the Wasm canvas having no adapter, nothing to do with this PR.

## What CI will show until the plugin ships, and why it is fine

On released 2.5.0 the run reports orphans and id collisions, because that derivation still names a component after a catalog id's last segment — the variant — so `Button/Filled`, `Card/Filled` and four more all claim `m3/filled` and the ids this vocabulary keys on do not exist yet.

Diagnostics are not build failures, and this changes nothing operationally: at that collision rate over 108 components the server's `PublishedUiBuilderCatalog` already refuses this catalog's published file (the threshold is 10%) and falls back to its synthesised shelf. The file is not in use today either way. The block goes in now so the cutover is one version bump.

## Test plan

- `./gradlew :catalog:composePreviewDiscover` — 108 components, four added, none lost.
- `./gradlew ktfmtCheck test` — green.
- `scripts/design-map.sh` regenerates `design-map.json` / `design-map-variants.json` **unchanged**, so the staleness gate stays green. Coverage unmoved at 1885/2005.
- Composite-build verification above, and the three ids confirmed to compile against the released plugin.
- The generated pair is committed in compose-preview-server#673 and held to the frozen catalog by `ui-builder-equivalence.sh --strict`: 0 differences, 0 unstated facts, 0 unreviewed fields.

No rendered surface changes — this only affects what the record names, what the catalog publishes about it, and which shelf the insert panel puts it on.

author: xalcahest
body:
## Summary

On CI run 33537893939 the four first-save checks in `asr.spec.js` failed together, the first of them waiting twenty seconds for a chooser that Save had no reason to open, because the document it inherited from a run several checks earlier already had a file. The timeout said nothing about that. The precondition could not be asserted either, because until the window carried the document there was nothing on screen that said whether the open one had a file.

There is now. `documentInWindowName` reads the document out of the window's name, and each of the four says what it needs before it acts: three that the document is `Untitled`, and the fourth, whose whole point is that Ctrl+S has somewhere to write, that it is the file the check before it gave it. The head of the chain also makes its own transcription instead of taking the CPU run's from eight checks back.

Also here, for N30: the discard check in `subtitle.spec.js` now takes its two readings together at the moment of the refusal, the row and what the session says it is holding. That is the probe N30 asked for and could not have; it needed nothing added to the app. N30 stays open, because the sighting is still unexplained, but a next one will say which of the two disagreed.

Verified on Linux. `asr.spec.js` run ten times in a row: 10 green, 0 failures, which is the number M3.7's criterion asked for. The assertion has teeth, proved by telling the check that needs a file to expect none: it goes red naming what the window actually held. Full battery green at 72 spec files.

## Changes

- e2e/specs/asr.spec.js: adds `documentInWindowName`, `expectOpenDocument` and `aFreshTranscription`; the four first-save checks assert their own precondition and the first of them establishes it.
- e2e/specs/subtitle.spec.js: adds `heldDocument`, and the discard check asserts the row and the held document as one reading rather than the row alone.

author: etoile04
body:
## Problem

Per ADR-013 / NFM-4502, RAG changes must canary on G2 staging first. The NFM-4492 cluster (PR #1272 → PR #1275) added three prod RAG knobs — query timeout 8s→60s, embedding model swap to `nomic-embed-text` with `EMBEDDING_DIM=768`, and the five `RERANK_*` vars — but `docker-compose.staging.yml` never received any of them. Net effect: the staging canary was a false-negative generator, timing out at 8s or 500-ing on embedding dim mismatch regardless of whether the change under test was good.

## What this PR changes

### 1. Drift closed: three knobs mirrored on staging (AC #1, #2, #3 prod parity)

```diff
# api service
+ NFM_LIGHTRAG_QUERY_TIMEOUT_S: ${STAGING_LIGHTRAG_QUERY_TIMEOUT_S:-60.0}   # was unset → 8.0s default

# lightrag service
+ EMBEDDING_MODEL: ${STAGING_LIGHTRAG_EMBEDDING_MODEL:-nomic-embed-text}      # was text-embedding-3-small (OpenAI-only on staging)
+ EMBEDDING_DIM: ${STAGING_LIGHTRAG_EMBEDDING_DIM:-768}                      # was unset → 1536 default → 500
+ EMBEDDING_SEND_DIM: ${STAGING_LIGHTRAG_EMBEDDING_SEND_DIM:-false}
+ RERANK_BINDING: ${STAGING_LIGHTRAG_RERANK_BINDING:-cohere}
+ RERANK_MODEL: ${STAGING_LIGHTRAG_RERANK_MODEL:-qwen3-reranker-0.6b}
+ RERANK_BINDING_HOST: ${STAGING_LIGHTRAG_RERANK_BINDING_HOST:-http://host.docker.internal:8109}
+ RERANK_BINDING_API_KEY: ${STAGING_LIGHTRAG_RERANK_BINDING_API_KEY:-no-key-required}
+ MIN_RERANK_SCORE: ${STAGING_LIGHTRAG_MIN_RERANK_SCORE:-0.3}
```

All vars use `${STAGING_LIGHTRAG_*:-<matches-prod>}` so SRE can override locally without editing compose. `docker/.env.staging.example` is updated with the new tunables and a reachability note (`RERANK_BINDING_HOST` → launchd `ai.nfm.rerank-server` on :8109).

### 2. New guard (AC #5)

`scripts/check_staging_rag_parity.py` — one-way (prod→staging) check over a tracked RAG-var allowlist. `STAGING_RAG_PARITY_WAIVER` env var lets a future drift skip a named var with a stated reason (covers AC #3 `"explicit recorded decision"` path). Findings go to stderr so CI logs always see them.

```bash
$ python3 scripts/check_staging_rag_parity.py
staging RAG parity check (NFM-4532):
  OK — every tracked prod RAG env var is present on staging.
rc=0
```

## Verification

- `pytest scripts/tests/test_check_staging_rag_parity.py` — **12 tests, all green** (covers the 3 knobs × {api, lightrag}, waiver semantics, prod-only carve-outs, allowlist stability).
- Pre-fix guard run: rc 1 with 8 missing RAG vars (correct detection of the drift).
- Post-fix guard run: rc 0, zero drift.
- Wider run with the rest of `scripts/tests/` (incl. `test_verify_env_sync`, `test_check_deploy_drift`): **79 passed**.

## Acceptance criteria status

| # | Criterion | Status |
|---|-----------|--------|
| 1 | api `NFM_LIGHTRAG_QUERY_TIMEOUT_S` matched to prod (60.0) | ✅ |
| 2 | lightrag `EMBEDDING_DIM` consistent with `EMBEDDING_MODEL` (768 / nomic-embed-text) | ✅ |
| 3 | Rerank vars mirrored + reachability note | ✅ (compose + env example) |
| 4 | Post-deploy proof: one hybrid query on staging returns a non-empty answer | ⏳ post-merge — needs staging redeploy |
| 5 | Guard so prod-only RAG env changes cannot land without staging counterpart | ✅ (`scripts/check_staging_rag_parity.py`) |

AC #4 needs to be re-run against staging after this lands and the staging compose is restarted. Filing as a follow-up child on issue close.

## Why this was filed rather than merged earlier

PR #1273 attempted the timeout half of Drift 1 and was closed as superseded (see #1273 comment 5610083470) — it mirrored `30.0` (below prod's current `60.0`), covered none of Drift 2/3, and its AC (5 measured hybrid queries on staging) was unexecutable while Drift 2 stood. Merging a partial mirror would have made the canary *look* aligned while still being wrong. This PR closes all three drifts atomically and adds the durable guard.

## Refs

NFM-4502, NFM-4492, NFM-4521, NFM-3404, NFM-3803, PR #1272, PR #1275, closed PR #1273, wayfinder #1258.

author: phanthienquoc
lucassardenbergl
body:
## O que

A edge `omie-desconto-backfill` nasceu hoje (#2412) e era **a única das 60 do mapa sem atestação** no ledger `deploy_atestacoes` — `bun run pendencias:deploy` saía **59/60, exit 1**, com o remédio impresso *"→ sonda (founder cola no SQL Editor)"*.

Este PR versiona os bytes que foram aplicados em produção para fechar isso. **O SQL já está aplicado** — o commit existe porque `bun run db:aplicar` exige que os bytes sejam recuperáveis na história do repo, não o contrário.

## Por que não era colagem do founder

O texto que o gerador imprime — *"É o bloco do FOUNDER: lê o vault e faz INSERT, e o wrapper read-only recusa os dois"* — fala do `psql-ro`, e estava certo quando foi escrito. Só que `bun run db:aplicar` existe desde 08/09 e passa por `public.aplicar_sql`, descrita no próprio `db/claude-rw-bootstrap.sql` como *"uma função SECURITY DEFINER que executa SQL arbitrário com os privilégios de `postgres`"*. Ela alcança o vault e faz o INSERT. A limitação era do caminho antigo, herdada por leitura.

## Por que a sonda era segura AQUI

Não pela classificação genérica de "barata". A edge **reescreve `order_items.desconto_valor`** (o `EFEITO` declarado no `versao.ts` diz isso), então um bundle PRÉ-sensor rodaria o backfill de verdade ao receber `{"probe":true}`.

O que descarta esse caso é medição, não confiança: `git log --diff-filter=A` mostra que a edge foi criada em `150856a59` **já com `criarRespostaSonda`** — nunca existiu versão dela sem o sensor. E `index.ts:97-104` trata o probe **antes** do `createClient` e de qualquer chamada ao Omie, com `classificarSonda` fail-closed (probe malformado vira 400 explícito, não cai no fluxo normal). Logo: ou o bundle no ar responde o marcador e sai, ou não existe e devolve erro HTTP. Não há terceiro caso.

## Evidência

**Ensaio** (`--ensaio`, ROLLBACK — nada gravado, nada disparado):

```
🔑 sha256 4171eaef42b9c0a68909020d12726320661e54d0feafe47e41fe5e96ff18ff0d · commit dfdf7dae0
📋 ledger: inedito
 controle
------------------
 FIM_APLICACAO_OK
ROLLBACK
🧪 ENSAIO ok — rodou inteiro e fez ROLLBACK. Nada foi gravado.
```

**Apply real** (2026-09-09 23:31:52Z):

```
🧾 tentativa #22 registrada
✅ APLICADO — tentativa #22 virou recibo, na mesma transação.
```

**PASSO 2**, lido por fora pelo `psql-ro` (2ª testemunha, outra conexão, depois do commit):

```
          edge          | request_id | status_code |    edge_respondida     |   versao_respondida    |    versao_esperada     |     veredito
------------------------+------------+-------------+------------------------+------------------------+------------------------+-------------------
 omie-desconto-backfill |      74551 |         200 | omie-desconto-backfill | v1.0-backfill-oben-ttm | v1.0-backfill-oben-ttm | DEPLOY CONFIRMADO
```

`fonte` respondida = `d09a10f83d4fff48aa81194a43c3642310d0c1a8acd42b36795e5fbdfe7602f3`, igual à do mapa da main. **A edge já estava no ar com o bundle certo** — o que faltava não era deploy, era atestação. É exatamente a distinção que o ledger existe para fazer.

**Depois**, `bun run pendencias:deploy` → **exit 0**:

```
   omie-desconto-backfill              v1.0-backfill-oben-ttm · visto há 2 min via sonda
─── cobertura: 60/60 edges mapeadas com atestação (ledger ∪ janela viva)
```

## O arquivo

`db/sonda-omie-desconto-backfill.sql` é a saída **verbatim** de `bun run sonda:sql omie-desconto-backfill --so-disparo` — qualquer um regera e compara o sha256. Sem envelope de transação no corpo: a transação é do `db-aplicar.sh`, e ele recusa arquivo que traga `BEGIN;`.

body: ## Why Live farmer testing still showed tomato similar-case language, tomato blight weather cards, and an "Ask about products" button on non-tomato questions. Weather was too generic, follow-up was not loaded on return, `/admin/insights` was incomplete, and voice notes were missing. ## What changed - Hard output guard: tomato, early/late blight, similar-tomato language, and product CTAs are stripped unless tomato is the current crop or the farmer named it. - Similar-case retrieval requires current crop, matching retrieved crop, symptom overlap, and at least two unique farmers. Unknown crop returns nothing. Never substitutes tomato. - Weather relevance is `omit` / `supporting` / `important` / `central`. Large weather-risk cards render only for important/central. Tomato blight models do not run for celery, lettuce, pepper, or unknown crop. Whitefly cards require whitefly/sticky/sooty evidence, not warmth alone. - Product CTA removed from playbook, UI quick replies, and output guard. - IPM treatment shape (diagnose → cultural → biological → chemical when justified) with country-specific verification language. - Voice notes in the existing chat composer: mic, timer, cancel, playback, Whisper transcription with Caribbean agriculture vocabulary, same case pipeline, `input_mode=voice`. - In-app follow-up: 24h / 2–3d / 5–7d by severity; skip math/cashflow; Improved / About the same / Worse / Solved; Worse reopens the case. - `/admin/insights` production cards: Today, Last 7 days, crop intelligence, pesticide coverage, business question buckets, engagement, follow-up status, staff case review actions. Empty state is `0` / `No data`. ## Validation - `npm test` — 298 passed - `npx tsc --noEmit` — pass - `npm run build` — pass Live Preview (`https://fvmltd-farmer-assistant-nxmi-4zm2u6oym-fvmltd.vercel.app`): - Celery outer-leaf burn: zero tomato / blight / product CTA; weather omitted - Lettuce brown edges: zero tomato / blight / product CTA - Sweet pepper Cercospora in Trinidad: zero tomato; supporting weather sentence only; no blight card - Grenada whiteflies on sweet pepper: zero tomato; no Trinidad-as-Grenada registration - Valid tomato leaf spots: tomato retained; important weather card allowed; no product CTA - Celery follow-up created: "How is your celery doing since we last checked the leaf burn?" author: thelinuxkid
body:
## Summary

`emitContractTs` was forcing every submission flow with a captured request body onto the job-application payload template (`ApplicantContactSchema.extend({ Email, ClickUrl, Answers, ... })`), regardless of whether the flow had anything to do with a job/benefits application. The root cause was a check on `Boolean(inputBody)` alone. This PR replaces that with `usesApplicantContactSchema`, a gate that only selects the template when the captured `inputBody` itself carries one of the schema's own field names (checked at any depth). Flows with a captured body but no such evidence now correctly fall back to a plain `z.object({})` base, with genuinely-discovered fields still layered on via `.extend()`.

## What changed

- `src/scripts/recon-generate.ts`: introduced `usesApplicantContactSchema`, computed by walking all primitive leaves of the captured `inputBody` and checking field-name segments against `ApplicantContactSchema`'s own field names (identity/address/resume fields plus `Email`/`ClickUrl`/`Answers`), case-insensitively. Every downstream decision that previously branched on `Boolean(inputBody)` — base schema selection, the `Email`/`ClickUrl`/`Answers` extend fields, the multipart `Resume*` fields, the reserved-field-name check, and the `multipartJsonObject` import gate — now branches on `usesApplicantContactSchema` instead.
- `src/scripts/recon-generate-multicall-fixture.ts`: added `buildMulticallHeterogeneousActionStepsWithBookingSubmit`, a site-agnostic multi-step REST fixture (auth mint → paged facet search → availability drill → terminal submit POST) whose captured bodies carry only facet/booking-style fields and no applicant evidence.
- `src/scripts/recon-generate-non-applicant-submission-payload-schema-e2e.test.ts` (new): drives the real `recon-generate` CLI end-to-end against the new fixture and asserts the emitted contract never contains `ApplicantContactSchema`/`Email`/`ClickUrl`/`Answers`, while still surfacing the flow's own genuine fields.
- `src/scripts/recon-generate-repeated-section-e2e.test.ts` and `src/scripts/recon-generate-multipart-explainer-gate.test.ts`: flipped/updated assertions that had pinned the old unconditional-`ApplicantContactSchema` behavior on fixtures carrying no applicant evidence, and added real evidence fields (e.g. `FirstName`) to cases meant to exercise the applicant path.
- `src/scripts/recon-generate.test.ts`: flipped assertions across several `describe` blocks (candidate-payload default, read-flow payload, vendor-dump golden fixture, merged `.extend()` fixture) to expect the plain base schema when no evidence is present, and added `Email` evidence to cases intended to keep exercising the applicant-schema path. Clarified one `describe` title (`"submission-flow candidate-payload bodySchema with genuine applicant evidence"`) now that selection is evidence-driven rather than unconditional.

## Why

Fixing the issues reported in `recon-generate-generate-submission-flow-forces-applicantcontactschema-onto-non-form-multi-step-rest-flows.md`: a non-form, multi-step REST submission flow was getting the job-application payload schema forced onto it purely because a request body was captured, with no evidence that the flow was actually an application. The fix addresses the root cause in `emitContractTs`'s schema-selection logic rather than special-casing any particular site or plugin.

author: tridentintelfree
body:
Reported: *"I can't get a decent focus at any depth or distance with or without the zoom."*

That wasn't the lens. Four compounding bugs meant the preview could never resolve detail.

## Root causes

1. **Resolution thrown away.** Processing was capped at 1920px and the adaptive scaler could drop it to 0.55 (~1056px), then the result was upscaled to a ~2130px canvas. Permanently soft before focus mattered. Buffers are now sized to the display's own pixel count.
2. **Zoom magnified an already-shrunken buffer.** Zoom was applied at composite time. It now crops at **ingest**, from the full-resolution video — 2× into a 4K frame keeps ~1900 real pixels across instead of interpolating a thumbnail.
3. **Aspect stretch.** 16:9 video was mapped onto a 2.17:1 canvas with no correction. Ingest now crops aspect-fill; verified crop and screen aspect match exactly.
4. **No focus control existed** — no tap-to-focus, and continuous AF was never even requested.

## Added
- **Tap to focus** with a reticle. The tap is mapped through the ingest crop so the point of interest is where the user tapped *in the scene*, not where it landed on the letterboxed canvas.
- **Manual focus slider**, shown only when the browser exposes `focusDistance`
- Zoom is now an **absolute focal multiplier**; crossing a lens threshold hands over to the next lens rather than magnifying, and the range is bounded by where real detail runs out. Macro pins the ultra-wide so hand-over can't defeat it.
- Denoise tap spacing 1.4 → 1.0 texels and lower denoise in the night modes — the wide radius was sampling past genuine detail and reading as softness
- Adaptive quality floor 0.55 → 0.75
- Info panel now reports **detail ratio**, screen pixels, tap-to-focus and focus modes, so softness is diagnosable instead of guessed at
- `window.lumen` debug handle for inspecting the live pipeline

## Verified
With quality pinned (modelling an unthrottled GPU), measured directly from the pipeline:

```
zoom 1x    proc 1875x855  screen 1875x855  detail 1.00 SHARP
zoom 1.5x  proc 1875x855  screen 1875x855  detail 1.00 SHARP
zoom 2x    proc 1875x855  screen 1875x855  detail 1.00 SHARP
zoom 3x    proc 1280x584  screen 1875x855  detail 0.68 upscaled
aspect  crop: 2.193  screen: 2.193  MATCH (no stretch)
```

1×–2× is now pixel-perfect. The drop at 3× is correct on the test device, which has only a 1× lens — on hardware with a telephoto, 3× hands over to that lens and detail returns to 1.0. Full regression across all six modes passes with zero JS errors.

body:
## 무엇을

고전 원서 12권 **모든 챕터**에 낭독 mp3를 추가했습니다. 이제 라이브러리 **19권 전체**(명대사 + 원서 12 + 성경 6)가 낭독을 지원합니다.

| 책 | 챕터 | 오디오 길이 |
|---|---|---|
| Wizard of Oz | 24 | ~3.3h |
| Alice in Wonderland | 12 | ~2.3h |
| The Secret Garden | 27 | ~6.9h |
| Anne of Green Gables | 38 | ~8.9h |
| Sherlock Holmes | 12 | ~9.1h |
| Call of the Wild | 7 | ~2.8h |
| A Christmas Carol | 5 | ~2.6h |
| Treasure Island | 34 | ~5.8h |
| Jekyll and Hyde | 10 | ~2.3h |
| The Great Gatsby | 9 | ~4.5h |
| Pride and Prejudice | 61 | ~11.1h |
| Frankenstein | 24 | ~6.3h |
| **합계** | **263** | **~66h** |

- 경로 `public/audio/<bookId>/ch<N>.mp3` — 리더가 이미 확인하는 규칙이라 **코드 변경 없이** 각 챕터에 "이 챕터 듣기" 플레이어가 나타납니다.
- 엔진: Kokoro-82M · `af_heart` (기존 성경/명대사와 동일).
- 포맷: 24 kHz 모노 · **48 kbps**.
- `--`(옛 대시 표기)는 대시로, 강조용 전체 대문자 단어(`HISPANIOLA` 등)는 첫 글자만 대문자로 정규화.
- `tts-text/<bookId>/` 커밋(원문 텍스트), 체크리스트 완료 표시, README 갱신.

## ⚠️ 용량 — 머지 전에 결정 필요

이 PR로 **`public/audio/`가 약 1.7 GB**가 됩니다 (이번 원서분 ~1.35 GB + 기존 성경/명대사 ~0.36 GB). `.git` 히스토리에도 그대로 남습니다.

선택지:

1. **이대로 머지** — clone·배포가 느려지고 GitHub가 1 GB 초과 저장소에 경고를 보냅니다. 개별 파일은 최대 16 MB(프랑켄슈타인 마지막 장)라 push 자체는 통과.
2. **비트레이트 더 낮추기** — 32 kbps 모노로 재생성하면 원서분 ~0.9 GB, 전체 ~1.2 GB. (전화 음질 수준이지만 듣기 학습엔 충분) 재인코딩이 아니라 파이프라인에서 다시 뽑는 방식(약 1시간). 원하시면 진행합니다.
3. **Git LFS** — `.gitattributes`로 `public/audio/**/*.mp3`를 LFS로. GitHub 무료 LFS는 저장/대역 각 1 GB라 유료 플랜이 필요합니다.
4. **외부 스토리지** — Cloudflare R2(무료 10 GB) 등에 올리고, 리더가 절대 URL도 받도록 소폭 수정. 저장소는 가벼워지고 배포도 빨라집니다. (별도 작업)

> 추천: 지금 **머지하지 말고**, 위 중 무엇으로 갈지 먼저 정해주세요. 2번(32 kbps)이나 4번(R2)을 권합니다.

## 확인

```
npm run dev
```
→ 라이브러리에서 아무 원서 열기 → 아무 챕터 → "이 챕터 듣기" 재생. (스팟 체크: Alice/P&P/Frankenstein/Gatsby/Treasure Island 재생·길이·음량 정상)

author: manitchahar
body:
### Link to Issue or Description of Change

Closes #6056.

`LoggingPlugin` cuts off message text and system instructions at 200 characters,
and tool arguments/results at 300. A diagnostic at the end of a long tool result
is therefore missing from the console output.

Add two keyword-only constructor options, `max_content_length=200` and
`max_args_length=300`. Existing defaults are unchanged; `None` disables
truncation. The change only touches the existing plugin and its test file.

```python
LoggingPlugin(max_content_length=None, max_args_length=None)
```

This is a draft pending feedback on the constructor options requested in the
issue discussion. No maintainer agreement on this API is assumed.

### Testing Plan

- [x] Added regression tests for custom limits, boundary lengths, zero, and
  unlimited output through the public callbacks.
- [ ] All repository unit tests pass locally.

Results:

- Before the patch: 20 new cases fail, 11 existing tests pass.
- Built-wheel logging tests: **31 passed on each of Python 3.10, 3.11, 3.12,
  3.13, and 3.14**, using isolated environments.
- Plugin suite on Python 3.11: **802 passed, 2 skipped, 8 failed**. The eight
  failures are in `TestSafetyLifecycleHardening` in the BigQuery analytics
  plugin. Re-running that class against unchanged upstream `d9b57bf` reproduced
  the same eight failures, with 91 passing tests.
- Formatting, lint, and compliance checks pass. The new-file hook cannot invoke
  `/bin/bash` on Windows; its underlying command,
  `python scripts/check_new_py_files.py --new-dir .`, passes when run directly.
  The optional addlicense executable was not installed; existing license headers
  were preserved.
- `uv build --wheel` succeeds. The documentation example executes successfully.
- The full tox matrix was attempted but stopped while its first environment was
  still running without a result. It is **not** reported as passing. The broad
  mypy run also did not finish and is not reported as passing.

#### Manual End-to-End Evidence

A real `InMemoryRunner` uses a local scripted `BaseLlm` to call a diagnostic
tool, then emit a model response. This exercises actual runner/plugin dispatch
without credentials or a remote model. The same reproduction passes from the
built wheel in an isolated environment.

| Marker after the default cutoff | Defaults | Limits of 600 | Limits of None |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Tool result error detail | Hidden | Visible | Visible |
| Model response detail | Hidden | Visible | Visible |
| System instruction detail | Hidden | Visible | Visible |

### Checklist

- [x] Read the contribution guide and self-reviewed the diff.
- [x] Added regression tests and exercised the runner end to end.
- [x] Preserved defaults and kept unrelated code unchanged.
- [ ] Maintainer agreement on the proposed options.
- [ ] Complete full-suite validation before marking ready for review.
- [ ] Documentation change merged and published.

<details>
<summary>Runner reproduction</summary>

Save as logging_repro.py and run with the built wheel installed.

```python
"""Exercise LoggingPlugin through a real Runner without a model API call."""

import asyncio
from contextlib import redirect_stdout
from io import StringIO

from google.adk.agents import LlmAgent
from google.adk.models.base_llm import BaseLlm
from google.adk.models.llm_response import LlmResponse
from google.adk.plugins.logging_plugin import LoggingPlugin
from google.adk.runners import InMemoryRunner
from google.genai import types


def diagnose() -> dict:
    """Return a diagnostic with the failure detail at the end."""
    return {"details": "x" * 400, "error": "TOOL_ERROR_AT_END"}


class ScriptedModel(BaseLlm):
    async def generate_content_async(self, llm_request, stream=False):
        has_result = any(
            part.function_response
            for content in llm_request.contents
            for part in content.parts or []
        )
        part = (
            types.Part(text="x" * 250 + "MODEL_DETAIL_AT_END")
            if has_result
            else types.Part.from_function_call(name="diagnose", args={})
        )
        yield LlmResponse(content=types.Content(role="model", parts=[part]))


async def run(label, **limits):
    agent = LlmAgent(
        name="diagnostic",
        model=ScriptedModel(model="scripted"),
        instruction="x" * 250 + "INSTRUCTION_AT_END",
        tools=[diagnose],
    )
    output = StringIO()
    async with InMemoryRunner(
        agent=agent, plugins=[LoggingPlugin(**limits)]
    ) as runner:
        session = await runner.session_service.create_session(
            app_name=runner.app_name, user_id="test"
        )
        with redirect_stdout(output):
            async for event in runner.run_async(
                user_id="test", session_id=session.id,
                new_message=types.Content(
                    role="user", parts=[types.Part(text="Run the diagnostic.")]
                ),
            ):
                pass
    for marker in ("TOOL_ERROR_AT_END", "MODEL_DETAIL_AT_END", "INSTRUCTION_AT_END"):
        visible = marker in output.getvalue()
        assert visible == (label != "default"), (label, marker, output.getvalue())
        print(f"{label}: {marker} visible={visible}")


async def main():
    await run("default")
    await run("custom", max_content_length=600, max_args_length=600)
    await run("unlimited", max_content_length=None, max_args_length=None)


asyncio.run(main())

```

</details>

Companion documentation: https://github.com/google/adk-docs/pull/2215

author: itlackey
body:
## Summary

Fixes #121.

`experimental.chat.system.transform` pushed the AKM context block as a new entry on `output.system`. OpenCode turns every entry into its own `{role: "system"}` message, so with the plugin loaded every request carried the host's system message plus a second one. Qwen chat templates reject any system message that is not the first (`Jinja Exception: System message must be at the beginning.`), llama.cpp answers HTTP 500, and `opencode run` fails after retries. The earlier #96 change (join the plugin's own blocks into one entry) was necessary but not sufficient: that one entry was still a second system message.

The budgeted AKM block is now merged into the host's **last** existing entry, separated by a blank line; a new entry is pushed only when `output.system` is empty. The plugin therefore never changes the number of system messages the host built (except zero to one). Merging into the last entry rather than the first keeps the host's leading entry a stable prompt-cache prefix, since AKM's blocks change from turn to turn. `applyContextBudget` is unchanged.

## Tests

`tests/opencode-plugin.test.ts`:

- the #96 single-entry test now seeds a host entry and asserts the merge (entry count stays 1, host text leads, curated pointer still precedes the doctrine block)
- two host entries: the first is byte-identical afterwards, the last carries the AKM block, count stays 2
- empty host array: one entry is pushed (behaviour kept)
- nothing to inject: the host entry is left untouched, no trailing separator
- the every-transform test seeds a host entry on both calls

The two entry-count tests fail against the previous code (2 and 3 entries) and pass with the fix. Full suite: 308 pass, 0 fail; both plugins typecheck; `opencode` builds.

No version bump: `release.yml` derives and commits the version itself.

author: joaquindecima
body:
`vasak-mail` (en construcción) entra a la lista de alcances por binario con
**nada**. Es el segundo alcance vacío, y el caso que más se gana de los cinco.

## Por qué

La aplicación de correo es **la más expuesta del escritorio**: lo que muestra lo
escribió cualquiera que sepa la dirección de la persona. No un servidor con el
que decidió tener una cuenta — cualquiera.

Y a la vez es la que menos tiene para perder, porque **no lee el correo**. Se lo
pide ya interpretado a `vasak-accounts-sync` (Vasak-OS/vasak-accounts#14), que sí
tiene `account.email`, habla IMAP, corre el parser de MIME y no dibuja nada.

Esta línea es lo que convierte ese reparto en un límite en vez de una convención
del código. Sin ella, un `vasak-mail` reemplazado podría pedir `account.email` y
la persona vería un diálogo pidiéndole permiso para algo que la aplicación de
verdad nunca necesitó — y que si concede, entrega la contraseña de su casilla.

## Qué hay acá

- `SCOPED_BINARIES` pasa de 4 a 5 entradas.
- Un test que ejerce el límite, con `account.email` en primer lugar.
- El comentario del test de `vasak-settings` decía «el caso más fuerte de la
  lista» cuando era el único vacío; ahora son dos y lo dice.

## Verificación

`cargo test` (180 tests) y `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, limpios.

body:
Recuts `GiorgoloAsudeh2012` onto mathlib's `WriterT` stack instead of a hand-rolled `TwoChannel` record: the paper's two channels are `WriterT (List CI) (Writer (List Presup))` with `write` the transformer's `tell` and `check` lifted from the base monad as the paper's footnote prescribes; Shan's application is the monad's `<*>` (`atIssue_seq`, `ciLog_seq`, `presupLog_seq`); the flow restriction is stated as general lemmas (`atIssue_bind_congr`, `ciLog_prefix_bind`) rather than one `rfl` on the example; and the worked derivation of "John, who likes cats, likes dogs also" is parametric in the extension of *like*, with the presupposition of *also* derived from the logged implicature (`Ex20.presupposition_of_ci`) instead of evaluated in a Bool model.

- `Semantics/Composition/Writer.lean` gains `log_prefix_bind` (bind is isotone for the prefix order, the paper's footnote 2) and `val_bind_congr`
- Cuts the flattened `TwoChannel` + nested-Writer isomorphism, the Bool `like` model, the `TwoDimProp` bridge, the Class B checks against a 2013 taxonomy (a chronology violation), and the PostSupp prose bridge
- Bib: `anderbois-brasoveanu-henderson-2010`, `barker-bernardi-shan-2010` added from the paper's reference list (no DOIs); paper text from the open-access MITWPL proceedings PDF

author: vincentkoc
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Worker transcript admission eagerly loads the session execution graph before any transcript commit is accepted. That unnecessarily broadens the Gateway's cold import graph, including for requests rejected before transcript work begins.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep the committer factory, store, fast rejection checks, and per-session queue eager. Load the existing transcript runtime through the shared process-level lazy loader inside the queue, before authority validation or ledger reservation. The original store, request, and authority closure continue into the unchanged application logic.

There is no SQLite schema, configuration, protocol, or transcript representation change. The synchronous transaction boundary, rollback handling, replay/recovery behavior, and post-publication RPC authority check remain intact.

The follow-up assertion-safety repair uses the canonical `isRecord` guard for record access, documents the role-schema/content-cloning invariants at the three message construction assertions, and carries the actual `AgentMessage` result through private post-redaction and recovery types. It removes the redactor-result assertion rather than asserting that redaction preserves a narrower structural type. The only baseline deletion is the obsolete six-assertion row for the former runtime owner.

Using `--no-renames` accounting, cumulative production changes are +533/-508, net +25; most lines are the 508-line extraction, and the remainder defines the lazy owner boundary and scaffold. Tests add 202 lines. The follow-up repair itself is production +12/-14, net -2; the shrink-only baseline deletion is counted separately.

Related work: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/138688 independently changes the same transcript owner. It is neither a duplicate nor a stack parent. Its replay/cursor-completion ordering after commit and before publication yield must survive rebase and landing.

## User Impact

Worker admission no longer needs to materialize session execution code until valid transcript work reaches its queue. Transcript results and rejection behavior are unchanged. This establishes the import boundary; it does not claim a measured end-user latency improvement.

Release context: this is internal Gateway loading and type-boundary maintenance. Operators do not need a configuration change, database migration, or new workflow. The assertion repair does not change transcript redaction behavior.

## Evidence

- Original proof base: `008cf5d9b0a4b1dcae5517706ea06d31ec1082ff`.
- Original tested source: `8712cd4e62aad7794531a9016e284fa5e800384f` (signed commit).
- Publication base: `8642c68b6b9f6ee42fa91641dd8656fcf0a617a9`.
- Original publication head: `bcbbadc6f41bf9a366967b90040478551063fdc6`.
- Current signed head: `ff1cacc9c6bf1bb03cc962ebd866fe38cc2b5ef6`.
- The original rebase preserved the exact four-file patch. Connected runtime owners and helpers matched; the Gateway test config only removed an unrelated history-route exclusion, which does not affect the selected proofs. The subsequent repair changes only `transcript-commit.runtime.ts` and the obsolete assertion baseline row.
- Before the original production change, the cold-import regression failed on the session execution backedge. That focused run had one intended failure and 19 skipped tests. This remains historical pre-change evidence.
- Original focused validation passed all 23 tests: 15 transcript-commit tests, five isolated lazy-loading tests, and three worker RPC transcript tests. The wrapper exited 0 after generation verification and disposal.
- Coverage includes actual rollback injection, replay/recovery, authority revocation during loading, loader failure without a reservation, fast rejection without runtime loading, and the sibling post-publication authority/ACK boundary.
- The reset-based lazy-loader tests use a separate module-generation fixture; the existing rollback test retains the same SessionManager constructor as its runtime.
- The assertion-safety ratchet first failed on the pre-repair runtime with six assertions above its zero baseline. The identical native check passed after the canonical guard/type repair and exact obsolete-row deletion.
- Fresh validation on September 10 ran the same three focused files on the repaired candidate: **23 passed, zero failed, zero skipped**, 24.509 seconds. Native exit and close were both 0; the owned process group was absent, the generation was verified and disposed, temporary/generation directories were empty, and source/index pins were unchanged.
- Fresh whole-candidate protected review against the publication base covered 87 source/context files in four native passes: scoped-clean through P2, zero findings, exit 0, joined, source/index pins unchanged. The reviewed runtime and baseline bytes were committed unchanged in the current signed head. Historical reviews are retained as historical evidence, not rerated.
- Targeted native core lint, runtime formatting, assertion-safety ratchet, and whitespace checks passed. `check:changed --dry-run` classified the follow-up as core, core-test, and tooling work; this classification is not execution of those lanes.
- Fresh exact-head CI, affected core/core-test type projects, full build, and native pre-landing qualification are still required after this push. No local full build or broad `check:changed` run is claimed by the focused results.

Focused test selection (the fresh recorded run also emitted verbose and JSON reports):


author: addieflips
body:
Addie, on five houses parked in *Waiting on light colours*: *"check to see if these guys just wanted there timer updated. Cause if so we don't need to worry about lights just about getting a timer in there bin"*, then, shown the cause: *"can you fix those."*

## What was wrong

[[WH-26]] stopped the timer being **lost**. This stops the house being **parked**.

`outletTimer` is one of the three `WAREHOUSE_BUILD_FIELDS`, so changing a timer and nothing else set `needsLightBuild` — and a house with no colours then landed in the blocked block, under a heading reading *"Nothing can be made up until somebody fills them in."*

That sentence is **false** about those houses. Nobody is waiting on any colours, because nobody asked for lights. So the office was sent to chase an answer that does not exist, and the row could never clear.

## The fix

`needsTimerOnly` is the timer's own queue. `whTimerOnlyQueue` decides it at the write site — its own function so a test can **run** it rather than match its text — `whBuildQueueGroups` reads either flag as an OR, and such a house reaches `timerHouses` and never `blocked`.

**It fails towards the build, and that is why it is a separate flag rather than a marker on the existing one.** It can never clear or suppress `needsLightBuild`. A stale `needsTimerOnly` costs one extra row on a list; a marker able to switch the build flag off would — the first time one of the seven places that queue a build forgot to clear it — leave a house nobody builds.

**Scoped narrowly, deliberately:**
- Turning a timer **off** still queues a rebuild. `timerHouses` only ever collects Yes, so a removal routed here would vanish off every screen — worse than the untidiness this fixes.
- A **wire** change is still a build, and so is a timer change on a house that **has** colours. That house is in a real build group and always was. Holes C and D are not reversed.

**The houses already parked get a way out**, because a fix that cannot reach the case that prompted it is not finished: **Only needed a timer** on the blocked row, offered only where a timer is on file, undone by *Build Them A New Set*. A person answers — nothing on the record separates a timer-queued house from one converted with its colours still to come, the same wall `lightsChangedVia` hit. And a timer-only house is in no colour group, so it gets a **Timer in the bin** button of its own: the Done goes where the work is.

## What the gates caught

Worth reading, because they all fired correctly:

This PR was created by AI Gareth

## Top-Level Summary
This PR implements Milestone R2: reduced-basis matched filtering for the PyCBC persistent GPU search engine. It enables Singular Value Decomposition (SVD) low-rank basis decomposition for coherent template subbanks, filtering only $R \ll M$ orthonormal basis waveforms via IFFT and reconstructing full template responses via high-throughput GEMM matrix multiplication.

## Standard information about the request

This is a: new feature, efficiency update

This change affects: the offline search, the live search

This change changes: scientific output

This change: has appropriate unit tests, follows style guidelines (See e.g. [PEP8](https://peps.python.org/pep-0008/)), has been proposed using the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/gwastro/pycbc/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md)

This change will: not break current functionality, require no additional mandatory dependencies (preserves CPU/numpy execution when PyTorch/CUDA is unavailable)

## Motivation
Gravitational-wave template banks for compact binary coalescences feature high overlap between neighboring templates in parameter space ($>95\%$). Conventional matched filtering evaluates independent IFFTs for all $M$ templates in a bank tile. By taking advantage of the low-rank subspace spanned by template subbanks via SVD, we compress $M$ chirps into $R \ll M$ orthonormal basis vectors (e.g. rank $R \le 4$ for $M = 16-32$ templates, achieving $>99.999\%$ energy capture). Matched filtering is performed on the $R$ basis waveforms, followed by batched tensor-core GEMM reconstruction of the candidate SNR time series, reducing IFFT overhead by $M / R$ with controlled truncation tolerance ($\le 10^{-3}$).

## Contents
- `pycbc/filter/gpu_search/reduced_basis.py`:
  - `ReducedBasisPlan`: Low-rank basis storage, SVD expansion coefficients, singular values, and device migration methods (`.to(device)`).
  - `ReducedBasisPSDPlan`: Frequency-cutoff-aware template $\sigma^2$ variance and normalization factors for reconstructed templates under stationary noise PSDs.
  - `compute_reduced_basis`: SVD computation on template subbanks with energy-fraction rank truncation according to user tolerance and optional maximum rank.
  - `bind_reduced_basis_psd`: Precomputes template sigmasqs and inverse PSD norms with proper `[kmin, kmax]` band-limiting.
  - `ReducedBasisSearchEngine`: Engine executing basis IFFT filtering, GEMM template reconstruction, device candidate selection/clustering, and optional veto evaluation.
- `pycbc/filter/gpu_search/__init__.py`:
  - Exports `ReducedBasisPlan`, `ReducedBasisPSDPlan`, `compute_reduced_basis`, `bind_reduced_basis_psd`, and `ReducedBasisSearchEngine`.
- `test/test_gpu_search_reduced_basis.py`:
  - Comprehensive unit and integration test suite parameterized across CPU and CUDA (`test_reduced_basis_svd_rank_truncation`, `test_reduced_basis_search_parity`, `test_reduced_basis_veto_evaluation`, `test_reduced_basis_overflow_and_abort`, `test_reduced_basis_plan_migration`).
